subject: ARCH
title: Introduction to the Built Environment
description: Introduction to the breadth of design in today’s global culture. Exploration of human responses to place, climate, culture, communication, and technology, with emphasis on the impact of scientific knowledge on environmental design. Open to nonmajors.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Fundamentals Studio I
description: Introduction to creative design processes focusing on the investigation of composition within defining perceivable space. Hands-on exploration of materials and structures as an introduction to design processes.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Fundamentals Studio II
description: Continued exploration of design processes. Introduction to CAD technologies, material exploration, and creative exploration including the relationship between digital, physical, and materials aspects of design.

subject: ARCH
title: Collaboration in Environmental Design
description: Investigation of the various disciplines in the environmental design field, including architecture, landscape architecture, interiors, historic preservation, urban design, and construction management. Emphasis given to collaborative methods to address critical issues. Open to non-majors.

subject: ARCH
title: Beginning Design Studio I
description: Exploration of critical judgment and means to conceptualize, develop, represent, and both visually and orally communicate form and space, including freehand drawing, mechanical drawing, physical model making, diagramming, and computer graphic techniques.

subject: ARCH
title: Beginning Design Studio II
description: Development of designs and processes to study precedents and explore solutions responding to human needs in built and natural environments. Analysis and representation of architectonic space and form using hand and computer techniques.

subject: ARCH
title: Introduction to Environmental Systems A
description: Introduction to building systems, including structural, environmental, life-safety, building envelope, building materials and building assemblies. Development of design skills with emphasis on elevating skills in assessing and selecting appropriate building systems.

subject: ARCH
title: World Architecture and Urbanism A
description: Investigation of the history and theory of architecture in the world’s major cultural regions, from early agricultural settlements to 1500 C.E. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces.

subject: ARCH
title: World Architecture and Urbanism B
description: Investigation of the history and theory of architecture from the 15th century C.E. to the present. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces.

subject: ARCH
title: Introduction to Environmental Systems B
description: Introduction to environmentalism; focusing on the impact of building systems of the global environment; the role of environmental regulations/certifications, and understanding of sustainable principles (economic, social, and natural systems).

subject: ARCH
title: Intermediate Design Studio I
description: Building and site design with emphasis on site development, analysis, and climatic response. Introduction to sustainable design, land use ordinances, description and delineation of property and land features, and urban and community design influences.

subject: ARCH
title: Intermediate Design Studio II
description: Architectural design with emphasis on space planning, building materials, technology, climatic responses, and codes including complex functional requirements, multi-story design issues, vertical transportation, structure, and finishes. Production of complete schematic design documents. Detailed writing instruction.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Architecture History
description: Survey of the history of landscape architecture from Mesopotamia to present. Review of the physical, cultural, social, economic, and political factors, as well as the environmental concerns, horticultural techniques, and technological innovations of historic landscapes.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Graphics Studio
description: Basic skills of landscape graphic communication through a creative process model. Learning free hand and technical drafting techniques to creative effective landscape graphics.

subject: ARCH
title: Tropical Landscape Planting Design Studio
description: Students will develop basic skills of residential landscape graphic and design processes in order to clearly articulate the ability to think, analyze, and extend a physical solution in the proper scale. (Alt. years)

subject: ARCH
title: Design Theory
description: Examination of theories, movements, and periods in architectural history focusing on contemporary issues. Requires a minimum of 4,000 words of writing, and three oral communication assignments.

subject: ARCH
title: Landform and Water
description: Essential topographic site design concepts and skills needed to reshape the land for human use, circulation, water management, and resilience. Topics will be reinforced through problem sets and analytical, computational, graphical, and technical exercises.

subject: ARCH
title: Concentration Design Studio
description: Professional experience combined with scholarly and research activity occurring in an off-campus location with a focus on architectural concentration areas.

subject: ARCH
title: Capstone Design Studio
description: Culminating design studio with focus on the development of a comprehensive design project integrating all major aspects of prior environmental design education.

subject: ARCH
title: Construction Project Management
description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor.

subject: ARCH
title: Professional Practice Law and Ethics
description: Knowledge of professional standards and a broad understanding of the practice of architecture, including professionalism; ethical conduct; public, client, consultant, contractor, and government relations; project administration, contracts, procedures, and compensation; land use and construction law.

subject: ARCH
title: Digital Design Synthesis
description: Investigation of processes for generating architectonic form using current digital technologies. Making advanced geometric models including investigation of morphological transformations. Study of design optimization, digital fabrication, information modeling, and generative algorithms.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Exchange
description: Seminar centered on academic and cultural exchanges, focused on advanced topics related to the design of built environments.

subject: ARCH
title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, and sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/HAER).
restrictions_raw: ARCH, ENVD, and AMST majors only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, up to 24 credits

subject: ARCH
title: History of American Architecture
description: History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning.

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation: Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific
description: Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions.

subject: ARCH
title: Urban Ecological Analysis and Design
description: Applied urban and landscape ecology principles and strategies for analysis, design, and management of urban regions and sites; emphasis on structure, functions, and processes that form urban landscapes at multiple scales and in diverse contexts.

subject: ARCH
title: Plants in Design
description: Introduction to the use of plants as design elements in the built environment across diverse scales. Examination of the spatial, sensory, ecological, and performative qualities of vegetation through analysis of historic and contemporary examples.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics
description: Selected topics in any aspect of architecture. Content to be announced.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture History
description: Specialized work on the history and theory of architecture.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
description: Specialized investigation of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
description: Work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics.

subject: ARCH
title: Explore Furniture Design
description: Exploration of design and building principles as related to furniture. Emphasis on fundamentals of practice and an understanding of materials and structure, with an intensive hands-on building experience.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Writing
description: Reading, research, and work on topics in architecture and design. Includes an intensive writing component. May include specialized research and/or studio experience in architecture, design, and the history and theory of architecture and design.

subject: ARCH
title: American Architecture
description: Cultural analysis of the evolution of American architecture from the Colonial period to the present involving sociopolitical and economic, as well as aesthetic, considerations.

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Communication for Landscape Architects
description: Theory and application in design communication, including drawing and presentation skills; emphasis on the design process and critical thinking through analog and digital media, diagramming, three-dimensional modeling, and various other presentation techniques.

subject: ARCH
title: Computer Applications in Landscape Architecture
description: Introduction to the use of computers in landscape architecture, emphasizing two- and three dimensional computer-aided drawings and graphics suitable to landscape architectural design and practice.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Plants: Identification and Use
description: Introduction to the identification, recognition, and use of plants in landscape design and built environment applications. Students will be introduced to a variety of landscape plants commonly used in Hawai‘i and the tropics.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Materials and Construction
description: Examination of materials and methods of landscape construction from source, extraction, and manufacturing, to use and reuse. Assignments include drawing standard construction details and a report on the history of material use, properties, and qualities. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Architectural Professional Practice
description: Introduction of practices and core methods of the landscape architecture profession. Subjects include business and governmental organization, elements of contract law, business management, professional relationships, marketing, professional licensure, and ethics. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Land Use Planning
description: Issues and methods of urban land use planning practice and plan making.

subject: ARCH
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawai‘i and the region. (Alt. years: spring only)

subject: ARCH
title: Vernacular Architecture
description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas.

subject: ARCH
title: Fundamentals of Landscape Design Studio
description: Theory and application of foundational landscape design principles, programming, and physical analysis to site-based design problems. Visual, formal, spatial, and functional design principles are applied to ecological and cultural influences in landscape design. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Site Design Studio
description: Landscape project design at the site scale; from concept development through detailed design. Synthesis of foundational skills into more complex, layered spatial, and functional problems. Emphasis on site research and design methods. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Environmental and Cultural Landscape Studio
description: Exploring, understanding, and implementing Hawaiian and Western cultural and environmental landscape design principles. A concentrated look at how to think about creating and respecting a sense of place through landscape design.

subject: ARCH
title: Environmental Landscape Technologies and Systems
description: Understanding the science and art of green landscape technologies, with a comprehensive understanding of LID (low impact design) principles and practices; to increase knowledge to help produce more viable and enduring built landscapes.

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation Field Seminar
description: Provides participants with basic knowledge of the field of historic preservation as well as the fundamental knowledge of how to document, conserve, and preserve both tangible and intangible cultural properties.

subject: ARCH
title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures. Graduate students only or consent.

subject: ARCH
title: Historic Preservation Planning
description: Local-level historic preservation, with an emphasis on historic districts, design guidelines, regulatory controls, and community consensus-building.

subject: ARCH
title: Elements of Style
description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/ cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present.

subject: ARCH
title: Building Well-Being: Health and the Built Environment
description: History, concepts, and theories behind the relationship between health and the built environment stressing transdisciplinary understanding and collaboration through readings, discussion, and real world-based exercises. Graduate students only.
restrictions_raw: LAND, ARCH, and PLAN majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) Preservation Field Study
description: On-site historic preservation field study. Site will rotate. Academic and hands-on preservation training. (B) Hawai‘i; (C) Asia; (D) Pacific. Each alpha

subject: ARCH
title: Historic Preservation Practicum
description: Applies course work in historic preservation to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and University faculty. Historic preservation certificate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics Seminar
description: Seminar on a wide range of architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
description: Specialized investigation at an advanced level of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
description: Intensive work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Furniture Design and Fabrication
description: Exploration of design and building principles as related to furniture. Emphasis on fundamentals of practice, an understanding of materials and structure, with an intensive hands-on building experience. Additionally, a survey of 20th Century furniture design.

subject: ARCH
title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought. ARCH and LAND majors only, or consent. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Landscape Architecture
description: Seminar on a wide range of landscape architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: MLA Thesis
description: Landscape architectural thesis research and design inquiry. Limited to MLA students under Plan A. Graduate students only. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: ARCH
title: Asia-Pacific Architectural History and Theory
description: Study of the history and theory of culture and the built environment with particular focus on the Asia-Pacific region. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture and Urban Design Theory
description: Detailed investigation of major theories in architecture and urban design and examination of their impact on contemporary architectural practice in varied geo-political contexts. Open to non-majors.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems I: Introduction to Systems
description: Study of building materials, assemblies, and integrated design including structural, environmental, life-safety, and building envelope systems. Development of ability to design, analyze and assess appropriate systems.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems II: Qualitative Bioclimatic and Structural Performance
description: Introduction to the theory of bioclimatic principles and structural systems and the ability to analyze, assess, select, design, and integrate them as initial determinants into the building design.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems III: Quantitative Structural Analysis and Design
description: Introduction to procedures and wood, steel, concrete, and masonry material properties used for structural analysis and design of individual structural elements and building structural systems.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems IV: Environmental Technology, Sustainability, and Analysis
description: Application and analysis of highperformance building design principles. Emphasis on climate-appropriate passive design, energy-efficient lighting and conditioning strategies, innovative water systems, and renewable energy production.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems V: Building Systems Integration
description: Properties, evolution, and range of building m aterials, assemblies, and systems and their applications in integrated high-performance building design with a focus on the role of detail and systems in the design process.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Communication I
description: (Lec, Lab) Exploration of digital technologies, their relationship to design, and their application to architectural analysis, conceptualization, design processes, communication, representation, and construction.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Communication II
description: (Lec, Lab) An interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to digital technology and its applications to current developments in practice and research within architecture and design. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Forms and Frames of Practice
description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice within the global context with emphasis on the Asia Pacific region. Exploration of information technology systems, materials and design process research, construction technology, computer aided manufacturing, and entrepreneurial approaches. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Communications III
description: Interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to architectural presentation techniques, particularly oral and written, to current developments in architectural practice.

subject: ARCH
title: Research Methods Seminar
description: Comprehensive assessment of objectives and function of research in architecture and landscape architecture. Lecture, seminar, independent work with emphasis on research project topic and proposal development. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio I: Intro to Design
description: Design theories and systematic analytic and synthetic methodologies applied to creation of building and site spaces responsive to environmental and human needs. Several individual projects.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio III
description: Design of complex, large scale building and site engaging social, cultural, code, sustainable systems, and acoustic issues. Production of schematic and design development documents. Graduate standing only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio IV: Urban Design
description: Urban design focused on Asian cities investigating social, cultural, political, and technological factors; study of historical precedents, building/block typology, circulation, infrastructure, and context response.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio V: Comprehensive Design
description: Design and programming for a moderately complex building and site. Production of design development and partial construction documents describing sustainable building assemblies and construction cost.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Practice
description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice investigating architect’s response to global forces, including entrepreneurial practice, office organization, project delivery, compensation, and construction law.

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) Professional Studio
description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off-campus location. (B) business; (C) community design; (E) alternative experience; (G) global; (H) Hawai‘i; (P) practicum; (T) China. Graduate standing only for (G), (H), and (T).

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) Research Studio in Professional Setting
description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off campus location. (C) China; (G) global. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) Architecture Studio
description: Urban design focused on investigating social, cultural, political, and technological factors; study of historical precedents, building/block typology, circulation, infrastructure, and context response. (C) China; (G) design research. ARCH Global Track only. Graduate standing only.

subject: ARCH
title: Research Seminar
description: Varied topics furthering knowledge and ability needed for professional design practice emphasizing communication methods for collaborative and integrated design using digital technologies.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Global Practice
description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice investigating architect’s response to global forces, including entrepreneurial practice, office organization, project delivery, compensation, and construction law.

subject: ARCH
title: Ecology, Community, and Design
description: Exploration of the interaction of landscape and community necessities in urban ecological design. Studio problems, design research projects, lectures, and discussion applied to the integration of ecological and social factors in urban contexts. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Project Design Studio: Comprehensive
description: Design and programming for a complex, medium-scale, multi-layered urban landscape architecture project. Iterative, advanced design inquiry and materials exploration. Production of in-depth, comprehensive design development and partial construction documents. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) Capstone Studio
description: Advanced landscape architectural design inquiry and applied research investigation. Serves as a capstone experience, synthesizing theory, values, and practice. Limited to MLA students under Plan B. (D) design (6 credits); (R) research (3 credits). Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time per alpha, up to 18 credits

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture History
description: Investigation of architectural history and theory in the world from antiquity to present. Examining social, political, technological, material, and environmental forces.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Research Methods and Design Inquiry
description: Individual development of a Doctorate Project or MArch Capstone proposal that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, and design.

subject: ARCH
title: Case Study and Analysis
description: Individual development of a case study project that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) MArch Capstone Studio
description: Advanced capstone architectural design research synthesizing theory and practice. (D) design; (R) research. MArch students only.

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) Doctorate Project I
description: Individual development of a doctorate project with an approved chair and doctorate project committee that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, and design; (H) Hawaii; (T) Tongji. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) Doctorate Project II
description: Individual development of a doctorate project with an approved chair and doctorate project committee that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions; (H) Hawaii; (T) Tongji. Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Doctorate Project II Extension
description: Extension of the development of a doctorate project with an approved committee that advances architectural knowledge through research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to American Studies
description: Introduction to different types of college-level writing through analyses of contemporary American culture and to the main themes and approaches used in American studies and the humanities.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to American Studies Writing
description: Introduction to different types of college level writing and information literacy with a focus on American culture and society.

subject: AMST
title: America and the World
description: Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

subject: AMST
title: America and the World
description: Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

subject: AMST
title: American Experience: Institutions and Movements
description: Emergence and transformation of laws, ideologies, institutions, and social movements from the 17th-21st centuries. Emphasis on relationships among structures of power, representational practices, belief systems, and social action. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives. DH

subject: AMST
title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
description: Literature and modern media; visual and performing arts; material culture and architecture; foodways and ritual as meaning-making processes that have shaped the diverse identities, spaces, and communities of the Americas. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives. DH

subject: AMST
title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
description: Literature and modern media; visual and performing arts; material culture and architecture; foodways and ritual as meaning-making processes that have shaped the diverse identities, spaces, and communities of the Americas. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Domestic Issues
description: Current debates in the U.S. over individual rights and nationalism; civil rights, citizenship, and sovereignty; sexuality, law, and religion; economic, racial, and gender equality; public health and environmental justice. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Global Issues
description: Interdisciplinary and transnational perspectives on global issues including international law and diplomacy; war, diaspora, and refugees; economic underdevelopment and environmental racism; globalization, race, and the feminization of poverty. Writing emphasis

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
description: Interdisciplinary survey that examines the histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of the indigenous peoples of the U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, and Samoans.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
description: Interdisciplinary survey that examines the histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of the indigenous peoples of the U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, and Samoans.

subject: AMST
title: Art and Social Change
description: Will analyze examples from the visual and performing arts, including murals, digital art, film, poetry, and music, paying particular attention to the connections and influence upon social and political movements, both historically and today. A-F only

subject: AMST
title: Hip-Hop and American Culture
description: Survey tracing hip-hop from its Afro-Carribean musical beginnings to contemporary adaptations and interpretations. Students will analyze various materials and will pay attention to the relationships between hip-hop and contemporary social forms.

subject: AMST
title: Justice and Asian America: Social Movements and the Law in American History
description: Examination of demands for and the changing nature of justice, historical and contemporary, through court cases, legislation, presidential orders, and social movements that address legal, social, and political definitions of Asian America.

subject: AMST
title: Japanese Americans: History, Culture, Lifestyles
description: Explores experiences of Japanese Americans in Hawaiʻi and the U.S.: historical and cultural heritage, biographical portraits, changing family ties, ethnic lifeways, gender relations, local identity, and the future of island living. Emphasis: oral communication skills. DH

subject: AMST
title: African Americans: Issues, Culture, History
description: Traces the history and culture of African Americans and outlines contemporary issues. Topics include: slavery and racism, community formation and resistance, cultural expression, African American diversity, civil rights, gender and class relations.

subject: AMST
title: U.S. Women’s History
description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work in and outside the household, women’s involvement in social movements, changing norms about gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences among women.

subject: AMST
title: American Music and Culture
description: Analysis of a variety of American musical genres and histories through focused writing assignments (record and performance reviews, personal narratives, interviews, research proposals, research papers).

subject: AMST
title: Asian America
description: History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation.

subject: AMST
title: America, Hawai‘i and World War II
description: Examines WWII as a watershed in American and Hawai‘i history and culture. Topics include: Pearl Harbor, Japanese American internment, sex and racial tensions, Anti-Semitism and the Holocaust, and the dawn of the Atomic Age.

subject: AMST
title: American Environments: Survey
description: Survey of social, political, and cultural relations in diverse, contemporary American environments, including: island societies, urban centers, suburbs, Indian reservations, farming communities, and national parks. Special emphasis on contemporary environmental issues in Hawai‘i.

subject: AMST
title: Religion and Law in the U.S.
description: Surveys church-state jurisprudence since the 1940s, with special attention to difficulty of defining religion, and applies the religion clauses to current issues. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: American Folklore and Folklife
description: Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism.

subject: AMST
title: Digital America: Online Communities and Virtual Worlds
description: Seminar on the impact of the digital revolution and virtual communities on American culture and society, with an emphasis on questions of identity and participatory democracy. Open to non majors.
prereq_raw: one DH, DA, or DL course, sophomore standing, or consent

subject: AMST
title: Religions in America
description: Examination of American religious traditions, both historical and contemporary, with an emphasis on the principles of religious liberty, non-establishment, and pluralism.

subject: AMST
title: War and Media
description: Examination of a range of media, including photography, film, print journalism, television, video games, and the internet, as they have shaped popular representations and experiences of war in America from the Civil War through the present. (Alt. years)

subject: AMST
title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
description: Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship with the total society. Pre-Colonial to end of Reconstruction.

subject: AMST
title: American Thought and Culture: 20th Century
description: Continuation of 343: 20th century.
prereq_raw: 150 or 201 or 202 or 211 or 212 or HIST 151 or HIST 152; or consent

subject: AMST
title: Religion and Conflict in American History
description: Analyzes selected historical examples of religious conflicts in America, discerning characteristic patterns of American religious discourse, and identifying the social structures, interests, and ethical principles at stake in conflicts about religion.

subject: AMST
title: American Design: An Historical Survey
description: Examination of design in American culture over the last century. Readings in industrial, graphic, interior, architectural, landscape, and user interface design used to study issues of gender, race, and class in the U.S. Open to all class standings. (Alt. years)

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Design
description: Investigates design in contemporary American culture. Graphic, industrial, urban, and user-interface design practices are situated within broader social and economic forces. Modes of design practice, production, and consumption studied as reflection of American society today. Open to all class standings. (Alt. years)

subject: AMST
title: Culture and the Arts in America
description: Study of the role of the arts in American society and diverse cultural practices in historical and contemporary contexts.

subject: AMST
title: Screening Asian Americans
description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship. SCA majors:

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Lands and Waters
description: Examines indigenous practices born of and located in Indigenous places. Analyzes how indigenous knowledge of place informs Indigenous cultural, linguistic, intellectual, and political survivance and sovereignty, and resistance.

subject: AMST
title: American Travel Writing
description: Survey examines the roles that travel writing plays in American identity- and nation-formation, from early colonial history to the present.

subject: AMST
title: American Cinema
description: Introductory history of American cinema from the silent to the digital era, with an emphasis on criticism, genre and style, as well as cultural and sociopolitical context.

subject: AMST
title: American Empire
description: Examines the interplay between an “American culture of empire” and the rise of the U.S. as a superpower. Topics: imperialism and political culture, social movements and international affairs, race, gender and class relations.

subject: AMST
title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics.

subject: AMST
title: Critical Research Methods
description: Overview of methods and methodologies drawn from various fields (including history, politics, literature, art, law and race, Indigenous, gender, and sexuality studies) for conducting interdisciplinary research. Models of writing from AMST faculty; emphasis on writing.

subject: AMST
title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Literature and Film
description: Interdisciplinary, comparative course examining native literary texts (novels, short fiction, poetry), films, etc. that address issues of representation and how native peoples actively resist colonial ideology.

subject: AMST
title: Asian American Music Cultures
description: An exploration of how Asian American music making is related to community formation, labor migration, and cultural sensibilities throughout the 20th century.

subject: AMST
title: Japanese Americans: Research Topics
description: Research and thematic seminar on Japanese American culture, issues, and history.

subject: AMST
title: Regionalism: The South
description: Definition of a Southern identity and its relation to the larger U.S. culture, using literary and polemical works of 19th- and 20th-century.

subject: AMST
title: Hawai‘i’s Multiculturalism
description: A multidisciplinary examination of the dynamics of the Hawaiian Islands’ racial and cultural diversity from the perspectives of historical trends, social processes, and contemporary political, social, and economic issues as they impact interracial relations.

subject: AMST
title: American Ideas of Nature
description: The natural world in American thought from Native Americans to modern ecologists.

subject: AMST
title: History of American Architecture
description: History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning.

subject: AMST
title: American Environmental History
description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

subject: AMST
title: History of American Workers
description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century.

subject: AMST
title: Slavery and Freedom
description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World.

subject: AMST
title: Islands, Empires, and the Arts
description: Colonialism, neocolonialism, and cultures of resistance in the Caribbean and its North American diaspora through literature, film, and the arts. Focus on political dissent; nation building; historical memory; construction of gender, race. Writing emphasis. A-F only

subject: AMST
title: Politics in Hawai‘i
description: Discussion of modern politics against the background of recent history and major contemporary issues.

subject: AMST
title: History of Crime and Punishment
description: History of American crime and punishment from 18th century to the present. Topics: changing crime patterns, evolving punishment methods, penal reform movements, convict resistance, growth of prison industrial complex, racism, class, and gender.

subject: AMST
title: Gender, Justice and Law
description: Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151, WGSS 175, WGSS 176, WGSS 202, WGSS 360, WGSS 381, or consent

subject: AMST
title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/ masculine/gender nonconforming/sexual)
description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration.

subject: AMST
title: Women and Globalization in Asia
description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory.
prereq_raw: one of 310, 316, 318, 373, 455, POLS 339, WGSS 360, WGSS 361, WGSS 439; or consent

subject: AMST
title: Race and Racism in America
description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history.

subject: AMST
title: Social Movements
description: Examination of mass mobilization in U.S. history from the Revolution forward, including abolitionism, feminism, civil rights, labor, and more. Concludes with analysis of various community organizing efforts today.

subject: AMST
title: Racism, American Culture and Film/ Media
description: An exploration of the critique of racial ideologies in American film. The course also examines how aggrieved communities develop cultural sensibilities, aesthetic choices and politicized identities through film, video and media work.

subject: AMST
title: Gender in Action Cinema
description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. Junior standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Food, Culture, and Empire
description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor

children.text: at least one course in WGSS

subject: AMST
title: Victims, Virtue, and Violence
description: Examination of the history and significance of melodrama as a dominant mode of American cultural production from the early republic to the present, with a focus on issues of race, gender, and national identity.

subject: AMST
title: Popular Culture
description: Major themes, modes, and media of popular or mass culture in the U.S.; emphasis on cultural trends and social implications.

subject: AMST
title: The ’20s and ’30s
description: Novelists, painters, poets, jazz musicians as examples of culture of the 1920s and 1930s in America.

subject: AMST
title: Culture, Society, and Literature
description: Literary and non-fictive exploration of the intellectual and moral response of Americans to institutions and culture of 20th-century marketplace economy.

subject: AMST
title: Fashioning America
description: Examines linkages between American identity, representation, labor and capital through fashion theory, clothing discourses and other practices of textile production over history.

subject: AMST
title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
description: Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities.

subject: AMST
title: Art of the United States
description: Emphasis on the 18th and 19th centuries.

subject: AMST
title: Museum Interpretations
description: Studies the interpretive strategies and methods used by museums to communicate with visitors in museums, art galleries, historic sites, parks, and related places. Considers how interpretations contribute to cultural knowledge.

subject: AMST
title: Film in American Culture
description: Comprehensive survey of varieties of film experience from historical and contemporary points of view.

subject: AMST
title: Sports in America
description: Sports as reflected in literature, films, and TV. Focus on ethical dimensions of sports and sporting cultures; writing emphasis.

subject: AMST
title: Early 20th Century American Art
description: American art in the first half of the 20th century and its impact on American culture. Junior standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: America’s World Role
description: Examination of America’s role in modern world affairs, against the background of history, perceptions, and values.

subject: AMST
title: America and Africa
description: American attitudes toward Africa, as well as how Africa has functioned within the dynamics of American culture and history.

subject: AMST
title: American Experience in Asia
description: Examination of various forms of U.S. engagement with Asia, with particular attention to the role of Hawai‘i as the site, agent, and object of engagement. Emphasis on developing critical reading and expository writing skills.

subject: AMST
title: Religion, Sex, and Gender in the U.S.
description: Examines religious and ethical conflicts about sexuality and gender nonconformity in contemporary America. Students gain knowledge, practical wisdom, and communication skills to negotiate moral disagreement in a pluralistic society.

subject: AMST
title: Preservation: Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific
description: Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions.

subject: AMST
title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/ Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/ HAER).
restrictions_raw: AMST, ARCH, and HIS majors only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, up to 24 credits

subject: AMST
title: Senior Capstone Project
description: Capstone course for American studies students to undertake a major research-based project.

subject: AMST
title: World Maritime History
description: Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples.

subject: AMST
title: (Alpha) Topics in American Studies
description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies undergraduate courses, focused within these areas: (B) social structure and interaction; (D) arts and environment.

subject: AMST
title: Readings in American Studies
description: Directed readings and research for majors.

subject: AMST
title: Approaches to American Studies
description: Introductory survey of methodological issues underlying research in American studies.

subject: AMST
title: Patterns of American Cultures
description: American cultural origins and development.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Research and Professional Development
description: Prepares advanced graduate students to present original research findings to colleagues, write for peer review, design undergraduate classes in their areas of expertise, and participate actively in their fields. Graduate students only.
prereq_raw: (600 and 601) with a minimum grade of B-

subject: AMST
title: Early America
description: Interdisciplinary approach to understanding early American culture and history.

subject: AMST
title: Asian America
description: The Asian American experience from an interdisciplinary and humanities perspective. Asian American history, literature, media, and theater arts. Comparative study of Hawai‘i and the Continental U.S.

subject: AMST
title: Women in American Culture
description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: American West
description: Examination of the U.S. colonization of the American West. Topics include: European-indigenous relations, migration and labor, regional literature, frontier ideology, ethnic conflict, and new community formation.

subject: AMST
title: Performance, Culture, and Theory
description: Survey of major critical works in fields of performing arts and public culture (e.g., dance, theater, music, commemoration). Topics include: theoretical application for the discipline of American studies, and the impact of social movements and labor migration on the performing arts.

subject: AMST
title: Gender and the African Diaspora in the Americas
description: Explores the impact of the African Diaspora on the cultures and histories of the Americas through interdisciplinary and feminist scholarship and cultural sources including fiction, foodways, film, poetry, religion, music, and dance. Graduate standing only.

subject: AMST
title: Social and Cultural Diversity in America
description: Examination of selected subcultures in America.

subject: AMST
title: American Sexualities
description: Aspects of sexual identity within the context of American culture.

subject: AMST
title: Slavery and Modern Memory
description: Exploration of contemporary resonances of slavery in the Americas through literature, historical scholarship, memory and trauma studies, and the visual and performing arts. Graduate students only.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Identity
description: Interdisciplinary and comparative focus on how Indigenous identity is constructed, negotiated, asserted, ascribed, and deconstructed within and without Indigenous communities with attention to the U.S. Graduate students only.

subject: AMST
title: American Architecture
description: Cultural analysis of the evolution of American architecture from the Colonial period to the present involving sociopolitical and economic, as well as aesthetic, considerations.

subject: AMST
title: Wilderness in America
description: American wilderness as both physical setting and social construction.

subject: AMST
title: Material Culture
description: Physical artifacts considered as documents of American cultural and regional development.

subject: AMST
title: Environment and Society
description: Technological development in cultural perspective; its relation to the American environment, science, capitalism, public policy, and values.

subject: AMST
title: Mass Media
description: Appraisal of major media of communications in American society with attention to political, educational, cultural, and ethical implications.

subject: AMST
title: Technologies of War and Media
description: Critical examination of the relationship between war and media with particular attention to the overlapping histories of technologies of perception and destruction in the modern era and to the military-entertainment complex today. Graduate students only or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Public History and Commemoration
description: Approaches to public presentations of history and examination of various ways in which historic memory is constructed in sites such as museums, memorials, and theme parks.

subject: AMST
title: American Punishment
description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prison-industrial complex. Graduate students only.

subject: AMST
title: Writing for Publication
description: Advanced seminar designed to convert graduate research projects into publishable scholarly articles.

subject: AMST
title: Revolutions and Social Movements
description: Examines the role of social movements in transforming American society and culture.

subject: AMST
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawai‘i and the region. (Alt. years: spring only)

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: Social/Cultural/ Intellectual
description: Readings and research on American social and intellectual history.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: Business/Labor/ Technology
description: Readings and research on American business, labor, and technological history.

subject: AMST
title: American Intellectual Traditions
description: Examination of intellectual figures and movements in American history.

subject: AMST
title: Field Mastery
description: Prepares students to achieve specialization in an American Studies-related academic field. Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times with different contents

subject: AMST
title: Film in America
description: Examination of various roles of motion picture film in America with particular respect to art form, cultural artifact, document, and myth.

subject: AMST
title: Arts in America: Modern to PostModern
description: Survey of the literature of the field.

subject: AMST
title: Transpacific Studies
description: Critical analysis of regional formation in and across the Pacific and the role of the U.S. therein; migrations within and across the Pacific; political, military, economic, cultural, and environmental dynamics of transpacific exchanges.

subject: AMST
title: Globalization and Transnationalism
description: Examines the socioeconomic and cultural meanings of globalization and transnationalism. Emphasis on how the deployment and flows of power beyond the nation-state have an impact on regional, national, and/ or local communities and cultures.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: America and the World
description: Historical and contemporary issues in America’s global relationships.

subject: AMST
title: Comparative Methods in American Studies
description: Examines approaches to American studies that use comparison as a primary method. Comparison of histories, institutions, of phenomena between the U.S. and another country as well as among communities in the U.S. Graduate standing only.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Curation and Museums: Practice Meets Theory
description: Seminar explores the history, evolution, and contemporary movement towards indigenous curation within museums, emphasis on the Americas and Oceania, as shaped by colonialism, globalization, multiculturalism, selfdetermination, and nationalism.

subject: AMST
title: 20th Century U.S. Literature
description: Selected works of 20th-century literature as cultural documents.

subject: AMST
title: African American Literature
description: Cultural and social imagination of blacks and whites as revealed in literature, poetry, and drama.

subject: AMST
title: Elements of Style
description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present.

subject: AMST
title: Historic Building Technology
description: History of buildings, building technologies, materials, and finishes, including construction techniques and methods of investigating older buildings. Emphasis on North American building practices c.1600–c.1960.

subject: AMST
title: Vernacular Architecture
description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes, and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas.

subject: AMST
title: Museums: Theory, History, Practice
description: History and theory of museums and related institutions (art galleries, historic houses, zoos, parks). Relationship between museums, collections, and communities. Introduction to governance, planning, legal, and ethical concerns.

subject: AMST
title: Museums and Collections
description: Work of museums and professionals (registrars, collections managers, conservators, curators and others) in the care of collections, interpretive studies of museum displays; field trips.

subject: AMST
title: Museums and Education
description: Overview of museum education including museum learning theories, informal learning programs, audience research, national and international policies and reports, and community projects.

subject: AMST
title: Museum Studies Practicum
description: Applies coursework in museum studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Museum studies certificate students only.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Studies Practicum
description: Applies course work in Indigenous studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Graduate students only.

subject: AMST
title: Research Seminar
description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies graduate courses; emphasis upon research methods.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
description: Nature of the world’s visual arts and their influences on personal expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and studio practice. (Not for art majors or minors)

subject: ART
title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
description: Nature of the world’s visual arts and their influences on personal expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and studio practice. (Not for art majors or minors)

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Printmaking
description: Foundation explorations in the processes of relief, intaglio, and stencil printmaking. Direct workshop studio experience in the basic techniques and concepts of wood cut, linoleum cut, drypoint, monotype, and basic stencil processes.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Introduction to Photography
description: Studio/lecture combining history, theory and practice of photography. (B) film and darkroom, students must have 35mm film-based camera with adjustable shutter speed, aperture, and light meter; (D) digital, students must have digital camera with manual control and image editing software.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Drawing
description: Descriptive, expressive, and formal aspects of visual language through drawing practice.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Three-Dimensional Composition
description: Basic concepts, elements, and principles of art.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Painting
description: Theory and practice of painting; material and technical procedures. A standalone course aimed at non-majors. ART majors should start with ART 223 after taking ART 113.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Glass
description: Basic techniques of working with cold and molten glass. Theory of glass studio operation and introduction to glass theory.

subject: ART
title: Survey of Global Art I
description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from prehistory to the 15th century. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

subject: ART
title: Survey of Global Art I
description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from prehistory to the 15th century. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

subject: ART
title: Survey of Global Art II
description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from the 15th century to the present. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

subject: ART
title: Survey of Global Art II
description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from the 15th century to the present. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Art
description: Integrated beginning studio art course, which offers students the opportunity to understand and express Hawaiian cultural perspectives through contemporary art practice.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Electronic Arts
description: Theory and practice course investigating language common to all arts activity particularly as related to the contemporary arts.
prereq_raw: any studio art course; or consent

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Digital Imaging
description: Combined theory and practice examining major techniques, concepts, and aesthetics in contemporary digital image production. Direct studio experience in essential software, printing techniques and hardware necessary in producing the gallery quality inkjet print.

subject: ART
title: Intermediate Photo (Black and White Darkroom)
description: Black and white photography emphasizing communication and self-expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and projects. Student must supply camera and material.

subject: ART
title: Intermediate Drawing
description: Extension of the observational foundation established in 113 to address contemporary conceptual and expressive approaches to drawing.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Life Drawing
description: Investigations of the figure concerning anatomical construction, light, space, diagramatic analysis, and thematic content.

subject: ART
title: Intaglio Printmaking
description: Studio practice in concepts and techniques of making prints from metal plates including etching, engraving, aquatint, and drypoint.

subject: ART
title: Screenprinting
description: Studio practice in screenprinting on paper. Copy camera and basic photo-stencil techniques introduced.

subject: ART
title: Relief Printmaking
description: Studio practice in the techniques and concepts of woodblock, linoleum cut, monotype, and calligraph printmaking. Emphasis on both traditional and contemporary practices.

subject: ART
title: Approaches to Painting
description: Theory and practice of painting; contemporary conceptual and expressive approaches.

subject: ART
title: Painting/Water-Based Media
description: An introduction to water-based media. Traditional transparent color, gouache and acrylics.

subject: ART
title: Glass Casting: Sand and Metal Molds
description: Expressive explorations in glass casting with wet sand, bonded sand, and metal molds.

subject: ART
title: Cold Glass Fabrication
description: Expressive explorations using architectural sheet glass. Development of 2D and 3D forms using engraving, sandblasting, and cold joinery techniques.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Ceramics
description: Three-dimensional concepts in clay; hand-building and wheel-throwing techniques. Projects, lectures, and demonstrations.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Metal Casting
description: Metal casting and development of associated practices and concepts.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Carving, Mixed Media
description: Investigations of traditional and contemporary carving concepts and methods.

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio I
description: Introduction to graphic design. Explorations of rhetorical and semiotic structures and their relationship to visual form and content. ART 176 is recommended as a prerequisite.

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio I Lab
description: Beginning instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, including hardware, software, and lab networking as it relates to graphic design production. ART 176 is recommended as a prerequisite.

subject: ART
title: Design: Typography I
description: Introduction to typography. Exploration of letterform and word compositions in the context of single-page structures. ART 176 is recommended as a prerequisite.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Electronic Arts Studio
description: Combined theory and practice studio course(s) that investigate language, processes, and personalized composing systems related to the use of technological media and its application to a variety of contemporary art areas and related disciplines. (B) imaging systems; (C) sound; (D) interactive systems.

subject: ART
title: Introduction to Contemporary Critical Theory
description: Examination of the significant themes and issues in contemporary critical theory as they relate to the production and reception of art.

subject: ART
title: Kiln-Formed Glass
description: Expressive explorations in the use of kiln-formed, fusible-sheet glasses and enameling on glass.

subject: ART
title: Digital Imaging: Professional Printing
description: Combined theory and practice. Investigates industry standard methods for archival pigment printing. Techniques include: device calibration and profiling, black and white, coating techniques, mounting and adhesive techniques, professional portfolio presentation.

subject: ART
title: Digital Imaging: Alternative Printing
description: Combined theory and practice. Merges digital printing, mark-making, photography, and traditional printmaking. Includes image transfers, lifts, precoating techniques, as well as printing on alternative substrates such as watercolor papers, metals, and cloth.

subject: ART
title: Lost Wax Glass Casting
description: Glass kiln casting techniques, lost wax fuse casting, pâte de verre.

subject: ART
title: Advanced Lighting
description: Emphasis on aesthetic and critical analysis. Techniques covered include continuous light, strobe and handheld flash.
prereq_raw: 107D and 202 with a minimum grade of B

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Advanced Photographic Techniques
description: Emphasis on aesthetic and critical analysis. (B) digital color photography and printing; (C) hand-applied emulsion. Each alpha is
prereq_raw: 107D and 202 with a minimum grade of B for (B); 202 and 207 with a minimum grade of B for (C)

subject: ART
title: Sound Design and Video Art
description: Combined theory and practice studio art course examining the techniques, concepts, and aesthetics of congtemporary sound design and video art.

subject: ART
title: Advanced Drawing
description: Studio practice in drawing emphasizing contemporary developments in art.

subject: ART
title: Intermediate Life Drawing
description: Further investigations of the figure concerning anatomical and diagramatic construction, light, space, and thematic content.

subject: ART
title: Experimental Art and Animation
description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation.
prereq_raw: 113 or CINE 216 (or concurrent) or CINE/DNCE/THEA 353 (or concurrent) or CINE/DNCE/THEA 356 (or concurrent)
restrictions_raw: SCA, ART, THEA, DNCE majors only.

subject: ART
title: Lithography
description: Studio practice in concepts and techniques of making prints from lithographic limestone and plates.
prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B) 215 or 217 or 218

subject: ART
title: Intermediate Printmaking
description: Intermediate level specialization in either intaglio, lithography, screenprinting, or relief printmaking. Concentration on the techniques and formats of color printing and sequential image development.
prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B) two of 215, 217, 218, or 316

subject: ART
title: Advanced Color
description: Theory and application of color as related to studio practice.

subject: ART
title: Advanced Painting I
description: Studio practice in painting emphasizing contemporary developments in art.

subject: ART
title: Painting from Life
description: Painting from the model; a survey of the figurative tradition.

subject: ART
title: Advanced Glass
description: Glass as an expressive medium. Individual problems; construction of studio equipment. Readings and discussions of contemporary glass issues.

subject: ART
title: Papermaking
description: Studio emphasis on handmade papermaking techniques, conceptual exploration in two and three dimensions.

subject: ART
title: Fiber Sculpture—Endurance and Impermanence
description: Studio exploration in contemporary dimensional fiber using both conventional and nonconventional materials and processes. Emphasis on concept development, sensitivity to the evocative potential of materials, context, surface treatment and its relationship to concept and structure.

subject: ART
title: Inter-woven Structures
description: Studio investigation of threads under tension. Thematic lens of environmental vulnerability and resiliency. Explores art practice as embodied knowledge. Specific attention to weaving as meaning and place-making. Engages writing as a significant tool for analysis.

subject: ART
title: Ceramics—Sculpture
description: Sculptural concepts and techniques specifically related to the medium of clay; advanced hand-building, throwing, glazing, and firing techniques.

subject: ART
title: Ceramics—Vessels
description: Exploration of the ceramic vessel as function, metaphor, and expression. Advanced hand-building, throwing, glazing, and firing techniques.

subject: ART
title: Ceramics—Low Temperature
description: Form and surface problems related to earthenware clay bodies and low-temperature glazes; mold-making for ceramics.

subject: ART
title: History of Western Ceramics
description: Western ceramics history from chronological, developmental, contextual, and theoretical standpoints; influence of Asian ceramics.

subject: ART
title: Technical Ceramics
description: Clay body development, glaze development, empirical and calculation methods. Emphasis on glaze maturity, surface, and color.
prereq_raw: 242, and one of 343, 344, or 345; or consent

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Figure Modeling
description: Figure modeling, mold making, and casting.

subject: ART
title: Kinetic Sculpture
description: The design and construction of objects incorporating movement as an integral element of their content.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Metal Fabrication
description: Metal fabrication and development of associated practices, concepts, and historical references.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Small-Scale
description: Fabrication and casting of forms on a small scale such as jewelry. The development of related practices, concepts, and historical references.

subject: ART
title: Utilitarian Sculpture
description: The design and construction of objects intended for use/interaction. Emphasis on wood and synthetic materials.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture—Contemporary
description: Contextualization of late 20th/early 21st century sculptural practice, including stylistic and theoretical frameworks, with references to influences of various historical Western and Asian traditions and applying this knowledge in the creation of sculpture.

subject: ART
title: Exhibition Design and Gallery Management
description: Design theory and techniques for presentation of artworks and mounting exhibitions.

subject: ART
title: Art Museums and Preservation Practices
description: Introduction to collections management and preservation techniques, incorporating both theoretical and practical approaches, and including hands-on work with the collections of the John Young Museum.

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio II
description: Intermediate graphic design. Emphasis on communication problems involving process and analysis. Introduction to modernist precedents and information theory.

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio II Lab
description: Intermediate instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, software, and peripheral devices, including intermediate layout. Introduction to graphic design industry standard multi-media and web design programs.

subject: ART
title: Design: Typography II
description: Intermediate typographic design, exploration of word and text composition in the context of multiple-page structures.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Study Abroad-Studio Art
description: Intensive study of topics in studio art at a UH Mānoa approved study abroad institution. (B) introductory; (C) upper-division.

subject: ART
title: Medieval Art
description: Arts of Europe from early Christian era to Renaissance.

subject: ART
title: Art of Greece and Rome
description: Minoan and Mycenaean arts; Greece and Rome.

subject: ART
title: Art of the 19th Century
description: Architecture, sculpture, and painting of Europe.

subject: ART
title: Early Art of Japan
description: Major developments, prehistoric through Kamakura; architecture, painting, sculpture.

subject: ART
title: Later Art of Japan
description: Major developments, Muromachi to modern period; painting, sculpture, architecture.

subject: ART
title: Philippine Visual Art from Burial Jars to Burning Effigies
description: Introduction to the arts and material culture of the Philippines from the pre-colonial to the contemporary period through the examination of sculpture, metalwork, ceramics, textiles, and painting from various ethnolinguistic groups.

subject: ART
title: Art of Korea
description: Ceramics, sculpture, painting, and architecture; neolithic through Yi periods.

subject: ART
title: Art and Culture of Early China
description: A culturally oriented study of Chinese visual arts; emphasis on jade, bronze, secular and religious sculptures, and paintings from prehistory to the 9th century.

subject: ART
title: Art and Culture of Late China
description: A culturally oriented study of Chinese visual arts; emphasis on the rise of literati painting and theory individualism in art and theory, garden, and architecture, and the Chinese pursuit of modernity and post-modernity in art.

subject: ART
title: Sculpture of China
description: Thematic introduction to sculpture in China from the Neolithic period through the present day.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Study Abroad-Art History
description: Intensive study of advanced topics in art history at a UH Mānoa-approved study abroad institution. (B) introductory; (C) upper-division.

subject: ART
title: Art of Africa, Pacific, North America
description: Contextual study of art from selected areas in Africa, the Pacific, and North America.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Art of Southeast Asia
description: Critical analysis of the historical and cultural development of Buddhist and Hindu art in Southeast Asia; (B) island Southeast Asia; (C) mainland Southeast Asia.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: ART
title: Art of India and South Asia
description: Art and architecture of South Asia in historical and cultural context. Art of India and South Asia.

subject: ART
title: Art Historical Methodology
description: Introduction to the methods and approaches of art history. Students will develop skills in perception and comprehension of visual art forms, and a critical understanding of the methods used by art historians to analyze them.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) History of Photography
description: History of photography from its beginnings to the present; emphasis on the evolution of photography as an art form; (B) nineteenth century, from the invention of photography through pictorialism; (C) twentieth century, from World War I to the present.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: ART
title: Directed Work
description: Individual projects; tutorial. Maximum: 3 credit hours per semester; total 3 for BA, 6 for BFA.
prereq_raw: two 200-level or above art courses in area of directed work, as well as consent of instructor and department associate chair

children.text: above art courses in area of directed work, as well as consent of instructor

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Special Topics
description: Intensive and specialized work at advanced level in fields of special interest of visiting or resident faculty; (B) studio art; (C) art history. Junior standing or higher and instructor consent only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times per alpha, up to 12 credits

subject: ART
title: Advanced Electronic Arts Studio
description: Tutorial studio that encourages exploration in combined and new media through independent work within an environment of theoretical and critical discourse.

subject: ART
title: Professional Practice in the Arts: Creative, Career, and Leadership
description: Examination of the role of the artist in society, the artist as self, as community member, as teacher. Professional Practice skills in the arts; planning, grantsmanship, fundraising, budgeting, marketing, outreach, and media relations. Senior standing or graduate students only.

subject: ART
title: Graduation Portfolio (BA)
description: Required graduation portfolio for BA Art History and Art Studio students. BA ART majors only. Undergraduates only. To be taken during the semester prior to expected graduation.

subject: ART
title: BFA Capstone Seminar/Studio
description: In conjunction with the production of art for the BFA annual exhibition, this seminar will examine, critique, and evaluate the student’s art within the context of contemporary art, professional practices, exhibition theory, and integrate theoretical and practical issues in the life of an artist.

subject: ART
title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
description: Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making. Engages writing as a significant tool for art-making and analysis.

subject: ART
title: Installation/Performance–Material in Context
description: Studio investigation of the transformation of space (ecological, social, political, psychological) through artist intervention. Experiments in non-object based interventions and into the evocative potential of materials. Engages writing and oral expression as significant analytical tools.
