subject: ART
title: Early 20th Century American Art
description: American art in the first half of the 20th century and its impact on American culture. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio III
description: Advanced graphic design. Emphasis on postmodernist theory, context, audience, and alternative media.

subject: ART
title: Design: Studio III Lab
description: Advanced instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, including software and peripheral devices. Instruction in image manipulation and editing still video images for the web, CD, DVD, and portable interface devices.

subject: ART
title: Design: Typography III
description: Advanced typographic design. Exploration of 2D, 3D, electronic, and intermedia. Emphasis on contemporary typographic models.

subject: ART
title: Design: Production Techniques
description: Advanced techniques in design production from printed and digital media.

subject: ART
title: Design: Production Techniques Lab
description: Advanced study of digital media for graphic designers. Focuses on skills and specific technical information to complement material covered in 467.

subject: ART
title: Design: Advanced Studio
description: Individual and team investigations of complex problems in graphic design. Emphasis on projects with actual clients (when available) and/or independent investigations addressing advanced and current questions in the graphic design field.
prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B- for (465 and 466) and credit for 465L
restrictions_raw: BFA majors only. ART majors only.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Renaissance Art
description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture: (B) early Renaissance in Italy; (C) northern Europe; (D) High Renaissance and mannerism in Italy.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: ART
title: Baroque and Rococo Art
description: Architecture, sculpture, and painting of Europe in the Baroque and Rococo periods.

subject: ART
title: Art of the United States
description: Emphasis on the 18th and 19th centuries.

subject: ART
title: Art of the First Half of 20th Century
description: Development of modern art in Europe 1900–1939.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Art Since 1945
description: Art since 1945, with a focus on the global expansion of the avantgarde; (B) contemporary art 1945-2000; (C) global contemporary art since 2000.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Art of the Pacific
description: Visual form and function of the arts in cultural context: (B) Melanesia and Australia; (C) Polynesia and Micronesia; (D) North Pacific coast Indian, Eskimo.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: ART
title: Art of Tribal Africa
description: Visual form and function of arts in cultural context. Mali, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Guinea, Nigeria, Ghana, Cameroon, Congo, Zaire.

subject: ART
title: Art of Indonesia
description: Architecture, sculpture, and textile traditions of indigenous Indonesia in cultural context.

subject: ART
title: Topics in Contemporary Art
description: Thematic approaches to contemporary art and visual culture. Course themes may include identity, local/global issues, and appropriation.

subject: ART
title: Art of Hawai‘i
description: Stylistic and aesthetic characteristics of art of ancient Hawai‘i; relationship to art from other parts of Polynesia.

subject: ART
title: Museum Interpretations
description: Studies the interpretive strategies and methods used by museums to communicate with visitors in museums, art galleries, historic sites, parks, and related places. Considers how interpretations contribute to cultural knowledge.

subject: ART
title: Applied Art of Japan
description: Ceramics, metalwork, lacquer, and textiles throughout Japanese history.

subject: ART
title: Contemporary Art and Ecology
description: Explores the recent history of environmental and ecological art; provides a critical framework for the contemporary image politics of environmentalism, ecology, sustainability, and climate change with an emphasis on writing and ethical reasoning.

subject: ART
title: Contemporary Art in Hawai‘i
description: History of contemporary art in Hawai‘i: the institutions, artists, critics, and historians that have shaped it. Strong focus on oral history of Hawai‘i artists.

subject: ART
title: Traditional Chinese Painting
description: Stylistic and historic development of two-dimensional arts; painting and calligraphy from prehistory through 18th century.

subject: ART
title: Modern and Contemporary Art of China
description: Introduction to the arts of China in the modern and contemporary periods, in all media and genres, from 1840 to the present.

subject: ART
title: Genres of Japanese Cinema
description: History of Japanese cinema, including silent films, samurai films, monster films, and literary adaptations, analyzed through the lens of genre theory. Students demonstrate mastery of assigned readings and lecture content via weekly writing assignments.

subject: ART
title: (Alpha) Special Topics in Southeast Asian Art History
description: Focused study of particular periods, regions and critical themes in Southeast Asian art and architectural history. (B) Angkor & art of Khmer civilization; (C) art & architecture of Thailand; (D) monuments & nationalism in Southeast Asia.

repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for up to two different alphas

subject: ART
title: Hindu Visual Culture
description: Art and architecture of South Asia in historical and cultural context. Hindu visual culture.

subject: ART
title: Art of Islam
description: Major developments in art and architecture.

subject: ART
title: Photography: Critical Issues
description: Seminar on theoretical, ethical and aesthetic issues relating to the practice of photography, past and present.

subject: ART
title: History of Modern Design
description: Major design movements in Europe and America from late 19th century to present; arts and crafts movement, art nouveau, modernist trends of the 20th century.

subject: ART
title: Topics in the History of Cinema
description: Specific period or national style of cinema studied in its historical context.

subject: ART
title: Graduate Studio Seminar in Art
description: Selected topics in art. A critique-based course with emphasis on the development of critical analysis, artistic research, and practice.

subject: ART
title: Methods in Contemporary Art
description: Examines processes of inquiry and experimentation within studio practice. Students explore a range of research methods as a way to challenge habitual methodologies and expand notions of art and art making.

subject: ART
title: Materials in Contemporary Art
description: Explores the physical, historical, symbolic, and contextual capacity of materials, as well as the mutually constitutive roles of artist and materials within the creative process.

subject: ART
title: Graduate Studio Teaching Practicum
description: Observation, analysis and participation in teaching a lower division course under the direction of an instructor in the student’s area of concentration.

title: Art Historical Methodology
description: An introduction to art historiography, analytical techniques, and research methods and materials.

subject: ART
title: Art of Oceania
description: Arts from Polynesia, Melanesia, Micronesia explored in context of issues involving belief systems and cultural change.

subject: ART
title: Topics in the Art of China
description: Research topics in the history of Chinese sculpture, ceramics, bronzes, jade, and textiles.

subject: ART
title: Seminar in Contemporary Critical Theory
description: Research and discussion seminar supporting advanced critical theory in the context of contemporary art and other creative practice.

subject: ART
title: Seminar in Global Contemporary Art
description: Selected topics in global contemporary art history.

subject: ART
title: Seminar in Western Art History
description: Selected topics in European and American art history.

subject: ART
title: Directed Work
description: Advanced individual projects; advanced tutorial. Maximum: 3 credit hours per semester; total 6 for MA Plan A, 9 for MA Plan B, MFA students must petition OGE for permission to apply toward degree requirement.
prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair

subject: ART
title: Seminar in Japanese Art
description: Selected topics in Japanese art history.

subject: ART
title: Seminar in South/Southeast Asian Art History
description: Selected topics in South and/or Southeast Asian art and architectural history with an emphasis on Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

subject: ART
title: Orientalism and Visual Culture
description: Investigates artistic representations, appropriations, and exchanges constructed on the basis of East/Orient vs. West/Occident differences. Includes analysis of: Orientalizing artistic traditions throughout history, history and concept of Orient, post-colonial critique of Orientalism.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Asian Studies
description: Introductory course focuses on change and continuity in the history, culture, values, and political institutions of South, East, and Southeast Asia, and the region’s interrelationships with the rest of the world.

subject: ASAN
title: Politics and Poetics of Climate Change in Asia
description: Examines the causes and impacts of, and responses to, climate change in Asia through interdisciplinary approaches: natural sciences, politics, economics, as well as legal, cultural, and creative/artistic dimensions.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Research and Writing in Asian Studies
description: Introduction to research and writing in Asian Studies provides a structured overview of the research and writing process from an interdisciplinary perspective, focused on Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Asian Studies: East Asia
description: Understanding East Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Asian Studies: South/ Southeast Asia
description: Understanding South and Southeast Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

subject: ASAN
title: East Asian Popular Cultures
description: East Asian popular culture, with a focus on Korea and Japan, as well as the Chinese language sphere. Analyzes social forces shaping pop culture industries, artists, and productions in the region from a global perspective.

subject: ASAN
title: Bollywood Dance, Music, and Film
description: Unique course combining mind and body, discussion and dancing. Learn and perform Bollywood dances and the richness of their Indian poetic, classical, and folk traditions. Understand “Bollywood” in the context of cross-cultural fusion and globalization.

subject: ASAN
title: Career Pathways in Asian Studies
description: Explore the range of careers related to Asian Studies and develop skills and materials to build your academic success into a meaningful career. Students create a job search portfolio they can share with prospective employers.

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Political Economy
description: Interdisciplinary review and analysis of the social and political issues in contemporary China, the interchange between state and society in national policies, the relationship between cultural tradition and technological modernization in the social transformation process. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ASAN
title: Studying Asia Culturally
description: Multidisciplinary. Classics of literature, philosophy, and religion shaping Asian beliefs and values.
prereq_raw: 201 and 202 are recommended, but not required

subject: ASAN
title: Contemporary Asia
description: Multidisciplinary examination of problems and issues affecting peoples and institutions of contemporary Asia: ethnic, language, religious, and cultural differences; population growth; public health; economic development; political and social change; environmental problems; etc.
prereq_raw: 201 and 202 are recommended, but not required

subject: ASAN
title: (Alpha) Asia Past and Present
description: Multidisciplinary examination of major Asian countries; cultural, social, economic, and political lives of their peoples. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (O) Okinawa; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Other.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times in different alphas

subject: ASAN
title: The Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
description: History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of the tea ceremony: Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics. Includes an emphasis on Oral Communication skills.

subject: ASAN
title: Chado-the Way of Tea Practicum
description: Actual practice of the tea ceremony as history and culture of Japan.

subject: ASAN
title: (Alpha) Japanese Film: Art and History
description: Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics.

subject: ASAN
title: Media, Advertising & Desire in East Asia
description: Examines concepts of beauty and desire in East Asian cultures within historical and contemporary media contexts. Uses critical theory and in-depth case studies to explore how images, language, and branding work in contemporary Asian societies.

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Film: Art and History
description: Study and analysis of Chinese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to the Performing Arts of Southeast Asia
description: Introduction to the history and development of major performing arts genres in Southeast Asia: theatre, dance-drama, opera, music, puppetry, ritual, and modern spoken drama. Topics include cultural identity, multiculturalism, modernization, and tourism. Online course.

subject: ASAN
title: Geography of Southeast Asia
description: An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change.

subject: ASAN
title: Buddhist Philosophy
description: Survey of central thinkers and schools.

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asian Literature in Translation
description: Survey in English traditional and modern literatures of Southeast Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent

subject: ASAN
title: (Alpha) Field Study in Asia
description: Students may submit proposals to have academic course work, field research, or work experience in Asia. See specific center for guidelines and procedures. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Other. A-F only for (C), (I), (J), (S), and (Z).

subject: ASAN
title: Modern Philippines
description: Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic.

subject: ASAN
title: Peace Processes in Philippines and Hawai‘i
description: History of Philippine Islam and the Moro struggle, the peace process in Mindanao and sovereignty movement for Hawaiian nation. 75 min. Lec, 75-min. joint online discussion with Philippine students. Junior standing only.

subject: ASAN
title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
description: Examines gender in Okinawa in relation to historical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region with attention to issues such as militarism and violence, colonialism and memory, and tourism and commodification of indigenous culture.

subject: ASAN
title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
description: Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies. (Alt. years)

subject: ASAN

description: Challenges associated with the management of land, water resources, fisheries, forests and agriculture in modern Southeast Asia. Case studies are used to illustrate current problems and evaluate potential management solutions.

subject: ASAN
title: Korean Cinema
description: Develop an understanding of Korean culture and society through visual, narrative, and contextual analysis of Korean films. Topics include post-Korean War experience, compressed modernity, authoritarianism, and postauthoritarian transformation. Special attention to independent films.

subject: ASAN
title: Contested Issues Korea and Japan
description: In-depth understanding of Korean-Japanese relations in the past and present by examining conflicting views and interpretations by Japanese, Korean, and Western scholars on important issues that divide the people of East Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: Sustainable Asian Development: Impact of Globalization
description: Investigates the impact of globalization on sustainable development in Asia. Globalization and sustainability often contradict, raising serious planning issues. Examines how these issues affect Asian development policies and urban planning.

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Cities: Evolution of Urban Space
description: Reviews the evolution of Asian urban space. Political history, migration, culture, and production are the determinants of urban changes. Uses visual material to illustrate the change in Asian cityscape.
prereq_raw: 310 or PLAN 310 or ASAN 312, or consent

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asian Archaeology
description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania.

subject: ASAN
title: Contested Issues in Contemporary Japan
description: Familiarizes students with public discourse in Japan by analyzing key current issues widely debated in the Japanese media and in public forums in light of their political, historical, cultural, social and economic contexts. Previous course work related to Japan or Asia will be helpful.

subject: ASAN
title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
description: Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g., with class, religion, ethnicity).

subject: ASAN
title: K-pop and J-pop: Korean and Japanese Popular Music and Society
description: Examines modern Japan and South Korea through popular music. Examines genres from early popular music, today’s K-pop and J-pop music.

subject: ASAN
title: Japan Cool: Anime, Manga, and Film
description: Focus on Japanese anime, manga, and films with an emphasis on oral communication. What can one learn about Japanese issues of gender, national identity, and race?

subject: ASAN
title: Transpacific Youth Pop Culture: From K-pop to Tiktok
description: Examines ties between East Asian and Asian American digital media, including comics, movies, TV shows, music, and video games, to examine the dreams, fears, and aspirations of young Asians and Asian Americans. A-F only

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Contemporary Asian Cinema
description: Acquaint students with significant films from the major countries in Asia and how these films reflect and comment on profound social, political, and historical changes that have occurred in recent decades.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in Chinese Cultural Studies: Visual Culture–Chinese Diaspora
description: Multidisciplinary and historically located study of Chinese culture through the examination of literary/visual texts and critical essays from cultural studies. Specific topics will depend upon term.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course or consent

subject: ASAN
title: Transnational Chinese Popular Culture
description: Survey of contemporary Chinese popular entertainment forms that are produced and appreciated transnationally. Examples include martial arts genres, kung fu films, commercial novels, ballroom dancing, karaoke culture, music videos and rock music. Material will be selected based upon availability and readings will include critical essays from the fields of popular culture, media studies, and literary criticism.
prereq_raw: any 300- or 400-level DL or DH course

subject: ASAN
title: Music Cultures: India
description: Approaches the cultural study of music and performance through a specific focus on South Asia. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ASAN

description: An exploration of the cultural and economic development of the countries of Southeast Asia from early times to the present day, with an emphasis on the effects of outside influences.

subject: ASAN
title: Film, Culture, and Modernity in Southeast Asia
description: Examines interplay between tradition and modernity; religion and secularism; individual and collective; youth, wisdom, and the world; and role of gender identification/community response as they find articulation in medium of film across Southeast Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: Asia Through Fiction
description: Explores core values and cultural principles of the four major Asian region as represented in major works of fiction from those regions.

subject: ASAN
title: Imperialism, Colonialism, and Nationalism in Southeast Asia
description: Theoretical and historical analysis of a global, nineteenth, and twentieth century phenomenon using an interdisciplinary approach organized around lectures, readings, and discussions.

subject: ASAN
title: Political Violence in Modern Southeast Asia
description: Why do Southeast Asian governments and political movements engage in mass killings? How do their perpetrators justify these atrocities? How do survivors deal with their trauma and get their voices heard?

subject: ASAN
title: Contemporary Chinese Development
description: Development and planning in contemporary China: economic policy and institutional structure in the development and urbanization process; urban and rural transformation in a socialist economy.

subject: ASAN
title: (Alpha) Topics in Asian Studies

subject: ASAN

description: Examines Asia’s role in the development of global foodways. Topics include the relationship between spices and imperialism, global popularity of Asian cuisines, Asian-influenced “hapa” cuisine in Hawai‘i, McDonaldization in Asia, and food security and sustainability.

subject: ASAN
title: Religions of Island Southeast Asia
description: A comparative, interdisciplinary examination of indigenous beliefs, Islam, Christianity, and Hinduism in island Southeast Asia, and how they have been adjusted because of economic and social change.

subject: ASAN
title: (Alpha) Approaches to Asian Studies
description: Major issues in and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of Asia and Asian regions; resources for the advanced study of Asia at UH; developing a research focus; preparing and presenting research proposals. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Inter-Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: Advanced Research and Writing in Asian Studies
description: Provides a structured overview of research and writing process, focused on Asia. Topics include research questions, abstracts, literature reviews, arguments, conceptualization, incorporating evidence, research ethics, and style. Students are required to produce a research paper.

subject: ASAN
title: Practicum in Asian Studies
repeatable_raw: Repeatable with consent up to nine credits

subject: ASAN
title: Politics and Development: China
description: Consists of three parts: key theories for socialist transition as basis for seminar discussion, policy evolution to illustrate the radical changes, and emerging and prominent current development and practice.

subject: ASAN
title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
description: Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in 20th Century Chinese Literary and Cultural Studies
description: Critical scholarship in Chinese literature and cultural studies, broadly defined to include the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and others. Reading knowledge of Chinese desirable but not required.

subject: ASAN
title: Problems/Issues of Contemporary Asia
description: Analysis from multidisciplinary perspective: rural development, urbanization, international relations, ethnicity, religion, language, etc.

subject: ASAN

subject: ASAN
title: Capitalism in Contemporary Asia
description: Historically grounded theoretical examination of capitalism in 20th-century Asia; multidisciplinary approach to fundamental change in political and economic structures and institutions, prospects for the future.

subject: ASAN
title: Ethnic Nationalism in Asia
description: Contemporary theories of ethnic and cultural nationalism from perspective of Asia. Issues of nationstate, power hierarchies, modernity, and identity in contemporary societies.

subject: ASAN

description: Comparative study of conceptualizations, practices and institutions of national security in Asia in light of their geographic and historic contexts. (Once a year)

subject: ASAN

description: Seafood production in Southeast Asia, including both regional fisheries and aquaculture. Case studies used to illustrate challenges to the implementation of sustainable seafood production and emerging approaches, such as community supported seafood.

subject: ASAN

description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

subject: ASAN

subject: ASAN

description: Examination of the impact of economy, society, and history on urban form; case studies of the evolution of Asian urban form.

subject: ASAN

Graduate standing or consent.

subject: ASAN

subject: ASAN

subject: ASAN
title: South Asia Now
description: Views South Asia as an interactive region. Examines common historical and cultural, economic, and political themes, including global interactions. Focus upon present state of the region. Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Telecom and the Internet in East Asia
description: Offers interdisciplinary approach to study of internet and telecommunications in East Asia. Examines growth and development of telecommunications networks in China, Japan, South and North Korea. Focuses on contemporary social media and government policy. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ASAN
title: Topics and Issues in Modern Korean Literature
description: Intensive study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary Korean fiction, focusing on texts that problematize critical sociocultural issues in the evolving contexts of modern Korean intellectual history.

subject: ASAN
title: Special Topics in East Asian Literary Culture & Society
description: In-depth study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary East Asian literary and cultural studies using an interdisciplinary, inter-regional, and transnational approach, from an intercultural perspective.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times in different topics, but need consent for second repeat

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asia and its Neighbors
description: Examines how Southeast Asian nations have recalibrated their international relationships in accordance with past experience and new concerns, focusing on interactions with Japan, China, and India, while integrating both global and domestic imperatives.

subject: ASAN
title: Law and Society in China
description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China.

subject: ASAN
title: Conflict and Cooperation in Asia
description: Explores conflict and cooperation among Asian nations. Topics may include economic integration, business networks, space and cyberspace, military alliances, territorial disputes, transnational crime, environmental cooperation, soft power, and regional institutional architecture. Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Foreign Policy
description: Examination of China’s rise and world view, review of China’s regional relations, China and U.S. relations, formation of a new world order.

subject: ASAN
title: International Relations in Asia
description: How well do international relations theories explain interstate relations in Asia? How do international issues interact with domestic politics? Covers Japan, China, Korea, ASEAN nations, India, and touches on Russia, Australia, and New Zealand. Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Field Study in Asia
description: With prior consent and supervision of an Asian Studies faculty, students design, conduct, and write the results of a field research project. Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN

subject: ASAN

repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: ASAN
title: Directed Research
description: Individual problems and research.

subject: ASAN

description: Bibliography, reference tools, and research methods in sources on Asia in Western and Asian languages. Discussion of published and archival repositories.

subject: ASAN
title: MAIA Capstone
description: Capstone experience for MAIA students that emphasizes practical applications of Asia knowledge. Should be taken in final semester or after completion of all or most of MAIA core requirements. Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Orientalism and Visual Culture
description: Investigates artistic representations, appropriations, and exchanges constructed on the basis of East/Orient vs. West/Occident differences. Includes analysis of: Orientalizing artistic traditions throughout history, history and concept of Orient, post-colonial critique of Orientalism.

subject: CALL
title: Exploring Expression: Foundations in Arts, Languages & Letters
description: First-year seminar for majors in the College of Arts, Languages & Letters that includes emphasis on the introduction to studies in a liberal arts curriculum and emphasizes the importance of writing in this discipline. CALL majors only, or consent. Freshmen only.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to Cinematic Digital Production
description: Introduction to the basic techniques of cinematic digital production and allows them to explore their personal voice in this process.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to 3D Computer Animation
description: A basic overview of the 3D animation production process, including modeling, texturing, rigging, animation, lighting, and rendering.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to 2D Animation
description: Introduction to traditional styles and methods of hand drawn 2D, digital, and stop motion animation through theory and practice.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to Cinema and Digital Media
description: Introduction to the study of cinema: history, aesthetics, and cultural impact.

subject: CINE
title: Cinematic Narrative Production
description: Production-intensive course with collaborative as well as individual projects. Theories and application of basic digital cinema productions, including camera, lighting, sound, and editing.

subject: CINE
title: Cinematography
description: Comprehensive course in visual styles supporting screen narratives through a study of principles of camera elements, operations, lighting, color and composition. Professional role and responsibilities of cinematographer. Project-oriented.

subject: CINE
title: Experimental Art and Animation
description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation.
prereq_raw: 216 (or concurrent) or ART 113 or CINE/DNCE/THEA 353 (or concurrent) or CINE/DNCE/THEA 356 (or concurrent)
restrictions_raw: SCA, ART, THEA, DNCE majors only.

subject: CINE
title: 3D Modeling
description: Essential principles of 3D modeling in order to create both organic character models and hard surface models. Students will create high-quality, animation-ready 3D models with textures and poses.

subject: CINE
title: 3D Animation
description: Creating the illusion of life through the principles of animation.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: CINE
title: 3D Lighting, Camera, and Rendering
description: Students develop the ability to manipulate light, shadow, and color within a virtual 3D space. Rendering and cinematography for 3D animation.

subject: CINE
title: Storyboarding and Animatics
description: Exposes students to the history, application, format, styles, and methods of creating storyboards and animatics. Visual storytelling will be analyzed by examining the foundational components of the visual language of a film.

subject: CINE
title: Visual Development for Animation
description: Visual design and development for animated characters and environments. Students will create concept art, character, and prop designs; movements styles; backgrounds; and layouts for animation pre-production.

subject: CINE
title: Visual Development for Animation
description: Visual design and development for animated characters and environments. Students will create concept art, character and prop designs, movement styles, backgrounds, and layouts for animation pre-production.

subject: CINE
title: Movement Study for Animation
description: Creating the illusion of life and expressive movement through the principles of 2D animation: timing, spacing, physics, staging, anatomy, attitude, and acting.

subject: CINE
title: Motion Graphics
description: A project-based introduction to motion graphics using Adobe After Effects.

subject: CINE
title: Independent Producing
description: Fundamentals of producing for independent filmmaking, focusing on business acumen and role of the producer through various stages of production. Topics include proposal writing, script breakdowns, budgeting, scheduling, legal issues, festival strategy, and distribution.

subject: CINE
title: Screenwriting
description: Introduction to the basics of writing a short narrative screenplay for film or animation. Students learn the fundamentals and format of screenwriting as well as basic elements of storytelling and character development.

subject: CINE
title: Screening Asian Americans
description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship. SCA majors:

subject: CINE
title: Scenic I: Beginning Scenic Design
description: Workshop introducing the basic principles and approaches of scenic design for theatre and dance, with emphasis on the creative process.
prereq_raw: a course in THEA or DNCE, production experience, or consent. (Consent required for production experience option)

children.text: ( Consent required for production experience option)

subject: CINE
title: Oral Tradition to Screenplay
description: Adapting the stories, styles, and cultural values of oral tradition storytelling to cinematic narratives.

subject: CINE
title: Costumes I: Beginning Costume Design
description: Basic principles and approaches to costume design for theatre and dance. Visual communication methods, creative process, historical research, and organizational practices.

subject: CINE
title: Indigenous Aesthetics
description: Aesthetic theories and practices of indigenous cultures of the Pacific and their adaptation to the screen in cinematic storytelling.

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Actor on Screen
description: Introduction of the screen-director to the craft of acting for the camera. Students will develop communication skills and learn practical techniques to elicit spontaneous and relaxed performances with actors from the Theatre program.

subject: CINE
title: Editing for Cinema
description: Advanced course examining the theory, techniques, and practices of motion picture editing; use of non-linear digital editing systems; and practical experience in digital editing projects.

subject: CINE
title: Post Production Sound
description: Practical course on the theory, art, and techniques of sound recording, editing, and design for cinema. Students work on projects involving dialogue and sound effects in post-production.

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Camera for the Screen
description: Detailed analysis of cinematic grammar, placement, movement, focus, and effects of the camera to create the mise-en-scene. Practical exercises to apply theory to individual creative work and in collaboration with actors from the Theatre program.

subject: CINE
title: Genre and Narrative Theory in Cinematic Arts
description: Focus on the concept of genre, genre films, genre film criticism, and popular genres such as the Western, film noir, documentary, and Chinese martial arts.

subject: CINE
title: Documentary Studies
description: In-depth study of the nature, history, and impact of documentary filmmaking traditions around the world, focusing on the interplay between filmmaker, subject, and audience.

subject: CINE
title: Authors in Cinematic Arts
description: In-depth study of the auteur theory and specific application to authors in cinematic arts, such as film directors, animators, screenwriters, or game designers.

subject: CINE
title: Study Abroad
description: Intensive study of selected topics, genres, filmmakers, or digital media production in the host country in a UH Manoa-approved study abroad location.

subject: CINE
title: Topics in Cinematic Arts
description: Topics of study and critical inquiry in a variety of areas in the cinematic arts. Taught by regular and visiting faculty.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time on different topics

subject: CINE
title: Techniques in Cinematic Arts
description: Specialized techniques in the creation of digital media: taught by regular and *visiting faculty.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time on different topics

subject: CINE
title: Workshop in Cinematic Arts
description: Intensive workshop in focused area of cinematic arts production.

subject: CINE
title: Independent Group Project
description: Participation in a group research or creative project under supervision of a faculty member. Only six credits of 399/499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major.

subject: CINE
title: Documentary Production
description: Analysis and practical knowledge of the documentary process including, but not limited to, research, organization and story structure, shooting, camera coverage, and editing.
prereq_raw: 310, 350, and one of the following: 312, 330, 370, 372, or 374

subject: CINE
title: Advanced Cinematic Production
description: Production of a major cinematic/digital narrative project. Working in groups, each student takes on creative and technical role and responsibilities of a principle crew position. Emphasis on artistic form in narrative development; timely execution from pre- to post-production.

subject: CINE
title: Advanced Cinematography
description: Applies the basic foundations, techniques, and theory of cinematography (covered in CINE 312) to a more informed and crafted practice with Camera and Lighting Scene study workshops, and research exercises and film projects.

subject: CINE
title: Animation Production I
description: Students work independently to produce a short, animated film. Emphasis on visual storytelling and character animation.

subject: CINE
title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course.

subject: CINE
title: Animation Production II
description: Student teams produce a short, animated film. Prior knowledge of 2D and 3D media authoring tools and animation techniques is necessary.

subject: CINE
title: Advanced Screenwriting
description: Application of narrative principles of character development, story structure, and thematic spine to screenplays for live action and animated short films, television, or transmedia projects.

subject: CINE
title: (Alpha) History and Film
description: Explores the many relationships between history and film including how film has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past. (C) Europe: emphasis on writing as historians and film critics; (E) world/ comparative: significant attention paid to developing writing skills that involve critically comparing history-related cinematic representations across regions and cultures. (C Cross-listed as HIST 452C; E Cross-listed as HIST 452E)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: CINE
title: Indigenous Filmmaking
description: Theories and studies of indigenous films and creation of a cinematic project based in indigenous cultural and value systems.
prereq_raw: 310, 350, and one of the following; 312, 330, 370, 372, or 374

subject: CINE
title: Ethics and Film
description: Ethical theory and dilemmas as reflected in film and filmmaking. Social responsibility for filmmakers.

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Motion Picture
description: Students direct a narrative live-action short film from pre- through post-production, learning how to develop a directorial vision and how to implement it through storyboarding, scheduling, and collaborative skill sets.

subject: CINE
title: Screenwriting Capstone
description: Culmination of beginning and advanced screenwriting classes. Students will write a treatment and first act for a feature-length project or pilot script and series bible for a television project.

subject: CINE
title: Oceanic Media and Culture
description: Involves close textual analysis of film, TV and multimedia content. The course includes cinematic and television screenings. Junior standing or higher.

subject: CINE
title: Data Visualization
description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization. Junior standing or higher.

subject: CINE
title: Seminar in Cinematic Arts
description: Intellectual issues in cinematic arts. Conducted by regular and visiting faculty with extensive student participation and scholarly presentation.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time on different topics

subject: CINE
title: Capstone Creative Production
description: Emphasis on advanced production skills in creating a capstone project in live-action fiction film, animation, documentary, or new media. Screenwriting students may also develop a feature screenplay or television pilot and series bible.

subject: CINE
title: Video Game Design and Development
description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments. Junior standing or higher.

subject: CINE
title: Global Media
description: Close textual analysis and strategic analysis of global media dynamics with an emphasis on transnational media corporations.

subject: CINE
title: Cinematic Arts Internship
description: Internship in professional cinematic, television, animation and/or digital media production company under professional and faculty supervision.

subject: CINE
title: Directed Study
description: Independent research or creative project under the supervision of a faculty member. Only six credits of 399/499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major.

subject: CHN
title: Elementary Mandarin I
description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, grammar. Meets one hour, four times a week.

subject: CHN
title: Elementary Mandarin II
description: Continuation of 101.

subject: CHN
title: Accelerated Elementary Mandarin
description: Content of 101 and 102 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, four times a week.

subject: CHN
title: Elementary Chinese for Business Professionals
description: Accelerated, intensive elementary course focusing on everyday listening, speaking, reading, and writing communicative needs of business professionals in the Chinese business context.

subject: CHN
title: Elementary Conversational Mandarin I
description: Development of basic skills (listening, speaking and grammar) of spoken Mandarin with application to some familiar everyday topics.

subject: CHN
title: Elementary Conversational Mandarin II
description: Continuation of 111.

subject: CHN
title: Intermediate Mandarin I
description: Continuation of 101 and 102. Meets one hour a day, four times a week.

subject: CHN
title: Intermediate Mandarin II
description: Continuation of 201.

subject: CHN
title: Accelerated Intermediate Mandarin
description: Content of 201 and 202 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, four times a week.
prereq_raw: placement test and 102 or 103 or 105; or consent

subject: CHN
title: Intermediate Chinese for Business Professionals
description: Accelerated, intensive intermediate course focusing on everyday listening, speaking, reading, and writing communicative needs of business professionals in the Chinese business context.

subject: CHN
title: Intermediate Conversational Mandarin I
description: Further development of listening and speaking skills in Mandarin. The student is expected to be able to comprehend and produce speech at the paragraph level.

subject: CHN
title: Intermediate Conversational Mandarin II
description: Continuation of 211.

subject: CHN
title: Reading and Writing Chinese I
description: For students who have completed the conversational Mandarin courses up through 212 and wish to continue on to 301, or others who can handle daily conversation in Mandarin but cannot read or write in the language.

subject: CHN
title: Reading and Writing Chinese II
description: Continuation of 251.

subject: CHN
title: Third-Level Mandarin I
description: Vocabulary building and extended mastery of sentence structures of modern Chinese through reading and related conversation. Meets one hour a day, three times a week.

subject: CHN
title: Third-Level Mandarin II
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: CHN
title: Accelerated Third-Level Mandarin
description: Content of 301 and 302 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, three times a week.

subject: CHN
title: Third-Year Chinese for Business Professionals
description: Accelerated, intensive advanced course focusing on general advanced listening, speaking, reading, and writing communicative needs of business professionals in the Chinese business context.

subject: CHN
title: Mandarin Conversation I
description: Systematic practice on everyday topics of conversation. Lab work.

subject: CHN
title: Mandarin Conversation II
description: Continuation of 311.

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Dialect Studies
description: Advanced Cantonese or other Chinese dialects. CR/NC for native Chinese speakers.

subject: CHN
title: Advanced Chinese Listening and Writing
description: Web-based training in Chinese listening, reading, and writing to develop skills at the advanced level. Activities combine independent work with communicative activities on the course website. Features language exchange with native speakers.

subject: CHN
title: Advanced Chinese Reading and Writing
description: Web-based training in Chinese reading and writing to develop skills at the advanced level. Activities combine independent work with communicative activities on the course web site. Ideal for in-service professionals seeking language development and maintenance.

subject: CHN
title: Directed Third-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in their area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses.

subject: CHN
title: Fourth-Level Mandarin I
description: Extensive reading in academic topics. Meets one hour a day, three times a week.

subject: CHN
title: Fourth-Level Mandarin II
description: Continuation of 401.

subject: CHN
title: Accelerated Fourth-Level Mandarin
description: Content of 401 and 402 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, three times a week.

subject: CHN
title: Fourth-Year Chinese for Business Professionals
description: Accelerated, intensive advanced course focusing on specialized advanced listening, speaking, reading, and writing communicative needs of business professionals in the Chinese business context.

subject: CHN
title: High-Advanced Chinese I
description: Authentic reading, writing, speaking, and listening with Advanced-high and Superior level discourse, content, and genres to build Superior Chinese proficiency and broaden knowledge of Chinese culture. Significant attention paid to developing Chinese writing skills.

subject: CHN
title: High-Advanced Chinese II
description: Aims to build Superior Level Chinese proficiency in reading, speaking, writing, and listening using authentic texts covering Chinese education, and economy, philosophy, while broadening and deepening knowledge of Chinese culture.

subject: CHN
title: Advanced Mandarin Conversation I
description: Systematic practice on academic topics of conversation. Lab work.

subject: CHN
title: Advanced Mandarin Conversation II
description: Continuation of 411.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Chinese Translation
description: Training in techniques; theory of translation. (B) Chinese–English; (C) English–Chinese.

subject: CHN
title: Media Analysis in Chinese
description: Use authentic materials, including texts, videos, and postings from social media with Advanced and Superior level discourse and content to build Superior Chinese proficiency and social media literacy, and understand society and contemporary issues.

subject: CHN
title: Fourth Year Reading and Writing: Advanced Topics
description: Asynchronous web-based course with focuses on (i) reading selected texts across a broad range of genres, and (ii) writing expository and argumentative essays by referencing and reflecting on the readings, along with interacting with peers.

subject: CHN
title: Fourth Year Reading and Writing: Contemporary Social Issues
description: Asynchronous web-based course with focuses on (i) authentic texts covering a variety of contemporary social issues, and (ii) writing expository/argumentative essays by referencing and reflecting on the readings, along with interacting with peers.

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Language and Linguistics
description: Covers major areas of linguistic description as applied to Chinese language, with significant attention paid to developing writing skills on demonstrating knowledge of the basics of Chinese linguistic features and analyzing Chinese language phenomena.

subject: CHN
title: Structure of Chinese
description: Introduction to syntax and semantics of Mandarin Chinese; some discussion of usage and linguistic geography.

subject: CHN
title: Study of Chinese Characters I
description: Origin, structure, and evolution.

subject: CHN
title: Study of Chinese Characters II
description: Continuation of 453.

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Pragmatics and Discourse
description: Introduction to pragmatics and discourse analysis of Mandarin Chinese; some discussion of usage and linguistic geography.

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Semantics and Communication
description: Study of the meaning of Chinese sentences in isolation, in discourse contexts, and in written texts. Pays equal attention to theoretical issues and practical problems in Chinese semantics and communication.

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Words and the Lexicon
description: Defines properties of the Chinese lexicon, introduces its principles, approaches, and methodologies in Chinese lexicology, outlines similarities and differences between the Chinese and English lexicons, and advances students’ Chinese language proficiency.

subject: CHN
title: Introduction to Classical Chinese
description: Analysis of basic structural patterns through selected readings in various texts.

subject: CHN
title: Language and Culture of China
description: Extensive exposure–chiefly through tape recordings, classroom conversation, and outside readings–to history, culture, and institutions.

subject: CHN
title: Professional Chinese
description: Focus on professional reading, writing, speaking, and listening in order to train students to the Superior (according to ACTFL standards) level of language proficiency.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time when taken in China as part of the UH Chinese Flagship Program

subject: CHN
title: Academic
description: Focus on academic reading, writing, speaking, and listening with emphasis on writing instruction in order to train students to the Superior (according to ACTFL standards) level of language proficiency.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time when taken in China as part of the UH Chinese Flagship Program

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Readings in 20th Century Chinese Literature
description: Representative works of writers from People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. (B) short stories; (C) poetry and drama; (D) novels and essays.

subject: CHN
title: Flagship Rhetoric and Composition Abroad
description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will improve their knowledge of and ability to use Chinese to effectively communicate in writing.

subject: CHN
title: Flagship Media and Society Abroad
description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will improve their knowledge of Chinese media, how it operates, and its effects on Chinese society.

subject: CHN
title: Flagship Experience Abroad
description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will take two courses taught in Chinese in their field at Nanjing or Beijing Union University.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits

subject: CHN
title: Oral Fluency Through Chinese Films
description: Increasing Chinese proficiency through film, which offers authentically rich cultural contexts. Focus on oral communication.

subject: CHN
title: Internship Program
description: Faculty supervised participation in the operations of an organization in a position making use of students’ Chinese language skills in Hawai‘i. Students must achieve a grade of B- in CHN 302 to take this course. Junior/senior standing only.
prereq_raw: 302 (with a minimum grade of B-) or consent
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits

subject: CHN
title: Overseas Internship in China
description: Supervised internships in a Chinese-speaking institution in China. Students must pass 486 with a B- or higher and be accepted to the Flagship Capstone Year in China to take this.
prereq_raw: 461 and 485 and 486 (with a minimum grade of B- or better) and proficiency assessment and acceptance to Flagship Capstone year in China

children.text: acceptance to Flagship Capstone year in China

repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits

subject: CHN
title: Directed Fourth-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. Primarily for graduate students from other departments.

subject: CHN
title: Introduction to Study of Contemporary Chinese Linguistics
description: Panoramic overview of major perspectives in contemporary Chinese linguistics. Readings on recent developments of fields. Report on selected research papers and present analysis of linguistic phenomena of interest.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Chinese Poetry
description: Critical study of major traditional Chinese poetic forms. (B) ancient (to 5th century); (C) medieval (5th–10th century).
prereq_raw: 461 or consent for (B), 610B or consent for (C)

subject: CHN
title: Traditional Chinese Fiction
description: Formal and thematic analysis of short stories, historical romances, and novels.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) History of Chinese Language
description: (B) phonology; (C) syntax.
prereq_raw: 451, LING 421, or consent for (B); 452 or consent for (C)

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Dialects
description: Synchronic description of a Chinese dialect other than Cantonese and Mandarin; contrastive and comparative studies with Mandarin.

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Syntax and Semantics
description: Verbal categories, aspects, focus devices, resultative and directional compounds, coverbial constructions. Interaction between syntax and semantics.

subject: CHN
title: Contrastive Analysis of Mandarin and English

subject: CHN
title: Methods in Teaching Chinese as Second Language
description: Problems in language learning and teaching. Practice in preparing and presenting lessons with materials based on comparative linguistic analysis. Materials, teaching aids, test construction.

subject: CHN
title: Practicum: Teaching Chinese Language
description: For graduate students pursuing teaching Chinese language. Students gain practical skills and hands-on experiences in creating instructional and assessment materials and teaching an actual Chinese language class using the self-developed materials effectively.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Topics in Chinese Language
description: Extensive studies of selected topics (B) teaching and testing: specific problems in teaching Chinese including characters and cultural elements; proficiency and communicative ability; (C) cognitive grammar. A-F only for (C).
prereq_raw: 451 and 452, or consent. Once a year

subject: CHN
title: Current Topics in Chinese Grammar
description: Current approaches to Chinese grammar and related issues and debates, focusing on the papers published by leading Chinese linguists employing these approaches.

subject: CHN
title: Second Semester Classical Chinese
description: Builds on the foundation laid in 461; introduces complex syntactic patterns, advanced vocabulary; teaches sophisticated reading strategies and cultural literary contexts; exposes students to a wide range of intermediate level texts.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Research Seminar in Chinese Language
description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Research Seminar in Chinese Literature
description: Study of authors, a genre, a period, or a problem. (M) modern; (T) traditional. A-F only for (M).
prereq_raw: EALL 611, WGSS 613, WGSS 615, or WGSS 650; or consent for (M); 612, or consent for (T). )

subject: JPN
title: Elementary Japanese, Special
description: Same material as 101, covered more quickly for students with some language background.

subject: JPN
title: Elementary Japanese I
description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, grammar. Meets one hour, four times a week, plus lab work.

subject: JPN
title: Elementary Japanese II
description: Continuation of 100 or 101.

subject: JPN
title: Accelerated Elementary Japanese
description: Content of 101 and 102 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, four times a week.

subject: JPN
title: Elementary Japanese for Oral Communication I
description: The first of a series of courses focusing on speaking and listening skills necessary to performing in common situations in Hawai‘i and Japan.

subject: JPN
title: Elementary Japanese for Oral Communication II
description: Continuation of 111.

subject: JPN
title: Intermediate Japanese I
description: Continuation of 101 and 102. Meets one hour, four times a week, plus lab work.

subject: JPN
title: Intermediate Japanese II
description: Continuation of 201.

subject: JPN
title: Accelerated Intermediate Japanese for Pre-Professionals
description: Content of 201 and 202 covered in one semester. Emphasis on practical Japanese used in professional contexts. Meets two hours, four times a week.

subject: JPN
title: Intermediate Japanese for Oral Communication I
description: Continuation of 111-112.

subject: JPN
title: Intermediate Japanese for Oral Communication II
description: Continuation of 211.

subject: JPN
title: Introduction to Japanese Reading and Writing with Basic Kanji
description: For students who have completed the oral communication courses up through JPN 212 and wish to continue on to JPN 301. Also appropriate for semi-bilingual students who lack literacy skills.

subject: JPN
title: Intermediate Japanese Abroad
description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the second-year level in Japanese language and culture in Japan.

subject: JPN
title: Intermediate Japanese Abroad
description: Continuation of 258.

subject: JPN
title: Third-Year Japanese I
description: Transitional course employing four skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing) and grammar training to prepare students to address academic content in Japanese. Meets one hour, four times a week, plus lab work.

subject: JPN
title: Third-Year Japanese II
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: JPN
title: Accelerated Third-Year Japanese
description: Content of 301 and 302 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, four times a week, plus lab work.

subject: JPN
title: Third-Year Japanese for Professional Communication I
description: Training in oral communication skills essential for operating in a Japanese-speaking professional environment or workplace, focusing on activities such as first-time meetings, small talk with coworkers, and making/handling requests and invitations.

subject: JPN
title: Third-Year Japanese for Professional Communication: Business Etiquette and Hospitality
description: Training in oral communication skills essential for operating in a Japanese-speaking professional environment or workplace, focusing on activities such as telephone conversations, customer service, and daily interaction with coworkers.

subject: JPN
title: Third-Year Japanese Aural Comprehension
description: Training in strategies for listening to various types of spoken material presented in narrations, interviews, news broadcasts, and lectures, etc.

subject: JPN
title: Oral Fluency Through Film
description: Training in oral communication and comprehension skills utilizing the spoken text and visual segments from Japanese film and television dramas.

subject: JPN
title: Linquistic Analysis of Manga & Anime
description: Study of basic linguistic concepts and phenomena through manga and anime (and other Japanese fiction). Class activities will consist of lecture, discussion, and analysis of linguistic data.

subject: JPN
title: Advanced Japanese Reading and Writing
description: Web-based training in Japanese reading and writing to develop skills at the advanced level. Course activities combine independent work with communicative activities on the website. Ideal for in-service professionals seeking language development and maintenance.

subject: JPN
title: Introduction to Japanese Linguistics
description: Introduction to major areas of linguistic description as applied to Japanese language.

subject: JPN
title: Third-Level Japanese Abroad
description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the third-year level in Japanese language and culture in Japan.

subject: JPN
title: Third-Level Japanese Abroad
description: Continuation of 358.

subject: JPN
title: Japanese Language Abroad Electives
description: Students will directly enroll in Japanese language courses at J.F. Oberlin University or Konan University.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times for different topics, up to nine credits

subject: JPN
title: Language in Japanese Society
description: Introduction to basic concepts and issues surrounding language in Japanese society. Covers historical, cultural, and sociolinguistic dimensions of the Japanese language. Topics are closely linked with contemporary ethical issues.

subject: JPN
title: Directed Third-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses.

subject: JPN
title: Fourth-Year Japanese I
description: Continuation of 302 and 305 emphasizing all four skills. Transition to longer and more complex written and spoken Japanese. Meets 50 minutes, four times a week.

subject: JPN
title: Fourth-Year Japanese II
description: Continuation of 401. Transition to longer and more complex written and spoken Japanese. Meets 50 minutes, four times a week.

subject: JPN
title: Fourth-Year Japanese for Advanced Speakers
description: 4th-year Japanese language course that provide bilingual and other advanced speakers with language training in formal Japanese with a focus on reading and oral communication skills.

subject: JPN
title: Fourth-Year Japanese for Advanced Written Communication
description: 4th-year Japanese language course that provide bilingual and other advanced speakers with language training in formal Japanese with a focus on reading and writing skills.

subject: JPN
title: Fourth-Level Japanese Reading: Accelerated
description: Content of 401 and 402 covered in one semester. Meets two hours, four times a week.

subject: JPN
title: (Alpha) Readings in Original Texts
description: (D) academic and journalistic texts; (E) modern literature.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time in different alphas

subject: JPN
title: Japanese Aural Comprehension
description: Training in comprehension of spoken material presented in news broadcasts, documentary narration, formal lectures, etc.
prereq_raw: 402, 405; or consent. May be concurrent with 407

subject: JPN
title: Fourth-Level Spoken Japanese
description: Training in oral communication skills in varied social contexts.

subject: JPN
title: Japanese Composition
description: Writing skills refined through practice in various styles (essays, letters, etc.).
