description: English language in Hawai‘i viewed historically and in a multicultural context, with attention to politics, religion, race, and education, from 1820 to present.
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses or consent

subject: ENG
title: Teaching Composition
description: Theory, observation, and practice in teaching writing, especially the use of one-on-one and small group instruction.
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses; or consent. Recommended: 306

subject: ENG
title: Advanced Argumentative Writing
description: Advanced study of both the philosophical and practical dimensions of written reasoning. Emphasis on argument as a process of inquiry.
prereq_raw: FW and either 200 or one ENG DL course, or consent

subject: ENG
title: Writing for Digital Media
description: Combined lecture/lab on writing and rhetoric in computermediated communication. May include online technical writing, courseware development, social media content creation.
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses or consent

subject: ENG
title: Professional Editing
description: Discussion and practice in the professional editing of articles, reports, books; logic, clarity, coherence, consistency of tone and style, grammar and punctuation.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Composition/Rhetoric/ Language
description: Intensive study of selected topics, questions, themes, issues, and/or writers in composition, rhetoric, and/or English language.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Form and Theory of Poetry
description: Poetic theories and techniques for students interested in writing poetry.

subject: ENG
title: Poetry Workshop
description: Writing, evaluating poems.

subject: ENG
title: Nonfiction Writing
description: Workshop analysis of nonfiction as a literary form. Significant attention paid to developing writing skills.

subject: ENG
title: Form and Theory of Fiction
description: Narrative techniques for students interested in writing fiction.

subject: ENG
title: Fiction Workshop
description: Writing, evaluating fiction.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Creative Writing
description: Intensive study of selected topics, questions, themes, writers, or modes of creative writing in a workshop setting.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literature and Culture
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in regard to cultural studies and the reading and interpretation of cultural texts.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Comparative Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in the field of comparative literature.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Medieval Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in Old/Middle English literature from 500-1500, including works in modern translation.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in 16th and 17th Century Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in texts written during the period 1500-1700.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in 18th Century Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in texts written during the period 1660-1830, the “long” 18th century.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in 19th Century Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in texts written during the 19th century.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in 20th and 21st Century Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, writers, traditions, or movements in texts written from the 20th century to the present.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Single Author
description: Intensive study of the works and literary milieu of a single author considered significant by most scholars in English Studies. The English Department maintains a list of versions focusing on specific authors.
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses or consent
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for a different author, with consent

subject: ENG
title: Geoffrey Chaucer
description: Intensive study of the works and literary milieu of Geoffrey Chaucer.
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses or consent

subject: ENG
title: William Shakespeare
description: Intensive study of the works and literary milieu of William Shakespeare.
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses or consent

subject: ENG
title: John Milton
description: Intensive study of the works and literary milieu of John Milton.
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses or consent

subject: ENG
title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
description: Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Film
description: Intensive study of selected topics in film, e.g.: genres, major filmmakers, film theory/criticism, or film and literature.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Life Writing
description: Intensive study of forms and theories of life writing in forms such as biographies, autobiographies, oral histories, diaries, journals, letters, film, drama, and portraiture with a focus on the ethical questions these materials present.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literary Forms, Genres, and Media
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, or movements in literary forms, genres, and media.
prereq_raw: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Asian American and Asian Diaspora Literatures
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, genres, or writers relating to Asia.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Postcolonial Literature
description: Intensive study of postcolonial literatures and of historical, cultural, and theoretical issues such as colonialism, migration, assimilation, national identity, or transnationalism.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Cultural Identities and Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, genres, and writers in relation to cultural identities such as race, ethnicity, class as the basis for literary inquiry.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Cultural and Literary Geographies
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, genres, or writers relating to space and place as the basis for literary inquiry. Topics may include migration, diaspora, and local histories.
prereq_raw: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Hawaiian and/or Pacific Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, writers, movements, and genres in the field of Hawaiian and/or Pacific literature.

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literature and Folklore
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, or genres in folklore and oral traditions and their performance and transformations within specific social and cultural contexts.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literature and Popular Culture
description: Intensive study of selected problems, issues, traditions, writers, movements, or genres in the field of popular literature and/or popular culture.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Studies in Literature and Sexuality and Gender
description: Intensive study of selected questions and issues in the construction and representation of sexuality and gender in specific genres, social and cultural contexts, or thematic/figurative clusters.
prereq_raw: 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: ENG
title: Study Abroad
description: Intensive study in the English language of selected topics, issues or writers from the host country in a UH Mānoa-approved study abroad location.
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses or consent

subject: ENG
title: Internship
description: Faculty supervised participation in the operations of an organization.
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses, junior standing, or consent

children.text: two ENG DL courses, junior standing

subject: ENG
title: Directed Reading
prereq_raw: two ENG DL courses or consent

subject: ENG
title: HWP Summer Institute WAC
description: Practicum in the current best approaches to teaching writing across the curriculum. Participants write, read published theory and research in composition, and demonstrate effective writing lessons.

subject: ENG
title: Old English
description: Structure of the language, relation to present English; reading of selected prose and poetry.

subject: ENG
title: Theory and Practice of Teaching Composition
description: Major contemporary theorists and classroom practices that evolve from their theories; observation and applications.

subject: ENG
title: Elements of Creative Writing
description: Intensive discussion of the craft and technique of creative writing through readings in poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and creative writing pedagogy.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Graduate Writing Workshop
description: Advanced practice and critical evaluation of the writing of poetry, fiction, or creative nonfiction. (B) poetry; (C) fiction; (D) nonfiction.
prereq_raw: graduate standing plus 411 for (B); 414 for (C); 412 for (D); or consent

children.text: plus 411 for (B) ; 414 for (C) ; 412 for (D) ; or consent

repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time in each English graduate degree

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Theories and Methods
description: Required course in the MA student’s area of concentration. (B) theories and methods of literary study; (C) introduction to composition and rhetoric; (D) foundations of creative writing; (E) theories in cultural studies.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Literary Theory and Criticism
description: (B) classical period through 18th century; (C) Romantic and post-Romantic.

subject: ENG
title: Biography
description: Study of one or more authors, English or American literature.

subject: ENG
title: MA Final Project
description: Individual reading and research towards preparation of MA project. 3 credit hours required.

subject: ENG
title: Supervised Practicum
description: Applies course work in literature, creative writing, cultural studies, or composition and rhetoric to hands-on activities engaging publics outside of the university under direction of practicing professionals and university faculty.

subject: ENG
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual reading or research.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable with consent of Graduate Director

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Composition Studies
description: Intensive study of selected issues in composition studies.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Rhetoric
description: Intensive study of selected topics in the history of rhetoric, rhetorical theory, or rhetorical criticism; topic to be announced.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Creative Writing
description: Advanced study in creative writing focused on thesis and dissertation projects.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time in each English graduate degree

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Techniques in Contemporary Literature
description: The study, from the point of view of the creative writer, of works written within the last 25 years. (B) techniques in fiction; (C) techniques in poetry; (D) techniques in creative nonfiction.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time in each ENG graduate degree

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Literary Criticism
description: Intensive study of selected topics in literary theory and its practical application; topics to be announced.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in English Literature
description: Study of authors or a period. (C) re-reading Chaucer; (N) 14th century poetry; (P) extended Victorian lyric; (Q) modern British fiction; (R) early 17th century poetry; (S) dominant Victorians: the 1840s; (T) Baroque and English literature; (U) literature and social change; (X) literature and history; (Y) studies in satire.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in American Literature
description: Study of authors or a period. (B) American modernism; (C) race in American literature; (D) 19th century American poetry; (E) American literature naturalism; (F) African American literature and theory; (G) American transcendentalism; (H) 19th century American novel; (J) contemporary American poetry; (N) poetry by 20th century American women; (P) women writers and multiculturalism; (Q) Asian American literature and theory; (R) relocating American literature; (S) early American literature; (T) H. Melville and T. Morrison.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Major Author
description: Study of one or more authors, English or American. (C) George Eliot; (D) Emily Dickinson; (M) Milton; (S) Chaucer and his backgrounds; (T) Austen; (U) Yeats and his circle; (X) Beowulf; (Y) Faulkner’s narrative; (Z) Virginia Woolf.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Shakespeare
description: Intensive study of Shakespeare.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Literary Genres
description: Study of one or more authors, English or American literature. (C) neoclassicism; (D) tragedy; (E) modern American short story; (F) sonnet and sonnet sequences; (G) Rest., 18th century dramatic comedy; (H) 18th century literature and art; (I) medieval drama; (J) narrative theory and criticism; (K) reinventing the author; (M) laughter and the comic arts; (N) nature of romance; (O) Victorian novel; (P) Jacobean drama; (Q) science fiction; (R) essay, past and present; (S) Eng. hymn in Western culture; (W) 18th century British women novelists; (Y) English romanticism; (Z) English novel and criticism.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Film Theory and Criticism
description: Classic theories of representation and aesthetics; modern and contemporary cultural, psychoanalytic, and aesthetic theories as they apply to film.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Life Writing
description: Intensive study of critical and theoretical issues raised by various forms of life writing (biography, autobiography, oral history, diaries, etc.) and of their history and methodology.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Cultural Studies in Asia/ Pacific
description: Intensive study of selected issues in cultural studies in Asia and the Pacific; topics to be announced.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Pacific Literatures
description: Intensive study of selected issues in the literatures of the Pacific in English, or translated into English. Topics to be announced.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Literatures of Hawai‘i
description: Introduction to comparative literature; relationship of Hawaiian to other literatures; sources and influences.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Hawaiian Literature
description: Intensive study of selected issues, genres, and traditions in Hawaiian literature written in English or translated from Hawaiian into English.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Cultural Studies
description: Intensive study of selected issues in cultural studies and cultural and social theory; topics to be announced.

subject: ENG
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Comparative Literature
description: Introduction to comparative literature; relationship of English to other literatures; sources and influences. (B) African lit. and literary theory; (F) folklore and literature; (G) theory/practice of poetry; (H) contemporary drama; (I) mythic method; (J) postmodern fiction; (M) modernism; (N) colonial/ postcolonial; (P) postmodernism and postcolonialism; (W) medieval women writers.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Special Topics
description: Content to be announced.

subject: ENG
title: Dissertation Research
prereq_raw: graduate standing and consent. Repeatable nine times

subject: HIST
title: World History to 1500
description: Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from prehistory to 1500; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

subject: HIST
title: World History since 1500
description: Continuation of 151. Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from 1500 to present; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

subject: HIST
title: Issues in World History
description: In examining aspects of the histories of Africa, Asia, the Americas, Europe and Oceania, this course highlights the myriad ways in which global contact has transformed our world and narratives of the past.

subject: HIST
title: World History of Human Disease
description: Examines how disease has affected humans in terms of society, culture, politics, religion, and economics. Explores the impact over a broad range of time periods, from pre-history to the present/future.

subject: HIST
title: Global Environmental History
description: Explores the influence of nature–climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms–on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them.

subject: HIST
title: Global History of Food
description: Exploration of food and eating from historical, cultural, economic, and geopolitical perspectives. Includes both historical and contemporary issues.

subject: HIST
title: World Cultures in Perspective
description: Development of civilizations from prehistoric origins to 1500. Offered as discussion and/or problems course. Alternative for 151 and 152; students in Honors program only.

subject: HIST
title: World Cultures in Perspective
description: Continuation of 161A. Development of civilization from 1500 to the present. Offered as discussion and/ or problems course. Alternative for 151 and 152; students in Honors program only.

subject: HIST
title: Early European Civilization
description: Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states before 1500, including classical and medieval eras. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: European Civilization 1500-1800
description: Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states. 1500–1800.

subject: HIST
title: Modern European Civilization 1800-
description: Continuation of 231. Major political, social, economic, and cultural trends from Napoleon to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Civilizations of Asia
description: Survey of major civilizations of Asia from earliest times to 1500; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

subject: HIST
title: Civilizations of Asia
description: Continuation of 241. Survey of major civilizations of Asia from 1500 to the present; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

subject: HIST
title: Atlantic History: Colonies to Revolutions
description: Comparative and historical survey of colonialism and revolutions in the Atlantic World from 1500 to 1830. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to American History
description: Interpretive survey from earliest settlement to 1865.

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to American History
description: Interpretive survey from 1865 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: History of the Hawaiian Islands
description: Survey of state and local history from Polynesian chiefdoms to Hawaiian Kingdom to American territory and state.

subject: HIST
title: Oceania Survey
description: Survey of major events, themes, and issues that make up the diverse histories of Oceania, including Hawai‘i, from ancestral origins to the present, with an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: HIST
title: History of the Philippines
description: Traces developments in Philippine history and society from precolonial to contemporary times and explores ways in which the peoples of the Philippines embraced, resisted or negotiated new modes of thought, behavior and social organization influenced by the Spanish, American, and Japanese regimes as well as the postcolonial global order.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in History
description: Introduction to methods of historical inquiry; current issues in World, American, European, or Pacific history. Emphasis on teaching writing. A-F only

subject: HIST
title: History of Early India
description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from Mohenjo-Daro to the Mughal Empire, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from ancient times to the 18th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of Modern India
description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from the Mughal Empire to the new millennium, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from the 18th century to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Early Modern Southeast Asia
description: Traces the development of Southeast Asia from early beginnings to the 19th century. Ethical issues and effective writing based on essays and ethical responses will form an important part of the course. DH

subject: HIST
title: Modern Southeast Asia
description: Continuation of 305, from 18th century to the present.

subject: HIST
title: East Asian Civilizations
description: Characteristics of East Asian civilizations as they developed in pre-modern China; variant patterns in Japan and Korea; the modernization process to 1500.

subject: HIST
title: East Asian Civilizations
description: Continuation of 309. Period after 1500.

subject: HIST
title: History of China
description: Chinese civilization to the 17th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of China
description: Continuation of 311. Period since the 17th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of Japan
description: Survey of culture, government, economics, and institutions, to 1700.

subject: HIST
title: History of Japan
description: Continuation of 321. Period from 1700.

subject: HIST
title: Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
description: History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of the tea ceremony: Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics. Includes an emphasis on Oral Communication skills.

subject: HIST
title: The Samurai of Japan
description: A social, military, and cultural history of Japan’s samurai (warrior) class.

subject: HIST
title: History of Premodern Korea
description: Survey of political, economic, social, and cultural developments from earliest times to 1400. Ethical issues in nationhood, central hegemony, myth-making, warfare, and memory politics are discussed.

subject: HIST
title: History of Modern Korea
description: Continuation of 327. From 1400 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: History of North Korea
description: History of North Korea in terms of industrialism, militarism, nationalism, and state power, from 1945 to today. Focus on construction of national sovereign identity and comparison with postcolonial world.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Greece I
description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Minoan, Mycenean, and Archaic periods.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Greece II
description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Classical and Hellenistic periods.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Rome: The Republic
description: Political, social, cultural history from the Etruscans to Augustus. Emphasis on discussion of literary and archaeological materials. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Rome: The Empire
description: Political, social, and cultural history from Augustus to 476 A.D. Emphasis on literary and archaeological materials. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: HIST
title: Early Medieval Europe 300–1050
description: Formation of European societies in relation to Byzantine and Islamic cultures. Writing exercises develop historical thinking and the analysis of primary sources through workshops with peer and instructor feedback on drafts and revisions.

subject: HIST
title: Medieval Europe 1050–1350
description: Main trends in European economy, society, religion, politics, thought, and the arts; interactions with Byzantine and Islamic worlds.

subject: HIST
title: European Intellectual History
description: Undergraduate seminar on great debates in Western thought. Discussion of primary source materials; the scientific revolution and Enlightenment.

subject: HIST
title: European Intellectual History
description: Continuation of 337. European thought from French Revolution to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Renaissance and Reformation
description: Political, social, cultural, and intellectual developments in Europe from 1300 to 1600. Emphasis on cultural and intellectual history and its impact on social and political developments; humanism and its influence on thought and reforming movements, Protestant and Catholic Reformations. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: HIST
title: Comparative Economic History
description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions.

subject: HIST
title: The History of Economic Thought
description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Reacting to the Past
description: Exploration of moments of crisis and the clash of ideas in their historical context through the use of simulation games.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Germany
description: Political, social, economic, and cultural history since 1547. Rise of Austria and Prussia, unification, Bismarckian era, World War I and Weimar Republic, Hitler’s Third Reich, post-World War II.

subject: HIST
title: France in the Old Regime
description: Major social, political, and intellectual developments: Renaissance, Reformation, religious wars, Richelieu, Louis XIV, Enlightenment, and Revolution.

subject: HIST
title: Modern France
description: Political, social, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments in France from Revolution and Napoleon to the present. Assignments emphasize engagement with course concepts through oral communication and individual and group presentation.

subject: HIST
title: Tudor-Stuart Britain
description: Traces major developments in British politics, society, and culture between the late Medieval and Modern Eras.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Britain 1688-1945
description: Interaction of 17th-, 18th-, and 19th-century intellectual, political, economic, and social changes, which together produced the British Empire and modern Britain.

subject: HIST
title: British Empire
description: Origins and expansion of the British empire between the seventeenth and twentieth centuries. Includes imperial policies affecting Britain, Australia, India, Ireland, and Southern Africa. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: Iberia in Asia and the Pacific
description: Comparative exploration of the Iberian empires–Spain and Portugal–and their political, economic, and cultural interactions with indigenous societies in Asia and the Pacific.

subject: HIST
title: France and Empire
description: Lecture/discussion exploring the history of France’s relationship with imperialism from the Renaissance to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to Islamic History
description: Muhammad, the Arab conquests, the Caliphate; fundamentals of Islam; classical Islamic civilization; development of Islam into modern times with emphasis on the Middle Eastern heartland.

subject: HIST
title: The Making of the Modern Middle East
description: Survey of developments that created the system of nation-states in the Middle East. History of the Ottoman Empire and the Republic of Turkey; Egypt; the Arab world; Israel and Iran.

subject: HIST
title: Survey of African History
description: The history of Africa from earliest times to the present: the rise of indigenous civilizations, European and Muslim impact, colonialism and nationalism, and current issues.

subject: HIST
title: The World of Mekong
description: Historical survey, from BC period to present, of the peoples of the Mekong region, an area covering southwestern China, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and southern Vietnam. Open to nonmajors.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Women’s History
description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work in and outside the household, women’s involvement in social movements, changing norms about gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences among women.

subject: HIST
title: Gender and Sexuality in the Classical World
description: Critical examination of the construction of gender identity and sexuality in ancient Greece and Rome. (Once a year)

subject: HIST
title: Women in Oceania
description: Uses research and writing to explore historical processes that have impacted the lives of Indigenous women in Oceania and women’s engagements with those processes over time, with a focus on women’s voices, agency, and empowerment.

subject: HIST
title: Global History of Sport
description: Explores the relationship between sport and society in historical perspective. Analyzes global processes of imperialism, nationalism, globalization, and international relations, and studies themes such as the politics of race, class, and gender.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Foreign Relations to 1898
description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from initial encounters between Europeans and Native Americans through the 1890s.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Foreign Relations From 1898
description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from the wars of 1898 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
description: Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship within the total society. Pre-Colonial to end of the 19th century.

subject: HIST
title: American Thought and Culture: 20th Century
description: Continuation of 373: the 20th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of American Business
description: The evolution of business enterprise from colonial times to the present. Emphasis on entrepreneurship, technological change, labor-management relations, government-business relations, and economic thought. Case studies of industrial development.

subject: HIST
title: American Empire
description: Examines the interplay between an “American culture of empire” and the rise of the U.S. as a superpower. Topics: imperialism and political culture, social movements and international affairs, race, gender and class relations.

subject: HIST
title: Caribbean History
description: Survey of the history of the Caribbean region from 1500 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: The Asia-Pacific War
description: Explores WWII in the Asia-Pacific region, focusing on the intersection of the grand strategy, military operations, and war crimes. Involves source analyses and discussions.

subject: HIST
title: History of Warfare to 1850
description: Classical and guerrilla warfare, revolution, and military systems and institutions.

subject: HIST
title: War and Peace Since 1850
description: Continuation of 391, from 1850 to present.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Military History
description: Survey of development of American military forces from War of Independence to war in Vietnam.

subject: HIST
title: History of Science to 1700
description: Evolution of scientific thought and its cultural context. Antiquity to 1700.

subject: HIST
title: History of Science Since 1700
description: Continuation of 394; science, technology, and society since 1700.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Historical Theories and Methods
description: Examination of the nature of historical understanding, research, and writing, and of recent trends in historical scholarship; preparation for senior thesis, including significant discipline-specific writing instruction and a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing. (B) historiography; (C) education.

subject: HIST
title: Digital History in the Global Village
description: History of the digital age in global perspective connecting people, media, and technology. Faculty and students will use digital media to introduce innovative approaches to doing history.

subject: HIST
title: History of the Indian Ocean World
description: Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women, and merchants. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Vietnam: History and Memory
description: Survey of Vietnamese history with particular attention to the multiple ways that the Vietnamese past has been remembered and represented by different peoples. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: Rivers, Seas, and Society in Southeast Asia
description: The rivers, seas, and extensive coastlines are a dominant environmental feature in Southeast Asia. Focuses on the dynamic interaction of water and society in shaping the history of the region.

subject: HIST
title: Themes of War in History
description: Explores cross-cutting themes of war from ancient times to the present, such as concepts of just war and unjust war, valor and heroism, and war trauma among combatants and civilian populations in conflict zones.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Philippines
description: Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Malaysia
description: History of Malay peninsula and northern Borneo, emphasizing developments since 18th century: trade, commerce, foreign migrations, pluralism, nationalism, and Islam.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Indonesia
description: Indonesia from 14th century to present. Emphasis on period from late 18th-century Western colonial impact to struggle for independence and problems of nationhood.

subject: HIST
title: History of Islamic Southeast Asia
description: History of the coming of Islam to Southeast Asia, the spread of its ideas, and its role in the lives of Muslim communities living in the region. GPA of 2.0 or higher.

subject: HIST
title: Twentieth-Century China
description: An examination of the political, intellectual, economic, cultural, and social transformations of China in the twentieth century. This lecture studies critical events in the making of modern China and explores important issues in the modernization of Chinese life in the twentieth century.

subject: HIST
title: Society and Culture in Traditional China
description: Ch’ing government and Chinese society from local and regional perspectives; modes of control and disorder during the 19th century.

subject: HIST
title: Local History of 20th-Century China
description: Sociopolitical change and continuity at local and regional levels since 1900, stressing provincial reform, Hsien and sub-Hsien politics, warlordism, Kuomintang tutelage, and the Chinese Communist movement and rule.

subject: HIST
title: Chinese Intellectual History
description: An interpretive survey of Chinese ideas and values in their cultural, social and political settings from classical age to 1600.

subject: HIST
title: Chinese Intellectual History
description: Interpretive survey of Chinese thought from 1600 to the contemporary period, with special emphasis on the themes of cultural collision and change.

subject: HIST
title: China’s Foreign Relations
description: Systematic review from traditional times, with emphasis on modern and contemporary history, analyses of foreign policy formulation, objectives, and implementation.

subject: HIST
title: The Search for Modern China
description: Origins, development, and meaning of modern revolution in China, 19th century to People’s Republic.

subject: HIST
title: People’s Republic of China
description: Salient developments from 1949 to the present. Social revolution and modernization, critically relevant foreign relations.

subject: HIST
title: China in World History
description: Interpretative survey of China’s changing position, significance, and function in the evolution of world history as a way to provide a better understanding of its past and present.

subject: HIST
title: Tokugawa Japan
description: Japanese history and culture, 1600–1867.

subject: HIST
title: Okinawa
description: Survey of social, cultural, economic, and political history from earliest times to present.

subject: HIST
title: Twentieth Century Japan
description: Problems of Japan’s political, economic, and social development since institutional consolidation of Meiji state (c.1890).

subject: HIST
title: Women in East Asian History
description: Survey of the changing political, social, economic, and cultural positions of women in China, Japan, and Korea from ancient times to the present.

subject: HIST
title: History of Japanese Cuisine and Foodways
description: Explores the history of Japanese cuisine and investigates the cultural, economic, and geopolitical aspects of food-ways in Japanese domestic and international identity.

subject: HIST
title: Topics on Transitional Justice
description: Explores how societies in the wake of armed conflict, repression, or mass human rights abuses build institutional capacities for promoting justice, human rights, and the rule of law

subject: HIST
title: War Crimes Trials in History
description: Explores war crimes trials in history since the end of WWII to the present. Involves extensive source analysis, discussion, research, and writing.

subject: HIST
title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age
description: Historical examination of the interaction between the Achaemenid and Parthian empires of Persia and the classical societies of the Mediterranean, such as the Greek city-states, Macedonia, the Hellenistic, and Roman Empires.

subject: HIST
title: Crisis and Conflict in the Middle East
description: In depth study and analysis of major crises and conflicts in the Middle East since World War II: the Arab–Israeli Wars, revolutions in the Arab countries, the Turkish experiment with secularism, the Iranian/ Islamic revolution, Afghanistan, the Gulf War.

subject: HIST
title: Medieval Cultures
description: Topical study of cultural and cross-cultural issues in the medieval period (circa 300-1500). Class discussion and written work emphasize analysis of primary source documents using cultural and world history theories. Regional focus and readings vary by semester.

subject: HIST
title: History of Christianity to 1500
description: Historical analysis of the main traditions of Christianity and elements of diversity within Europe and in relation to other parts of the world. Focus on the interpretation of primary sources and discussion of cultural issues. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: HIST
title: World Environmental History, 1500 to Present
description: Explores interactions between humans and the natural world from early modern era to the present. Topics include invader species and biotic exchange; environmental politics; and the ecological impact of industrialization, urbanization, science, technology, war, etc.

subject: HIST
title: The Darwinian Revolution
description: Social and intellectual origins of evolutionary thought and its continuing impact; emphasis on Darwin and the Victorian scientific community.

subject: HIST
title: 20th-Century Europe
description: Contemporary problems and their historical background.

subject: HIST
title: Expansion of Europe
description: Historical processes in modern European colonization from 16th to 20th century; impact on non-Europeans in Asia and Africa. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: HIST
title: War and Violence in Early Modern Europe
description: History of the intellectual, social, and cultural causes and consequences of violence, including military conflicts.

subject: HIST
title: Nazi Germany
description: Origins, establishment, and impact of Hitler’s Third Reich.

subject: HIST
title: The History of the Holocaust
description: The origins and progression of the Holocaust, the almost complete destruction of European Jews, and other Nazi genocidal policies. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: French Revolution and Napoleon
description: Causes, course, and conduct of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic periods, their impact upon Europe; emphasis on the conflict of ideologies inherent in the Revolutionary process.

subject: HIST
title: Europe, 1914-1945: War, Peace, and Revolution
description: Explores war and peace in Europe, from the start of the Great War through the formal end of World War II. Topics include key battles, civilians, peace movements, treaties, the Shoah, Fascism, and Soviet Revolution.

subject: HIST
title: Imperial Spain and Portugal
description: The influence of Spain and Portugal on people and cultures in Europe, Africa, America, and Asia; Portugal’s captivity and the defeat of the Spanish Armada.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in African History
description: Selected themes important in African history, including, for example, the politics, economics, societies, and cultures of pre-colonial, colonial, or modern Africa. Topics to be pre-announced. (Once a year)

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) History and Literature
description: Explores the many relationships between history and literature, including how literature has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past; (B) United States; (C) Europe; (D) Asia/ Pacific; (E) World/Comparative; (F) Provisional topics.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas, not repeatable for (C)

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) History and Film
description: Explores the many relationships between history and film including how film has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past. (B) United States; (C) Europe: emphasis on writing as historians and film critics; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) world/ comparative: significant attention paid to developing writing skills that involve critically comparing history-related cinematic representations across regions and cultures. (Once a year for (D))(C Cross-listed as CINE 452C); (E Cross-listed as CINE 452E)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: HIST
title: Colonial Medicine
description: Evolution of Western medical traditions; challenges created by European expansion and colonial interactions; development of modern racial and gender theories.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Russia
description: Creation of the Soviet Union, Stalinization, the Cold War, the collapse of the empire, the post-Soviet era.

subject: HIST
title: Russia in Asia and the Pacific
description: Russian/Soviet Siberia and Central Asia; Russian American Company and the Pacific; evolving relations with Asian and Pacific powers.

subject: HIST
title: The American Revolution
description: Lecture/ discussion on the origins, development, and consequences of the American Revolution, explored within the context of the broader revolutionary Atlantic world.

subject: HIST
title: African American History
description: Lecture/ discussion on the origins of racial slavery, slave and free black culture, slave resistance and antislavery, post-emancipation black life, the rise of Jim Crow, the Harlem Renaissance, and the Civil Rights Movement.

subject: HIST
title: Native American History
description: Lecture/ discussion on the history of North American Indians from the seventeenth century to the present. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: Early America
description: Lecture/discussion on Native Americans, Africans, and Europeans in North America from contact to independence. Social, cultural, and economic themes and intersections of race, class, and gender explored.

subject: HIST
title: The Early American Republic
description: Lecture/discussion on the Constitution, the growth of partisan politics, the market revolution, religious revivalism, abolitionism and the expansion of slavery in the U.S. during the age of Jefferson and Jackson.

subject: HIST
title: American Civil War Era 1841–1877
description: The crisis of the Union: antebellum society and culture, slavery, reform, sectionalism, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

subject: HIST
title: Transformation of America 1877–1920
description: Selected themes that explain major changes in American life during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, including the westward movement, consolidation of capitalism, world power diplomacy, popular culture, progressivism, and World War I.

subject: HIST
title: The United States 1920–1948
description: The Roaring Twenties, the Depression, New Deal, coming of World War II, America during the war, origins of the Cold War.

subject: HIST
title: The U.S.: 1948 to the Present
description: The atomic age and the Cold War, the age of anxiety, the 1960s, the Vietnam War, the Reagan-Bush era, and beyond.

subject: HIST
title: American Television History
description: Lecture/discussion examining the impact of television on American society, culture and politics. Analyzed in depth are family sitcoms, presidential politics, Vietnam and the presentation of gender and ethnicity. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: Viva Las Vegas!
description: Upper-division lecture on the historical and cultural significance of Las Vegas in twentieth-century America. Open to non-majors.

subject: HIST
title: The Cold War
description: Cold War as a global struggle. Topics will include U.S.-Soviet economic and political rivalry, Capitalism vs. Communism as practical policy and ideology, and the force of Third World anti-colonial nationalism.

subject: HIST
title: Music, Industry, and Society
description: History of U.S. music and recording industry. How industry relates to economy as a whole, and how it reflects broad patterns and trends in American culture and society.

subject: HIST
title: Slavery and Freedom
description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World.

subject: HIST
title: The American West
description: Lecture/ discussion surveying the conquest, colonization, and consolidation of North American frontiers and the post-frontier development of the American West.

subject: HIST
title: Constitutional History of the U.S.
description: Origins, development of Constitution, Colonial to modern times.

subject: HIST
title: Race and Racism in America
description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history.

subject: HIST
title: History of American Workers
description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century.

subject: HIST
title: Colonial Latin America
description: PreColumbian civilizations: Spanish and Portuguese colonization; political, economic, social, and religious evolution to 1810; independence.

subject: HIST
title: Latin America Since Independence
description: Political, economic, and social development since 1825; case studies from Brazil, Mexico, and Cuba.

subject: HIST
title: American Environmental History
description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Histories of Oceania I
description: Explores the diverse, interconnected histories of Oceania from ancestral origins through the early colonial period. Topics include voyaging, orality, land, gender, power, exchange, cross-cultural encounter, disease, colonization, resistance, and historiography. Additional focus on oral communication. DH

subject: HIST
title: Histories of Oceania II
description: Examines Oceania’s histories of protest during the colonial and post-colonial eras as responses to empire expansion. Explores ethical issues concerning these movements, emphasizing Hawai‘i experiences and their intersection with those across Oceania.

subject: HIST
title: United States in the Pacific
description: Growth of economic and political interests and policies.

subject: HIST
title: The Hawaiian Kingdom 1819–1893
description: Transformation of Hawai‘i into a state influenced by American and European ideas and institutions and Asian peoples, with an emphasis on instruction on writing.

subject: HIST
title: History of 20th-Century Hawai‘i
description: Formation of an American Hawai‘i with its unique local culture from 1898 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: World Maritime History
description: Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples.

subject: HIST
title: Women and Revolution
description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons

subject: HIST
title: Library Treasures: Exploring Special Collections & Archives
description: Conduct original research using general library materials, special collections, rare books, archives, and manuscripts, maps, and other historical documents that are uniquely available at libraries and archives at UH and beyond.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) History Colloquium
description: Extensive or intensive treatment of special problems. (B) Philippines and Indonesia; (C) U.S. foreign relations; (D) history in Oceania; (E) Chinese traditional government. Recommended for honors students.
prereq_raw: 372 (or concurrent) or consent for (C); consent for (B) and (E)

subject: HIST
title: Senior Tutorial in History
description: Analysis of sources and evaluation of methods of historical writing. Students undertake a major research and writing project in field of special interest. Capstone course requires a 20-25 page minimum final research paper.

subject: HIST
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual projects in various fields. History majors with consent. Maximum 5 credit hours. (1) American; (2) Pacific; (3) Japanese; (4) European; (5) English; (6) Chinese; (7) Russian; (8) Hawaiian; (9) South Asian; (10) Southeast Asian; (11) Korean.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Historiography
description: History of history and historians; philosophies of history.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Digital History
description: Examines the various ways that the production, presentation, and learning of history through digital media is changing the way people access and process information about the past. Graduate standing only.

subject: HIST
title: Advanced Topics in Environmental History
description: Introduction to leading themes, methodologies, and topics in world environmental history. Drawing on new and influential scholarship, readings explore the diverse forces that shape humans’ adaptation to and impact on the natural world. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Seminar on Water in History
description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in World History
description: Analysis, research, and discussion of themes and issues in study of history of humankind.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in World History
description: Selected themes— feudalism, economic and industrial development, etc.— important in global history. Topics pre-announced.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Advanced Readings in European History
description: Selected topics for advanced reading; (B) ancient; (C) medieval; (D) early modern; (E) modern; (G) intellectual.
prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent. (Alt. years: spring for (D)); (Alt. years: fall for (E))

children.text: ( Alt. years: spring for (D) ) ; ( Alt. years: fall for (E) )

subject: HIST
title: Ethnographic History
description: Critical inquiry into historical representations of the “other” and ways in which modern historians have used culture and other anthropological concepts to write and think about the past.

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to Cultural Studies
description: Graduate seminar designed to introduce history students to the multidisciplinary theories that are appropriate to cultural studies.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Research in European History
description: Selected topics for advanced research. (B) ancient; (C) medieval; (D) early modern; (E) modern; (G) intellectual.
prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent. (Once a year)

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Topics in European Colonialism
description: Selected topics for comparative advanced reading and research. (D) early modern; (E) modern.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in Historical Methods and Theory
description: Seminar covering one specific approach to historical methods or theory. The goal is a deep engagement with a particular historical approach via research and reading not bounded by region, time, or specialty. Graduate standing only.

subject: HIST
title: Atrocity Crimes: Law and History
description: Seminar on history of mass atrocity and international justice in the modern world. Topics include postWWII Allied war crimes prosecution, post-cold war ad hoc international criminal tribunals, and contemporary international law and national legal systems.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Advanced Readings in Russian History
description: (B) early Russia; (C) modern.

subject: HIST
title: Slavery and Modern Memory
description: Exploration of contemporary resonances of slavery in the Americas through literature, historical scholarship, memory and trauma studies, and the visual and performing arts. Graduate students only.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Advanced Readings in American History
description: Interpretations and literature of important themes and problems. (B) early America; (C) the Republic to 1877; (D) industrial America; (E) recent America.
prereq_raw: appropriate 400-level U.S. history course or consent for (D) and (E); graduate standing or consent for (B) and (C). (Alt. years for (B)) ((B) Cross-listed as AMST 610)

children.text: for (D) and ( E); graduate standing or consent for (B) and ( C). ( Alt. years for (B) ) ( ( B) Cross-listed as AMST 610 )

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Research in American History
description: (B) early America; (C) the Republic to 1877; (D) industrial America; (E) recent America; (F) foreign relations.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Advanced Topics in American History
description: Seminar in advanced research and readings: (B) social and intellectual; (C) foreign relations; (F) the West; (K) business, labor, and technology.
prereq_raw: graduate standing and consent. ((B) Cross-listed as AMST 646); ((F) Cross-listed as AMST 614); ((K) Cross-listed as AMST 647)

children.text: ( ( B) Cross-listed as AMST 646 ) ; ( ( F) Cross-listed as AMST 614 ) ; ( ( K) Cross-listed as AMST 647 )

subject: HIST
title: Seminar: Comparative Asia
description: This reading seminar in the comparative history of modern Asia will introduce graduate students to themes, particularly in social, cultural, and intellectual history, which lend themselves to comparison across the region.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in Southeast Asia
description: Reading and research seminar on themes about the past and present of Southeast Asia in a comparative framework.

subject: HIST
title: Historiography of Southeast Asia
description: Examination of contested boundaries of Southeast Asia, the various historiographic traditions, the colonial legacy, and the current issues emerging from a dialogue of historians from the “region” and the outside world.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Modern Southeast Asian History
description: Graduate level reading seminar in modern Southeast Asian history.

subject: HIST
title: The Seas in Southeast Asian History
description: Seminar on the seas in Southeast Asian history. (Alt. years)

subject: HIST
title: Seminar: Vietnamese History
description: Reading and research seminar on Vietnamese history.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Chinese History
description: Problems and readings in political, social, and cultural history. (B) early; (C) middle; (D) modern.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar: Islam and Islamic Civilization
description: Readings on the rise, spread, and development of Islamic cultures and civilizations throughout the world down to modern times.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in South Asian History
description: Graduate-level reading and research seminar on topics in Indian and South Asian history.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Japanese History
description: Problems, principal sources of bibliographic information. (B) traditional period to c.1600; (C) early modern 1600–1868; (D) 1868 to present; (E) 20th-century diplomatic.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Korean History
description: Reading major interpretive works, and research in selected topics. (B) reading; (C) research.

subject: HIST
title: Topics on War in History
description: Research seminars on topics on war in history.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in Histories of Oceania
description: Reading and research on major issues, topics, and themes in the history of Oceania.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in History of Hawai‘i
description: Reading seminar with short papers required. Covers Kingdom of Hawai‘i and 20th-century Hawai‘i in alternate years. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: HIST
title: Hawaiian Historical Research: Documents and Methods
description: Research and writings emphasizing the interpretation of Hawaiian and English language primary sources. Development of source materials, approaches, and methods in Hawaiian history. Graduate standing only.
prereq_raw: HAW 301 with a B or better, or instructor consent

subject: HIST
title: Directed Research
description: Individual research topics. (1) American; (2) Pacific; (3) Japanese; (4) European; (5) English; (6) Chinese; (7) Russian; (8) Hawaiian; (9) South Asian; (10) Southeast Asian; (11) Korean. Restricted to plan A (thesis) students. Maximum 2 credit hours.

subject: HIST
title: Institutional History of Korea
description: Major political, economic, and social institutions.

subject: HIST
title: Chinese Historical Literature
description: Reading and use of numerous genres of Chinese historical literature and documents. Chinese bibliography. Knowledge of Chinese required.

subject: HIST
title: Teaching History
description: HIST 100-level faculty supervisors mentor their Teaching Assistants who teach the discussion labs. Course addresses issues of teaching strategy, grading and historical content. Enrollment limited to current Teaching Assistants in the World History Program.
prereq_raw: History graduate Teaching Assistants assigned to 151-152

prereq_tree.text: History graduate Teaching Assistants assigned to 151 -152

subject: ARAB
title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
description: Designed to provide students with basic knowledge of Modern Standard Arabic. Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language, as well as formal spoken Arabic.

subject: ARAB
title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
description: Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language as well as formal spoken Arabic. It introduces a wide range of situation-based texts and topics that build vocabulary, grammar, and general communicative competence.

subject: ARAB
title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
description: Designed for students who have successfully completed a year of Elementary Arabic. Focus is on acquisition of more complex grammatical structures, expanding vocabulary, and developing competence in a wide range of communicative situations.

subject: ARAB
title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
description: Designed for students who have successfully completed three semesters of Arabic. Focus is on intensive practice of interactive functional skills such as listening comprehension and fundamental conversation strategies.

subject: ARAB
title: Third-Level Arabic I
description: Develop proficiency in reading/listening comprehension in Modern Standard Arabic. The instructional materials consist of authentic written, visual and audio materials. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

subject: ARAB
title: Third-Level Arabic II
description: Continuation of third-level Arabic I. Emphasis on developing writing and interaction ability at advanced levels of proficiency. Course includes extensive reading, composition exercises, listening skills, conversation practice and extensive review of Arabic grammar. Developing fluency is the main objective of this course. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

subject: CAM
title: Introductory Khmer I
description: Face to face course aims to develop students’ proficiency in speaking, listening, reading, and writing Khmer at the introductory level, with structural points introduced inductively. Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CAM
title: Introductory Khmer II
description: Continuation of 101. Face to face course continues to develop students’ proficiency in speaking, listening, reading, and writing Khmer at the introductory level, with structural points introduced inductively. Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CAM
title: Conversing in Khmer I
description: Online course aims to develop students’ proficiency in speaking and listening to Khmer at the introductory level for the purpose of communication, travel, and for enjoyment.

subject: CAM
title: Conversing in Khmer II
description: Continuation of 103. Online course continues to develop students’ proficiency in speaking and listening to Khmer at the introductory level for the purpose of communication, travel, and for enjoyment.

subject: CAM
title: Reading/Writing in Khmer I
description: Online course aims to develop proficiency in reading and writing Khmer at the introductory level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement online instruction.

subject: CAM
title: Reading/Writing in Khmer II
description: Continuation of 105. Online course continues to develop proficiency in reading and writing Khmer at the introductory level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement online instruction.

subject: CAM
title: Intermediate Khmer I
description: Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse, and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the intermediate level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement the online instruction.

subject: CAM
title: Intermediate Khmer II
description: Continuation of 201. Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the intermediate level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement the online instruction.

subject: CAM
title: Cambodian Folktales of the Hare I
description: Intermediate level online course familiarizes students with basic language, culture and customs through study of classical Cambodian folktales of the Hare, “Judge Rabbit,” one of the most famous figures in oral folktale stories.

subject: CAM
title: Cambodian Folktales of the Hare II
description: Continuation of 203. Intermediate level online course familiarizes students with basic language, cultures and customs through study of classical Cambodian folktales of the Hare, “Judge Rabbit,” one of the most famous figures in oral folktale stories.

subject: CAM
title: Advanced Khmer I
description: Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the advanced level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement the web-based instruction.

subject: CAM
title: Advanced Khmer II
description: Continuation of 301. Provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the advanced level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and a textbook to complement the online instruction.

subject: CAM
title: Accelerated Third-Level Cambodian
description: Continuation of 212. Practice in idiomatic conversation and extensive reading. Integrated development of listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Meets 10 hours weekly.

subject: CAM
title: Fourth-Level Khmer
description: Continuation of 302. Computer assisted learning. Advanced reading in current literature; discussion of social and cultural issues; advanced conversation and composition.

subject: CAM
title: Fourth-Level Khmer
description: Continuation of 401. Computer assisted learning.

subject: CAM
title: Khmer Language in the Media
description: Focus on advanced reading, writing, aural comprehension and speaking skills through the study of Khmer newspaper, radio, TV, audio/video clips and film.

subject: CHAM
title: Elementary Chamorro
description: Introduction to Chamorro, emphasis on listening and speaking, language structure. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: CHAM
title: Elementary Chamorro
description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills; emphasis on oral and reading proficiency. Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CHAM
title: Intermediate Chamorro
description: Continuation of 102. Emphasis on comprehension and language production (speaking). Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CHAM
title: Intermediate Chamorro
description: Continuation of 201. Emphasis on comprehension and language production.

subject: FIL
title: Beginning Filipino
description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Beginning Filipino
description: Continuation of 101.

subject: FIL
title: Intermediate Filipino
description: Continuation of 102. Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Intermediate Filipino
description: Continuation of 201.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino for Education
description: Continuation of 102. Lessons focus on various aspects of Philippine culture and specialized topics that cater to the needs of teachers intending to teach Filipino immigrant students or teach Filipino as a second language. Meets five hours a week; daily lab work.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino for Education
description: Continuation of 202 or 224.

subject: FIL
title: Third-Level Filipino I
description: Conversation, advanced reading and composition on traditional culture and indigenous knowledge. Includes emphasis on developing oral communication and written skills. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Third-Level Filipino II
description: Conversation, advanced reading, and composition on contemporary issues. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Aural Comprehension
description: Training in comprehension of spoken authentic/ simulated authentic materials presented in news broadcasts, songs, documentary narration, formal lectures, radio and television soap operas, etc.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Film: Art and History
description: Study and analysis of Filipino films: its history, forms, development and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic context.

subject: FIL
title: Fourth-Level Filipino I
description: Advanced reading in traditional literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced oral communication and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Fourth-Level Filipino II
description: Advanced reading in current literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced conversation and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Advanced Filipino Aural Comprehension
description: Continuation of 315. Training in comprehension and analysis/criticism of spoken authentic materials through films.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Translation Techniques
description: Techniques of bilingual translation: Filipino to English and English to Filipino.

subject: FIL
title: Structure of Filipino
description: Introduction to phonology, morphology, syntax.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Contemporary Literature
description: Selected readings in poetry, short stories, and plays from early 1900s to present. Co-curricular cultural activities included.

subject: HNDI
title: Elementary Hindi I
description: Learn to express yourself in Hindi-a language that comes with a beautiful script, ancient philosophy, spicy food, and Bollywood! The course is communicative, creative, flexibly personalized for student interests. No textbook to buy.

subject: HNDI
title: Elementary Hindi II

description: Combined lecture/discussion. Examination of critical political, social, and economic issues in the Pacific Islands region today.

subject: PACS
title: Thinking Through Pacific Arts, Ritual, and Performance
description: Lecture, discussion, and workshop series surveys arts, ritual, and performance practices throughout the Pacific. Engaging with Pacific traditions of thought, and creative approaches to research, students also return findings to Pacific communities.

subject: PACS
title: Islands and Archipelagos
description: Applies an island studies perspective to critically evaluate the commonalities and differences across islands and archipelagos in several world regions. Examines how island geographies influence social identities and movements and are impacted by environmental conditions.

subject: PACS
title: Literature of the Pacific
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of the literature of the Pacific, including Pacific voyagers and contemporary writings in English by Pacific Islanders.
prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: PACS
title: Pacific Islander Collaborative Research
description: Engage in intensive collaborative research with a Pacific Islander community in Hawaiʻi, culminating in a research paper and public presentation. Oral communication is an essential component of this course.

subject: PACS
title: Drama and Theatre of Oceania
description: Survey of the contemporary drama and theatre of Oceania that combines island and Western traditions. Includes Papua New Guinea, Hawai‘i, Fiji, Samoa, Australia, New Zealand.

subject: PACS
title: Studies in Hawaiian and/or Pacific Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, writers, movements, or genres in the field of Pacific literature.
prereq_raw: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course

subject: PACS
title: Moving Images in the Pacific Islands
description: Critically examines indigenous and foreign representations of the Pacific Islands and is designed to make film a central focus of inquiry for students interested in the contemporary Pacific.

subject: PACS
title: Culture and Consumption in Oceania
description: Lecture on changing patterns of consumption in Oceania, and the historical, political, cultural, artistic, and economic forces shaping such practices.

subject: PACS
title: Learning Oceania
description: Graduate seminar. Introduction to the nature and origins of Pacific Studies as an organized field of study. Epistemological, conceptual, political and ethical issues facing students of the region today.

subject: PACS
title: Re/Presenting Oceania: Pacific and American Perspectives
description: Graduate seminar. Critical analysis of the way physical, social and cultural aspects of Oceania have been represented in scholarly and popular media.

subject: PACS
title: Researching Oceania: Creative and Conventional Methods of Inquiry
description: Graduate seminar. Literacy, theory and method in the creation of a Master’s research project.

subject: PACS
title: Women in Oceania
description: Will look at feminist theory, ethnography, culture, activism and globalization in the context of writing, research and film on or by Women in Oceania.

subject: PACS
title: Topics in Histories of Oceania
description: Reading and research on major issues, topics, and themes in the history of Oceania.
prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent. (Cross-listed as HIST 675

subject: PACS
title: Graduate Seminar: Change in the Pacific
description: Interrelationship of change in selected Pacific Islands regions, institutions, and processes.

subject: PACS
title: Master’s Portfolio Project
description: Independent study for students working on MA portfolio projects. A grade of satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.

subject: PAS
title: Overseas Study

title: Introduction to Philosophy: Morals and Society

subject: PHIL
title: Asian Traditions
description: Universal themes and problems from Asian perspective.

description: Universal themes and problems from Asian perspective.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to Philosophy: Environmental Philosophy
description: A critical examination of environmental issues; analyzing the nature of the human being, the nature of nature, and the relationship of the human being to nature.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy Through Computer Science
description: Introduction to classic philosophical issues (e.g., external world skepticism and free will) through computational concepts grounded in an introduction to computer science using Python.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to Deductive Logic
description: Principles of modern deductive logic.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to Deductive Logic
description: Principles of modern deductive logic.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to Inductive Logic
description: Introduction to the theory of arguments based on probabilities and to the theory of decision-making in the context of uncertainty.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to Critical Thinking

subject: PHIL

description: Everyone wants to be happy. What is happiness? How do we become happy? Students examine and practice proposals from ancient philosophy and tragedy and recent psychology about the ingredients, methods, and difficulties of living well.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to World Philosophy I
description: Introduction to philosophy as it has manifested itself differently across cultures throughout the world. Focus on the development of philosophical thought from its beginnings up until 1500 CE.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to World Philosophy II
description: Philosophy attempts to understand the human being and the societies they form. Introduces students to the notion of world philosophy, focusing upon thinkers who have helped to shape our present.

subject: PHIL
title: Ancient Philosophy
description: An introduction to the history of philosophy based on translations of texts originally written in classical Greek or Latin.

subject: PHIL
title: Medieval to Enlightenment Philosophy
description: Introduction to the history of philosophy based on translations of texts originally written by men and women in post-classical Latin and Arabic. Significant attention is paid to developing writing skills.

subject: PHIL
title: Modern Philosophy
description: Introduction to the history of philosophy based on texts or translations of “modern” works, that is works originally written in a modern European language.

subject: PHIL
title: Women Philosophers

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy and Science Fiction
description: Will use important works of science fiction and philosophy to explore philosophical questions, such as the nature of personal identity and the meaning of human life.

subject: PHIL
title: Love and Sex
description: Survey of classical and contemporary perspectives of the philosophy of love, marriage, relationships, sex, sexual identity, representations of sex and sexuality.

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL
title: Political Philosophy

prereq_raw: any course 101 or above in PHIL or above 100 in POLS or SOC, or consent

subject: PHIL
title: Social Philosophy

prereq_raw: any course 101 or above in PHIL or above 100 in POLS or SOC, or consent

subject: PHIL

prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL, or consent

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Religion
description: Problems and methods. Nature of religious experience, alternatives to theism, existence of god, relation between faith and reason, nature of religious language.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Art
description: Problems and methods in aesthetic valuation and in appreciation, creation, and criticism of artworks.

subject: PHIL
title: Theory of Knowledge

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy of Science

prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL, or 200 or above with either DB or DP designation; or consent

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL

prereq_raw: any 101 course or above in PHIL or above 100 in POLS or SOC; or consent. (Once a year)

subject: PHIL

description: Explores the ethical and epistemological implications of the theory of evolution. (Alt. years)

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL

prereq_raw: any 100-level PHIL course or above, or consent

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL

subject: PHIL

subject: REL
