description: Origin and development of early Christian message as set forth in the New Testament; special attention to Jesus and Paul.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Indian Religions
description: Historical survey of the teachings and practices of major religious traditions of India.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Chinese Religions
description: Taoist, Confucian, Buddhist and folk beliefs and practices in their social and historical context.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Japanese Religions
description: Broad survey, with primary focus on Shinto, Buddhist, and modern sectarian movements, analyzed in relation to social and cultural themes of major historical periods.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Hawaiian Religion
description: Major teachings and practices from ancient times to present, their cultural influence; analysis of religious texts; relation to other traditions of Oceania and to Christianity.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Buddhism
description: Survey of major forms and practices.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Judaism
description: Survey from origin to modern times with an emphasis on writing-based analysis of Jewish thought in Talmudic and Medieval Periods.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Islam
description: Historical survey of the beliefs and practices of Islam as a world religion, including the prophet Muhammad, scriptures, philosophy and science, theology, law, major sectarian movements, relations with other religious traditions, and fundamentalism. (Alt. years)

subject: REL
title: Understanding Christianity
description: History of ideas concentrating on events, persons, and issues with the greatest impact on the evolution of Christianity.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Ancient Religions
description: Comparative and historical survey of the religious beliefs and practices in ancient times throughout Egypt, Mesopotamia, Syria-Canaan, Anatolia, Persia, Greece, and Rome.

subject: REL
title: Viking Religion
description: Introduction to the Scandinavian religions in the Viking Age, their depiction in popular culture, and reconstruction in the form of new religious movements.

subject: REL
title: Myth, Religion, and Society
description: Theories and methods used in the study of myth, ritual, and religion. DH

subject: REL
title: Biblical Hebrew I
description: Orthography and structure of Biblical Hebrew, history and development of Hebrew as the sacred language of Judaism, overview of religious and historical development of the Hebrew Bible.

subject: REL
title: Biblical Hebrew II
description: Reading of selected prose passages from the Hebrew Bible; essay-based analysis of literary forms, with attention given both to stories important to the development of the Abrahamic religions and writing-based interpretation of religious traditions.

subject: REL
title: Creation and Evolution
description: An exploration of interactions between science and religion with a focus on cosmogonies.

subject: REL
title: Indigenous & Decolonial Approaches to Religion and Culture
description: Introduction to indigenous and decolonial approaches to the study of religion and culture. Includes a critical assessment of tools and terminology traditionally used in academia.

subject: REL
title: Sacred Animals
description: Critical study of the ethical treatment of nonhuman animals and the religious beliefs and practices associated with them throughout history and across various cultures. Emphasis on teaching oral communication.

subject: REL
title: Zen (Ch’an) Buddhist Masters
description: Study of lives, teachings, practices of Zen masters in China, Japan, Korea, and the West.

subject: REL
title: Global Christianity
description: Christianity as a transcultural religion, through the study of Christian art, literature, ritual, and theology in diverse cultures; including the Near East, Africa, Latin America, and the Pacific.

subject: REL
title: Ka Baibala ‘Ôlelo Hawai‘i (The Bible in Hawaiian)
description: Survey of and selected readings from the Hawaiian Bible (Baibala Hemolele). Conducted in Hawaiian.

subject: REL
title: Cults and New Religions
description: Study of cults and new religious movements in America, the Pacific, and East Asia; examining types, causes, and functions of these movements.

subject: REL
title: Religion and Conflict in American History
description: Analyzes selected historical examples of religious conflicts in America, discerning characteristic patterns of American religious discourse, and identifying the social structures, interests, and ethical principles at stake in conflicts about religion.

subject: REL
title: Religion, Politics, and Society
description: Exploration of the diverse approaches and perspectives that American religious groups embrace in addressing controversial and diverse issues of contemporary American life. Emphasis on considering and discussing ethical approaches and practicing oral communication. DH

subject: REL
title: Christian Ethics in Modern Life
description: The meaning of Christian faith for the moral life with reference to contemporary moral issues.

subject: REL
title: Sufism: Mystical Traditions of Islam
description: Introduction to the history, literature, and worldview of Sufism. Students will encounter the following topics in relation to Islamic mysticism: asceticism, monotheism, philosophy, love, union, sainthood, ecstatic experience, and spiritual uses of art.
prereq_raw: 209 or 383 or PHIL 330 or HIST 354, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: REL
title: Witches and Witchcraft
description: Persecution of witches, witchcraft in Europe, 1300–1700, examined as crisis of church and theology; origins, effects on church and society.
prereq_raw: one of 201, HIST 151, HIST 152, PSY 100, or consent

subject: REL
title: Islam in History
description: Examination of the historical connections between Islam and other civilizations will focus on the role of Islam in world history.

subject: REL
title: Women and Religion
description: Examining roles of, and attitudes toward, women in major religious traditions through autobiographies, films, and primary texts.
prereq_raw: 149 or WGSS 149 or REL 150 or HIST 151 or WGSS 151

subject: REL
title: Love, Sex, and Religion
description: Love and sex as themes in religions of Asia and the West.

subject: REL
title: Religion and Art
description: The uses of art in religion are studied with historical examples.

subject: REL
title: Prophecies of the Last Days
description: In-depth look at ancient Judeo-Christian apocalyptic texts and the communities in which they originated, followed by a survey of the medieval and modern day heirs of apocalyptic traditions.

subject: REL
title: Vedic Hindu Mythology
description: Study of major Hindu myths of the Vedic Sanskrit literature within the perspective of ancient Indian civilization. Literary sources will be tapped for understanding creation, cosmogony and celestial, atmospheric and terrestrial divinities. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: REL
title: Classical Hindu Mythology
description: Study of major myths of Epic Sanskrit literature, primarily with focus of the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Literary sources will be tapped for appreciating myths and epics, especially with reference to dharma, karma, ways of life. Sophomore standing or consent.

subject: REL
title: Mysticism East and West
description: Mystic traditions of the West from desert monasticism to Renaissance mystics compared with those of South and East Asia. Focuses on the ethical lives of these mystics, and developing oral communication skills.

subject: REL
title: Hawaiian Gods
description: The traditions and practices related to one or more major indigenous gods, or class of gods, will be studied by the interpretation and analysis of primary texts. Develops written communication skills.

subject: REL
title: On Death and Dying
description: Aspects of death and dying; relation to our culture and society, to understanding of each other and of ourselves.

subject: REL
title: Life and Teachings of Jesus
description: Critical study of synoptic gospels and of extra-Biblical sources.

subject: REL
title: Anthropology of Magic, Witchcraft, and Religion
description: Cults, legends, millennial movements, myths, possession, rituals, sacred healing, shamanism, sorcery, spirits, symbolism, witchcraft, and other forms of religious and symbolic expression and experience, from small scale to highly urban societies.

subject: REL
title: Health/Medicine in Religion
description: Issues of health and disease in the light of religious beliefs and practices with a focus on ethical matters shaping policies in the U.S. and the world.

subject: REL
title: Religion and Food
description: Writing-based seminar exploring foodways as a basic component in the practice of religions. Examines theoretical issues, foodways as creators of community and identity, sustainability, and other ethical issues, abstinence and fasting, and healing.

subject: REL
title: Anthropology of Buddhism
description: Selected aspects of national, regional and local manifestations of Buddhism are explored through the perspective of anthropology with an emphasis on the daily lives of monks, nuns and lay persons in their socio-cultural contexts.

subject: REL
title: Spiritual Ecology
description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of the relationships between religions, environment and environmentalism. Junior standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Sacred Places
description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of sites which societies recognize as sacred and their cultural, ecological and conservation aspects. Junior standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Sociology of Religion
description: Seminar on research in sociological aspects of religious sectarianism, historical and current; special reference to Hawai‘i.

subject: REL
title: Seminar on Buddhism
description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Buddhism; topics and geographical focus to be announced each semester.

subject: REL
title: Daoism: Philosophy and Religion
description: Seminar on religious Taoism, its historical development and its role in the present-day context.

subject: REL

description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites.

subject: REL
title: Field Methods in Religion

subject: REL
title: Buddhism in Japan

subject: REL
title: Polynesian Religions

description: Application of principles, procedures and techniques of organizing a small retail business in a brick-and-click world. Students develop, write, and evaluate business plans creatively using low and high tech resources and oral communication skills. Junior standing or higher. FDM majors only; open to non-majors with instructor’s consent.
prereq_raw: one FS or FQ course, or consent

subject: FDM
title: Costume Museum Management
description: Investigation of skills and techniques needed for handling textile and apparel artifacts in museums and other collections. Active involvement in documenting, researching, interpreting, and exhibiting costumes and textiles. Involves written work and oral presentations.

subject: FDM
title: International Apparel Trade Issues
description: Theories, concepts, problems of international trade of textile and apparel products. Issues of importing and exporting apparel products globally. Social, economic, and ethical factors affecting textile and apparel trade.

subject: FDM
title: Topics in Fashion
description: Study and discussion of special topics, problems. Offered by staff and visiting faculty.

subject: FDM
title: Internship
description: Examination of issues and opportunities associated with careers in fashion and related businesses and industries. Topics include interpersonal skills development, job search and interview strategies, and ethical issues in the workplace. Junior standing or higher.

subject: FDM
title: Capstone Portfolio
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Includes extensive instruction in writing and communication.

subject: FDM
title: Field Study in the Fashion Industry
description: Study tours to various centers of the world to examine historical and modern apparel and textiles. Merchandising and design methods and operations examined.

subject: HDFS
title: Human Development
description: Concepts, issues, theories of human growth and development from conception to death; systems approaches to inquiry into factors affecting growth and development.

subject: HDFS
title: Infancy and Early Childhood
description: Growth and development from prenatal period to age 5. Historical and current issues and research based on ecological, cross-cultural perspective. Focus on optimal development.

subject: HDFS
title: Childhood
description: Intensive investigation into developmental aspects of 6–12 year old children. Historical and current issues, research, and examination of the role of schools and other community resources. Focus on optimal development.

subject: HDFS
title: Adolescence and Early Adulthood
description: Problems, concepts, and research related to development from puberty through early adulthood. Examination of biological, cognitive, social, and cultural factors affecting the individual.

subject: HDFS
title: Middle Age and Aging
description: Change and continuity in midlife and late life from theoretical and applied perspectives. Written assignments communicate information about physical and psychological age-related events, as well as social attitudes, values, to scholarly and community audiences.

subject: HDFS
title: Intimacy, Marriages and Families
description: Study of intimate relationships, marriages and families, their dynamics, strengths, growth and development, challenges, choices and opportunities, in the context of social change and cultural diversity.
prereq_raw: 230 or PSY 100 or SOC 100; or consent

subject: HDFS
title: Parenting
description: Parenting theories, methods, skills, issues, and resources; parent-child relations in various cultural contexts.

subject: HDFS
title: Leadership and Group Process
description: Exploration of leadership research and theories and their application to leadership development; designed to enhance personal and interactive leadership.

subject: HDFS
title: Community Needs and Resources
description: Theory and practice in determining community needs and resources; community resources development based on needs identification.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Resource Management
description: Concepts, principles, and practices in managing family and household resources.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Financial Planning
description: Analytical approach to family financial planning from the perspective of changing family demands over the life cycle.
prereq_raw: 360 or an ECON course, or consent

subject: HDFS
title: Consumer Economics
description: Consumer rights, responsibilities, and resources; consumer decision-making; factors affecting consumer functioning within economy.
prereq_raw: 360 or an ECON course, or consent

subject: HDFS
title: Soft Skills for Success in the Workplace
description: Employers regard soft skills as key criteria when hiring and retaining employees. Students learn critical skills essential to work place success. This class prepares students to be work ready.

subject: HDFS
title: Research Methodology
description: Fundamental scientific methodology, design and data collection; introduction to statistics and program evaluations, analysis of ethical issues. FDM, HDFS, or TPSS majors only.
prereq_raw: 230 or FDM 200 or TPSS 200/SUST 211, or consent

subject: HDFS
title: Research Methodology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Test design, computer use, data analysis. FDM, HDFS, or TPSS majors only.

subject: HDFS
title: Partnerships with Families and Professionals
description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, prepares students for direct, educational work with parents and children and for continued graduate work in child and family studies, counseling, psychology, social work and/or family life education.

subject: HDFS
title: Mindfulness and Skillful Living
description: Lecture, discussion, and experiential activities of principles and practice of an evidence-based contemplative science discipline. Focuses on development of writing skills and ethical applications to daily life, with implications for youth, families, and society.
prereq_raw: completed DS course (with a minimum grade of C)

children.text: completed DS course ( with a minimum grade of C

subject: HDFS
title: Marriage Development
description: Marital interaction and development; divorce and remarriage; resources and techniques for marital adjustment, enrichment, and growth.

subject: HDFS
title: Contemporary Family Issues
description: Investigation of current issues with impact upon family quality of life, with emphasis on the interdependent nature of families and their environments.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Life Education Methodology
description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, with service learning on Family Life Education Methodology.

subject: HDFS
title: Community Program Development
description: Concepts and theories of community program development; principles, practices, and procedures in administration and supervision of volunteer services surveyed and analyzed.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Public Policy
description: Cross-national survey of family public policy; analysis, revision, and development of family public policy; impacts of policy on consumers and families.

subject: HDFS
title: Consumer Communications
description: Development, production, analysis, and evaluation of consumer materials for print media. Use of desktop publishing computer programs.
prereq_raw: 360 or an ECON course, or consent

subject: HDFS
title: Family Economics
description: Study of personal family resources and its interaction with the economy. Focuses on contemporary economic problems that affect the welfare of families.
prereq_raw: 360 or an ECON course, or consent

subject: HDFS
title: Topics in Family Resources
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

subject: HDFS
title: Internship
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills in supervised work at an approved internship site and through analytical writing assignments and class discussions.
prereq_raw: (230, 340, 360, 380, and 380L) with a minimum grade of C

subject: HDFS
title: Capstone Portfolio
description: Preparation of a senior portfolio to be used as assessment of competence relative to national FCS standards. Includes extensive instruction on writing.
prereq_raw: (230, 340, 360, 380, 380L, and 492 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C

subject: HDFS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Independent reading and research on a topic, done under supervision of a faculty member; outcomes contracted in writing with faculty member at beginning of semester.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times or up to nine credits

subject: ANSC
title: Humans, Animals, and Agriculture
description: Introduction to animal agriculture, animal science, and the use of animals by humans. Ethics and importance of human use of animals in agriculture are emphasized.

subject: ANSC
title: Principles and Practices of Animal Science
description: Biology, behavior, and management of animals of economic and social importance. Topics include physiology, genetics, nutrition, reproduction, behavior, care, and management to achieve productivity, performance, and welfare. (lecture, discussion, and field trips)

subject: ANSC
title: Comparative Nutrition
description: Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors.
prereq_raw: (200 (or concurrent), CHEM 161/161L or higher) with a minimum grade of C.  DB

subject: ANSC
title: Anatomy of Domestic Animals
description: Micro and gross anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals.
prereq_raw: 200 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C

subject: ANSC
title: Domestic Animal Anatomy Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany 301, with an emphasis on teaching scientific and technical writing. Dissection and identification of anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals.
prereq_raw: 200 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C

subject: ANSC
title: Applied Animal Nutrition
description: Application of the principles of nutrition to feeding of farm animals; composition and nutritional value of feed stuffs; nutritional requirements of beef cattle, dairy cattle, horses, poultry, and swine.
prereq_raw: (201 (or concurrent), and 244 or FSHN 244) with a minimum grade of C

subject: ANSC
title: Humans, Food, and Animals: Ethics, Issues, and Controversies
description: Ethical issues and other controversies related to human and animal needs; their impact on resource sustainability and quality of life are explored from scientific perspectives.

subject: ANSC
title: Horses and Horsemanship
description: Origin of species, breeds, nutrition, care, management. Lab on management practices with work on light horses.

subject: ANSC
title: Laboratory Skills in Animal Science
description: Provides students with basic and essential laboratory skills required in various fields of animal science such as nutrition, genetics, reproductive physiology, meat science, clinical pathology, parasitology, and animal handling.
prereq_raw: (200 or 201, and BIOL 171 and 171L and CHEM 161) with a minimum grade of D-

subject: ANSC
title: Poultry Production
description: Students will learn about poultry health and hygiene, husbandry, production, biosecurity, hands-on skills, and recent advances in poultry farming systems for meat and egg production. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANSC
title: Beef Production
description: Principles of economic beef production, including beef breeds, selection, breeding, management systems, feeding, and marketing under tropical conditions.

subject: ANSC
title: Swine Production
description: Principles of efficient pork production, including comparative breed evaluation, breeding, feeding, management, marketing, and business aspects. Problems and practices associated with tropical environment emphasized.

subject: ANSC
title: Tropical Dairying
description: Principles involved in economical milk production in the tropics, including management, recordkeeping, breeds, breeding, selection, culling, feeding, housing, milking, quality control, and raising young animals.

subject: ANSC
title: Genetics and Animal Breeding
description: Review and application of genetic principles to livestock, poultry, companion, aquatic, and laboratory research animals. Current practices and future developments.
prereq_raw: (BIOL 171/171L or ZOOL 101/101L, and MATH 140X or higher) with a minimum grade of C. Recommended: biochemistry and genetics or equivalent

children.text: Recommended: biochemistry and genetics or equivalent

subject: ANSC
title: Genes and Animal Biology
description: An understanding of animal biology at the level of genes and their regulations; emphasis on gene structure, recombinant DNA, transgenic animals and functional genomics being used for agricultural, nutritional and biomedical sciences. Open to nonmajors.
prereq_raw: (301, BIOL 171 or ZOOL 101) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: ANSC
title: Aquaculture Production
description: Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery.
prereq_raw: 321 and 445: or BIOL 172/L and CHEM 162/L or higher

children.text: : or BIOL 172 / L and CHEM 162 / L or higher

subject: ANSC
title: Physiology of Domestic Animals
description: Functions and relationships of organs and organ systems of domestic animals excluding reproduction and lactation. Problem-based learning and case studies are emphasized.
prereq_raw: 301 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent

subject: ANSC
title: Animal Diseases and Their Control
description: Disease problems of livestock, poultry, and companion animals; their economic significance, causes, public health implications, and control.

subject: ANSC
title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology
description: Development, growth, function, carcass evaluation of muscle tissue.

subject: ANSC
title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Livestock and poultry slaughter, carcass evaluation, meat chemistry, muscle physiology and biochemistry, meat microbiology, and meat processing.

subject: ANSC
title: Companion Animals and Society
description: Explore human and companion animal relationships in biological, social, cultural, economic, legal, health, and welfare contexts to prepare students for careers in the various animal-related fields in Hawai‘i, the Pacific rim, and worldwide. Sophomore standing or higher.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (with a minimum grade of C), or consent

subject: ANSC
title: Biology and Culture of Shrimp and Prawns
description: Aspects of the biology and culture of the freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii and marine shrimp Penaeus (sp) species. Scientific research results and case studies presented and analyzed.

subject: ANSC
title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination
description: Introductory exploration of anatomy, development, and physiology of reproduction of domestic animals and artificial insemination.

subject: ANSC
title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination Lab
description: Reproductive anatomy and physiology of domestic animals, estorus synchronization, breeding soundness, and artificial insemination laboratory, field trips. One week offisland field trip. ANSC majors or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Aquaculture Production Laboratory
description: Intensive, hands-on course involving the culture of larvae and juveniles of marine shrimp, freshwater prawns, molluscs, fish, and their food. Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing and flexible time for continuous live animal care. Lab fee required.

subject: ANSC
title: Comparative Endocrinology
description: Structure and function of endocrine systems across vertebrate groups, surveying how hormones mediate adaptive responses to dynamic environments and coordinate key aspects of growth, development, metabolism, osmoregulation, and stress.

subject: ANSC
title: Aquaculture Business Planning and Entrepreneurship
description: Practical aspects of planning and developing an aquaculture business from conceptualization to a final business plan. Topics include species/technology, project planning, business structuring, permitting, contracts, production plans, financial planning and analysis, market/competition analysis, capital acquisition, intellectual property and legal issues.
prereq_raw: 450 or OCN 450. Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing aquaculture animals and flexible time for live animal care

children.text: Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing aquaculture animals and flexible time for live animal care

subject: ANSC
title: Topics in Animal Sciences
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable five times, up to 18 credits

subject: ANSC
title: Field Experience
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report.

subject: ANSC
title: Directed Study or Research
description: Limited to exceptional undergraduate students, generally with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major. Exceptions may be granted for students with high achievement in last three semesters.

subject: ANSC
title: The Science of Food Systems
description: (1 50-min Lec, 1 2-hr Discussion) Discussion of food systems as they apply to animal science, food science, and human nutrition.

subject: ANSC
title: Experimental Design
description: Design of experiments and variance analyses in biological and agricultural research.
prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent. Recommended: ZOOL 632

subject: ANSC
title: Seminar in Animal Sciences
description: Topics of current interest and current research related to nutrition, genetics, and physiology.

subject: ANSC
title: Advanced Animal Nutrition
description: An advanced course in the nutrition of mono-gastric, ruminant, avian, and aquatic species. Topics include digestive system structures, utilization of nutrients, energy metabolism, and experimental techniques used in the study of animal nutrition.

subject: ANSC
title: Physiology of Reproduction
description: Comparative differentiation, development, growth, and function of the reproductive systems of mammals and birds; external factors that influence response; artificial insemination.

subject: ANSC
title: Growth Biology of Meat Animals
description: Growth and development of meat-producing animals; skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and bone; protein turnover, lipid metabolism, and bioenergetics; regulation of animal growth.

subject: ANSC
title: DNA and Genetic Analysis
description: Combined lecture-lab for students interested in genetic analysis of humans, animals, and other species. Molecular techniques, such as PCR, DNA marker identifications, transgenics, expression analysis and functional genomics, are included. Open to nonmajors.

subject: ANSC
title: Information Research Skills
description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

subject: ANSC
title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review. Open to CTAHR graduate students only; others with consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Advanced Topics in Animal Sciences
description: Advanced topics in animal sciences, from basic to applied research, including current issues and critical analysis of current research literature. Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to nine credits

subject: ANSC
title: Advanced Laboratory Techniques
description: Advanced laboratory techniques used in food science and human nutrition research.
prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent and MBBE 402/402L, and FSHN 477; or BIOC 441

subject: ANSC
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Plan B students work with their advisor to select, revise, and defend before a three-person faculty committee a report of work the student has produced in the project. Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, credit earned up to 9 credits

subject: FSHN
title: Food Service Safety and Sanitation
description: Principles and procedures of sanitation and safety in the food service industry, including the study of foodborne illnesses, biological, chemical, physical hazards and cross-contamination as they may occur during the flow of food.

subject: FSHN
title: Culture and Cuisine: The Global Diversity of Food
description: A timeline of the world history of food and how it relates to culture, diversity, ethnicity, and religion. International food demonstrations and tastings included.

subject: FSHN
title: Introduction to Food Preparation
description: Lectures, discussions, and demonstrations on how food components contribute to the functional, sensory, and safety characteristics of foods, and what changes occur in foods due to preparation, processing, and storage.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Preparation Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments in foods emphasizing ingredient function and standard preparation methods for food groups.

subject: FSHN
title: The Science of Human Nutrition
description: Integration of natural science concepts basic to the study of human nutrition. Emphasis on nutrient requirements of healthy individuals, food sources, functions of nutrients.

subject: FSHN
title: Comparative Nutrition
description: Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors.
prereq_raw: (ANSC 200 (or concurrent), CHEM 161/161L or higher) with a minimum grade of C

subject: FSHN
title: Food Service Systems Management
description: Critical and essential aspects of management and effective leadership practices to direct and delivery quality foodservices. Focus on the role and competencies of the Registered Dietitian (RD) working in these environments.
prereq_raw: (181 and 181L (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Food Service Production and Operations
description: Principles and procedures of menu planning, quantity food production, production scheduling, recipe adaptation, equipment operation, and formula costing. Principles of procurement including purchasing, selection, storage of equipment and quantity foods.
prereq_raw: (181 and 181L) with a minimum grade of C, or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Marketing Nutrition and Food
description: Fundamental marketing principles applied to nutrition and food. Will include concepts such as the psychology of food purchasing decisions and consumer behavior. Field trips and group projects included. Open to non-majors.

subject: FSHN
title: Humans, Food, and Animals: Ethics, Issues, and Controversies
description: Ethical issues and other controversies related to human and animal needs; their impact on resource sustainability and quality of life are explored from scientific perspectives.

subject: FSHN
title: Applied Professional Skills in Nutrition
description: Will apply skills in technology, research, and career development to nutrition. Students will identify evidence-based nutrition information and demonstrate their academic skill sets for future professional success through technology.

subject: FSHN
title: Lifespan Nutrition
description: Physiological changes and nutritional requirements during human life stages: prepregnancy, pregnancy, infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: B or better in 185; C or better in CHEM 161/161L; C or better in PHYL 142/142L (or concurrent)

subject: FSHN
title: Experimental Foods
description: Experimental approach to study food preparation problems. Applying basic food science research design to conduct experiments, interpret data and write reports. Subject matter used to practice critical thinking and problem solving skills.
prereq_raw: (181/181L, CHEM 161/161L) with a minimum grade of C

subject: FSHN
title: Experimental Foods Laboratory
description: Experimental approach to study food preparation, food formulation, and sensory evaluation with laboratory exercises in a certified kitchen environment. Applying basic food science research design to conduct experiments, interpret data and write reports.
prereq_raw: (181/181L, CHEM 161/161L) with a minimum grade of D

subject: FSHN
title: Nutritional Assessment
description: Addresses concepts and uses of nutrition assessment tools at individual and community levels. Students will be introduced to national surveys and new, more sophisticated body composition measurements. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: (185 and 370 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C

subject: FSHN
title: Microbiology of Foods
description: Microorganisms encountered in foods; types of food spoilage; microbial hazards in food; methods of food preservation.
prereq_raw: (MICR 130 and MICR 140L, or MICR 351 and MICR 351L) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Food Engineering
description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation.
prereq_raw: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A, MATH 243 or MATH 253A, PHYS 151 or PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C; or consent. (Once a year)

subject: FSHN
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
prereq_raw: (ECE 160, ECE 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Food Chemistry
description: Chemical properties of food constituents studied in relationship to their effects on processing, nutrition, and spoilage.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Chemistry Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Application of different chemical methods in the study of food constituents—proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, pigments, enzymes, etc.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Safety
description: Discussion of potential microbiological, parasitic, chemical, and natural food hazards; food laws and standards; and related aspects of consumer protection.
prereq_raw: (181, BIOL 171, and CHEM 272) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Food Quality Control
description: Fundamental principles of quality control in the food industry: measurement of quality parameters, utilization and integration of the individual test procedures into grades and standards of quality, sampling, and reporting results.

subject: FSHN
title: Community Nutrition and Nutrition Education
description: Concepts and methods of nutrition program planning and nutrition education; analysis of nutritional problems of local, national, and international communities; strategies used to educate groups or individuals.
prereq_raw: (370 and either HDFS 380 or NREM 310) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Foundation of Childhood Obesity Prevention in the Pacific
description: Provide students with a basic overview of the causes and effects of childhood obesity, evidence-based approaches, community-based research, and policies to prevent childhood obesity as it relates to the Pacific region.

subject: FSHN
title: Childhood Anthropometric and Dietary Assessment Field Techniques
description: Teaches techniques for measuring anthropometry and collecting dietary intake in children. Online course imitates hands-on training through partnering with local organizations and the use of technology.

subject: FSHN
title: Child Health and Nutrition Monotiring
description: Covers topics related to health and nutritional status monitoring and surveillance, including epidemiology, biostatistics, health and nutrition surveillance systems, and the uses of technology for conducting these activities.

subject: FSHN
title: Culture and Child Health in the Pacific
description: In-depth study of Pacific culture, land, people, and history and its relationship to child health. Explores cultural competency, cultural safety, and multidisciplinary approaches to promote a healthy Pacific. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Processing Operations
description: Principles and applications of food dehydration, thermal processing, low temperature preservation, chemical and biochemical preservation, irradiation, packaging, manufacturing, plant sanitation, water and waste management.

subject: FSHN
title: Medical Nutrition Therapy I
description: Development of dietary, anthropometric and clinical lab assessment skills measuring nutritional status. Understanding pathophysiology of disease processes, medical terminology and nutritional intervention, utilizing case studies.
prereq_raw: (389 and 486) with a minimum grade of C or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II
description: Understanding of the pathophysiology of disease processes and nutritional intervention, using medical terminology and case studies.
prereq_raw: 467 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Nutrition Counseling Skills
description: Theory and practice in nutritional counseling. Combined lecture and discussion on nutrition/dietary counseling. Knowledge and theories. Application through lab experiences including role playing, case presentations, and performing actual counseling sessions.

subject: FSHN
title: Applied Human Nutrition
description: Application of basic nutrition principles; includes sources and functions of essential nutrients and food patterns compatible with nutrient needs, health, disease prevention, and sustainability. Intended for undergraduate and graduate students.
prereq_raw: CHEM 161 (or higher) or BIOC 241 (or higher); PHYL 141, BIOL 171; or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Cultural Aspects of Food Habits
description: Study of eating from behavioral perspectives. Implications for health practitioners and health education.
prereq_raw: two classes from ANTH 151 or higher or SOC 100 or higher or PSY 100 or higher

children.text: two classes from ANTH 151 or higher

subject: FSHN
title: Food Analysis
description: Principles of sample preparation and chemical and physical analysis of food components using current methodology.
prereq_raw: 430; and CHEM 162 or higher; and BIOL 402 or MBBE 402 or PEPS 402

subject: FSHN
title: Food Analysis Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Application of different chemical and physical methods for the identification and quantitation of food components.

subject: FSHN
title: Nutrition in Exercise and Sport
description: Effects of physiologic demands of exercise on nutrition. Emphasis on physiologic and biochemical basis for nutrition recommendations to enhance exercise participation and optimize athletic performance.
prereq_raw: (185, and PHYL 103 or 141 or 301) with a minimum grade of C

subject: FSHN
title: Nutritional Biochemistry I
description: Metabolism and biochemistry of carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins, including chemical structure, digestion, absorption, transport, cellular/molecular functions in human nutrition; integration of metabolic pathways; energy metabolism and balance, including relevance to chronic disease.
prereq_raw: 185; PHYL 142/142L or PHYL 302/302L; BIOC 341 or higher (or concurrent) or MBBE 402 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Nutritional Biochemistry II
description: Metabolism and biochemistry of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber, including chemical structure, digestion, absorption, transport, and cellular/ molecular functions in human nutrition; relevance to establishing nutrient requirements and to mechanisms of chronic disease.
prereq_raw: 485 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Obesity, Science, and Issues
description: In-depth study of obesity, including research, etiology, treatment, and prevention.
prereq_raw: 485 with a minimum grade of C

subject: FSHN
title: Topics in Food Science and Human Nutrition
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems, or laboratory experiments.

subject: FSHN
title: Field Experience
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Science Capstone
description: Field practicum designed to integrate knowledge from previous FSHN courses to develop novel and innovative food products. Students deal with shelflife, marketing, packaging, labeling, sensory evaluation, and quality assurance.
prereq_raw: (381 and 460) with a minimum grade of C, or consent

subject: FSHN
title: The Science of Food Systems
description: (1 50-min Lec, 1 2-hr discussion) Discussion of food systems as they apply to animal science, food science, and human nutrition.

subject: FSHN
title: Advanced Food Science I
description: Advanced topics in chemical and physical characteristics of foods as well as their role in human nutrition.
prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological science, physics, and biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected; or consent

children.text: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological science, physics,
biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected;

subject: FSHN
title: Advanced Food Science II
description: Advances in sensory quality and evaluation, deterioration of foods and food safety, as well as food processing technology.
prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological sciences, physics, and biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected; or consent

children.text: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological sciences, physics,
biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected;

subject: FSHN
title: Advanced Food Safety
description: Real and perceived food hazards, their ethical issues and implications, advanced emerging topics in food safety, and controls, including laws and regulations of food safety issues and public perception of food safety will be discussed.
prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in biochemistry, microbiology, food processing, physics and organic chemistry. Basic food science knowledge is required; or consent

subject: FSHN
title: International Nutrition
description: Analysis of major nutrition problems in developing countries. Comparative review of the design, implementation, and evaluation of programs to intervene in the development of malnutrition.
