title: DNA and Genetic Analysis
description: Combined lecture-lab for students interested in genetic analysis of humans, animals, and other species. Molecular techniques, such as PCR, DNA marker identifications, transgenics, expression analysis and functional genomics, are included. Open to nonmajors.

subject: FSHN
title: Information Research Skills
description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

subject: FSHN
title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review. Open to CTAHR graduate students only; others with consent.

subject: FSHN
title: Dietetics Supervised Practice
description: ISPP activities and assignments completed at designed facilities in community, clinical, food service, and other settings that stress planning, delivery, and evaluation of dietetics services to individuals and populations. MS Nutritional Sciences students only. Graduate students only.
prereq_raw: admission to the Individualized Supervised Practice Pathway program and consent

children.text: admission to the Individualized Supervised Practice Pathway program

subject: FSHN
title: Advanced Topics in Dietetics
description: Advanced topics in professional dietetics practice. Students will further their knowledge and skills in professional practice areas of dietetics; including clinical, community, and food systems management. MS Nutritional Sciences students only.

subject: FSHN
title: Seminar in Food and Nutritional Sciences
description: Student presentation of literature reviews and research.

subject: FSHN
title: Topics in Nutritional Sciences
description: Advanced topics in nutritional sciences, from basic to applied research, including current issues in nutrition and critical analysis of current research literature.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits

subject: FSHN
title: Global Nutrition
description: Examination of global food and nutrition problems, programs, issues, policies, and strategies for improvement.

subject: FSHN
title: Supplemental and Nutritional Approaches in Disease Prevention and Treatment
description: Examines a variety of issues associated with nutritional and supplemental approaches to reduce disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies.

subject: FSHN
title: Nutrition and Disease: Cellular and Molecular Aspects
description: In-depth lecture, discussion, and student presentations on selected topics relating nutrition to the etiology and prevention of chronic diseases at the cellular and molecular level.
prereq_raw: (485 and 486) with a minimum grade of C; statistics; or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Advanced Child and Adolescent Nutrition
description: Addresses nutrition, growth, and development in children and adolescents and nutrition-related issues, such as childhood obesity and chronic disease risk factors, with a focus on current research in the Pacific region.

subject: FSHN
title: Advanced Lab Techniques
description: Advanced laboratory techniques used in food science and human nutrition research.
prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent and 477 and MBBE 402/402L; or BIOC 441

subject: FSHN
title: Indigenous Peoples’ Food Systems, Environment and Health
description: Explores Indigenous Peoples’ food systems as local food resources Indigenous People acquire through specific cultural knowledge of traditional territories. Global forces transforming these food systems and their impact on population health and nutrition are explored. Graduate students only.

subject: FSHN
title: Nutritional Epidemiology
description: Dietary, biochemical, anthropometric and clinical methods used for evaluating nutrition and diet in the etiology and epidemiology of disease.

subject: FSHN
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B Master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.

subject: FSHN
title: Topics in Food Science
description: Advanced topics in food science and technology, from basic to applied research, including current issues in food science and technology and critical analysis of current research literature.

subject: FSHN
title: Epidemiology of Diabetes and Obesity
description: Provides an overview of the epidemiology and prevention of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and associated complications. Discusses methodological issues associated with evaluating these in epidemiologic studies.
prereq_raw: 663 (with a minimum grade of B-) or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Dietary Fiber, Bioactive Food Components and Health
description: Lecture/discussion of current research on gut physiology, gut microbes, dietary fiber, bioactive food components, and their impact on health, including colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, heart disease, diabetes, and immune function.
prereq_raw: 485 and 486 (or equivalent), statistics, physiology; or consent

children.text: ( or equivalent), statistics, physiology; or consent

subject: FSHN
title: Diet and Cancer Seminar
description: Presentation-discussion of selected research topics in the field of diet-cancer relationships including: nutritional epidemiology of cancer, diet and supplement intervention trials, and cellular/molecular effects of diet on cancer pathophysiology.

subject: FSHN
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation in nutrition. Graduate standing only. Satisfactory/ Unsatisfactory only.

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Sustainable Engineering
description: Sustainability and its social and technical significance; global population growth; resource management and quantification; designs for sustainable society; challenges interfacing technology and culture/religion; green and ecological engineering; life cycle analyses; engineering ethics; selected case studies.

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Quantitative Biology
description: Quantitative approach to applied topics in biology including synthesis and metabolism, kinetics, physiological systems, cellular processes and signaling, informatics, and emerging technologies for health, biological production/processing, and discovery.
prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) and CHEM 162 (or concurrent), or consent. (Once a year)

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Biological Engineering
description: Discussion and experimental investigation of physical and chemical principles underlying representative biological processes and systems. Bioproduction, energy conversion processes, physiological systems, biological treatment, biosensors, biomechanics, and related natural and engineered systems.

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Applications in Biological Engineering
description: Discussion and investigation of special topics, problems and applications of biological engineering.

subject: BE
title: Mass and Energy Balances
description: Introduction of the principles of mass and energy conservation; development of systematic approaches to apply these principles in calculations for design and analysis of biochemical, chemical, and physical processes.
prereq_raw: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or 171 or 181A, PHYS 170, and MATH 242 or 252A) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent

subject: BE
title: Dynamic Systems Modeling
description: Introduction to analytical and numerical solutions for systems of differential equations. Modeling and computer simulation of representative dynamic systems encountered in biological engineering.
prereq_raw: (260, ECE 110 or 160, MATH 243 or 253A, CEE 270) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent

subject: BE
title: Dynamic Systems Modeling Laboratory
description: Industry field trips and lab experiences to illustrate behavior of representative dynamic systems in biological engineering. Data acquisition and model validation.

subject: BE
title: Transport Phenomena
description: Fundamental principles and applications relating to mass, momentum, and energy transfers in biosystems and other systems for engineers and scientists.

subject: BE
title: Engineering Economics
description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decision-making, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 (with a minimum grade of C-) or 130 (with a minimum grade of C-), and senior standing
restrictions_raw: BENG, CE, CEM, CNST, ECE, and ME majors only.

subject: BE
title: Biomass Conversion to Biofuels and Bioenergy
description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production; fundamental concepts in biofuel/ bioenergy production; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel/bioenergy; biodiesel production; environmental impacts, economics and life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies.
prereq_raw: 373 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent. (Once a year)

subject: BE
title: Food Engineering
description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation.
prereq_raw: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A, MATH 243 or MATH 253A, PHYS 151 or PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C; or consent. (Once a year)

subject: BE
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
prereq_raw: (ECE 160, ECE 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: BE
title: Environmental Biotechnology
description: Environmental impact and control; the microorganism and its nutrition and growth conditions; microbial growth and substrate removal kinetics; bioreactors; biological treatment systems; biodegredation of xenobiotic organic chemicals; case studies.

subject: BE
title: Biosystems Unit Operations
description: Introduction to unit operations in biological, environmental, food, and manufacturing processes. Integration of biology and chemistry into engineering using basic concepts in mass and energy conservation and transport in reacting and non-reacting systems.
prereq_raw: (373; and either CEE 320 or ME 322) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent

subject: BE
title: Bioremediation: Principles and Practices
description: Soil environment, fate and transport of contaminants; microbial ecology, metabolism, and energy production; biodegradation of selected compounds. In situ treatment, solid-phase bioremediation, slurry-phase bioremediation, and vapor-phase biological treatment. Open to nonmajors.

subject: BE
title: Bioreactor Design and Analysis
description: Application of mass/energy balances and reaction kinetics for the design and analysis of bioreactors for microbial, plant, and animal cell cultures.
prereq_raw: 373 or CEE 320 or ME 322; or consent

subject: BE
title: Bioprocess Design and Analysis
description: Combined lecture/computer lab on theory and practice of bioprocess design and analysis, involving biological basics and engineering principles of bioprocessing, computer-aided unit operations, process integration, and economic evaluation.
prereq_raw: 373, or 437 (or concurrent) or 460 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: BE
title: Senior Engineering Design I
description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) First course in a two-semester major open-ended design experience for senior students in biological engineering, with heavy emphasis on teaching written/oral engineering communication. Design process; project management; methodology; modeling; optimization; engineering economics.
prereq_raw: (350/350L, 373, CEE 320 (or concurrent) or ME 322 (or concurrent), ME 311, ECE 211) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent

subject: BE
title: Senior Engineering Design II
description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Continuation of 481 with emphasis on written/oral communication and engineering ethics. Properties of biological materials; risk and reliability; guest lectures on design by engineers; project completion with submission of a final design report.
prereq_raw: 481 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent

subject: BE
title: Biological Engineering Topics
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

subject: BE
title: Internship
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer.

subject: BE
title: Directed Research
description: Research in the area of biosystems engineering.

subject: BE
title: Instrumentation and Measurement
description: Measurement concepts and operating principles applied to the selection and use of instruments important to scientists and engineers dealing with biological systems, including automatic data acquisition and processing.
prereq_raw: CHEM 151, MATH 241, and ME 311; or consent

subject: BE
title: Biofuel and Bioenergy
description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production, biorefinery concept; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel; biodiesel production; algal-biofuel; environmental impacts, life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies; term paper and presentation.

subject: BE
title: Experimental Methods in Cause-Effect Modeling
description: Factorial designs and fractional factorial designs for screening variable and response optimization. Response surface methodology. Experimental designs appropriate to building and testing multi-variable behavior relationships. Sequential experimental designs.

subject: BE
title: Biological Instrumentation
description: System integration for computer-based control, automation, and study of biological systems. Topics include physical, chemical, and biological sensors, actuators, digital interfacing/communication, image analysis, and structured code for microcontrollers and other portable computers.

subject: BE
title: Biological Treatment
description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil.

subject: BE
title: Biosystems Modeling
description: Introduction to system thinking, procedures for developing system models, characteristics of important agricultural system models, computer approach to evaluation and optimization of system models.
prereq_raw: one of MATH 215, MATH 241, MATH 251A; or consent

subject: BE
title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
description: Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

subject: BE
title: Seminar
description: Use of computer and video technology in technical presentation, review of current biosystems engineering research.

subject: AREC
title: Biosystems Modeling
description: Introduction to system thinking, procedures for developing system models, characteristics of important agricultural system modes, computer approach to evaluation and optimization of system models.
prereq_raw: one of MATH 215, MATH 241, MATH 251A; or consent

subject: AREC
title: Econometrics I
description: Review of probability, estimation, small sample and asymptotic properties. Bivariate and multiple regression and matrix algebra formulation. Regression diagnostics. Introduction to heteroskedastidity, autocorrelation, simultaneity, dichotomous variables, advanced topics.
prereq_raw: NREM 310 or ECON 321, and MATH 241; or consent

subject: AREC
title: Econometrics II
description: Specification, statistical estimation, inference, and forecasting of economic models. Includes advanced topics for single-equation models, pooled models, qualitative dependent variables, simultaneous systems, distributed lags, and time series.

subject: PEPS
title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PEPS
title: The World of Insects
description: Biology/ecology of insects with emphasis on relationships to plants, animals, and especially people in Hawai‘i and the tropics. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PEPS
title: Environment and Agriculture
description: Overview of environmental issues related to agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts. Ethical issues on impact of agriculture on the environment will be discussed.

subject: PEPS
title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawai‘i.
prereq_raw: (BIOL 171 and BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Invasive Pest Species
description: Ecological, economic and sociological impacts of invasive species on tropical ecosystems; characteristics of invasive species and vulnerability of habitats; ethical issues on impacts of management options on evolution, biodiversity and eco-stability and human life. Open to nonmajors. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: PEPS
title: General Entomology
description: Biology, diversity, and ecology of insects with emphasis on Hawaiian fauna. Classification to order level.
prereq_raw: (BOT 101 or ZOOL 101 or BIOL 171) with a minimum grade of C; or consent. DB

subject: PEPS
title: General Entomology Laboratory
description: Laboratory in the biology and classification to family level of Hawai‘i’s insects and arthropods.
prereq_raw: (363 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent. DY

subject: PEPS
title: Genetics: Theory to Application
description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

subject: PEPS
title: Plant Pathogens and Diseases
description: Classification, morphology, ecology, and biology of bacteria, fungi, nematodes, and viruses that attack economic crops. Etiology and control of plant diseases.
prereq_raw: 210/SUST 210 or BOT 101 or MICR 130, or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: PEPS
title: Turfgrass Pest Management
description: Provides students with knowledge and real world experience on common turfgrass pests and management strategies in Hawai‘i, with emphasis on integrated pest management. Common cool-season turfgrass and pest management are also discussed.

subject: PEPS
title: Foundations of Pest Management
description: Principles and concepts of insect pest management using biological, ecological, cultural, behavioral, legislative, microbial and chemical methods.
prereq_raw: one of the following: 250 or 363, BIOL 171, BIOL 172, or BOT 101; or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
description: Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management.

subject: PEPS
title: Plant Disease Management
description: Diagnosis, epidemiology, and integrated management of important plant diseases and pathogens for key plants and cultivated crops in various agroecosystems in Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and the global tropics.

subject: PEPS
title: Environmental Law
description: Exploration of federal laws, regulations, and precedents that govern our interaction with the environment. Analysis of laws regulating air, water, toxins, pests, endangered species, and environmental justice.

subject: PEPS
title: Medical and Urban Entomology
description: Biology, ecology, health and economic impacts, and control of urban insect pests and medically important arthropods that act as vectors of diseases.
prereq_raw: (363 or BIOL 265) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.  DB

subject: PEPS
title: Weed Science
description: Weed classification, identification, adaptations for weediness; principles of weed control; properties, uses, and action of herbicides. Lab: pesticide application equipment and techniques, no-till farming, greenhouse and field experiments.
prereq_raw: (CHEM 152 and TPSS 200/ SUST 211) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.   DB

subject: PEPS
title: Insect-Plant Interactions
description: Study of the coevolutionary relationships between insects and plants, with emphasis on the behavior, physiology, and symbiotic relationships of insects. Discussed in the context of sustainable agriculture, anthropogenic change, and climate change. A-C only.
prereq_raw: 363 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent. DB

subject: PEPS
title: Topics in Plant & Environmental Protection
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. May be offered by visiting faculty, extension faculty or research faculty.

subject: PEPS
title: PEPS Capstone
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development, Directed Research, field studies, employment with cooperating businesses, government or schools are all options.

subject: PEPS
title: Directed Research
description: Conduct original research in environmental protection sciences. Limited to qualified undergraduate students.

subject: PEPS
title: Agrosecurity and Food Safety
description: Concepts of agrosecurity and food safety (including plant and animal biosecurity), global impacts of introduced pests and diseases, and current mechanisms for interception of pests and mitigation of disease.

subject: PEPS
title: Biology of Plant Pathogens: Fungi and Nematodes
description: Principles and concepts in pathogen biology, epidemiology and management of plant diseases caused by fungi, oomycetes, and nematodes. Laboratory techniques for isolation and identification of pathogens and disease diagnosis.

subject: PEPS
title: Biology of Plant Pathogens: Bacteria and Viruses
description: Principles and concepts in pathogen biology, epidemiology, and management of plant diseases caused by bacteria and viruses. Laboratory techniques for isolation and identification of pathogens and disease diagnosis.

subject: PEPS
title: Professional Development
description: Lecture/discussion targets students exiting from graduate degree programs and provides preparation as a career professional; topics include establishing a professional identity; CV and cover letters, job-seeking due diligence, and negotiation skills. Graduate students only.

subject: PEPS
title: Diagnosis and Management of Tropical Plant Diseases
description: Iterative and interactive course integrating plant pathogen and pest biology with diagnostic and management approaches. Will use biological information about pathogens, anthropods, and abiotic stresses to diagnose diseases, disorders, or other injuries of plants.
prereq_raw: (605 and 606) with a minimum grade of B, or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Diagnosis and Management of Tropical Plant Diseases Laboratory
description: Diagnosis and management of plant pathogen and pest problems in laboratory and field. Taught concurrently with 615.
prereq_raw: (605 and 606) with a minimum grade of B, or equivalent

subject: PEPS
title: Molecular Diagnostics: Principles and Practices
description: Molecular diagnostics principles, comparative genomics, genome annotation and bio-informatics, phylogenetics, gene target selection, advanced primer, and probe design. Graduate students only or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Insect Physiology
description: Study of the principal physiological and biochemical functions in insects, with emphasis on hormonal interactions.

subject: PEPS
title: Molecular Plant–Fungal Interactions
description: Focuses on the actions of plant pathogenic fungi/ oomycetes and their host responses at the molecular and cellular level. Current genetic and genomic approaches to study plant-fungal interactions will be discussed. Graduate standing only.

subject: PEPS
title: Seminar in Plant Pathology
description: Seminar on research and topics in plant pathology.

subject: PEPS
title: Systematics and Phylogenetics
description: Classification and study of diversity among insects and other life forms. Use of morphological and molecular characters to reconstruct evolutionary histories.

subject: PEPS
title: Insect Ecology
description: Insects as living units in an environment of physical and biotic factors.

subject: PEPS
title: Biological Control of Pests
description: Fundamental concepts. Critical study of major biological control projects.
prereq_raw: 421 or consent. Recommended: 662; and ZOOL 631 or 632

subject: PEPS
title: Biological Control of Weeds
description: Examine approaches to weed biological control of invasive plants in various environments with different agents (insects, pathogens, and vertebrates), integration with other management tactics, sociopolitical aspects, and history of the practice. Graduate students only.

subject: PEPS
title: Invertebrate Microbiology
description: In-depth study of the molecular and cellular interactions between microbes and animals. Topics will cover types of symbioses, gut microbiome, parasites, and agricultural pathogens, and disease and human health disease.

subject: PEPS
title: Seminar in Entomology
description: Seminars on research and topics in entomology.

subject: PEPS
title: Special Topics
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in plant and environmental protection sciences at an advanced level. Offered by visiting or existing faculty as a special course.

subject: PEPS
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in entomology or tropical plant pathology

children.text: in entomology or tropical plant pathology

subject: PEPS
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research, critical reviews in environmental protection sciences, entomology, or plant pathology.

subject: PEPS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: PEPS
title: Advanced Plant Nematology
description: Advanced study of nematode taxonomy, genetics, behavior, host interactions, and sustainable management in an integrated lecture-laboratory.
prereq_raw: 605 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Advanced Plant Virology
description: Characterization, genome organization, gene expression, and molecular mechanisms of plant viruses.
prereq_raw: 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Advanced Plant-Bacteria Interactions
description: Molecular biology, genomics, molecular genetics, and infection mechanisms of bacterial plant pathogens and symbionts.
prereq_raw: 606 (with a minimum grade of B or better) or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Proposal/Defense Seminar
description: Thesis/ dissertation proposal and defense seminars.

subject: PEPS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. CR/ NC only.

subject: TAHR
title: International Exchange Study/Research
description: Study overseas in an approved international or similar exchange program.

subject: TAHR
title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

subject: TAHR
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: TAHR
title: Extension Education & Outreach
description: Introduces an essential component of the Land Grant Mission. Students will explore the foundational components of extension education including agent expectations, program development and evaluation, audience engagement, building partnerships, funding structures.

subject: DIS
title: Foundations in Disability and Diversity
description: Focuses on disability as a category of diversity and identity, as well as diversity within disability. Different strategies used to increase the freedom or liberty of people with disabilities are critically examined.

subject: DIS
title: Accessible Learning Technology
description: Focuses on creating accessible technology and instructional media, developing long-term resources, advancing accessible social interaction between students and students with instructors, and using case studies as examples of good practices.

subject: DIS
title: Disability History and Culture: From Homer to Hip Hop
description: How have people over many centuries, and from broad geographical perspectives perceived and treated individuals with disabilities? An overview of the history of the conditions in which people with disabilities lived.

subject: DIS
title: Introduction to Research in Curriculum and Teaching
description: Classroom-based research covers the fundamentals of qualitative, quantitative, Action Research, mixed methods, and Curriculum Based Assessment. Exploratory, explanatory, and confirmatory research will be highlighted culminating in an outline for Plan B/Thesis proposal.

subject: DIS
title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Pedagogy and Practice
description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawai‘i and our global community.

subject: DIS
title: Sexuality & Health
description: Examines concepts, theories, and skills-based practices of sexuality and health. Topics on underserved populations, disability, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Utilizes research-based curriculum/strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health.

subject: DIS
title: Supporting Multilingual Learners
description: Strategies for identifying and adopting best practices that support all students in inclusive learning environments with an emphasis on STEM curriculum for English Language Learners; (B) science; (C) technology; (D) math.

subject: DIS
title: Practicum in Applied Behavior Analysis
description: Supervised field experience in applied behavior analysis. The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable four times or up to 15 credits

subject: DIS
title: Disability History Through the Ages
description: A historical overview of disability that visits diverse perspectives, attitudes, and treatment toward individuals with disabilities through many centuries, societies, and cultures throughout the world; and how people with disabilities perceived themselves.

subject: DIS
title: Multicultural Issues in Disabilities
description: Provide background and understanding of various Pacific Rim cultural issues in the conceptualization and treatment of individuals with disabilities and their families.

subject: DIS
title: Special Topics in Disability and Diversity Studies
description: Explores disability and diversity across time to gain an understanding and context of issues such as difference, culture, identity, community, privilege, and oppression and how the past affects the present and future.

subject: DIS
title: Interdisciplinary Disability and Diversity Issues
description: Develop understanding of current issues faced by individuals with disabilities and their families within the disability paradigm and across cultures.

subject: DIS
title: Interdisciplinary Team Development
description: Develop knowledge and skills to participate effectively on interdisciplinary teams for the common goal of promoting service integration and coordination of education, social, health, mental health, and other services with individuals with disabilities and their families.

subject: DIS
title: Interdisciplinary Assessment
description: Assessment methods and techniques to instructional research-based practices and supports across disciplines, cultures and PK-12 that address barriers to learning for all students with the context of the Comprehensive Student Support System (CSSS).

subject: DIS
title: Advanced Interdisciplinary Assessment
description: Assessment methods and techniques to instructional research-based practices and supports across disciplines, cultures and PK-12 that address barriers to learning for all students with the context of the Comprehensive Student Support System (CSSS).

subject: DIS
title: Seminar on Disability Issues
description: In-depth explorations of current and compelling interdisciplinary topics related to advancing the social, political, educational, and economic integration of individuals with disabilities of all ages.

subject: DIS
title: Portfolio/Field Work
description: Interdisciplinary community experience and portfolio in disability and diversity studies.

subject: DIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Directed reading and/or research.

subject: DIS
title: Mixed Methods Research Design
description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal. (Once a year)

subject: EDCS
title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years)
description: Emphasizes interrelated historical and philosophical roots and socio-cultural context and their influence on policy and practice in early childhood education settings.

subject: EDCS
title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years) Lab
description: Direct experience with children in early childhood settings in order to apply concepts from 415 and gain perspective on the role of the practitioner in ECE settings.

subject: EDCS
title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children
description: Continuation of 415: focuses on the design, implementation, evaluation of meaningful, challenging integrated curriculum that promotes comprehensive developmental and learning outcomes for diverse young children (pK-3).

subject: EDCS
title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children Lab
description: Continuation of 415L.

subject: EDCS
title: STEM Pedagogy
description: Introduction to STEM education pedagogy with emphasis on ethical issues and effective oral communication. Designed to integrate educational theory, pedagogy, content, and practical concerns into teaching practices in the STEM fields.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits

subject: EDCS
title: Collaborative Language and Learning
description: Examination of language (talking, reading, and writing) processes within a collaborative teaching framework in the secondary curriculum. Field experience may be required.

subject: EDCS
title: Adolescent Literature and Literacy
description: Selection and interpretation of young adult literature, including multicultural literature for middle level and high school students. Theory and teaching strategies for integrating literacy instruction in the literature program for diverse student populations.

subject: EDCS
title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning.

subject: EDCS
title: Multicultural and Social Justice Education
description: Exploring social justice and multilingual, multicultural education with attention to Hawai‘i as our place of learning and teaching.

subject: EDCS
title: Methods and Materials in Science
description: Selecting and using methods and materials, demonstrations and simulations, open-ended experimentation, inquiry and discovery, task analysis measurement tools and techniques, activities from various curricula, opportunity for individualized goals and projects.
prereq_raw: STE 323, STE 404(H), teaching experience; or consent

subject: EDCS
title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers, including criteria for evaluation and planning.
prereq_raw: (HDFS 230 (or concurrent), HDFS 331 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B-; or consent

subject: EDCS
title: Gender Issues in Education
description: Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close attention to the writing process and the skills needed to compose a well-written research paper.

subject: EDCS
title: Issues in Computer Education
description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education.

subject: EDCS
title: Problem Solving in Mathematics Education
description: Experiencing and learning to teach heuristics of solving mathematical problems; designing curricula, classroom organization, evaluative measures for problem solving.

subject: EDCS
title: Difficulties in Learning Mathematics
description: Identification, analysis, and remediation of difficulties in learning mathematics.

subject: EDCS
title: Language, Learning and Teaching
description: Examines the role that language plays in the social construction of knowledge within various disciplines, K–adult. Collaborative group learning strategies will be modeled.
prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent

subject: EDEP
title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models.

subject: EDEP
title: Design and Analysis of Psychological Experiments
description: Analysis of variance and other models of assessing results of experiments. Relation of analysis to design.

subject: EDEP
title: Applied Regression and Analysis of Variance
description: Introduction to linear statistical models as principle of data analysis. Topics include multiple regression models with continuous and categorical predictors. ANOVA with multiple factors, ANOVA with repeated measures, and ANCOVA.
prereq_raw: 601 or EDEA 629 (with a grade of B+), or consent

subject: EDEP
title: Multivariate Methods
description: Builds on prior knowledge of multiple regression and will include applications of MANOVA, canonical correlation, logistic regression, discriminant function analysis, cluster analysis, multidimensional scaling, and mixture models.

subject: EDEP
title: Nonparametric Methods for Behavioral Science
description: Conditions for valid applications of nonparametric statistical techniques in education and behavioral sciences; theoretical and methodological perspectives.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Educational Research
description: Fundamental design and evaluation procedures in educational research. Topics include an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research, the review of literature, developing research questions, research design, instrumentation, data collection, and writing a research proposal.
prereq_raw: 601 (or concurrent) (with a minimum grade of B or higher) or consent

subject: EDEP
title: Graduate Introduction to Educational Psychology
description: Graduate level introduction to educational psychology theories, research, and topics.

subject: EDEP
title: Multilevel Modeling for Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Data
description: Theories and applications of multilevel model to analyze cross-sectional and longitudinal data. Topics include two-level and three-level models, growth models, and multilevel logistic regression.
prereq_raw: 604, PSY 610, 612 (with a minimum grade of B or higher), or consent

subject: EDEP
title: Qualitative Research Methods in Education
description: Introduction to methods of qualitative research in education. (Meets PhD common core requirement.)

subject: EDEP
title: Measurement in Education and Social Sciences
description: Measurement and psychometric theories and applications using psychometric programs. Topics include classical test theory, reliability, validity, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, item bias, and item response theory.

subject: EDEP
title: Categorical Data Analysis
description: Theories and methods for data analysis with categorical and discrete variables; analysis of contingency tables, loglinear models, introduction to generalized linear models for binary, nominal, ordinal, and count outcomes in cross-sectional and longitudinal data sets.

subject: EDEP
title: Structural Equation Modeling
description: Theories and applications to test models with manifest and latent variables. Topics include path analysis, factor analysis, latent variable model, multi-group analysis, latent means model, and other advanced topics in SEM.

subject: EDEP
title: Psychometric Methods
description: Theories and applications of modern psychometrics. Topics include item response theory, detecting biased items, measurement invariance, and current issues in psychometrics.
prereq_raw: 604 (with a minimum grade of B+) or consent

subject: EDEP
title: Adolescence and Education
description: Discussion-based course presenting an overview of educational psychology applied to teaching adolescents, including theory and research on human learning, adolescent development and its social context, and student assessment.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Program Evaluation
description: Introduction to concepts and issues related to program evaluation. Topics include preparing for an evaluation, formative and summative uses, and qualitative and quantitative design approaches.

subject: EDEP
title: Development and Learning
description: Theories and research on learning and development and their educational applications. Analysis of how learning and development are interrelated.

subject: EDEP
title: Social Context of Learning
description: Analysis of the social context in the learning process and education, including peer, family, community, and cultural influences.

subject: EDEP
title: Models of Cognitive Learning
description: Cognitive models of knowledge acquisition, organization, and utilization; theory and research relating learning and cognition to interactive instructional models.

subject: EDEP
title: Instructional Psychology
description: Application of learning theory and cognitive skills training in instructional settings.

subject: EDEP
title: Social Cognition and Competence
description: Systematic analysis of social reasoning abilities conjunctive with or prerequisite to effective social interaction in educational settings.

subject: EDEP
title: Capstone Project in Educational Psychology
description: To be taken in the final semester or the second to last semester to complete the certificate. Students are expected to integrate, extend, critique and apply knowledge learned in the certificate program.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits

subject: EDEP
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research.

subject: EDEP
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: EDEP
title: Educational Research Methods
description: Research techniques and thesis development.

subject: EDEP
title: Practicum in Educational Psychology
description: Supervised practicum in teaching or program evaluation as each is reflected by professional activities of the members of the faculty.

subject: EDEP
title: Creative Learning Strategies for Adults
description: Analysis of psychology of adult learner; forces that affect learning in dynamics of individual, group, and organizational behavior; concept of lifelong learning vis-à-vis development of creative strategies that assist maturing, self-directed persons to develop their potentialities.

subject: EDEP
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Educational Psychology
description: Current issues and problems in the context of education: (B) general; (C) learning; (D) measurement; (E) statistics; (F) psycho-social development; (G) educational evaluation; (H) research methodology.
prereq_raw: consent. Seminar may be repeated for credit as topics vary

children.text: Seminar may be repeated for credit as topics vary

subject: EDEP
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: EDUC
title: Action Research in Education
description: Theory and practice in collaborative action research; critical inquiry into current educational work in schools with goals of improvement of teaching and participation in school and curriculum reform.

subject: EDUC
title: Professional Doctorate Practicum: Consultancy Project
description: Practicum in the EdD program in professional practice; involves a group consultancy project requiring independent research and reflective activity embedded in a group project dealing with a problem of practice. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice.

subject: EDUC
title: Professional Doctorate Practicum: Individual Applied Research Project
description: Practicum in conducting individual practitioner research within the EdD. Includes the formulation of individual applied research project, developing a plan of action, selection of appropriate methods, implementation of plan and composition of practitioner research report. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice.

subject: EDUC
title: EdD Conference
description: Capstone for the Doctoral Degree in Professional Education Practice. Involves a conference presentation of research project results to an audience of faculty, fellow graduate students, and interested members of the public. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice.

subject: EDUC
title: Field Project
description: Practicum experience in area of specialization. Variable credit: minimum of 3 credit hours, maximum of 6 credit hours.

subject: EDUC
title: Internship in College Teaching
description: Introduction to college-level teaching; doctoral students serve as apprentices to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching, planning and evaluation.
prereq_raw: admission to PhD candidacy and consent

subject: EDUC
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: ESEE
title: Learner in the Environment I: Social and Cultural Contexts for Learning
description: Knowledge and skills related to the context of teaching. Teacher candidates will examine the impact of culture, family, school, classroom, and individual characteristics on learning, and orally present, in varied formats, acquired knowledge and competencies.

subject: ESEE
title: Learner in the Environment II: Classroom and Behavior Management
description: Teacher candidates explore the ethical implications for establishing, maintaining, and restoring the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning.

subject: ESEE
title: Learner in the Environment III: Behavior Project Implementation
description: Teacher candidates demonstrate the ability to establish, maintain, and (when necessary) restore the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning. Candidates demonstrate ability to identify maladaptive student behaviors and implement effective, research-based interventions.

subject: ESEE
title: Assessment I: Foundations of Assessment
description: Introduction to foundational aspects of assessment and emphasizes the importance of linking assessment with planning and instruction. Candidates develop knowledge, skills, and dispositions important for designing, implementing, and analyzing effective assessments for diverse learners.

subject: ESEE
title: Assessment II: Formal Assessment
description: Understand techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate disabilities. Inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment is stressed. Significant instruction on writing individualized education programs.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Introduction to Inclusive Teaching
description: Teacher candidates engage in reflective, procedural, and research writing to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Science
description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to the teaching and learning of science in elementary settings, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, using evidence-based practices.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Mathematics in Inclusive Settings
description: Prepares beginning elementary school teachers of mathematics, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: STEM
description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to teaching and learning of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) content for inclusive elementary classrooms, K-6. Teacher candidates focus on planning, teaching, and assessing STEM.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Integrating Social Studies and the Performing Arts
description: Social Studies and Performing Arts integrated content in diverse K-6 classrooms. Teacher candidates engage with social issues through collaborative, expressive, aesthetic, creative, and critical pedagogy. Candidates perform, present, and teach to develop oral communication skills.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy I: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, K-3
description: Overview of principles and practices for teaching reading (phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension) to diverse students, grades K-3; including planning, instruction, and assessment. Writing assignments include lesson reflections, case studies, modules, and reading responses.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy II: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, Grades 4-6
description: Teacher candidates demonstrate essential reading comprehension strategies, engaging students in complex text by planning, instructing, and assessing elementary students in grades 4-6, in inclusive settings. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy III: Writing and Visual Arts in Inclusive Settings, K-6
description: Methods, programs, and strategies for planning, teaching, and assessing writing for elementary students in inclusive settings, grades K-6. Visual arts methods are integrated to develop visual literacy.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Experience I: Response to Intervention in Reading
description: Teacher candidates in this field based course will use an evidencebased practice in reading within a response to intervention (Rtl) framework. Supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Rounds
description: Field-based course engages teacher candidates in a variety of purposeful observation and reflection activities aligned with course work. Field settings are appropriate to concurrent classes; supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Experience II: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Experience III: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight.

subject: ESEE
title: Student Teaching in Elementary and Special Education Classrooms
description: Full-time student teaching in grades K-6 in an elementary school inclusion classroom, or a combination of general education and special education settings. The experience is directed by a qualified mentor teacher and has university-provided supervision.

subject: ESEE
title: Seminar for Student Teaching
description: Seminar to support student teaching experiences and prepare teacher candidates to transition into a full time teacher, examine ethical issues in the field, prepare for employment, and demonstrate ability to meet professional standards.

subject: KRS
title: Physical Fitness
description: Conditioning exercises and activities to develop and maintain physical efficiency. Motor fitness tests administered to measure status and progress.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Aerobic Fitness
description: Aerobic fitness improvement upon completion of course by regularly attending and practicing safe workout routines. Learn fitness components, names of muscles and exercises associated with each one.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Swimming: Beginning
description: Adjusting to and immersing in water, floating, sculling; correct arm stroke, leg kick, breathing techniques and their coordination. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Swimming: Intermediate
description: Perfecting and integrating basic strokes with added emphasis for speed and distance. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Swimming: Advanced
description: Correct techniques used in competitive swimming, racing starts, correct turning techniques, long-distance swimming. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: SCUBA Diving: Beginning
description: Learning watermanship, equipment handling skills, and the knowledge to become safe divers. Additional costs for equipment, diver manual, dive tables, and certification fee.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Aqua-Aerobic Fitness
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on aerobic fitness improvement through total body aquatic workouts with music, and development of individualized aquatics fitness program. Open to all students.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Golf: Beginning
description: Rules, etiquette, grip, stance, drive, normal iron shots, approach shots, putting.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Golf: Intermediate
description: Corrective work on basic swing mechanics and rhythm; adjustments for bunker play, uphill lies, downhill lies, short game around and on the green; handicapping and match play competition.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Golf: Advanced
description: Improving drive, fairway wood shots, long iron shots, control shots, trouble shots, putting, course management, competitive strategy, problems in rules. Greens fees paid by students for play on courses.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Human Physiology and Anatomy
description: Introduction to human physiology and anatomy designed to serve the needs of those interested in pursuing health-related careers. Structure and function of major systems examined (gross anatomy, microanatomy, physiology, and pathology).

subject: KRS
title: Bowling
description: Rules, etiquette, arm swing, approach, execution, scoring, spare pickups. Students pay charge for use of alley.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Badminton
description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, smash, drive, net play, offensive and defensive strategy; singles and doubles play.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Folk and National Dances
description: Popular dances of various national groups, including square dances.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Dances of Hawai‘i
description: Background and fundamentals of hula. Selected dances with and without instruments.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Dances of Hawai‘i: Advanced
description: Advanced techniques in hula movements. Selected dances taught will be more complex, including work with instruments. Individual choreography will be emphasized.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Social Dance: Ballroom
description: Social dances including fox trot, waltz, swing, and other popular dances. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Social Dance: Latin
description: Social dances of a Latin flavor including rhumba, cha-cha, tango, samba, and others. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Tennis: Beginning
description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, volleying; singles and doubles play.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Tennis: Intermediate
description: Corrective work in three basic strokes and in net play; the lob, drop shot, overhead smash, and half-volley; applying spin in basic strokes; basic strategy in singles and doubles play.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Tennis: Advanced
description: Improving upon the strokes introduced in 130 and 131; advanced competitive strategy; problems in rules; officiating; elements of tournament play.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Volleyball: Beginning
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on beginner skills and knowledge relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy. Open to all students.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Volleyball: Intermediate
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on improving skills and knowledge through practice and cognitive activities relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy. Open to all students.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Basketball
description: Rules, passing, shooting, dribbling, rebounding, individual defensive and offensive maneuvers; team offense and defense.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Adapted and Prescribed Exercises
description: Small group and individual guidance and instruction for students recommended by student health service.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Weight Training
description: Kinesiology of lifting and weight training, various types of exercises and methods of training with resistance.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Olympic and Power Lifting
description: Exercise technique and prescription with an emphasis on anaerobic exercise. Explores advanced periodization models and their utilization, mastery of Olympic lifts, and plyometric programs.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Tumbling and Rebound Tumbling
description: Single and combination stunts on tumbling mats and trampoline, balancing stunts; techniques of spotting; safety procedures.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Heavy Apparatus
description: Single and combination stunts on side horse, horizontal bar, parallel bars, still rings; techniques of spotting; safety procedures.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Judo
description: Rules, etiquette, method of falling and breaking the fall, simple throws and their counters, simple holds and breaking of such holds, randori. (Student to provide own gi.)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Aikido
description: Rules, etiquette, basic rolls, simple holds and the breaking of such holds, specific physical conditioning exercises. (Student to provide own gi.)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: T’ai Chi Ch’uan
description: Classic forms of t’ai chi ch’uan.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Karate: Beginning
description: Rules, etiquette, basic stances, blocks, thrusts, kicks, ippon kumite, and selected kata. (Student to provide own gi.)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Karate: Intermediate
description: Emphasis on improving the basic techniques (stances, punches, kicks, forms, and sparring); introduction to combination techniques. (Student to provide own gi.)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Wrestling: Beginning
description: Rules: fundamental defensive and offensive maneuvers and competitive strategy, i.e., takedowns, reversals, escapes, and pinning combinations; conditioning exercises.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Yoga: Beginning
description: Experiencing yoga and its effects on body, mind and consciousness of individual. Encompasses exercise, breathing techniques, deep relaxation, meditation, practice in concentration, and yogic postures.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Yoga: Intermediate
description: Corrective work and improvement of basic techniques. Exercise sets and combinations designed to develop endurance, flexibility, muscle and nerve strength, meditation, and deep relaxation technique.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Water Polo
description: Fundamentals of basic water polo skills, namely, ball handling, passing, shooting, dribbling plus a brief introduction into beginning techniques of individual offense and defense.
prereq_raw: 104 or consent. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

children.text: ( Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Sport Proficiency I: Invasion
description: Knowledge, skill development, and strategy of various invasion type games and sports. Sports like basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee and/or others are introduced within a tactical framework.

subject: KRS
title: Sport Proficiency II: Net, Field, and Target
description: Knowledge, skill development, position, and strategy of net, field and target sports. Sports like volleyball, tennis, softball, and golf are introduced within a tactical framework.

subject: KRS
title: Floor Exercise Gymnastics
description: An entry-level course designed to develop students’ knowledge of men’s and women’s gymnastics floor exercise routines, including injury prevention, skill progression, spotting techniques, and routine choreography. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Track and Field for Physical Education
description: Knowledge, skills, and rules of various track and field events. Organization of track meets and strategy in competition. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Softball
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on basic skills, rules, etiquette, offensive and defensive strategies, position play, and game situations. Open to all students.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: School Health Problems: Elementary
description: Responsibilities of elementary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing teacher’s role in health instruction, health services, school health policies.

subject: KRS
title: School Health Problems: Secondary
description: Responsibilities of secondary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing health instruction, health services, healthful school living, school health policies.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Kinesiology
description: Kinesiology as a professional field. Overview of history, philosophy, and current trends in kinesiology. Survey of psychological and sociological foundations of kinesiology, exercise, fitness and sport. KRS majors or approval.

subject: KRS
title: Recreation Services in Contemporary Society
description: Theories and philosophies in recreation: history; contemporary issues; roles in modern society; relationship to health, physical education, and exercise science.

subject: KRS
title: Human Development
description: Developmental processes across the life span. Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Human growth and development from conception to death with major theories and related research on maintaining healthy lifestyles.

subject: KRS
title: Safety and Risk Management
description: Understanding the fundamental principles and techniques of safety and accident-prevention programming emphasizing school, home, public places, on the job, and motor vehicle situations.

subject: KRS
title: Outdoor Recreation Management
description: Objectives and values of outdoor recreation; characteristics and determinants of programs; planning, organization, leadership, and facilities for recreational uses of natural environments.

subject: KRS
title: Health Education Curriculum
description: Objectives of school health program, emphasizing scope and sequence of health instruction; critical examination of health curriculum guides from various states.

subject: KRS
title: Programming and Leadership
description: Factors in planning and leading recreation programs; characteristics and responsibilities of leadership in relation to nature, scope, and resources of a variety of programs.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Health and Physical Education
description: Introduction to foundational knowledge for effective teaching, history, philosophy, and current practices in physical education. Provides the basis for later coursework in K-12 physical education. Required field experience.

subject: KRS
title: Performance Based Assessment in Health and Physical Education
description: Assessment and evaluative techniques applied to health and physical education, including test construction, performance-based assessment, measurement criteria and instruments, interpretation of data and content, as well as program evaluation.

subject: KRS
title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
description: Understanding standards-based planning, teaching, and assessment in health with a focus on advocacy, as well as the incidence, prevalence, and prevention of disease within sub-topics of health (mental, social, emotional, environmental, financial, etc.).

subject: KRS
title: Principles of Sports Medicine
description: Examines with some depth, principles of risk management and pathology of athletic injuries, major musculoskeletal structures, and concepts of evaluative skills, treatment, and rehabilitation for common athletic injuries.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Football
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive football coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Basketball
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive basketball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Baseball
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive baseball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Volleyball
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive volleyball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

subject: KRS
title: Music and Rhythm in Physical Education
description: Use of music in physical education programming (K-12), emphasizing selection of appropriate music for specific activities as expressive or creative movement, movement exploration, rhythmic gymnastics, and dancing. A variety of strategies for teaching dance will be shared.

subject: KRS
title: Managing Recreation Services
description: Administrative framework and procedures pertinent to the operation of agencies providing recreational services to the various publics.

subject: KRS
title: Water Safety Training
description: Theory and methods of advanced lifesaving and water safety leading to American Red Cross Water Safety Instructor (WSI) certification.
prereq_raw: 104 or consent. (Student to provide own swim attire approved by the instructor.)

children.text: ( Student to provide own swim attire approved by the instructor.)

subject: KRS
title: Emergency Care and First Aid Training
description: Practicum in training of persons to become qualified in emergency care knowledge, basic life support, and first aid skills. First Aid and CPR certificates may be earned.

subject: KRS
title: Movement Education I
description: A movement-based approach to teaching basic motor skills in preschool/elementary physical education. Students actively participate and learn about developmentally appropriate content and pedagogy for children in grades P–5/6. Peer bit teaching is included.

subject: KRS
title: Movement Education II
description: Content and pedadogy for teaching Pre/K-5 physical education. Students will learn to plan and teach physical education for children. Peer bit and field teaching included.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, but credit earned one time only

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Track and Field
description: Techniques and rules of sprints, distance runs, relays, hurdles, long jump, high jump, pole vault, shot put, discus, and javelin throws; conduct of track and field meets; specific conditioning and training problems.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Swimming
description: Theory and methods of coaching competitive swimming. Technical, organizational, and administrative aspects. Emphasis on stroke mechanics and training methods.

subject: KRS
title: Fieldwork in Recreation I
description: Initial supervised leadership experience in recreational agencies. One hour per week in class discussion sessions. For recreation majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Special Recreation
description: Special recreation as a professional field. Overview of special recreation services. Emphasis on recreation services for special populations.

subject: KRS
title: Structural Kinesiology
description: Gross human anatomy, emphasizing identification and description of parts of the musculoskeletal system; selected applications to motor activity.
prereq_raw: 113 or BIOL 171/171L or PHYL 103 or PHYL 141/141L or PHYL 301/301L

subject: KRS
title: Exercise and Sport Physiology
description: Emphasis on physiological responses to exercises and physical training as related to strength, muscular endurance, cardio-respiratory endurance. Primarily for KRS majors, but open to others with consent. Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/ Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.
prereq_raw: 113 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 142/142L (or concurrent), or BIOL 171/171L (or concurrent); or consent

subject: KRS
title: Exercise and Sport Physiology Lab
description: Laboratory section to accompany KRS 354. Emphasis will be hands-on data collection and analysis of the physiological responses to exercise and physical training. Lab report development and scientific writing will also be emphasized. Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.
prereq_raw: 113 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 142/142L (or concurrent), or BIOL 171/171L (or concurrent); or consent

subject: KRS
title: Teaching Techniques I: Elementary
description: Teaching techniques and methods of elementary physical education. Content to include basic skills and games in a school-based experience. Primarily for KRS majors.

subject: KRS
title: Teaching Techniques II: Secondary
description: Teaching techniques and methods of secondary physical education. Content to include invasion, net, field, and target activities. Emphasizes the tactical approach in a school-based experience. Primarily for KRS majors.

subject: KRS
title: Drugs and Society
description: Introduction to psychoactive drugs and their effects; drug regulations; education and rehabilitation programs; psycho-social variables related to the decisions to use/abuse drugs.

subject: KRS
title: Physical Fitness for Physical Education Teachers
description: Diagnosis and prescription for basic health and fitness problems, scientific principles of training, guidelines for exercise; essentials of scientifically based individualized physical fitness program.

subject: KRS
title: Field Work in Strength and Conditioning I
description: Supervised practicum in strength training and conditioning. Students will be exposed to the theory and practice of designing and implementing both strength/power, and general conditioning programs.

subject: KRS
title: Personal Health and Wellness
description: Core concepts in health allow students to take responsibility for their own health-related behaviors by developing basic competencies in identifying, analyzing, and responsibly deliberating contemporary ethical issues related to health and wellness.

subject: KRS

repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, but credit earned one time only
