subject: KRS
title: Psychosocial Aspects of Sport
description: Examination and application of sociological and psychological theories to sport including the influence of race, ethnicity, gender, identity and human development, social class, disabilities, and sexual orientation on the sport experience.

subject: KRS
title: Prevent/Care of Athletic Injuries
description: An examination of the most recent practices and procedures in the prevention and care of athletic and sports injuries. Observational field experiences in athletic training will be required.

subject: KRS
title: Fundamentals of Ergonomics
description: Introduction to ergonomics principles and their application in understanding and prevention of Muscular Skeletal Disorders encountered in the working environment including introduction to legal aspects of ergonomics. Post-Master’s Certificate in Nursing majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Administration in Athletic Training, Exercise Science, Allied Health
description: An examination of organization and administration in Athletic Training, Allied Health and Exercise Science. Content includes leadership and motivation models, legal liability, ethical considerations and management strategies for all aspects of Health Care Administration.

subject: KRS
title: Lower Extremity Assessment
description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the lower extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals.

subject: KRS
title: Upper Extremity Assessment
description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the upper extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals. Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Curriculum and Supervision
description: Effective program development, planning, and supervision, including issues in legal liability and administration of all aspects of physical education programming in grades K-12.

subject: KRS
title: Current Issues in Leisure Services
description: Philosophical foundations and current and emerging issues in leisure services management and programming. Coverage of leisure research and its implications to practice.

subject: KRS
title: Evaluating and Marketing Leisure Services
description: Basic methods in marketing, planning, evaluating programs and problem-solving methods, survey research, research design, data analysis, and report generation for park, recreation, and tourism systems.

subject: KRS
title: Emergency Care for the Professional Rescuer
description: Combined lecture-lab on advanced emergency care for injuries and illnesses and includes certifications for CPR/First Aid/AED. Class size of approximately 20 students. Open to all majors.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching Athletics
description: Combined lecture-lab with emphasis on scientific principles, theory and practice, and professional qualities of the coach. Writing is integrated with the intent that students will enhance their communication skills through writing. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: Camp Resources and Planning
description: Combined lecture-lab for camp counselors and camp leadership. Plan and evaluate camp experiences for children and youth, including those with disabilities. Includes field trips.

subject: KRS
title: Practicum in Camping
description: Supervised leadership at a camp setting with children and youth, including those with disabilities. Day or residential camps. One full week camping for each credit hour. Maximum of four credit hours.

subject: KRS
title: Disability and Diversity in Physical Activity
description: Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience.

subject: KRS
title: Sport Biomechanics

subject: KRS
title: Fitness for Life

subject: KRS

subject: KRS
title: Learning Communities
description: Theory, basic research, interactive process, and methodology of the cooperative learning process known as Tribes. Will develop participants’ abilities to foster and facilitate learning communities in a variety of settings.

subject: KRS
title: Sociocultural Issues in Physical Activity
description: Contemporary and historical perspective on socio-cultural issues that influence health and physical activity settings. Understanding ethics and culturally responsive practice around race, gender, sexuality, class, etc. Emphasis on ethics and teaching writing for the profession.

subject: KRS
title: Statistics

subject: KRS
title: Motor Learning and Performance
description: Basic consideration is kinesthesis, motor ability, fatigue, developmental factors, practice, motivation in relation to motor learning and human performance.

subject: KRS
title: Motor Development and Learning
description: Motor development through the lifespan with an emphasis on fundamental principles and patterns. Areas such as memory, knowledge of performance, and motivation are incorporated and demonstrated through multiple writing assignments. Required field experience. Primarily for KRS majors.

subject: KRS
title: Adapted Physical Activity in Early Childhood
description: Concepts of developmentally appropriate practice, importance of movement in overall development, and design of physical activity sessions and environments for young children with and without disabilities are covered.

subject: KRS
title: Nutrition in Exercise and Sport
description: Effects of physiologic demands of exercise on nutrition. Emphasis on physiologic and biochemical basis for nutrition recommendations to enhance exercise participation and optimize athletic performance.
prereq_raw: (FSHN 185, and KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or (PHYL 141/141L and 142/142L) or PHYL 301) with a minimum grade of C

subject: KRS

subject: KRS

subject: KRS

subject: KRS

subject: LTEC
title: Developing Online Learning
description: Design and development of online instruction for educational and training settings. Implementation of online course elements and strategies for content delivery, course management, student interaction, course evaluation and assessment of student learning. LTEC majors only or consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Emerging Technologies for K-12 Teaching
description: Exploration and impact of emerging technologies in K-12 classroom teaching and learning and ramifications of these technologies on administrative structure of schools. LTEC majors only or consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Facilitating E-learning Communities
description: Exploration of tools and design considerations for effective online communication and development of learning communities.

subject: LTEC
title: Educational Technology in Informal Learning Environments
description: Exploring the nature, application, and use of educational technology in informal learning environments, such as museums, cultural institutions, tourist attractions, and visitor information centers. Focusing on the analysis, selection, and development of various media choices.

subject: LTEC
title: (Alpha) Learning with Emerging Technologies
description: Exploration and evaluation of new tools and strategies for teaching and learning. (B) mobile learning; (C) free/open software; (D) educational games and simulations; (E) critical trends.
prereq_raw: LTEC major or consent. (Fall only for (B) and (D)) (Spring only for (C) and (E))

children.text: ( Fall only for (B) and ( D)) ( Spring only for (C) and ( E))

subject: LTEC
title: Interactive Multimedia Production
description: The utilization and application of advanced authoring tools, combining video, animation, graphics, and sound to develop student-centered learning. Primarily for advanced LTEC students. LTEC majors only or consent.

subject: LTEC
title: (Alpha) Authoring E-learning Environments
description: Conceptualization of instructional design and its application to the development for e-learning environments: (B) assisted instruction (CAI); (C) managed instruction; (D) virtual reality; (E) animation. LTEC majors only or consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Programming for Games and Simulations
description: Project-based exploration of the breadth of programming in the context of educational games and simulations.

subject: LTEC
title: Design Thinking for Creative Problem Solving
description: Using real-world problems, students learn an agile design and problem-solving process that is human-centered, iterative, and cultivates individual and group creativity.

subject: LTEC
title: Assessment and Evaluation in Educational Technology
description: Evaluation and assessment processes, sources, and instruments applicable to systematic appraisal of learning with technology.

subject: LTEC
title: Research Design: Multiple Methods and Traditions
description: Explores research methods used in educational technology with a focus on developing a design for dissertation research. Emphasis is on the use of digital technologies in data collection and analysis. LTEC PhD majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: LTEC
title: Qualitative Research in Educational Technology
description: Introduction to qualitative research traditions and designs. Emphasis will be on the use of digital technologies in data collection and analysis. LTEC PhD majors only. EDUC PhD majors only with consent. (Once a year)

subject: LTEC
title: Quantitative Research in Educational Technology
description: Application of methodological and statistical concepts in a projects-based classroom framework. Formative and summative evaluation, measurements, descriptive, and inferential statistics. LTEC PhD majors only. EDUC PhD majors only with consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Distance Education Technology
description: Technical and instructional considerations for developing, delivering, managing, and evaluating distance education including voice, video, print, hypermedia and data transmissions.

subject: LTEC
title: Designing Online Learning
description: Planning, needs assessment, standards and learning theory applied to the design of online learning and assessment plans. LTEC majors only or consent.

subject: LTEC
title: (Alpha) Technical Issues in Educational Technology
description: Applying theory of management in instructional technology support services and delivery systems. (B) management; (C) systems; (D) networks.

subject: LTEC
title: Social and Ethical Issues in Educational Technology
description: Examination of social and ethical issues as they relate to technology in instructional settings. Focus on social justice and societal impact.

subject: LTEC
title: Cognition and Technology
description: Interdisciplinary course that introduces a range of empirical research examining aspects of cognition such as attention, memory and learning, and how technologies can enhance and/or hinder these cognitive processes.

subject: LTEC
title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure.

subject: LTEC
title: Learning Design Studio
description: Practicum in instructional design, development, and technology in academic and non-academic settings, under close supervision, plus regular class meetings in seminar format. LTEC majors only or consent.

subject: LTEC
title: LTEC Training and Evaluation Practicum
description: Practicum in educational technology training and evaluation in formal and informal settings, under close supervision, plus class meetings in hybrid format. LTEC majors only or consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Seminar in Technology Leadership
description: Supervised activity in application of research in learning design and technology to teaching/training experiences. LTEC majors only and consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Practicum in E-learning
description: Practicum in e-learning in academic or non-academic settings, under close supervision, plus regular class meetings. LTEC majors only or consent.

subject: LTEC
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable for 3 credit hours maximum each time

subject: LTEC
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: LTEC
title: Instructional Design Studio
description: Covers multiple instructional design models within the context of theory and research. Studio approach to focus on facilitating learning and improving performance by creating, using, and managing appropriate technological processes and resources. LTEC PhD majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: LTEC
title: Special Topics in Educational Technology
description: Issues of topical interest in educational technology. Concentrates on a topic of current interest, including the new technologies for learning and teaching, and innovative strategies for design and delivery of instruction.

subject: LTEC
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Educational Technology Issues
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. (B) instructional development; (C) online communities; (D) the future; (E) research. LTEC PhD majors only.

subject: LTEC
title: Seminar in Educational Technology Theory
description: Doctoral level seminar for advanced students examining the theoretical foundations of research in the learning sciences and technology. LTEC PhD majors only.

subject: LTEC
title: Mixed Methods Research Design
description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal. (Once a year)

subject: LTEC
title: Advanced Qualitative Analysis in LTEC
description: Advanced research methods focused on management and analysis of qualitative data using technology. Reviews of different qualitative designs, data types, analytical methods, and software. Focused study of one qualitative design. Includes independent research project. EDUC, LTEC PhD majors only.
prereq_raw: 667 or graduate level qualitative research course

subject: LTEC
title: Design-Based Research in Education
description: Provides an introduction to design-based research in education. Reviews different design-based methods and guides students through the process of conducting original design-based research. Focuses on the gap between research and practice.
prereq_raw: 667 (with a minimum grade of B) and 668 (or concurrent)

subject: LTEC
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: SPED
title: Disability and Diversity in the Media
description: Explores the changing disability experience as described in contemporary film, literature, advertising, news, sports and dialogue with persons with disabilities in the Pacific region and around the world.

subject: SPED
title: Global and Historical Perspectives of Disability in the Media
description: Explores the history of disability representation across cultures. Emphasis is placed on examining evolving perceptions of disability as depicted in art, literature, print, film, and digital media. FGB

subject: SPED
title: Foundations of Inclusive Schooling
description: Foundations of “special education” exploring philosophies, diverse and historical viewpoints, laws, and service delivery. Students reflect upon texts, films and interviews with persons with disabilities, their families and professionals to understand the culture of disability.

subject: SPED
title: Special Education Law and Compliance
description: Analysis of legislation, litigation, and administrative rulings in special education, with an emphasis on teaching expository writing and developing legally sound policies/procedures that ensure educationally meaningful and legally correct education for students with disabilities. BEd in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Introduction to Special Education Assessment
description: Assessment methods and techniques to inform special education decisions, including the use of standardized assessments for initial eligibility, reevaluations, and annual reviews for special education services. BEd in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Introduction to Specialized Instruction
description: Characteristics and educational programming for students with disabilities. Role and responsibilities of the special educator, founding principles and current practices in special education with an emphasis on teaching writing. BEd in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Field Training – Blended ECE
description: Students spend 15 hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled classes; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor.

subject: SPED
title: Young Children with Communication Needs
description: Communication development of infants and young children, ages birth through age 8, with and without disabilities. Assessment and intervention to support the development of communication skills in inclusive community and school environments.

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Student Teaching in Special Education
description: Full-time supervised experience in school. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified.

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Seminar for Student Teachers in Special Education
description: Seminar relating current educational theories with experiences. (B) elementary/ special education; (C) early childhood education/ special education; (D) unclassified.
prereq_raw: requirements for registration listed under “student teaching.”

prereq_tree.text: requirements for registration listed under “student teaching.”

subject: SPED
title: Student Teaching in Special Education Modified
description: Modified student teaching for students from another institution completing student teaching at UH or for students who have prior extensive teaching experience.
prereq_raw: requirements for registration listed under “Student Teaching,” approval of review committee and consent

children.text: requirements for registration listed under “Student Teaching,” approval of review committee

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Field Training in Special Education
description: Students participate in classroom settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by department field supervisor; (B) first semester; (C) second semester, with ethical issues in education discussed and applied in field settings; (D) third semester, with emphasis on writing and oral communication for application in field settings.
prereq_raw: 304 (or concurrent) or consent for (B); 400B for (C); 400C for (D)

subject: SPED
title: Writing for Educational Professionals
description: Instruction on learning to write as professional educators. Strategies for developing and enhancing professional writing for the field of education. Peer and instructor feedback on writing throughout course. Technologies used to assist with writing.

subject: SPED
title: Individuals with Severe Disabilities/ Autism
description: Etiology, characteristics, and development of individuals with severe disabilities and autism; historical, theoretical, and legal issues affecting individuals with severe disabilities and autism; multicultural, family, and consumer issues; professional and ethical issues in providing services.

subject: SPED
title: Education of Gifted Students
description: Characteristics and educational provisions for gifted children and youth with particular attention to psychological aspects of creativity

subject: SPED
title: Education Program for the Gifted/ Talented
description: Utilization and evaluation of teaching/ learning models for gifted/talented students, including consideration of roles, expectancies for learning, and organizational procedures.

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Strategies for Reading Difficulties
description: Overview of methods, programs, and strategies for reading instruction designed to improve the performance of elementary students, grades K-6, who experience difficulties in reading acquisition, fluency, and comprehension. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified.

subject: SPED
title: Vocabulary Comprehension, Fluency & Writing Interventions for Students with Disabilities
description: Development of and intervention for fluent reading vocabulary acquisition, comprehension and writing in students with disabilities. Explicit and systematic instruction of core aspects of reading and writing.

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Partnerships with Families and Professionals
description: Knowledge and skills for relating effectively with families and professionals on behalf of the children and youth with and without disabilities. Coverage of the context in which family members and school personnel interact. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified.

subject: SPED
title: Disability and Diversity in Physical Activity
description: Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience.

subject: SPED
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Elementary
description: Teaching elementary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SPED
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Secondary
description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction. Collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Special Education
description: Study of issues, trends, and research into special education programming and service delivery.

subject: SPED
title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers including criteria for evaluation and planning.
prereq_raw: HDFS 230 (or concurrent) and HDFS 331 (or concurrent), or consent

subject: SPED
title: Preschool Children–Special Needs
description: Examination of application of current research and practices for serving preschool children with special needs.

subject: SPED
title: Physical and Medical Needs-Severe Disabilities/Autism
description: Learning to teach children with physical and health impairments, with a focus on developing independence. Instructional and assistive strategies for meeting the student’s physical and medical needs as well as managing medical conditions. BEd in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Non-School-Age Individuals with Severe Disabilities/Autism
description: Effective planning, instruction, and support for non-school-age individuals (infants, toddlers, and adults) with severe disabilities or ASD across natural environments. BEd in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Secondary Transition-Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Transition planning for youth with disabilities in preparation for postsecondary education, employment, and community living. BEd in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Introduction to Assessment and Instruction-Severe Disabilities/Autism
description: Assessment methods and tools, instructional and assistive strategies, and special procedures to support the participation of students with severe disabilities and autism in inclusive settings. BEd in SPED majors only. (Fall only

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Assessment, Planning, and Instruction for Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate disabilities. Stress on program development to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities into general education environment. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood elementary/special education; (D) unclassified; (E) secondary. BEd in SPED majors only for (E). (Spring only for (E))

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Assessment, Planning, and Instruction for Students with Severe Disabilities/ Autism
description: Techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with severe disabilities/autism. Focus on program development to facilitate the inclusion of students with disabilities into general education settings. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education, emphasis on writing instruction in teaching special education; (D) unclassified.

subject: SPED
title: Inclusive Practices Across the Curriculum-Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Strategies for teaching science, math, and social studies to students with mild/moderate disabilities in secondary settings; selection of appropriate materials, teaching techniques, and curriculum development. BEd in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Assistant-Level Applied Behavior Analysis Fieldwork
description: Field experience in applied behavior analysis at the assistant level supervised by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable nine times, up to 20 credits

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Instructional and Assistive Technology
description: Addresses instructional and assistive technologies for special education and general education settings; technology-based instructional strategies that support inclusion and address academic and behavioral objectives; and application of Universal Design for Learning to support access to the general curriculum for diverse students in the PreK-12 classroom setting. (B) elementary/special education; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time per alpha; repeatable up to six credits for (B)

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Classroom Organization and Management
description: Knowledge and skills related to basic organizational management of an inclusive classroom, including scheduling, grouping, and stress and time management; techniques of applied behavior management, emphasizing behavior change and practical implementation of learning principles. (B) elementary/special education, V credits; (C) early childhood education/special education; (D) unclassified.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable up to six credits for (B)

subject: SPED
title: Theoretical Basis for Teaching Special-Needs Students
description: Survey of biophysical, behavioral, social/ecological, psychodynamic/ psychoeducational, cognitive/developmental, counter-theoretical approaches to teaching exceptional students. Opportunity for the development and/ or strengthening of one’s own theoretical frame of reference.

subject: SPED
title: Characteristics/Strategies for Teaching At-Risk Students
description: Survey of educational, behavioral, and emotional characteristics of students who are at-risk for school failure and strategies to work with such students.

subject: SPED
title: Intensive Behavioral Interventions
description: Principles of behavior, emphasizing positive methods for eliminating significant behavior problems and improving behavior and learning for students with severe disabilities and autism. BEd in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading, research, and/or projects under direct supervision of instructors.
prereq_raw: consent of instructor or department chair

subject: SPED
title: Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education Program Seminar
description: Mandatory program seminar for Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education (PBSPED) teacher candidates; access to tools and skills necessary for distance education program success; Introduction to the Special Education teaching profession. Post-Bac in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Field Experience in Special Education-Post Baccalaureate
description: Students spend between 100-135 hours over a semester in settings appropriate to SPED-PCert program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe/autism); supervision provided by participating teacher and/or college supervisor. Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to 6 credits

subject: SPED
title: Student Teaching in Special EducationPost Baccalaureate Programs
description: Supervised student teaching with a master teacher in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to SPED-Pcert emphasis (mildmoderate, severe/autism); minimum 280 hours in minimum 11 weeks. Supervision by master teacher and university supervisor.

subject: SPED
title: Internship in Special Education-Post Baccalaureate Programs
description: Supervised teaching experience in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to SPED-Pcert program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe/autism); supervision provided by master teacher/university mentor, and university supervisor. Must enroll for two consecutive semesters.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to 14 credits

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Practicum in Special Education
description: For in-service school/community personnel to present new ideas, approaches, instructional methods, materials for teaching exceptional individuals. (B–E) general SPED; (F–G) secondary programming/ SPED; (H–I) bilingual/multicultural/special needs; (J–K) severe disabilities; (M–N) early childhood/ special needs; (O–P) career/vocational/special needs; (Q–R) computer/special needs; (S–T) arts/special needs; (U–W) computer training/special needs; (X–Y) consultant skills/special needs; (Z) Ho‘okoho.

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Practicum in Special Education
description: For in-service school/community personnel to present new ideas, approaches, instructional methods, materials for teaching exceptional individuals. (B–E) general SPED; (F–G) secondary programming/SPED; (H–I) bilingual/multicultural/special needs; (J–K) needs; (Q–R) computer/special needs; (S–T) arts/ special needs; (U–W) computer training/special needs; (X–Y) consultant skills/special needs; (Z) Ho‘okoho.

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Practicum in Special Education
description: For in-service school/community personnel to present new ideas, approaches, instructional methods, materials for teaching exceptional individuals. (B–E) general SPED; (F–G) secondary programming/ SPED; (H–I) bilingual/multicultural/special needs; (J–K) severe disabilities; (M–N) early childhood/ special needs; (O–P) career/vocational/special needs; (Q–R) computer/special needs; (S–T) arts/special needs; (U–W) computer training/special needs; (X–Y) consultant skills/special needs; (Z) Ho‘okoho.

subject: SPED
title: Internship, Special Education
description: Supervised field activities involving the programming and instruction of special-needs students within training programs in Hawai‘i and the Pacific Basin.

subject: SPED
title: Foundations of Exceptionality
description: Theoretical, legal and multicultural foundations for assessing, teaching and developing individual service plans across the lifespan for persons with disabilities.

subject: SPED
title: Instructional/Assistive Technology and Universal Design for Learning
description: Strategies for using instructional and assistive technology, digital tools and media, and Universal Design for Learning to support learning needs of students with disabilities and other diverse learners in the K-12 classroom.

subject: SPED
title: Special Education Law and Compliance
description: Examination of the federal, state, and local government roles in special education with special emphasis on case and regulatory law. Focus on understanding special education law necessary in providing services to students with disabilities in a variety of placements. Appropriate for special/general education teachers, administrators, or related service providers.

subject: SPED
title: Principles of Behavior
description: Principles and laws governing behavior and methods that can be used to accomplish educationally relevant changes in student performance. Emphasis on the conceptual basis for changing behavior and use of technologies for changing behavior in school and community settings.

subject: SPED
title: Collaboration in School and Community Settings
description: Collaboration skills necessary to function as team members and to ensure the success of students with disabilities in inclusive school and community settings.

subject: SPED
title: Language Development for Deaf Children
description: General theories of first and second language development applied to development of ASL and English in deaf children. Relationship of theory to educational practice. Taught in ASL and English.
prereq_raw: admission into Deaf Education program or consent

subject: SPED
title: Audiology and Spoken English for Deaf Students
description: Developmental principles of audiology and speech (i.e., spoken English) will be used to examine assessment procedures and intervention strategies appropriate to deaf students in a variety of educational placements. Classroom applications will be presented. Taught in ASL and English.
prereq_raw: admission into Deaf Education program or consent

subject: SPED
title: Literacy Development for Deaf Students
description: Basic concepts related to language, language development and recognition of language-related learning problems of deaf students; strategies for teaching reading and writing to deaf students.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Bilingual Deaf Education
description: Study of issues, trends and methods in ASL/ English bilingual education for deaf students. Taught in ASL and English.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Assessment and Curriculum Development–Deaf
description: Assessment methods and techniques used with deaf students that emphasize the bond between curriculum-based assessment and curriculum-based programming through planning and providing cyclical instruction across content areas based on ongoing diagnostic assessment. Taught in ASL and English.

subject: SPED
title: Methods and Strategies for Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Techniques for providing effective instruction including: best instructional practice, lesson planning, teacher-directed and student-mediated instructional strategies, and curricular approaches for working with students with mild/moderate disabilities.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Assessment and Curriculum Development
description: Assessment methods and techniques that emphasize the bond between curriculum-based assessment and curriculum-based programming. Planning and cyclical instruction across content areas based on ongoing diagnostic assessment.

subject: SPED
title: Assessment and Instruction—Severe Disabilities and Autism
description: Basic principles of assessment, instruction, and curriculum development; application of formal and informal assessment procedures for goal selection, formulating instructional plans, and adapting instructional materials to accommodate learning needs of students with severe disabilities and autism.

subject: SPED
title: Family-Centered Approaches in Deaf Education
description: Prepare teachers to deliver family-centered home-based services to families of deaf children using the SKI-HI model. Course will be taught in ASL and English.

subject: SPED
title: Collaboration–Working with Deaf Students in Inclusive Settings
description: Collaboration skills for working with general education teachers, specialists, paraprofessionals, families and community members to support the success of deaf students in inclusive settings. Taught in ASL and English.

subject: SPED
title: Transition Strategies for Deaf Students
description: Collaborative model for facilitating the transition of deaf and hard-of-hearing students to develop appropriate transition plans and effective plans of study. Taught in ASL and English.

subject: SPED
title: Adaptations and Special ProceduresStudents/Severe Disabilities/Autism
description: Adaptations and special intervention procedures to support the participation of individuals with severe motor, communication, and/or adaptive behavior disabilities in inclusive school and community settings. Includes lab work.

subject: SPED
title: Strategies Across Content Area
description: Strategies for teaching math, science, and social sciences to students of all ages with mild/moderate disabilities; selection of appropriate materials, teaching techniques, curriculum development.

subject: SPED
title: Language Arts Strategies: Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Basic concepts related to language, language development, and recognition of language-related learning problems of students with mild/moderate disabilities; strategies for teaching language arts curricula (listening, speaking, reading, writing) to students of all ages with learning problems.

subject: SPED
title: Children’s Literature for Deaf Students
description: Introduction to English literature translated into American Sign Language (ASL) including discussion of ASL literature genres, the importance of translation, selection of literature; story reading, book reading, and retelling. Taught in ASL.

subject: SPED
title: Teaching Skills for Social Competence
description: Issues in social development, self-determination, and social skills competence training for children and youth with disabilities; experience in group social skills training and development of individualized programs.
prereq_raw: either 485 or 630, and either 611 or 614; or consent

subject: SPED
title: Field Experiences in Special Education
description: Students spend a minimum of nine hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Practicum
description: Supervised education/community experiences; minimum of 20 hours weekly with special-needs population (MR, LD, SED, SMH); pre-school through postsecondary settings (public/private). Related seminar or equivalent and completion of SPED core required.

subject: SPED
title: Internship
description: Supervised education/ community experiences with special needs populations, preschool through postsecondary settings.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to six credits

subject: SPED
title: Clinical Practice Special Projects
description: Development and implementation of a field-based research professional development project under the direction of the student’s advisor; limited to students enrolled in the interdisciplinary program.

subject: SPED
title: Positive Behavioral Support-Severe Disabilities and Autism
description: Principles and laws governing human behavior and positive methods for eliminating significant behavior problems for students with severe disabilities and autism. Emphasis on the functions of behavior, experimental techniques for documenting behavior change, and the use of technologies for improving behavior in school and community settings.

subject: SPED
title: Early Intervention for Special Populations
description: Issues important to early childhood special education. Early screening and assessment, working with families, curriculum options/models, program evaluation.

subject: SPED
title: Language/Communication Intervention-Communication Disorders/Autism
description: Current research in normal language learning, assessment, planning, implementation, evaluation of language delayed/disordered children, including children with autism. Procedures for attaining language/functional communication objectives using ongoing routines/activities.

subject: SPED
title: Motor Development/Intervention for Students with Severe Disabilities
description: Normal/ abnormal motor development; description/etiology of physically disabling conditions influencing motor development; analysis/application of assessment/intervention strategies to promote motor development; positioning and handling skills.

subject: SPED
title: Inclusive Physical Activity
description: Advanced knowledge on issues of socio-cultural, learning styles, diversity, and exceptionalities, and how these influence instruction, engagement, and behavior in physical activity settings across the lifespan.

subject: SPED
title: Procedures for Early Childhood Special Education
description: Assessment and intervention strategies to promote behavior change with young children with disabilities. Promoting child skill gains and integrated programming options.

subject: SPED
title: Topics and Issues in Reading Difficulties
description: Introduction of foundational knowledge of language and literacy development. Current topics and issues related to literacy development in students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties.

subject: SPED
title: Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
description: Introduction of basic linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for beginning or struggling readers. Covers evidence-based practices for teaching literacy to students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
description: Advanced linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for older students. Covers diagnostic assessment, planning, instruction, and progress monitoring for students with Dyslexia or related reading difficulties.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar on Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: Study of issues, research, program development in the area of mild/moderate disabilities.

subject: SPED
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Issues in Special Education
description: Seminar on issues, trends, research, and program development in the field of special education. (B) current issues and trends; (C) technology; (D) foundations; (E) developmental disabilities; (F) cultural and linguistic diversity; (G) evidence-based practices; (H) single case research.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time per alpha, repeatable two times for (H)

subject: SPED
title: Seminar on Applied Research/Special Education
description: Study and development of applied research topics in special education.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar on Severe/Multiple Disabilities
description: Research, program development trends/issues in the area of severe/multiple disabilities (birth through adulthood). College of Education majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Early Childhood Special Education
description: Study of issues/trends. Research and program development in early childhood special education.
prereq_raw: (631 and 635) with a minimum grade of B- or better, or consent

subject: SPED
title: Leadership in Special Education
description: Seminar on topics related to leadership in the field of special education, including issues for teacher leaders, administrators, and teacher preparation personnel.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar on Universal Design for Learning
description: Seminar on issues of research and practice on the application of universal design for learning in K-12 and higher education settings. Focus on culturally and linguistically diverse students diversity, non-traditional students and students with disabilities.

subject: SPED
title: Transition/Supported Employment
description: Transition planning for youth with disabilities in preparation for employment as adults in private and public sector businesses.

subject: SPED
title: Reading Assessment & Tiered Intervention for Students with Disabilities
description: Selection and administration of formal and informal assessments within a problem-solving model for designing robust reading instruction for struggling readers. Guiding planning and reading intervention using data-based decision-making. Graduate students only.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Diagnostic-Prescriptive Reading Intervention
description: Structural and functional features of reading development using diagnostic-prescriptive reading intervention. Advanced diagnostic-prescriptive intervention selection and design for students with reading disabilities using tool-component-composite analysis. Graduate students only.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)

subject: SPED
title: Ethics and Professional Conduct
description: Focuses on content on the Behavior Analysis Certification Board’s code for ethical conduct as well as advanced concepts, principles, and processes of applied behavior analysis.

subject: SPED
title: Applied Behavior Analysis Fieldwork
description: Field experience in applied behavior analysis supervised by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.

subject: SPED

subject: SPED
title: Plan B Master’s Project

subject: SPED
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading/research.

subject: SPED
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Exceptionalities
description: Current and historical topics, issues, and trends in the field of exceptionalities.

subject: SPED
title: Doctoral Internship

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Introduction to Teaching, Elementary

Developing knowledgeable, effective, caring professionals to support student’s academic, social, emotional, physical needs. Emphasis on writing instruction; lecture/lab; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Principles and Methods of Reading Instruction
description: First of two methods courses focusing on theories and research-based practices related to reading instruction in elementary classrooms. Emphasis on writing instruction; lecture/lab; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Principles and Methods of Writing Instruction
description: Second of two methods courses focusing on theories and research-based practices related to writing instruction in elementary classrooms. Emphasis on writing instruction; lecture/lab; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

subject: STE
title: Field Training – Blended ECE
description: Students spend 15 hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled classes; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor.

subject: STE
title: Field Experience

repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times or up to 9 credits per alpha

subject: STE
title: Child Development from Prenatal Through Age Eight
description: Growth and development of children from prenatal through age eight. Historical and current issues through a research-based ecological, cross-cultural perspective. Focus on children’s optimal development and how this informs teaching practices in early education.

subject: STE
title: Children’s Literature

subject: STE
title: Instructional and Assessment Methods for Multilingual Learners

subject: STE
title: Social Studies and Science in Early Childhood Education
description: Assessment, instructional methods, and materials for teaching social studies and science to children in preschool through grade 3. Emphasis on developmentally appropriate practices and lesson planning for teaching social studies and science.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Social Studies, Elementary
description: Purposes, methods, curriculum, and assessment in teaching social studies. Focus: enriching children’s understanding of the communities of which they are a part through inquiry, investigation, collaboration, and expository skills. Emphasis on writing instruction; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Science, Elementary
description: Science education in elementary school; methods and materials; laboratory activities selected from new science curricula; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education. Each alpha
repeatable_raw: repeatable one time, up to 3 credits

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Mathematics, Elementary
description: Inquiry-based approach to concepts and algorithms of whole numbers and introduction to geometry/ measurement. Laboratory experiences with appropriate manipulatives; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Mathematics, Elementary II
description: Inquiry-based approach to concepts and algorithms of fractions, decimals, graphing, and probability and statistics. Laboratory experiences with appropriate manipulatives; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Visual Art, Elementary
description: Scope and organization of art in pK-6 school curriculum, creative use of art media through laboratory experience; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

subject: STE
title: Curriculum, Materials, and Assessment Development for Multilingual Learners

subject: STE
title: Responsive Pedagogy for Multilingual Learners
description: Introduction to the teaching of multilingual learners (MLL) in an elementary school context. Teacher candidates will learn specific strategies and methods for teaching non-native speakers of English.

subject: STE

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Personal and Social K-6 Health Skills
description: Standards-based planning, teaching, assessment in health education. Developing interactive learning opportunities to teach personal and social responsibility for health through curriculum integration. Training, practice and evaluation of oral communication skills; (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary education.

subject: STE

subject: STE

subject: STE

subject: STE
title: Teaching Marketing and Distribution

subject: STE

description: Goals, concepts, literature, materials, procedures, and evaluation for teaching music in grades K–6. For students in elementary education. Not intended for elementary music majors.

subject: STE

description: Concepts and methods to develop sensitivity and awareness of cultural influences on behaviors related to schooling. description: With student teaching as context, examination of knowledge, skills, and dispositions for teaching; standards-based planning, teaching, assessment, and reflection; inclusive classroom management; professional growth and development; integration of research, theory, and practice. Emphasis on writing instruction and ethical issues in teaching. (B) dual preparation in ECE and elementary education; (C) elementary (2); (D) secondary; (M) dual preparation in elementary education and multilingual learning (2); (S) dual preparation in elementary and special education (1).

subject: STE

description: Field experience in early childhood settings to facilitate young children’s growth and learning.

title: Foundations of Early Childhood Education, Ages 3–8
description: Planning child-centered, responsive programs for children. Focuses on play, learning environments, integrated thematic instructional design, guidance, assessment, and family engagement in early childhood and early elementary to promote enjoyment, growth, and development.

title: Supervision of Student Teaching
description: Principles and methods; role of supervisor; human resources supervision in student teaching. Open to teachers interested in pre-service teacher education.

title: Family and Community Centered Programs
description: Knowledge and appreciation for the complex characteristics of children, families, and communities. Analysis and development of skills for creating respectful, reciprocal relationships with diverse children and families from diverse backgrounds. Lecture/lab.
prereq_raw: 318 (or concurrent), or HDFS 331 (or concurrent), or consent

subject: STE
title: Advanced Supervision of Student Teaching
description: Advanced principles and methods: clinical supervision, observation recording, analysis, interpretation of classroom teaching; human resources supervision in student teaching.

subject: STE

description: Historical and philosophical foundations of vocational technical education, overview of federal and state legislation and contemporary practices. Special emphasis on vocational education program in Hawai‘i.

subject: STE
title: Office and Marketing Technology
description: Understanding and use of word processing, spreadsheet, and database software for business applications. Explore software across the office and marketing content areas.

subject: STE
title: Multicultural and Social Justice Education
description: Exploring social justice and multilingual, multicultural education with attention to Hawai‘i as our place of learning and teaching.

subject: STE
title: Hawaiian Studies, Methods
description: Examination of issues in Hawaiian and U.S. views of education and their application to the teaching of Hawaiian studies. Field experience required.
prereq_raw: 312C, 312D; or consent. Co-requisite for BEd students: 317

subject: STE
title: Education of Exceptional Children in Regular Classroom
description: Practices that facilitate teaching special needs students in regular classrooms. Techniques for meeting academic needs, managing behavior, motivating students, increasing peer interactions, communication between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: STE
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms, Secondary
description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: STE
title: Issues in Computer Education
description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education.

subject: STE
title: Directed Activity
description: Individual work supervised by instructor. May consist of reading, research, teaching, and/or projects.

title: Common Core State Standards in ELA: Content and Curriculum for Teachers
description: Professional development for K-12 teachers to upgrade their knowledge of ELA content and develop their instructional strategies to be consistent with the ELA practices of the Common Core State Standards.

subject: STE
title: Common Core State Standards in Mathematics: Content and Curriculum for Teachers
description: Professional development for K-12 teachers to upgrade their knowledge of mathematics content and develop their instructional strategies to be consistent with the mathematical practices of the Common Core State Standards.
