title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research.

subject: CEE
title: Surveying/Geodesy/Geomatics
description: Plane surveying for cadastral, engineering, and construction applications including taping, leveling, traverses, bearings and azimuths, areas and volumes, EDM. Geodesy, map projections, satellite geodesy (GPS), geodetic surveying and photogrammetry. Field lab in notes and procedures. Restricted to CEE majors. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: CEE
title: CAD/BIM/3D Visualization
description: Computer-aided drafting (CAD) tools using AutoCAD and Revit. AutoCAD interface, titleblocks, model/paper space, viewports, texts and annotation, dimensioning. Basics of BIM, toolbox, modeling techniques, annotating, dimensioning. CAD drafting to real-world engineering applications. Restricted to CEE majors.

subject: CEE
title: Applied Mechanics I
description: Forces, resultants, and equilibrium; analysis of trusses, frames, and machines; centroids, moments of inertia; friction.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of the following: PHYS 170; MATH 242 or 252A; and either MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

children.text: grade of C or better in all of the following: PHYS 170

subject: CEE
title: Applied Mechanics II
description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy.
prereq_raw: C or better in 270; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)
restrictions_raw: CE, CNST, ENGS, ME majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Applied Probability and Statistics
description: Description of sample data; correlation and regression; probability and statistical distributions; estimations of population parameters; fitting distributions to histograms; hypothesis testing.

subject: CEE
title: Fluid Mechanics Fundamentals
description: Compressible and incompressible fluid properties; fluid statics; kinematics, energy and momentum considerations in steady flows; application of steady flow concepts to various fluid processes; with an emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Engineering
description: Parameters and indices of environmental quality; materials balances; chemical kinetics; ideal reactor models; water and air pollution control; solid and hazardous waste management; emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

subject: CEE
title: Geotechnical Engineering I
description: Introduction to geotechnical engineering: soil characterization, index properties, seepage and flow in soil, stresses in soils, compressibility, consolidation, shear strength. Substantial emphasis on writing lab reports.

subject: CEE
title: Fundamentals of Transportation
description: Transportation modes: land, air, water, pipelines. Tourist, urban transportation. Geometric design, human factors, vehicular flow models, capacity analysis. Overview: traffic impact, air quality, parking studies.

subject: CEE
title: Mechanics of Solids
description: Introduction to analysis and design of deformable bodies subject to loading. Stress, strain, constitutive relation, axially loading, torsion, statically indeterminate systems, Mohr’s circle, failure criteria, buckling, defection due to axial, shear, torsional, and flexural loading.
prereq_raw: C or better in all of the following: 270; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

subject: CEE
title: Mechanics of Materials Lab
description: Tension, compression, and torsion of bars, and bending of beams.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Materials
description: Concrete properties, role of aggregates, concrete mix design, supplementary cementitious materials, chemical admixtures, behavior of concrete, concrete testing, field practices. Emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: 305 (or concurrent); and 370 with a minimum grade of C or better

subject: CEE
title: Structural Analysis
description: Analysis of statically determinate plane and space trusses and frames; deflections; introduction to matrix methods; computer applications.
prereq_raw: 370 with a minimum grade of C or better

subject: CEE
title: Engineering Economics
description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decision-making, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 (with a minimum grade of C-) or 130 (with a minimum grade of C-), and senior standing
restrictions_raw: BENG, CE, CEM, CNST, ECE, and ME majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Computer Methods in Engineering Systems
description: Numerical solutions of engineering problems using digital computers. Regression analysis; numerical differentiation and integration; solutions of algebraic, transcendental, and differential equations; and analysis of large structural systems.

subject: CEE
title: Engineering Hydraulics
description: Hydraulics of closed conduits and open channels with emphasis on engineering applications. Topics also include pump hydraulics, bridge hydraulics, urban drainage engineering, and flood plain management.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
description: Introduction to basic concepts of pollutant transport phenomenon through theoretical modeling, lab and field experiments and observations. Specific topics include mass balance, jets and plumes, mixing and transport in rivers, reservoirs, groundwater and estuaries; non point course pollution.

subject: CEE
title: Applied Hydrology
description: Surface water hydrology topics include hydrologic cycle, hydrographs, regression methods, urban rain-runoff process, flood frequency analysis, flood routing and hydrology for detention basin design. Groundwater hydrology topics include seawater intrusion, theory of groundwater flow and solutions to steady and unsteady aquifer flows.

subject: CEE
title: Water and Wastewater Engineering
description: Hydrologic fundamentals of water demand and supply; water and wastewater distribution; collection systems; quality characterization; analytical methods for water quality management.

subject: CEE
title: Water/Wastewater Treatment Design
description: Physical operations, chemical and biological processes, design flow and process loading rates, pilot plant testing, and treatment plant design.

subject: CEE
title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation.

subject: CEE
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro.

subject: CEE
title: Infrastructure: Project Impacts, Policy and Sustainability
description: Evaluation of infrastructure impacts. Impacts regulation and mitigation. Effects of environmental and other policies on infrastructure. Infrastructure relations to sustainability. Energy consumption, transportation efficiency and infrastructure recycling. Lectures and presentations by experts and enrolled students. Senior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: senior standing, open to engineering, science, urban planning, and economics majors

children.text: open to engineering, science, urban planning,

subject: CEE
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. Senior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Geotechnical Engineering II
description: Continuation of 355 field exploration, lateral earth pressures, bearing capacity theory, slope stability, use of geosynthetics.

subject: CEE
title: Pavement Engineering
description: Design principles of flexible and rigid pavements; HMA mixture design, equipment and construction; and application of life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) in pavement engineering. Includes laboratory sessions for aggregate testing and Superpave mix design.

subject: CEE
title: Traffic Engineering
description: Design/analysis of signalized, unsignalized intersections, urban networks. Traffic impact studies; analysis steps and applications. Design/redesign options. Parking studies: demand, alternative designs (lot layouts).

subject: CEE
title: Urban and Regional Transportation Planning
description: Application of travel demand forecasting models to transportation planning. Evaluation and decision-making. Term projects.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Methods
description: Methods of construction, primarily buildings. Construction types: light and heavy wood; steel; plain, reinforced, and prestressed concrete; masonry. Foundations; associated details of frames, walls, roofs, floors, openings, finishes. Disasters, failures, and their causes. Industrialization of the building process.
restrictions_raw: CE, CEM, CNST, ECE, ME majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Project Management
description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor.
restrictions_raw: CE, CEM, CNST, ECE, and ME majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Equipment and Methods
description: Methods and equipment used on horizontal/ heavy engineering projects. Available equipment, their production, and how they are used to excavate, move, process, and place the earth.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Estimating and Bidding
description: Estimating science; techniques of estimating quantities and pricing of work for construction contracting; classification of costs, analysis of plans and specifications for estimating; computerized estimating; cash flow, bidding strategy, preparation and submission.
restrictions_raw: CEE, CNST, ECE, ME, OE majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Planning and Scheduling
description: To teach the theory and the practice of planning, scheduling, and reporting a construction project through the use of bar chart and CPM. Format to include lectures, text, outside speakers, site visits, discussions, case study, and computers.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Safety
description: Safety and health concepts, laws and requirements for civilian and contractor personnel in construction, including applications in project management and construction activities.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Law
description: In-depth exploration of the legal regimes governing construction. Construction contracts, contractors, and subcontractors. Breach of contracts, claims and litigation in construction projects. Senior standing or higher.

subject: CEE
title: Undergraduate Structural Research
description: Individual research project for undergraduate students in the structures track. Topic to be determined by consultation with structural faculty advisor.

subject: CEE
title: Structural Loads
description: Introduction to the minimum load requirements for buildings and other structures used in current structural design codes. Derive and apply dead, live, rain, soil, snow, wind, earthquake, flood, inundation, and other loads to structural systems.

subject: CEE
title: Reinforced Concrete Design
description: Behavior and design of reinforced concrete beams, one-way slabs and columns. Laboratory section includes design and hands-on manufacturing and testing of reinforced concrete members.

subject: CEE
title: Structural Steel Design
description: Basic properties of steel; behavior and design of steel beams, columns, and connections; introduction to rigid frames.

subject: CEE
title: Senior Design Project & Professional Ethics
description: Design problem involving several areas of civil engineering and requiring a team approach for a solution. Oral communication skills are assessed through multiple presentations to an industry. Engineering ethics, ethical decision making and deliberation. CEE or CNST majors only. Senior standing only.

subject: CEE
title: Senior Design Project
description: (Lec/Lab) Design problem involving several areas of civil engineering and requiring a team approach for a solution. Oral communication skills will be assessed through multiple presentations to an industry panel.
prereq_raw: senior standing in CEE or CNST and 489B

subject: CEE
title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
description: Will reflect special interests of visiting and/or permanent faculty.
prereq_raw: junior or senior standing, and consent

subject: CEE
title: Special Problems
description: Individual investigation in civil and environmental engineering topics as approved by instructor.
prereq_raw: senior standing, and minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum GPA of 3.0 in engineering

subject: CEE
title: Master’s Plan B/C Studies
description: CR/NC only

subject: CEE
title: Operations Management
description: Linear programming, simplex method, graphical representation: dual; degeneracy; transportation problem; assignment problems; data envelopment analysis; applications; case studies; managerial reporting; LINDO software. Graduate students only.
prereq_raw: 476 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B-), and consent

children.text: ( or equivalent) ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , and consent

subject: CEE
title: Cost Engineering and Quality Control
description: Study and applications of cost/schedule control systems criteria, earned value analysis, probabilistic cost estimating, construction risk management, construction quality control, and operations research in construction.

subject: CEE
title: Machine Learning in Civil and Environmental Engineering and Earth Science
description: Statistical machine learning and deep learning methods. Script languages for data-driven model training, validation and test. Analysis with linear algebra and statistics. Applications to engineering and earth science problems.
prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of Python Programming desirable

subject: CEE
title: Risk Analysis and Decision Making
description: Risk analysis and decision making are fundamental areas of construction and project management. Students will benefit from analyzing risks and learning various decision making techniques for real-time applications.

subject: CEE
title: Negotiation and Alternative Dispute Resolution
description: Lawyers negotiate settlements in almost all their cases. This class presents a “hands-on,” skill-building approach to the newest ideas, as well as centuries-old techniques, about the skill lawyers will use most often in their private practice-negotiation. The class also examines the rapidly developing field of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), including mediation, facilitation, arbitration, and court-annexed ADR.

subject: CEE
title: Parallel Computing for Engineers
description: Concepts and techniques in high performance parallel computing. Topics include parallel language and algorithms, parallelizing pre-existing serial codes, statistical analysis, and techniques up to increase computational speed and accuracy for problems requiring large memory size.

subject: CEE
title: Organizations: Theory and Change
description: Explores characteristics and structural, human resources, political, and cultural frames of organizational theory. Focus on organizational change strategies and theories. Discusses how to use these frames and theories in everyday management of public service organizations. Graduate students only.
restrictions_raw: BE, CEE, ECE, ME majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk.
prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable

subject: CEE
title: Fluid Mechanics
description: Theory of fluid dynamics in differential form, covering equation of motion, vortex generation, flow in rotating frame, potential theory, laminar flow, and introduction to turbulence.

subject: CEE
title: Groundwater Modeling
description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation.

subject: CEE
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change.

subject: CEE
title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
description: Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

subject: CEE
title: Surface Water Hydrology
description: Deterministic and probabilistic methods include reliability of empirical distributions, multiple regression analysis, extreme value analysis and domain of attraction. Short-memory models for stochastic simulation of streamflows include autoregressive, Markov chain and moving average models. Time series analysis of hydrologic data is discussed.

subject: CEE
title: Groundwater Hydrology
description: Groundwater occurrence, movement, quality, and resource evaluation, development, and management. Emphasis on saltwater encroachment, well evaluation, aquifer protection, recharge with wastewater, and Hawai‘i type hydrology.

subject: CEE
title: Physical and Chemical Treatment
description: Introduction to physical and chemical processes for water and wastewater treatment: Review of momentum and mass transfer, chemical reactions, colloidal chemistry, coagulation and flocculation, granular filtration, sedimentation, carbon adsorption, gas transfer, disinfection and oxidation.

subject: CEE
title: Biological Treatment
description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Chemistry
description: Basic concepts of chemistry as related to the environment, with more emphasis on water. Topics include chemical kinetics, equilibrium, acid-base, precipitation and dissolution redox reactions, sorption, organic chemicals in the environment.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Microbiology
description: Combined lecture-discussion on major topics in environmental microbiology, microbial ecology, and a broad understanding of microbial processes in natural and engineered environments.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in CEE or consent

subject: CEE
title: Applied Mathematics for Engineers
description: Application of advanced mathematics to engineering phenomena; linear algebra, Eigen systems; partial differentiation and multiple integrals; vector/tensor analysis; Fourier series/transforms and Laplace transform; ordinary/partial differential equations; probability and statistics. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: fall)
restrictions_raw: CE, ME, ORE, and ECE majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Hazardous Waste Remediation
description: Introduces the national problems dealing with the contamination of groundwater and presents remedial measures. Such measures include pump and treat (PAT) technology, in-situ bioremediation, soil vapor extraction, air sparging, electrokinetics, hydraulic fracturing, reactive walls, and phytoremediation.

subject: CEE
title: Water Quality Modeling
description: Mathematical formulation of pollutant transport and mixing in the water environment. Kinetics formulation and parameter identification, model calibration and verification. Design projects.

subject: CEE
title: Membrane Separations
description: Applications of membrane separations to desalination, power generation, and ultrapure water systems. Discussion of reverse osmosis, osmosis-driven processes, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, electrodialysis and ion exchange technologies. Membrane fouling and concentration polarization from practical/theoretical standpoints.

subject: CEE
title: Seepage, Drainage, and Dewatering
description: Theory of seepage, field and laboratory methods of measurement; graphical and numerical methods; design of drainage structures; construction dewatering.

subject: CEE
title: Deep Foundations
description: Analysis and design of deep foundations; driven piles and drilled shafts.
prereq_raw: 355 (with a minimum grade of D) and 455 (with a minimum grade of D)

subject: CEE
title: Numerical Methods in Geotechnical Engineering
description: Finite element and finite difference formulation and analyses to solve problems in geotechnical engineering. Also covers constitutive modelling.
prereq_raw: 355 (with a minimum grade of C) and 455 (with a minimum grade of C), or consent

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
description: Soil continuum mechanics principles; elastic, plastic, and Cam clay soil behavior; critical state and strength; interpretation of laboratory test results.

subject: CEE
title: Slope and Earth Structures
description: Classification of landslides and triggering mechanisms; field investigation procedures; limit equilibrium slope stability methods; numerical techniques; seepage and dynamic considerations; case studies.

subject: CEE
title: Marine Geotechnics
description: Principles of geotechnical engineering applied to marine environments; marine geology; surveying and sampling methods; seabed sediment types, properties, and behavior; coastal and offshore foundations.

subject: CEE
title: Earth Pressures
description: Estimation of lateral earth pressures; analysis and design of retaining walls and excavation support systems.
prereq_raw: 355 (with a minimum grade of D) and 455 (with a minimum grade of D)

subject: CEE
title: Systems Analysis for Engineers
description: Optimization used in design and management of systems for minimizing resources or optimizing outcomes. Evaluation of alternatives, economic efficiency and effectiveness analysis. Logistics. Open to engineering students. Computer applications and labs.

subject: CEE
title: Intelligent Transportation Systems
description: Definition, technologies and their attributes. Analysis and implementation based on FHWA’s User Services. Automated incident detection algorithms. Machine vision applications to traffic engineering.

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Transportation Modeling and Statistics
description: Demand modeling, discrete choice and activity-based modeling. Demand forecasting by simulation. Transportation surveys and sampling methods. Application of cluster, factor, regression, logistic and ARIMA analyses to transportation.

subject: CEE
title: Pavement Design and Rehabilitation
description: Pavement engineering with emphasis given to understanding fundamental issues such as historical development of pavement design, approaches used for design of new pavements and overlays, understanding of construction issues and their effects on pavement performance, and various design factors: environmental, loading and materials characterization. Introduction of pavement management systems.

subject: CEE
title: Continuum Mechanics
description: Cartesian tensors in mechanics; coordinate transformations; analysis of stress and strain; principal values, invariants, equilibrium and compatibility equations; constitutive relations; field equations. Problems in elasticity.

subject: CEE
title: Project Management Systems
description: Project integration and PMIS; organizational power; conflict, strategic, and life-cycle management in construction management; matrix structure compared to projectized structure; project success; team building; change and culture in construction organizations; competitive bidding.

subject: CEE
title: Negotiation
description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations.

subject: CEE
title: Structural Dynamics I
description: Response of single and multi degree-of-freedom systems due to dynamic forces. Direct integration of equations of motion. Response spectrum analysis. Application to earthquake loading. Systems with distributed mass and elasticity.

subject: CEE
title: Structural Dynamics II
description: Elastic and inelastic response of structures due to earthquakes. Seismic design criteria. Code design procedures. Advanced topics in time- and frequency-domain dynamic analysis of structures.

subject: CEE
title: Smart Structures Technology
description: Fundamentals of sensor technologies for structural engineering applications. Control devices and strategies for protection of structures against extreme events, i.e. earthquakes, strong winds, etc. Structural health monitoring and smart sensor networks. Smart materials for civil structures.

subject: CEE
title: Modern Structural Analysis
description: Fundamentals of modern structural analysis theory, with emphasis on frame structures. Virtual work. Member stiffness/flexibility. Matrix formulation of stiffness and flexibility methods. Computer modeling issues.

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete Design
description: Slender columns; biaxial bending; combined shear and torsion. Building lateral load resisting frame analysis and design—shearwalls, rigid frames. Floor system analysis and design—flat slabs, joist systems. Computer applications.

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Structural Steel Design
description: Load and resistance factored design (LRFD); steel building modeling and analysis; moment-resisting frames; bracing systems; beam-columns; moment connections; composite construction; and plate girders.

subject: CEE
title: Finite Elements in Structures
description: Finite element method in structural engineering. Extension of structural theory. Virtual work. One- two-, and three-dimensional elements; axisymmetric elements; plate bending. Application to linear problems.

subject: CEE
title: Prestressed Concrete
description: Behavior of prestressed concrete members, including prestress losses. Analysis and design of prestressed beams, slabs, and composite sections. Anchorage zone design; continuous systems.

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Concrete Technology
description: Composition and hydration of concrete, chemical, and mineral admixtures, fresh and hardened properties, mix proportions, high performance concretes, durability and retrofitting technology, non-destructive testing, and advanced material characterization techniques. Graduate students only.

subject: CEE
title: Seminar in Civil and Environmental Engineering
description: Discussions and reports on literature, research, developments and activities in civil engineering. One unit of all graduate students for each graduate degree. Student presentations are required.

subject: CEE
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in CEE or consent

subject: CEE
title: Selected Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
description: Highly specialized topics in structures, soils, hydraulics, sanitary, water resources, applied mechanics, transportation.

subject: CEE
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: CEE
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.
prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD in civil engineering

prereq_tree.text: candidacy for PhD in civil engineering

subject: ECE
title: Electrical Engineering Skills
description: Electrical engineering subjects in a skill acquisition context at the freshman level. Learning, creative problem solving, brainstorming, technical information assimilation, and presentation skills development.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Engineering Computation
description: Engineering problem solving using MATLAB. Basic programming concepts include input/output, branching, looping, functions, file input/output, and data structures such as arrays and structures. Matrix operations for solving linear equations. Engineering computations and visualization.
prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent

subject: ECE
title: Programming for Engineers
description: Introduction to computer programming and modern computing environments with an emphasis on algorithm and program design, implementation, and debugging. Includes a hands-on laboratory to develop and practice programming skills.
prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent
restrictions_raw: BENG, CE, CENG, ECE, ME, PREN, CNST, and ENGS majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Freshman Project
description: Freshman level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. This project provides early student entry into ECE hands-on project activity providing practical skills, ECE subject exposure and experience. Second semester freshman standing required.
restrictions_raw: CENG, ECE, and PREN majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Object Oriented Programming
description: Second programming for computer engineers. System programming language, such as C. Object-oriented programming paradigm, definition and use of classes, fundamentals of object-oriented design, such as C++. Common data structures. Common searching and sorting algorithms.
restrictions_raw: CEE, ECE, ME, PREN majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Basic Circuit Analysis I
description: Linear passive circuits, time domain analysis, transient and steady-state responses, phasors, impedance and admittance; power and energy, frequency responses, resonance.
prereq_raw: MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253 (or concurrent), and PHYS 272 (or concurrent); or consent
restrictions_raw: BENG, CE, CENG, ECE, ME, PREN, and ENGS majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Basic Circuit Analysis II
description: Laplace transforms and their application to circuits, Fourier transforms and their applications to circuits, frequency selective circuits, introduction to and design of active filters, convolution, and state space analysis of circuits.
prereq_raw: 211, and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Digital Design
description: Introduction to the design of digital systems with an emphasis on design methods and the implementation and use of fundamental digital components.

subject: ECE
title: Sophomore Project
description: Sophomore level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills.
restrictions_raw: CENG, ECE, and PREN majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Signal and Systems Analysis
description: Discrete-time and continuous time signals and systems, linear systems, convolution, Fourier series, Fourier transform, sampling.
prereq_raw: 213 and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A; or consent

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits I
description: Semiconductor structures, operating principles and characteristics of diodes and amplifying devices. Their application as circuit elements in building basic digital, analog, and integrated circuit subsystems.

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits I Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments on linear and logic properties of diodes and transistor networks.

subject: ECE
title: Physical Electronics
description: Review of quantum mechanics fundamentals, H-atom, and chemical bonding. Introduction to band structure models and materials. Semiconductor doping, charge carrier statistics and charge transport, including ambipolar transport. Metal-semiconductor and PN junctions.
prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A, and PHYS 274; or consent

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits II
description: Principles and design of linear electronic circuits including differential, operational, feedback, and tuned amplifiers; integrated circuits, current mirrors, signal generators, filters, and stability.

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits II Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 326, experiments on linear and analog electronics. Includes an emphasis on writing laboratory reports.

subject: ECE
title: Theory and Design of IC Devices
description: Band structure models and carrier transport physics review. Theory and design of semiconductor IC devices: Schottky diodes, bipolar devices (PN junction diodes, BJTs), FETs (MOSFETs, JFETs, and MESFETs).
prereq_raw: 324 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A; or consent

subject: ECE
title: Microcircuit Fabrication
description: Technology principles, materials, and methods for the design and fabrication of semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, and microelectromechanical systems.

subject: ECE
title: Microcircuit Fabrication Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on laboratory where students make various electronic and electromechanical micro-devices using IC technology. Devices are also tested and analyzed.

subject: ECE
title: Probability and Statistics
description: Probability, statistics, random variables, distributions, densities, expectations, limit theorems, and applications to electrical engineering.
prereq_raw: 315 (or concurrent) and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A; or consent

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Communication Systems
description: Signal representation, Fourier analysis; amplitude and angle modulated systems; sampling theorems, pulse and digital modulation systems; carrier modulation by digital signals.

subject: ECE
title: Communication Systems Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of communication systems. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.

subject: ECE
title: Networking I
description: Covers 4 semesters from the Cisco Networking Academy plus supplementary material; hands-on experience with routers and switches; prepares students for the CCNA. Topics include TCP/IP, LANs, WANs, routing protocols, network security; PPP; ISDN, frame relay.

subject: ECE
title: Linear Algebra and Machine Learning
description: Mathematical and algorithmic fundamentals of linear algebra and their applications and illustrations to machine learning. Lab introduces programming with data and uses machine learning libraries for an introduction to commonly used technologies.
restrictions_raw: MATH, ECE, CENG, CECE, ME, ICS majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems
description: Analysis/design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.

subject: ECE
title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Provides experience in applying theoretical tools to analyze linear systems. Extensive use is made of computer-aided analysis and design packages study system performance.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Systems and Computer Design
description: Design methodology, processor design, control design, memory organization, system organization.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Systems and Computer Design Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 361, experiments on digital systems and interfacing. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.

subject: ECE
title: Discrete Math for Engineers
description: Logic, sets, number theory, properties of functions, properties of relations, methods of proofs, recursion, counting, probability, trees, graphs, analysis of algorithms, finite state autonoma.

subject: ECE
title: CMOS VLSI Design
description: Introduction to the design of very large scale integrated (VLSI) systems and use of CAD tools and design languages. Lab includes hands-on use of CAD tools and experiments with field programmable logic devices.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Design and analysis of data structures and algorithms, including correctness and performance. Topics include time complexity, hash tables, sorting, search trees, self-balancing trees, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, and graph algorithms.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 367. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.

subject: ECE
title: Cyber-Physical Systems and the Internet of Things
description: Topics include General Purpose Input/Output (GPIO), serial communications, sensors, actuators, low-power wireless communications. TCP/IP networking, dynamic service discovery, distributed network messaging, machine-to-machine communication and cloud-computing interaction.

subject: ECE
title: Computational Media Systems
description: Intermediate object-oriented programming within the context of interactive media systems and video game development. Topics: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, event-driven programming, vectors, geometric primitives, game mechanics, and relevant design patterns.
restrictions_raw: ECE, CENG, ICS, CM, CSCI, THEA, DNCE majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Engineering Electromagnetics I
description: Transient and steady-state waves on transmission lines. Plane wave solutions of Maxwell’s equations. Application of Maxwell’s equations under static and time-varying conditions.

subject: ECE
title: Engineering Electromagnetics II
description: Solution of Maxwell’s equations under various boundary conditions. Introduction to radiation, guided waves, and principles of optics.

subject: ECE
title: Engineering Electromagnetics Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of electromagnetics and optics.

subject: ECE
title: Junior Project
description: Junior level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills. It may be a continuation of ECE 296 or a new project. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Computer and Network Security
description: Review basic network mechanisms, introduce basic cryptography concepts, and study algorithms and protocols used in computer and network security. Discuss practical security mechanisms.
prereq_raw: 361 or ICS 312 or ICS 331 or instructor consent. (Once a year)

subject: ECE
title: Digital Signal Processing
description: Discrete-time signals and systems, sampling, Z-transform, transform, transform analysis of linear time-invariant systems, filter design, discrete Fourier transform, and computation of discrete Fourier transform.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Digital Image Processing
description: Digital image representation, intensity transformations, spatial filtering, filtering in the frequency domain, image restoration, color spaces and transformations, the fast wavelet transform, image compression.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Optimization
description: Application of linear, nonlinear and integer optimization models and algorithms to communications, control, signal processing, computer networking, financial engineering, manufacturing, production and distribution systems. CE, ECE, ME, or CBA majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
prereq_raw: (160, 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: ECE
title: Instrumentation Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 422.

subject: ECE
title: Computer-Aided Analysis and Design
description: Algorithms and techniques used in computer-aided analysis and design of electronic circuits. Circuit simulation with interactive computers.

subject: ECE
title: Electronic Instrumentation II
description: Instrumentation systems and circuits for measurement, control, signal processing, transmission, and detection. Noise and interference, ADC/DAC, modulation demodulation, high-frequency and high-speed techniques, IC applications.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Si IC and Solid State Devices
description: State of the art Si-based devices including advanced bipolar and MOS devices, heterojunction devices, new device trends. Topics from the most current literature included.
prereq_raw: 327 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A, or consent

subject: ECE
title: Computer-Aided Circuit Design
description: Application of the computer to the analysis, design, simulation, and construction of analog and digital circuits.

subject: ECE
title: Electric Power Systems
description: Design/operation of “the grid.” History of electric power systems, three-phrase power, real and reactive power, transformers, transmission, distribution, circuit analysis, protection, load flow, load frequency control, optimal power flow, and renewable energy integration.

subject: ECE
title: Renewable Energy
description: Fundamentals of power, electric power grid and conventional electricity generation. Wind and solar power systems. Photovoltaic materials and systems. Distributed generation and energy storage. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Communications
description: Baseband transmission, intersymbol interference and pulse shaping, partial response signaling, equalization, bandpass modulation and demodulation, channel coding, synchronization, multiplexing and multiple access, spread spectrum techniques.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Machine Learning
description: Foundation for algorithms, practice, and theory behind common machine-learning applications. Includes projects, statistical programming, and an introduction to the unique challenges of high-dimensional problems.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and MATH 307 ( or equivalent)

restrictions_raw: ECE, CENG, CEE, ME, MATH, ICS majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Information Theory and Coding
description: Models of communication systems. Channel noise, measurement, and coding of information. Intrinsic limits of performance of communication systems.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Communication Networks
description: ISO Reference Model. Physical Layer, Data Link Layer, Network Layer and Transport Layer protocols. Wired and wireless local-area networks. Structure and operation of the Internet including routing, congestion control and flow control.
prereq_raw: 315 and one of 342, or MATH 371 or MATH 471; or consent

subject: ECE
title: Digital Control Systems
description: Sampling/reconstruction, Z-transform, DT transfer function. Reachability/observability. State and output feedback, observer design, input-output models, diophantine equations. Implementation procedures.

subject: ECE
title: Modern Control Theory
description: Analysis and synthesis of nonlinear control systems by means of Lagrange’s equation, state space techniques, maximum principle. Lyapunov’s theorems, the phase plane, and Z-transform techniques. Optimization and adaptation by means of gradient methods, calculus of variations, dynamic programming.

subject: ECE
title: Design of Intelligent Robots
description: Study of the design principles of computer-controlled, intelligent robots such as roving vehicles, hand-eye systems.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Architecture
description: Structure of stored program machines, data flow machines, pipelining, fault-tolerant computing, instruction set design, effects of compilation on architecture, RISC vs. CISC architecture, uses of parallelism.

subject: ECE
title: Object-oriented Software Engineering
description: Introduction to advanced techniques for designing, implementing, and testing computer software with a particular focus on using object-oriented design, analysis, and programming to produce high-quality computer programs that solve non-trivial problems.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Operating Systems
description: Computer system organization; multiprocessor systems, memory hierarchies, assemblers, compilers, operating systems, virtual machine, memory management, processor management; information management. Emphasis on written communication through written assignments on relevant topics.

subject: ECE
title: Wireless Data Networks
description: Mobile agent’s platforms and systems, mobile agent-based service implementation, middleware, and configuration, wireless local area networks, wireless protocols, network architecture supporting wireless applications, routing protocols in mobile and wireless networks, handoff in mobile and wireless networks.

subject: ECE
title: Physical Optics
description: Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics.
prereq_raw: 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-) or PHYS 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C), or consent

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C- ) or PHYS 450 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C ) , or consent

subject: ECE
title: Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
description: Introduction to computational methods used to simulate/solve engineering design problems focusing on electromagnetics. Finite difference, method of moments, and finite elements methods will be described; students will write computer programs in each.

subject: ECE
title: Microwave Engineering
description: Passive and active microwave devices and circuits for RF and wireless applications. Scattering parameters, signal-flow graphs, and computer-aided design.

subject: ECE
title: Antennas
description: Electromagnetic wave propagation in free space and ionized media. Geomagnetic and solar effects on the ionosphere. Absorption and dispersion. Antenna arrays, apertures, horns, impedance. Design of antenna systems.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Communications
description: Principles and applications of optical fibers and waveguides. Fundamentals of optical communication systems (optical links, high-speed systems, wavelength-division-multiplexing networks, and network elements) and optical components (guided-wave circuits, lasers, detectors, and optical amplifiers). System and network integration issues.

subject: ECE
title: Fundamentals of Radar, Sonar, and Navigation Systems
description: Discussion of basic radar detection and position- and velocity-measurement principles. Applications to various types of radar and sonar systems. Modern navigation aids.
prereq_raw: 371 (or equivalent), and familiarity with waveguides or waveguide theory

children.text: ( or equivalent), and familiarity with waveguides or waveguide theory

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Biomedical and Clinical Engineering
description: Application of engineering principles and technology to biological and medical problems. Introduction to human anatomy, physiology, medical terminology, clinical measurements. Systems modeling, physiological control systems, computer applications, health-related problems.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Engineering Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Measurement of bioelectrical signals, computer and electronic simulation of biological systems, design and evaluation of electronic circuits for biomedical measurements, evaluation of instruments for patient safety.

subject: ECE
title: Bioelectric Phenomena
description: Study of electrical phenomena in living systems. Mechanisms underlying bioelectric activity. Membrane and transepithelial potentials, skin impedance, electrocardiography, neuroelectric signals, diagnostic considerations, laboratory demonstrations.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Instrumentation
description: Principles, applications, and design of biomedical instrumentation. Transducers, IC and microcomputer applications, patient safety.

subject: ECE
title: (Alpha) Special Topics in Electrical Engineering
description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty; to be oriented toward juniors and seniors. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (G) computer vision; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

subject: ECE
title: Provisional Topics
description: Upper division course with subject matter to be announced.

subject: ECE
title: Ethics in Electrical Engineering
description: Equip electrical engineers with the necessary background for ethical reasoning, as it pertains to technology, society, workplace issues, and the environment.
prereq_raw: senior standing or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ECE
title: Capstone Design Project
description: Significant project integrating the design content of previous courses and incorporating engineering standards and realistic constraints. Written report must document all aspects of the design process: reliability, safety, economics, ethics.

subject: ECE
title: Directed Reading
description: Investigation of advanced engineering problems.

subject: ECE
title: Graph Theory and Its Applications
description: Graphs and subgraphs, trees and treelike graphs, planar graphs, connectivity and edge-connectivity, applications.

subject: ECE
title: Algorithm I
description: Design and evaluation of machine representations, techniques and algorithms for sorting, pattern processing, computational geometry, mathematical computations, and engineering applications. Introduction to computational issues of time, space, communication, and program correctness.

subject: ECE
title: Artificial Intelligence
description: LISP for machine intelligence applications, or related constraint object and logic-oriented languages.

subject: ECE
title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects.
prereq_raw: 467 or ICS 313 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: ( or equivalent), graduate standing ; or consent . ( Once a year)

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Network Algorithms
description: Network algorithms, protocols, and packet switching systems for the internet including TCP/IP, routing algorithms, transmission scheduling, link management, buffer management, and simple network management.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Networks
description: Propagation of signals in fibers, components, modulation and demodulation, transmission system engineering, network systems and architectures, network design, control and management and packet switching.

subject: ECE
title: Computer and Network Security
description: Basic security theory, current practices, and emerging research issues. First covering the fundamentals of computer and network security, then will work on research projects on computer and network security.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing
description: An advanced course in digital processing. Topics include fast DFT algorithms, multirate systems and filter banks, power spectrum estimation, linear prediction, optimum linear filters, and adaptive filtering. Open to nonmajors for CR/NC only.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Image Processing
description: Human visual perception, image formation, sampling and quantization, enhancement and restoration, color image processing, wavelets and multiresolution representations, image and video compression.

subject: ECE
title: Linear and Convex Optimization
description: Algorithms for linear, nonlinear, and convex optimization. Emphasis is on methodology and the underlying mathematical structures. Topics include simplex method, network flow methods, optimality conditions, duality, Newton’s method and interior point methods.
restrictions_raw: ECE, ME, MIS and MATH majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Dynamic Programming and Stochastic Control
description: Sequential decision-making via dynamic programming. Optimal control of stochastic dynamic systems. Applications in linear-quadratic control, inventory control, resource allocation, scheduling, and control of queues. Rollout and other suboptimal methods. Value and policy iteration.
prereq_raw: 342 or MATH 371 or MATH 471, or consent

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Electronic Circuits
description: Electronic circuits for precision measurement, computation, and signal processing. Low noise and interference reduction techniques. High-frequency and high-speed techniques. Micro-processor and biomedical applications.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Solid-State Devices
description: Advanced physical principles and design of modern solid-state electronic devices. Heterostructures, photodetectors, LED, junction lasers, and other devices of current importance identified from the current literature.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Electronics I
description: Fundamentals of optical radiation, including stimulated and spontaneous processes. Optical electronics including optical resonators, lasers, optical detectors, light-guiding, and applications.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Electronics II
description: Electro-optics, noise detection, light and sound dielectric waveguide phenomena, lasers, optics, phase conjugation.

subject: ECE
title: Microsensors and Microactuators I
description: Technology methods and physical principles of microsensors and microactuators. Vacuum technology, thin film deposition and characterization techniques, solid mechanics, micromachining, acoustics, piezoelectricity and principles of current microtransducers.

subject: ECE
title: Rapid Prototyping of Electrophysical Devices
description: Hands on experience in designing, fabricating, testing, and iterating according to rapid-prototyping principles. Students learn state-of-the-art equipment for making their designs, software for simulating designs, and working in design teams. Graduate students only.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Topics in Physical Electronics
description: Recent developments in phenomena and devices of physical electronics.

subject: ECE
title: Analysis and Design of Integrated Circuits
description: Fabrication constraints and design guidelines for integrated circuits. Nonlinear model of integrated circuit transistor. Design and analysis of integrated logic circuits and linear circuits.

subject: ECE
title: Smart Grids and Renewable Energy Integration
description: Challenges and solutions for integrating intermittent renewable energy sources into the power system, with a focus on “smart grid” approaches and demand-response. Using linear programming and other modeling techniques to answer policy-relevant questions. Graduate students only.

subject: ECE
title: Applied Random Processes
description: Random variables, multivariate distributions, random sequences, stochastic convergence, stationary and nonstationary processes, spectral analysis, Karhunen-Loeve expansion, Markov processes, mean square estimation, Kalman filters.

subject: ECE
title: Queueing Theory
description: Poisson, Markov, and renewal processes, M/G/1 queue, G/M/1 queue, queueing networks, simulation, and performance evaluation of computer systems and communication networks.

subject: ECE
title: Detection and Estimation Theory
description: Fundamentals of signal detection and estimation theory. Hypothesis testing, parametric and nonparametric detection, sequential detection, parametric estimation, linear estimation, robust detection and estimation, and applications to communication systems.

subject: ECE
title: Communication System Performance
description: Fundamental performance limits, signal detection and estimation, modulation, intersymbol interference, equalization adaptive filtering, sequence detection, synchronization, fading multipath channels, spread spectrum.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Communication Networks
description: Fundamentals of computer communication networks including modeling, performance evaluation, routing, flow control, local area networks, distributed algorithms, and optimization algorithms.

subject: ECE
title: Machine Learning
description: Learning theory, pattern recognition and regression; gradient based algorithms and least square algorithms; Kernel methods; Bayesian learning algorithms; ensemble learning and boosting; principal component analysis; independent component analysis, and clustering; reinforcement learning and approximate dynamic programming.
restrictions_raw: ECE, ME, ICS, MATH majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Information Theory
description: Measure of information, coding for discrete sources, discrete memoryless channels and capacity, the noisy channel coding theorem, source coding with fidelity criterion, rate-distortion theory, multiuser channels.

subject: ECE
title: Source Coding
description: Theory and applications of source coding, rate-distortion theory, companding, lattice coding, tree coding, trellis coding, entropy-constrained coding, asymptotic theory, predictive and differential encoding, combined source/channel coding, vector quantization.

subject: ECE
title: Error-Control Coding I
description: Linear block codes, soft and hard decision decodings, correction of random errors, cyclic codes, BCH codes, Reed-Solomon codes, majority logic decodable codes, burst-error correcting codes, concatenated codes.

subject: ECE
title: Error-Control Coding II
description: Convolutional codes, Viterbi algorithm, coded modulation, multistage decoding, concatenated coded modulation, probabilistic decoding, turbo codes, low density parity check codes and iterative decoding.

subject: ECE
title: Linear System Theory
description: State space theory of linear systems, controllability, observability, stability, irreducible realizations.

subject: ECE
title: Nonlinear Control Systems
description: Digital simulations, phase-plane analysis, limit cycles and amplitude bounds, Lyapunov’s theorem, circle criterion of stability, lure systems, Popov’s stability theorem.

subject: ECE
title: Optimal Control Systems
description: Optimal controls introduced through parametric optimization, calculus of variations, Euler-Lagrange and Hamilton-Jacobi equations, Pontryagin’s maximum principle, minimum-time and minimum-fuel problems, dynamic programming, applications.

subject: ECE
title: Robust Control
description: Multivariable frequency response design, signals and systems, linear fractional transformations, LQG Control, Full Information H-infinity Controller Synthesis, H-infinity filtering, model reduction, the four-block problem.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Architecture I
description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs.
restrictions_raw: CECE, ECE, and ME majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Systems
description: Modern operating system software, process communication, distributed systems, device drivers. Software development and maintenance, integration of software packages. Projects reflecting special interests of faculty.

subject: ECE
title: Telecommunication Networks
description: Telecommunication-network architecture; switching, broadcast, and wireless networks; protocols, interfaces, routing, flow- and congestion-control techniques; intelligent network architecture; service creation capabilities; multimedia, voice, data, and video networks and services.

subject: ECE
title: Wireless and Mobile Security
description: Security and privacy design principles and application in wireless and mobile devices, networks, and services, as well as research methodology in wireless and mobile security.

subject: ECE
title: Electromagnetic Theory and Applications
description: Solutions of Maxwell’s equations and applications to radiation and propagation of electromagnetic waves.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Microwave Engineering
description: Advanced RF and microwave circuit design for wireless applications.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
description: Develop comprehensive understanding of computations techniques for solving engineering electromagnetic problems formulated in terms of integral or differential equations. Eigenvalue problems, radiation, and electromagnetics scattering problems will be discussed and computer programming is required.
prereq_raw: 471 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent
restrictions_raw: ECE, BE, and CENG majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Engineering Systems
description: Systems analysis and electronic instrumentation methods in biomedicine. Network and control-loop modeling, computer simulation, biological transducers, and analysis of electronic and physiological systems.

subject: ECE
title: Biosensors and Bioelectronics
description: Advanced topics in the design of biological detection technologies. Topics include fundamentals of electrochemistry, electrochemical biosensors, DNA and protein biochips, and bioelectronics for bio-signal conditioning and processing.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Microdevices
description: Design and fabrication of micro- and nanodevices for biomedical applications. Topics include micro- and nanoscale physics, microfluidic physics and microfluidic devices, and micro- and nanoscale fabrication techniques.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Signal Processing and Analysis
description: Biomedical signals, digital filters and filter banks, spike train analysis, time-scale and time-frequency representations, nonlinear techniques, Lomb’s algorithm and the Hilbert transform, modeling, Volterra series, Wiener series, Poisson-Wiener series, multichannel data, causality. CE, ECE, ME, ICS majors only and any graduate student in JABSOM who has a suitable technical background.

subject: ECE
title: (Alpha) Special Topics in Electrical Engineering
description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

subject: ECE
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.
prereq_raw: candidacy for MS in electrical and computer engineering

subject: ECE
title: Directed Instruction
description: Student assists in classroom instruction under direction and close supervision of faculty member.

subject: ECE
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.
prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD in electrical and computer engineering

subject: ENGR
title: Engineering Freshman Seminar
description: Overview of the engineering field, the different disciplines, and opportunities. Success strategies for studying engineering.

subject: ENGR
title: Introduction to Engineering
description: Topics include the engineering disciplines, the development of problem solving and technical communication skills, the design process and analysis methods using a team design project, and introduction to programming in Matlab for engineering applications. Freshman standing only.

subject: ENGR
title: Introduction to Technology-Based Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: Introduces modern tools for launching technology-based new ventures. Teams of students engage in term projects to learn design thinking, business model generation, product development, rapid prototyping, customer validation, and pitching to investors. Freshmen only.

subject: ENGR
title: Freshman Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for freshman-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a sophomore (ENGR 296).
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits

subject: ENGR
title: Personal Development for Effective Teams
description: Exploration and application of basic leadership theories and processes which foster personal and interpersonal development via cognitive experiential classroom methods and mentoring relationships with experienced peer leaders.

subject: ENGR
title: Sophomore Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for sophomore-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a junior (ENGR 396). Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ENGR
title: Career Development Seminar
description: Introduction to career development as it pertains to engineering and business industry; client relations, networking, job skills, career assessment and direction.

subject: ENGR
title: Junior Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for junior-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a senior. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ENGR
title: Engineering Management
description: Introduction to engineering management of projects and its outcomes. Development of professional skills for the systematic formulation of problems and solutions to efficiently deduce project viability. Emphasis on collaborative teamwork and performance evaluations and improvements.

subject: ENGR
title: Field Experience
description: Supervised internship in engineering practice under professional and faculty direction.
prereq_raw: junior standing in engineering and consent

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Engineering Design I
description: Introductory experience in analysis, synthesis, and design. Teamwork and project required.

subject: ME
title: Space Exploration
description: Introduction to science and engineering of Solar System exploration with laboratory exercises. Covers planetary science, model-based systems engineering, mission planning, constraints on payload and spacecraft design, human spaceflight technology. Research projects emphasize written communication.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Engineering Design
description: Introductory experience in communication, presentation, professional ethics, social responsibility, engineering economics, quality control, and computer-aided drafting. Teamwork and project required.

subject: ME
title: Applied Mechanics II
description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy.
prereq_raw: C or better in CEE 270; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).  D
restrictions_raw: CE, CNST, ENGS, ME majors only.

subject: ME
title: Space Science and Instrumentation
description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces and their measurement. Design of space flight instrumentation.
prereq_raw: EPET 201, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272

subject: ME
title: Thermodynamics
description: Basic laws, closed and open systems. Work, heat, concept of entropy. Properties of pure simple substances. Ideal gases. Introduction to power and refrigeration cycles.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A), PHYS 170 and MATH 244 (or MATH 253A)

children.text: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (

subject: ME
title: Mechanics of Fluids and Lab
description: Incompressible and compressible ideal fluids, effects of viscosity. Similitude, boundary layer flow. Measurement techniques in thermodynamics and fluid mechanics. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermofluid systems. Emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of 311 and CEE 271 (or ME 271)

children.text: grade of C or better in all of 311

subject: ME
title: Materials Science and Engineering
description: Electronic, atomic, and crystalline structure of materials and their effect on the mechanical, electrical, optical, and magnetic properties of engineering metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A), MATH 242 (or MATH 252A), and PHYS 170

children.text: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (

subject: ME
title: Manufacturing Processes and Lab
description: Energy requirements for manufacturing methods. Manufacturing methods to obtain components with desired size/shape/properties. Conduct manufacturing experiments. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ME
title: Manufacturing Processes Lab
description: Manufacturing laboratory: tension/ compression tests, cold rolling, welding, casting, statistical process control, programming and milling using a CNC machine.

subject: ME
title: Computer Methods in Engineering
description: Numerical solutions for algebraic and transcendental equations, simultaneous linear algebraic equations, integration and differentiation; integration of ordinary differential equations. Engineering applications.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of ECE 160 (or ECE 110 or ICS 111), MATH 244 (or MATH 253A), and MATH 302 (or MATH 307)

children.text: grade of C or better in all of ECE 160 (
