subject: ME
title: Mechanics of Solids
description: Introduction to analysis and design of deformable bodies subject to loading. Stress, strain, consitutive relation, axially loading, torsion, statically indeterminate systems, Mohr’s circle, failure criteria, buckling, defection due to axial, shear, torsional, and flexural loading.
prereq_raw: C or better in all of the following: CEE 270; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

subject: ME
title: Component Design
description: Design, analysis, and selection of machine components: shafts, screws, fasteners, welds, rolling contact bearings, journal bearings, gears, clutches, brakes, belts, and roller chains.

subject: ME
title: Kinematics/Dynamics Machinery
description: Velocity and acceleration analysis of planar mechanisms; kinematic synthesis of linkages, cams, and gears; static and dynamic force analysis of mechanisms; balancing of machinery.
prereq_raw: CEE 271 or ME 271 (C or better), MATH 244 (or MATH 253A) and either MATH 302 or MATH 307

children.text: ( or MATH 253A ) and either MATH 302 or MATH 307

subject: ME
title: Dynamics of Machines and Systems and Lab
description: Lumped-parameter modeling of dynamic systems. Methods of analysis, including transform techniques. Time and frequency response. Feedback control. Engineering instrumentation. Data acquisition. Dynamic measurements. Design and testing. Lab report writing.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CEE 271 (or ME 271) and MATH 302 (or MATH 307)

children.text: grade of C or better in all of CEE 271 (

subject: ME
title: Space Mission Design
description: Covers all aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, budgets, and ethical issues that are important to consider in producing a fully successful mission.

subject: ME
title: Capstone Project: Producing a Science Satellite
description: Develops a space mission with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists. Will build a small spacecraft and payload and seeks to answer important science questions. Emphasizes review report and proposal writing.

subject: ME
title: Dynamics Systems Laboratory
description: Analysis, design, fabrication, testing and characterization of engineering instrumentation. Computer-based data acquisition methods. Techniques and procedures associated with carrying out dynamic measurements within the constraints of cost, time and accuracy.
prereq_raw: one of 360, MATH 407, or PHYS 305 (or concurrent for any); and 375 (or concurrent)

children.text: ( or concurrent for any); and 375 (or concurrent)

subject: ME
title: Advanced Mathematics for Engineers
description: Applications of ordinary differential equations, Laplace transform, vector field theory, matrices, line integrals.

children.text: ( or MATH 253A ) , and MATH 302 ( or MATH 307 )

subject: ME
title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: Basic computational fluid dynamics; four important partial differential equations; introduction to finite element method: Interpolation and Galerkin method; finite element method for transport phenomena; some algorithms for parallel computing.
prereq_raw: 422 (or concurrent ), and either 360, MATH 407 or PHYS 305; or consent

subject: ME
title: Orbital Mechanics
description: Basic theory of orbits of space objects, including spacecraft, small satellites, planets and small planets, and other fundamentals of astrodynamics and applications to aerospace engineering. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of the following: 271; 375; MATH 244 or MATH 253A; MATH 302 or MATH 307; ECE 160 or ICS 111

children.text: grade of C or better in all of the following: 271

subject: ME
title: Optimal Control for Aerospace Applications
description: Fundamentals of optimal control theory and calculus of variations. Application of this theory to aerospace engineering problems, including mission design problems and a wide range of space maneuvers. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of the following: 271; 375; MATH 244 or MATH 253A; MATH 302 or MATH 307; ECE 160 or ICS 111

children.text: grade of C or better in all of the following: 271

subject: ME
title: Applied Thermodynamics
description: Gas mixtures, generalized thermodynamic relationships, combustion and thermochemistry, chemical equilibrium, power and refrigeration cycles.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in 311

prereq_tree.text: grade of C or better in 311

subject: ME
title: Applied Thermal Engineering
description: Principles, design and analysis of practical thermal systems. Engineering applications. Valve, compressor, condenser and evaporator technologies. System integration and control. Thermal loads and thermal comfort.

subject: ME
title: Power and Propulsion
description: Principles, performance, and design of gas turbine power plants and propulsion systems.

subject: ME
title: Astronautics
description: The space environment (vacuum, neutral, radiation, and plasma); motion in gravitational fields; orbit transfers; Earth-satellite operations; rocketry; propulsion analysis and performance; reentry dynamics; interplanetary trajectories; attitude dynamics and stabilization.

subject: ME
title: Heat Transfer and Lab
description: Steady and unsteady conduction; steady convection and radiation; heat exchangers. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ME
title: Mass Transfer
description: Elementary mass diffusion; diffusion in a stationary medium; diffusion in a moving medium; low and high mass transfer theories; simultaneous heat and mass transfer; condensation, evaporation, and boiling; transpiration cooling; species boundary layers; engineering and design of heat and mass exchangers; current refrigerants and environmental regulations.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Gas Dynamics
description: One-dimensional compressible flow involving change of area, friction, heat transfer. Normal and oblique shocks. Prandtl-Meyer flow. Application to nozzles, diffusers, airfoils.

subject: ME
title: Thermal Management of Electronic Systems
description: To introduce concepts in the thermal management of electronics, and to develop sound technical tools to approach modern electronic packaging and cooling applications.

subject: ME
title: Scaling Methods in Engineering
description: Scaling methods and optimization under global constraints; multi-scale optimal design of mechanical, thermal, and natural systems; effectiveness of heat, fluid, and convective trees; theoretical design optimization of manmade and natural power systems; analysis of time dependent structures.

subject: ME
title: Solar Thermal Engineering
description: Fundamentals of solar energy, solar engineering material characteristics, and solar thermal and photovoltaic systems. Will learn solar thermal system components, and be able to perform simple system design. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Failures in Materials
description: Analysis of component failures due to imperfections, fatigue, brittle fracture, wear, corrosion, bending, impact, and overload. Fracture mechanics. Case studies.

subject: ME
title: Materials Selection for Design
description: Methodology for the selection of materials for mechanical applications to prevent mechanical failure and environmental degradation. Design considerations associated with the use of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.

subject: ME
title: Experimental Methods in Materials Research
description: Common experimental techniques in materials testing and research: x-ray diffraction, optical and electron microscopy, thermal and mechanical properties, electrochemical methods—theory and hands-on experience.

subject: ME
title: Corrosion Engineering
description: Basics of corrosion processes and emphasis on corrosion control. Thermodynamics and kinetics of corrosion, metal alloys and their behavior, corrosion control techniques (cathodic protection, anodic protection, coatings, and inhibitors).

subject: ME
title: Mechatronics
description: Modern mechatronics components and design principles; functionality of products, processes and systems; electrical circuits and mechanical components; programming and control; hands on technology; application case studies.
restrictions_raw: ME, ECE, CE, ICS majors only.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Materials Manufacturing
description: Introduction to anisotropic materials, advanced manufacturing techniques for composite and intelligent materials, joining of composites, thin film processing and stereolithography, computer aided manufacturing and rapid prototyping, manufacturing process optimization, open-ended manufacturing projects.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Nanotechnology
description: Tools and techniques of micro- and nanotechnology in design, modeling, simulations, analysis, fabrication, testing and characterization; nano-materials, nano-structures, nano-composites, nano-coating, nano-optics, nano-electronics and nano-biotechnology.

subject: ME
title: Nanosystem and Microsystem Design
description: Fabrication, design, and analysis of physical systems, sensors, and actuators at the nanoscale and microscale. Microfabrication/nanofabrication, fabrication process design, electrostatistic and electromagnetic interactions, signal transduction, measurements. Course work will focus on process and system design.
prereq_raw: 331 (with a minimum grade of C-), 375 (with a minimum grade of C-), or consent

subject: ME
title: Research Methods in Engineering
description: Introduces the basic skills of preparing and publishing scientific research. Students will learn how to prepare, write, publish, and present a scientific paper, while working on a research project related to thermofluids. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Feedback-Control Systems
description: Analysis/design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.

subject: ME
title: Robotics
description: Principles and design methods for autonomous systems.

subject: ME
title: Energy Conversion Systems
description: Energy conversion and its impact on the environment. Conventional, hydroelectric, nuclear fission and fusion, solar, wind, ocean, geothermal, and biomass power; energy storage, transmission and conservation.

subject: ME
title: Nuclear Power Engineering
description: Nuclear reactor principles. Reactor heat transfer, heat generation and removal. Design and analysis of reactor power systems and plants.

subject: ME
title: Flow Visualization and Measurement
description: Overview of flow visualization and measurement techniques including high speed photography of wakes, jets, shear layer, particle motion. Experimental design, statistics, image processing and data analysis. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Materials for Solar Energy Conversion
description: Atom structure, electromagnetic waves and energy, electronic and energetic properties of semi-conducting materials, junctions, solar cells operations, bulk and thin film materials synthesis, integration of solar cells into the electric grid.
prereq_raw: (331 or ECE 324) with a minimum grade of C-

subject: ME
title: Electrochemical Power Sources: Principles, Applications, and Sustainability
description: Electrochemistry, batteries, fuel cells, flow batteries, electrochemical capacitors, electric vehicles, electrochemical grid storage.
prereq_raw: 331, CHEM 162, CHEM 171, or CHEM 181A (with a grade of C- or better)

subject: ME
title: Experimental Stress Analysis
description: (1-3 hr Lab) Techniques of experimental stress analysis: strain and deflection measurement of beams and shafts, strain to stress conversion, principal and maximum shearing stresses, failure in biaxial stress states, stress concentrations, residual stresses, buckling, creep, electrical resistance strain gages, brittle coatings, photoelastic methods, transducers.

subject: ME
title: Mechanical Vibrations
description: Response of machines and systems to transient and periodic excitation. Vibration isolation and transmissibility. Modal analysis of multi-degree-of-freedom systems. Applications to design.

subject: ME
title: Fundamentals of Acoustics
description: Plane and spherical acoustic waves. Transmission, reflection, radiation, and absorption. Near and far fields, radiation patterns. Applications to noise control. Instruments.

subject: ME
title: Thermofluid Measurements and Design
description: Measurement techniques in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermofluid systems. Contemporary engineering ethics issues. Final report and presentation are required.

subject: ME
title: Design Project I
description: (2 1-hr Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Heuristic application of engineering design process and project planning via a significant, open-ended design project that includes realistic constraints involving economics, environmental sustainability, manufacturability, ethics, health, safety, society, and politics. Extensive written communication required.

subject: ME
title: Design Project II
description: Continuation of design project initiated in ME 481. Extension of conceptual design to final design. Manufacturing of prototype: material and part selection, procurement, manufacturing specifications/ drawings. Testing of complex systems. Extensive oral communication required.

subject: ME
title: Research and Experiment Design
description: Introduction to research and experimentation via pursuit and reporting of an open-ended design project. Ethical issues in research and experimentation. Engineering, Biological Engineering, and Ocean & Resources Engineering majors only.

subject: ME
title: System Engineering
description: Will cover system engineering design, analysis, and development concepts, requirements derivation/management, and program management processes, such as risk identification/ management and fiscal/schedule tools. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Pearl Harbor Co-op
description: Provides real-world engineering experience through project assignment and working alongside a practicing engineer at the Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard. Senior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: (322, 341, 372, and 375) with a minimum grade of C

subject: ME
title: (Alpha) Mentored Projects
description: Investigation of advanced problems, making use of faculty expertise for specific domains of work. (B) Design Project I; (C) Design Project II; (D) Research and Experiment Design. Junior or senior standing only.

subject: ME
title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
description: Specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, systems, or design.

subject: ME
title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
description: Specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, systems, or design.

subject: ME
title: Project
description: Investigation of advanced problems in mechanical engineering design or development. Student must find faculty sponsor before registering.

subject: ME
title: Renewable Energy Engineering and Sustainability
description: Analysis of principles of operation of renewable energy systems, and its interactions with sustainability. Fundamentals of renewable energy production, storage, and distribution.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Thermodynamics
description: Introduction to general principles of classical thermodynamics. Main topics include equilibrium conditions, thermodynamic relations, Legendre transformations, Maxwell relations, stability of thermodynamic systems, phase transitions, and critical phenomena. Graduate students only.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Statistical Thermodynamics
description: Fundamentals of statistical thermodynamics. Main topics include entropy, Boltzmann law, thermodynamic driving forces, statistical mechanics, chemical equilibria, solutions and mixtures, and applications of statistical thermodynamics in biology, chemistry, physics, and nanoscience.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Aerodynamics
description: Advanced topics in aerodynamics, two- and three-dimensional wing theory, slender-body theory, lifting surface methods, vortex and wave drag, analytical and numerical methods, for computing unsteady aerodynamic behavior and introduction to flightdynamics.

subject: ME
title: Thermal Environmental Engineering
description: Physiological response to thermal environment, designs of passive and active cooling systems, student project.

subject: ME
title: Boiling and Two-Phase Flow
description: Two-phase flow pattern and flow pattern maps; two-phase flow models (homogeneous, separate, drift flux, annular); laminar and turbulent film condensations; boiling incipience; pool boiling heat transfer; flow boiling heat transfer; critical heat flux (CHF).

subject: ME
title: Biological Fluid Mechanics
description: Review of Newtonian fluid mechanics. Blood rheology and flow in elastic tubes. Murray’s Law and pulsatile flow propagation. Microcirculation dynamics and biological transport. Aquatic movement and comparative biological examples.

subject: ME
title: Conduction Heat Transfer
description: Steady and unsteady heat conduction with and without heat sources in solids. Analytical, numerical, graphical, analog methods for solving heat conduction problems.

subject: ME
title: Convection Heat Transfer
description: Heat transfer in laminar and turbulent boundary layers. Analogy between heat, momentum, mass transfer.

subject: ME
title: Radiation Heat Transfer

subject: ME

subject: ME

subject: ME

subject: ME

subject: ME

subject: ME

subject: ME

subject: ME
title: Automatic Control

subject: ME
title: Guidance, Navigation and Control
description: Develop modern and advanced techniques in the design, development, and implementation of guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) systems for flight vehicles and other controllable dynamical systems. Graduate students only.

subject: ME

subject: HAW

subject: HAW

subject: HAW

subject: HAW
title: Listening Comprehension and Transcription

subject: HAW

prereq_raw: completion of 202 or consent. (Once a year)

subject: HAW
title: E Pū Pa‘akai Kākou: A Study of Traditional Hawaiian and Contemporary Food Culture
description: A study of traditional Hawaiian and contemporary food culture through hands-on applications and lectures.

subject: HAW

subject: HAW

description: Research methodology course utilizing active research in the major repositories of Hawaiian language materials and Hawaiian-related knowledge.

description: Study of Hawaiian political thought in writing from ca. 1825 to the present, with emphasis on theory and research methods.

description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Introduction to a variety of fibers used in the Hawaiian culture. Emphasis on cultivation, preparation, uses and conservation of the fibers. Areas explored are kapa, plaiting, netting and twining.

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Painting and Drawing Studio
description: Research and express personal relationship to specific Hawaiian paradigms through Hawaiian visual culture. Introduction to painting and drawing media and exploration of various materials and techniques as applied to individual student styles.

subject: HWST

subject: HWST

subject: HWST

subject: HWST

subject: HWST
title: Ho‘okele II Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands on experience on voyaging skills and sailing canoes to accompany 282.

title: Lā‘au Lapa‘au: Hawaiian Medicinal Herbs

description: Interdisciplinary lectures and discussions examining traditional and contemporary experiences in Hawaiian society and setting; resources, methods, and techniques.

description: Survey of Hawaiian chiefs from 1778 to the present, including genealogy, political function, and historical impact.

Sophomore or higher standing.

subject: HWST
title: Ka Mana Mo‘olelo: Topics in Hawaiian and Indigenous Mo‘olelo
description: Advanced course of study focusing on pressing topics connected with Hawaiian and Indigenous literatures, such as land struggle, climate change, or issues of governance and sovereignty.

subject: HWST
title: Mâhele Land Awards
description: Practical guide to the researching of land awards and change in title for a single ahupua‘a, 1848 to present. Focus on field trips.

subject: HWST
title: Ceded Lands: Focus on Crown and Government Lands (1848 to Present)
description: Inventorying “Ceded Lands” in Hawai‘i with emphasis on historical, legal, and cultural changes from the Kingdom through statehood.

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Indigenous Research Methods
description: Survey course introduces students to a range of methods by beginning with a critical analysis of dominant research methodologies from the perspective of Indigenous scholars. Junior/senior standing only.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Institutions
description: Comprehensive analysis of institutions like Bishop Estate/Kamehameha Schools, OHA, Lili‘uokalani Trust, Department of Hawaiian Home Lands and The Queen’s Hospital.

subject: HWST
title: Wehe Ka ‘Āina: Cultivating a Sovereign Land Base
description: A Mālama ‘Āina and Kukulu ‘Aupuni course that identifies modern options in land access for reestablishing or resuming Hawaiian traditional and customary practices relating to food sovereignty and self-sustainability. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: Ola I Ka Wai; Water and Sovereignty in Hawai‘i
description: Focus on Hawaiian relationships with Ka Wai Ola a Kane (water), traditional and contemporary water management practices, as well as contemporary resource management issues and native Hawaiian community advocacy for water.

subject: HWST
title: Kia‘i Kanaloa–Guarding Our Ocean Resources
description: Students will actively monitor and practice coastal and ocean stewardship in support of local communities and practitioners while also exploring how the Hawaiian worldview can plan a role in aloha ‘âina conservation movements. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: ‘Āina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawai‘i.

subject: HWST
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.

subject: HWST
title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O‘ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.

subject: HWST
title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawai‘i. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives.

subject: HWST
title: Hawai‘i & Indigenous Economies
description: Students will map out indigenous economies by articulating cultural similarity and diversity between academic experience and professional experiences.

subject: HWST
title: Mālama ‘Āina Field Methods Course
description: Intensive field methods program to research Mālama ‘Āina strategies. Introduces students to a variety of field techniques including land research, historical documents, ecological surveys, and Papakūmakawalu. Junior standing or higher.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to 12 credits

subject: HWST
title: ‘Ike Akua Papakū Makawalu: Ancestral Understanding of Elements
description: Uses Dr. Pualani Kanahele’s Papakū Makawalu methodology to analyze akua as elements and as a paradigm for understanding ancestral knowledge. Senior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: Mele Au Hou: Music and Native Identity
description: Presents Hawaiian music as it has been an avenue for native social, cultural and political expression in traditional and contemporary society.

subject: HWST
title: Mahi Lā‘au Lapa‘au: Hawaiian Medicinal Horticulture
description: The science of planting and harvesting Hawaiian medicinal plants and exploring production and marketing strategies.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Aquatic Medicine
description: Identification, extraction and preparation of complexes of aquatic herbs to formulate a healing combination to contribute to maintaining overall health.

subject: HWST
title: Senior Seminar in Hawaiian Studies
description: Critical examination of existing research; individual or team development, execution, and evaluation of selected projects.
prereq_raw: senior major in Hawaiian studies or consent

subject: HWST
title: Senior Capstone Project in Hawaiian Studies
description: Capstone seminar designed to provide a culminating academic experience through in-depth examination, analysis, articulation, and projects relevant to a HWST area of concentration. Senior standing only.
prereq_raw: 341, 342, [343 or 390 or 490 (or concurrent)] and [207/SUST 217 or 285 or 307/SUST 317 or 356/SUST 356] and [222 or 224 or 225 or 372 or 478]

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Political Speech: Ha‘i ‘Ōlelo Ku‘e
description: Senior seminar in short, extemporaneous speeches in persuasive, passionate and dynamic styles of Native Hawaiian orators.
prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341, 342, or HAW 202; or consent. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: Modern Pacific Women’s Poetry
description: Critical examination of modern indigenous women’s poetry from the Pacific Islands. Thematic concentration on land, family, sexual and national oppression.

subject: HWST
title: Kumu Kānāwai: Western Law and Hawai‘i
description: The rise of Western law in Hawai‘i, its contribution to nation building and colonialism.

subject: HWST
title: Kānāwai II: Practical Application of Rights
description: Historical analysis of land use, race and self-determination; introduced to legal case briefing, analysis of legal precedent, practical impacts of rules and regulations and the sociopolitical factors that influence law and law enforcement.

subject: HWST
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading/research.

subject: HWST
title: Indigenous Research Methodologies
description: Reading seminar for developing a Native Hawaiian epistemology from sources in comparative indigenous thought.
prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Archival Research
description: Research seminar aimed at familiarizing students with the rich historical primary sources existent in various archives in Honolulu.
prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: HWST
title: Review of Hawaiian Literature
description: Seminar in review of Hawaiian literature to understand the significance of secondary sources in Hawaiian subjects. This makes up part of the Hawaiian Studies graduate core.
prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: HWST
title: Writing a Hawaiian Thesis
description: Seminar to help fashion student’s research and thesis proposal. To be taken by all HWST MA students as they begin designing their capstone project. Course will be team-taught by HWST faculty.

subject: HWST
title: ‘Ike Pono-Visual/Cultural Interpretations
description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that examines (from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint) colonial imaging; collecting and site of contestation; resilience and resistance; and re-righting.
prereq_raw: 107, and one course from 220-225, and one course from 320-325; or consent

subject: HWST
title: ‘Ike Maka-Visual/Cultural Knowledge
description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that carefully examines and develops critical consciousness–from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint–visual hegemony, rhetorical tropes; and representation–imag(in)ing and reimag(in)-ing.

subject: HWST
title: Pono Science: Ethical Implications of Science in Hawai‘i
description: Support student dialogue on the foundations of pono science. Through discussions and structured guidance, students will explore Hawaiian ethics, implications of research, and decolonizing methodology. Graduate students only.

subject: HWST
title: Mo‘olelo ‘Ōiwi: Historical Perspectives
description: Research seminar for developing interpretations of the past from Native Hawaiian and foreign world views with particular emphasis on understanding the meaning of culturally-based knowledge systems.

subject: HWST
title: Mele Hawa‘i: Mele as Systems of Knowledge
description: Seminar on Mele Hawai‘i (Songs, Poetry, Chants) as systems of knowledge that record, communicate, and critique historical, political, environmental, and cultural information. Will include learning and analysis of mele, culminating with a research project.
prereq_raw: HAW 302 and (HWST 478 or HAW 384 or HAW 484)

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Geography and Resource Management
description: Seminar in geography of Hawai‘i from a Native Hawaiian perspective that will enable the researcher to define and develop resource management methods consistent with Native Hawaiian understandings and traditions.
prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent). (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: ‘Āina Waiwai: Water, Food Sovereignty, and Ancestral Abundance
description: Topical graduate seminar focuses on indigenous perspectives on water, food sovereignty, Hawaiian terrestrial and marine food production systems, and ancestral abundance. Seminar perspective to change each term.

subject: HWST
title: Kānāwai Lawai‘a: Hawa‘i’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance. (Alt. years: Fall)

subject: HWST
title: Historic Preservation Law
description: Introduction to the protection of cultural, archaeological, and historical resources with emphasis on key federal and state laws. (Once a year)

subject: HWST
title: He Ali‘i Ka ‘Āina; Land, Resources, and Leadership
description: Seminar focused on leadership challenges in MVâlama ‘Āina to bridge ancestral and contemporary systems to better steward resources, produce abundance, work with and in community, and pivot large institutions for a better Aloha ‘Āina future.

subject: HWST
title: Kumu Kahiki: Comparative Hawaiian and Tahitian Cosmogonies
description: Seminar comparing Gods/myths from Ancient Tahiti by Teiura Henry (600 pages) with the six volumes of Hawaiian historians Kamakau and Malo.

subject: HWST
title: Kumu Kahiki: Pacific Life Narratives in Mixed Media and Literature
description: Research seminar in relevant literary traditions, histories of interaction, colonization, and literary politics in the Pacific region through the examination of life narratives in mixed media and literature.

subject: HWST
title: Indigenous Futurisms: Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, and Beyond
description: Seminar on Indigenous Futurisms as developed in Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, and other Indigenous contexts, and expressed through art, literature, film, music, and scholarship.

subject: HWST
title: Huaka‘i Huli Heiau Hawai‘inuiākea: Study Abroad on Polynesian Temples
description: Comparative study of Hawaiian/Polynesian temple design taught over a 3-week period in Hawai‘i and Polynesia. Travel costs to be paid by student.
prereq_raw: 670 (with a minimum grade of B) and HAW 302 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: HWST
title: Kūkulu Aupuni: Envisioning the Nation
description: A research seminar designed to provide an overview of community activism and Native Hawaiian empowerment in Hawai‘i in contexts that range from local to international, and to provide a foundation for further study and professional growth.
prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: HWST
title: Kūkulu Aupuni: Sovereign Hawaiian State, Domestic Kingdom Law, Governance and Politics
description: Research seminar on the subject of domestic law, governance, and politics of the Hawaiian Kingdom and the historical relevance of this to the contemporary case for independent, sovereign state continuity under public international law. (Alt. years)

subject: HWST
title: Practicum Research Plan B
description: Practicum for Plan B.

subject: HWST
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. (F) Full-time. S/U for (F) only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable up to six credits; Repeatable unlimited times for (F)

subject: HSSW
title: Southeast Asian Cultures in Health/ Social Welfare
description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in Southeast and South Asian region.

subject: HSSW
title: Pacific Cultures in Health/Social Welfare
description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in the Pacific region.

subject: CIS
title: Communication/Information Theories of Society
description: A critical review of major theoretical and empirical traditions in communication and information sciences. Focus on European, American, Third World, and applied research.

subject: CIS
title: Communication/Information Technologies
description: Technological concepts underlying data communications; information processing and computers; communication channels and networks, information storage and retrieval, and computer hardware and software.

subject: CIS
title: Communication/Information Research Methods
description: Current research methodologies in decision sciences, computer science, library science, and communication. Emphasis on methodologies suitable for interdisciplinary analysis.

subject: CIS
title: Special Topics in Communication and Information Sciences
description: Seminar reflecting research interests of faculty and current interdisciplinary topics in communication and information sciences. Graduate students only.

subject: CIS
title: Data Science Foundations
description: All aspects of data science: the methodology and processes; ethics and regulatory issues; programming tools; data acquisition, cleaning, analysis and mining; visualization, publication, curation, and preservation; applications in various fields. Graduate students only.

subject: CIS
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Communication and Information Sciences
description: Exploration of relationships between disciplines in social sciences, science and technology, and humanities. Faculty and student presentations.

subject: CIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading and/or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses.
prereq_raw: consent. Plan must include goals and rationale

children.text: Plan must include goals and rationale

subject: SUST
title: Dynamic Earth
description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip. DP

subject: SUST
title: The Natural Environment
description: Introduction to physical geography including weather, climate, vegetation, soils, geology, and landforms. Environmental issues and natural hazards. DP

subject: SUST
title: The Natural Environment Lab
description: A survey of field and laboratory methods commonly used by physical geographers.

subject: SUST
title: An Introduction to Integrative Systems Biology: Hawaiian Biomes as a Framework
description: Lecture/discussion introduces students to the field of biology through the integration of microbiology and macrobiology into a single, comprehensive systems biology with a focus on Hawaiian biomes and ecosystem sustainability.

subject: SUST
title: Biology & Society Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawai‘i. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
prereq_raw: 112 (or concurrent) or GES 102 (or concurrent) or OCN 102 (or concurrent)

subject: SUST
title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Cities
description: How do we plan cities to meet long-term social, economic, and environmental needs? Students will learn about sustainability as it relates to issues like energy, transportation, housing, land, water, and food. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability in a Changing World
description: Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawai‘i/Oceania. Active learning environment.

subject: SUST
title: Humans and the Environment
description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale.

subject: SUST
title: Chemistry in a Sustainable World
description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of the role of natural and man-made chemicals in everyday life, with an emphasis on sustainable and environmentally-sensitive use of chemicals to improve our world. Students who successfully completed CHEM 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 120/CHEM 110 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 120/CHEM 110 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 100 without instructor override.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Food and Energy Field Course
description: Examines the nexus of food, energy, and water in Hawai‘i for sustainable development.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to nine credits

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental History
description: Explores the influence of nature–climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms–on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them.

subject: SUST
title: Religion and the Environment
description: Examines the roles contemporary religious groups play in ground movements for sustainability. Introduces students to key scholars, religious leaders, and activists who are implementing sustainable solutions to pressing environmental problems. FGB

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change
description: Introduction to the science of climate change focusing on Earth’s past, present and future, specifically, the causes, consequences, and record of past changes; future projections, mitigation, and adaptation. Appropriate for both science and non-science majors.
prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 111 or ERTH 130 or ATMO 101 or GES 102, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Historical Ecology of Hawai‘i
description: The Hawaiian socio-ecosystem is the product of centuries of human land use and resource exploitation. Explores the events and processes that have shaped the islands’ ecology and future sustainability.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

subject: SUST
title: Agriculture, Environment, and Society
description: Relationship of plants, soils, and the environment, and how they relate to cultural practices and society in agroecosystems with an emphasis on Hawai‘i as a model system.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Perspectives in Ahupua‘a
description: Examination of the ahupua‘a system as it was conceptualized by the ancient Hawaiians, and exploration of its relevance in modern society; an introductory class to the malama ‘aina track designed to build critical writing skills.

subject: SUST
title: Agricultural and Resource Economics
description: Introduction to basic economics concepts, including demand, supply, exchange, market price and market failure. Economic evaluation and policy for the uses of various natural resource endowments, especially in production agriculture, is included.

subject: SUST
title: Organic Food Crop Production
description: Combined lecture/lab on the theory and practice of certified organic food production. Field visits to organic farms/markets included. Open to nonmajors.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiians
description: The sustainable social system, culture, spirituality, language, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians. Transformation of the sustainable Hawaiian social system by a capitalist economy. Resiliency, land issues, and Native Hawaiian quest for sovereign governance.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

subject: SUST
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Environmental Humanities
description: Introduction to the environmental humanities, which rests at the intersection of the arts, humanities, and environmental studies.

subject: SUST
title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawai‘i. ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only. (Alt years: Spring) DP

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Issues
description: Global environmental problems in historical perspective; physical, biological, sociocultural views.
prereq_raw: one of BIOL 101, BIOL 123, or GEO 101; or consent

subject: SUST
title: Conservation Ethics
description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology.
prereq_raw: any DB course or consent. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Natural Resources Management
description: Biological and physical science aspects of natural resource management at local, national, and global scales. Topics covered include resource management of soil, water, forests, wetlands, coasts and wildlife.
prereq_raw: (NREM/TPSS 251 or 210; CHEM 151 or higher; and BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent

subject: SUST
title: Natural Resource and Environmental Policy
description: Introduction to natural resource and environmental public policy at U.S. federal, Hawai‘i state, local, and international levels. Policy principles, legal structure, governmental agencies, statutes and programs, analytical techniques, program assessments, and contemporary ethical issues.
prereq_raw: SUST/ NREM/PEPS 210 or or NREM/SOCS/TPSS 251 or (BIOL 101 or higher) or GEO 101 or (ERTH 101 or higher); and NREM/SUST 220 or one ECON course or two DS courses

subject: SUST
title: Plant Conservation Biology
description: Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-inpractice in Hawai‘i and elsewhere.
prereq_raw: BOT/ BIOL 305 or consent. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
description: Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components.

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental Issues
description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Water and Society
description: Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Ethics
description: Application of traditional moral theories to environmental issues. Development and evaluation of specific environmental ethical theories. Application of ethical theories to environmental decision-making.
prereq_raw: 210 or GEO 101 or PHIL 101 or PHIL 103

subject: SUST
title: Malama ‘Āina Resource Management Visual Technologies
description: Requires a broad set of knowledge systems. Will introduce students to a variety of visual technologies for use in resource management and the ethical application of these technologies.

subject: SUST
title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
description: Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Environment and Agriculture
description: Overview of environmental issues related to agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts. Ethical issues on impact of agriculture on the environment will be discussed.

subject: SUST
title: Hawai‘i and the Pacific
description: Hawai‘i as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples.

subject: SUST
title: Globalization and Environment
description: Debates on globalization and development, population and resources; root causes of environmental degradation; impacts of globalization on environmentalism and environmental change; social approaches to managing environmental change.

subject: SUST
title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental Politics
description: Evolution of international politics, law and decision-making on a variety of environmental concerns; from endangered species to pollution to climate change. Interaction of population, development, and environment in global governance.

subject: SUST
title: Communicating Sustainability
description: Application of scientific communication theory, strategic communication, and multimedia techniques to select issues of environmental sustainability.
prereq_raw: COM 201 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: SUST
title: Geography, Environment, and Society
description: Examines the geography of resources and environmental change with a holistic and multi-scale perspective. Social approaches to resolving environmental problems.

subject: SUST
title: Culture and Environment
description: Critically examines changing views of nature, nature-culture relationships, and perceptions of the environment across different cultures.

subject: SUST
title: Economics of Global Climate Change
description: Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation.
prereq_raw: 120 or 130 or 131, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
description: Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: SUST
title: Society and Environment
description: Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems.

subject: SUST
title: Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources.

subject: SUST
title: Inter-woven Structures
description: Studio investigation of threads under tension. Thematic lens of environmental vulnerability and resiliency. Explores art practice as embodied knowledge. Specific attention to weaving as meaning and place-making. Engages writing as a significant tool for analysis.

subject: SUST
title: Human Values and the Environment
description: Examination of nature-culture dynamic over a range of contexts–literary ecology, systems ecology, political ecology, eco-feminism, environmental ethics–in order to articulate new possibilities for interdisciplinary understanding of the human place in nature.
prereq_raw: any ENG DL or PHIL or GEO course, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawai‘i
description: Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Development
description: Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawai‘i. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls.
prereq_raw: 120 or 130 or 131, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: SUST
title: Economic Change and Hawai‘i’s People
description: Hawai‘i’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy.

subject: SUST
title: Aloha Kanaloa-Marine Resources and Abundance
description: Undergraduate course exposing students to the resources and processes of the ocean, research, and management approaches, as well as a Hawaiian worldview of oceanic elements. Junior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Basic Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
description: Fundamentals of benefit-cost analysis with extensions to environmental impacts and projects; case studies.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
prereq_raw: WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent

children.text: -level WS course, or SOC 100 or any 200 -level SOC course, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Genetics: Theory to Application
description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Law and Politics
description: Focuses on theories, laws, policies, ethics, and sustainable futures of Hawai‘i and the U.S. Sophomore standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level POLS course, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Politics of the Ocean
description: Study of the ocean as a political place. Engagement with theories, policies, and lived-experiences of the ocean through a political lens, including literature and experiential learning. Sophomore standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200-level POLS course, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Internship for Sustainability and Social Justice
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience in addressing sustainability issues. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent. Consent of instructor.

subject: SUST
title: History of the Indian Ocean World
description: Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women, and merchants. (Alt. years)

subject: SUST
title: Climate, Air Quality, & Policy
description: Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legal aspects of pollution control.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: SUST
title: Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
description: Introduces fundamental techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

subject: SUST
title: The Ocean Economy
description: Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection.

subject: SUST
title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
description: Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: SUST
title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies.

subject: SUST
title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Community and Natural Resource Management
description: Theory and tools for working with groups and communities in the management of natural resources is presented using a participatory format. Topics include sustainable development, extension programming, participatory learning and communication, evaluation, and conflict management.
prereq_raw: two social science courses (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent

children.text: two social science courses ( with a minimum grade of C-

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Tourism Policies and Practices
description: Seminar examining the social, environmental, economic factors of sustainable tourism development. Emphasis on methods and processes and the role of stakeholders (government, industry, host community, tourists). Group projects.

subject: SUST
title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
description: Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management.

subject: SUST
title: Agriculture, Food and Society
description: Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to nonmajors.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Geochemistry
description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants.

subject: SUST
title: Environment, Resources and Society
description: Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues.

subject: SUST
title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
description: Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites. Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning.

subject: SUST
title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
description: Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making. Engages writing as a significant tool for art-making and analysis.

subject: SUST
title: Installation/Performance–Material in Context
description: Studio investigation of the transformation of space (ecological, social, political, psychological) through artist intervention. Experiments in non-object based interventions and into the evocative potential of materials. Engages writing and oral expression as significant analytical tools.

subject: SUST
title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation.

subject: SUST
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.

subject: SUST
title: Infrastructure: Project Impacts, Policy and Sustainability
description: Evaluation of infrastructure impacts. Impacts regulation and mitigation. Effects of environmental and other policies on infrastructure. Infrastructure relations to sustainability. Energy consumption, transportation efficiency and infrastructure recycling. Lectures and presentations by experts and enrolled students. Senior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: senior standing, open to engineering, science, urban planning, and economics majors

children.text: open to engineering, science, urban planning,

subject: SUST
title: Ethnoecology and Conservation
description: Ecological implications of cultural uses of plants. Examines the biological basis for, and ecological effects of traditional and local resource management systems.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
description: Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork.

subject: SUST
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. Senior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
description: Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota.
prereq_raw: one semester of biological sciences at college level

prereq_tree.text: one semester of biological sciences at college level

subject: SUST
title: Wildlife Ecology and Management
description: Lecture-based overview of the history, ecology, and management of wildlife species from around the world and Hawai‘i.
prereq_raw: BIOL 172 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Sovereignty in Pacific Context
description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C)

subject: SUST
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
prereq_raw: HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 307/ SUST 317 or HWST/SUST 356 (Cross-listed as HWST 458 and NREM 458

subject: SUST
title: ‘Āina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawai‘i.

subject: SUST
title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
description: Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources.

subject: SUST
title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O‘ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.

subject: SUST
title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawai‘i. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives.

subject: SUST
title: Global Ethnic Conflict
description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

subject: SUST
title: Applied Forest Ecology
description: Application of ecological theory to sustainable management of forest resources in Hawaii and beyond, including silviculture (production of timber and nontimber forest products), restoration (restoring damaged or degraded forests), and conservation (conserving existing forest resources).
prereq_raw: (311/NREM 310 and NREM 380) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent

subject: SUST
title: American Environmental History
description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

subject: SUST
title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
description: Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature.

subject: SUST
title: Contemporary Art and Ecology
description: Explores the recent history of environmental and ecological art; provides a critical framework for the contemporary image politics of environmentalism, ecology, sustainability, and climate change with an emphasis on writing and ethical reasoning.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Problem Solving
description: Senior-level capstone for NREM and related majors. Ecosystem management within problemsolving context. Applications of research and analytical methods, management tools to case studies. Focus on student teamwork and oral communications.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability Capstone
description: Capstone for undergraduate students in interdisciplinary studies focusing on sustainability. The capstone experience provides an opportunity for students to gain knowledge and research experience in an applied setting.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas.

subject: SUST
title: Literacy Across the Disciplines
description: Explores theoretical and practical principles of literacy and sustainability across academic disciplines, investigating the role of language and literate practices of reading, writing, speaking, visualizing, and representing in social, cultural, and educational contexts. Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Seminar on Water in History
description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history.

subject: SUST
title: Resource and Environmental Policy Analysis
description: Exploration of institutional and policy dimensions of natural resource development, management, allocation, markets and pricing, focusing on their environmental impacts. Emphasis on policy analysis using case studies and empirical findings. Original paper required.
prereq_raw: grade of Cor above in ECON 130 or NREM/SUST 220, or consent

children.text: grade of Cor above in ECON 130

subject: SUST
title: Predicting and Controlling Degradation in Human-Dominated Terrestrial Ecosystems
description: Historic, present, and projected trends in understanding and managing human-dominated ecosystems; predicting, measuring and mitigating degradation especially in terrestrial ecosystems with a focus on small volcanic islands in tropical settings.
prereq_raw: NREM 301/ SUST 311 and NREM 304 (or equivalent) and NREM 600. Recommended NREM 461, or consent

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent

subject: SUST
title: Advanced Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
description: Introduces advanced techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Planning and Policy
description: Overview of urbanization and environmental change. An examination of environmental laws, policies, planning and urban design strategies designed to minimize and mitigate urban impacts.

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk.
prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable

subject: SUST
title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy.

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change.

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the Asia/Pacific Region
description: Analysis of planning responses to human-induced climate change and related environmental problems. Part of the Asia/Pacific Initiative taught in collaboration with universities throughout the region via videoconferencing.

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Geology
description: Geological history and geologic framework of the Hawaiian shoreline. Modern climate change, paleoclimate, focus on sea level change. Modern coastal management and problems in the coastal environment. Coastal planning.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, credit earned one time

subject: SUST
title: Urban Environmental Problems
description: Seminar that examines environmental problems associated with urbanization. Reviews strategic approaches and collaboration among key actors to address such problems.

subject: SUST
title: Planning in Hawai‘i and Pacific Islands
description: Urban and regional planning in island settings. Experiences in Hawai‘i, Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia. Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options.
prereq_raw: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent

subject: SUST
title: Resource Economics
description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Resource Economics
description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development.

subject: SUST
title: Land Systems Science
description: Through discussion of primary land systems science literature and use of environmental modeling software, this interdisciplinary course explores how drivers, states, and trends in human appropriation of land affect socio-ecological system function.
prereq_raw: NREM 477 or NREM 677 or GEO 470 or GEO 476 or ERTH 460 or ERTH 461

subject: SUST
title: (Alpha) Seminar
description: Study in trends, research, and problems of implementation in teaching field. (P) place-based education. Each alpha COE-related majors only.
prereq_raw: graduate and/or undergraduate courses in education and/ or social sciences or consent

subject: SUST
title: Urban and Regional Planning for Sustainability
description: Focus on ideology, conceptual models, accounting frameworks, appropriate technologies, and indicators of planning for sustainability. Central and local policies, plans, and best practices in various countries and settings will be covered. Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Kānāwai Lawai‘a: Hawa‘i’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance. (Alt. years: Fall)

subject: SUST
title: Advanced Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
description: Advanced environmental benefit-cost analysis will require that proficiency be demonstrated on fundamentals and address topics related to sustainability, including income equality, non-market goods, risk, cost of public funds, and the social discount rate.

subject: SUST
title: He Ali‘i Ka ‘Āina; Land, Resources, and Leadership
description: Seminar focused on leadership challenges in Mālama ‘Āina to bridge ancestral and contemporary systems to better steward resources, produce abundance, work with and in community, and pivot large institutions for a better Aloha ‘Āina future.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
description: Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips.

subject: SUST
title: Sociology of Sustainability
description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives. Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Marine Renewable Energy
description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power.
prereq_raw: ORE 607; basic knowledge of thermodynamics desirable

subject: SUST
title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought. Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas.

subject: ANAT
title: (Alpha) Unit VII Anatomy Electives
description: Advanced study of human anatomy by dissection and individual observation of surgical procedures. (C) topics in reproductive biology.
prereq_raw: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531 or 532; or consent

children.text: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531

subject: ANAT
title: Independent Study in Anatomy
description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology.

subject: ANAT
title: Lower Extremity, Thorax, and Abdomen
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the lower extremity, thorax, and abdomen. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

subject: ANAT
title: Upper Extremity, Head, Neck, and Spine
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the upper extremity, head, neck, and spine. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

subject: ANAT
title: Human Embryology
description: Systematic study of human development, including implantation, placentation, basics of development of each organ system with reference to pertinent congenital anomalies and their surgical repair.

subject: ANAT
title: Seminar in Anatomy Teaching
description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses in anatomical sciences, development and evaluation of exams, experience in teaching with audiovisual/ computer aids. Open to graduate students in physiology or KRS.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable eight times, up to 32 credits

subject: BIOC
title: Fundamentals of Biochemistry
description: Biological chemistry stressing integration of concepts of general, inorganic, and biochemistry and application to life chemistry.
prereq_raw: beginning algebra and high school science

subject: BIOC
title: Elements of Biochemistry
description: Biochemical principles and concepts as applied to living systems, including sufficient organic chemistry to understand these principles.
prereq_raw: 141 with C or better, or consent

subject: BIOC
title: Basic Biochemistry
description: Principles of biochemistry, applicable to medicine and real-life situations, involving metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, and vitamins. Taught by biomedical researchers. Evaluated based on exams, quizzes, homework, and group presentation.

subject: BIOC
title: Directed Research and Reading
description: Independent research or selected reading of current literature in the area of biochemistry and biophysics.

subject: BIOC
title: Topics in Biochemistry
description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students take an in-depth study of selected topics in biochemistry.

subject: BIOC
title: Highlights of Organ-System Biochemistry
description: Provides highly interactive, small group discussions on concepts of biochemistry important to the various organ systems; such as cardiac, respiratory, hematology, gastrointestinal, endocrine, musculoskeletal and neurological systems, and relevant to clinical medicine.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Physiology and Anatomy
description: Introduction to human physiology and anatomy designed to serve the needs of dental hygiene students and others interested in pursuing health-related careers.

subject: PHYL
title: Physiology and Anatomy Lab
description: Laboratory to complement 103.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology
description: Anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics of human organ systems presented in integrated anatomy-physiology format. Priority to students in nursing.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
description: Anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics of human organ systems presented in integrated anatomy-physiology format. Priority to students in nursing.

subject: PHYL
