title: Human Anatomy and Physiology
description: Continuation of 141.
prereq_raw: should have an understanding of basic physiology concepts as presented in 141 or equivalent

children.text: should have an understanding of basic physiology concepts as presented in 141

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
description: Anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics of human organ systems presented in integrated anatomy-physiology format. Priority to students in nursing.

subject: PHYL
title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology
description: Integrated presentation of human anatomy and physiology. An optional laboratory (PHYL 301L) is available separately.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172, or any PHYL course; and CHEM 161 (or higher) or any BIOC course; or consent

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
description: Laboratory study of human anatomy and physiology by means of models, histology slides, experiments, and demonstrations.

subject: PHYL
title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology
description: Continuation of 301.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
description: Continuation of 301L.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Physiology: Organ Systems
description: Basic function of the major organ systems in man. Covers cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, acid-base, and gastrointestinal physiology.

subject: PHYL
title: Human Physiology: Integrative Systems
description: Senior-level course in integrative systems (central nervous system and endocrinology). Complements 401.
prereq_raw: 401 and either BIOC 341 or CHEM 152, or consent

subject: PHYL
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Students will learn fundamental concepts and multiple techniques in molecular biology, physiology, and histology for cardiovascular research through the projects in the lab. Junior or senior standing only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned to two credits only

subject: REPR
title: Seminar in Biomedical Sciences
description: Presentation and discussion of current research topics in biomedical sciences.

subject: REPR
title: Special Topics in Reproductive Biology
description: In-depth discussion of selected areas of reproductive biology, with special emphasis on recent research results and methodologies. May be retaken for credit.

subject: BIOM
title: Directed Research and Reading
description: To provide elective courses for undergraduates in the biomedical sciences specialties.

subject: BIOM
title: Clinical Research Review
description: Research elective for medical students. MD students only.

subject: BIOM
title: Global Health and Medicine: Emerging Problems and Impact
description: Analysis of emerging problems and impact in countries on a multidimensional perspective.
restrictions_raw: BIOM, NURS, PH, SPA majors only.

subject: BIOM
title: Introduction to Clinical Nutrition
description: Overview of applied clinical nutrition that includes nutrients, dietary recommendations for healthy populations and medical nutrition therapies for patients with diet related diseases or conditions. Graduate students only.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (or higher) or PHYL 141 or ZOOL 141 or consent

subject: BIOM
title: Introduction to Clinical Research
description: Instruction in developing clinical research questions and creating a concise protocol that includes a literature review, study design, subject recruitment and sampling, instruments, other measures and bioinformatics, sample size, consent form, budget and timetable.

subject: BIOM
title: Legal and Regulatory Issues and Bioethics
description: Ethical dilemmas in clinical research are identified and resolved in cases, research on human subjects regulation are discussed. Research misconduct is defined. Ethical considerations in protocol developed in the Designing Clinical Research course are resolved.

subject: BIOM
title: Translational Research Methods
description: Lectures focus on translational research methods through selected genetic and acquired diseases including cancer, neurodevelopmental, inflammatoryimmune, and metabolic conditions with insight into analyses of DNA, RNA, genomics-proteomics, cell and animal models, and advanced imaging.

subject: BIOM
title: Clinical Protocol Development
description: Provides training in proposal development. Governance structures of funding agencies; funding opportunities and decisions; review processes; NIH application and processes; reading RFAs; compliance issues; cultural sensitivity; and types of questions using databases are addressed.

subject: BIOM
title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research I
description: Introductory lecture-seminar on the conduct of multidisciplinary research from a culturally competent perspective.

subject: BIOM
title: Foundations of Biomedical Ethics
description: Explores the foundations of biomedical ethics via small group seminars and discussion, presentations. Enrolled in MS or PhD in Biomedical Sciences program only. (Alt. years)

subject: BIOM
title: Advanced Ethics in Biomedical Research II
description: Develop biomedical ethics through case studies to incite discussions on topics such as gene therapy, gene enhancement, genetic counseling, informed consent, health care professional/patient and investigator/student participant communication, advanced directives and living wills, clinical research in developing countries, clinical research in ethnic minority and socio-economically disadvantaged populations, and non-discrimination in health care and research settings.

subject: BIOM
title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research II
description: Explore topics in cultural competence in greater depth, encouraging trainees to address issues from a unified yet flexible conceptual framework. Involves building knowledge, skills and action plans to address a range of learning styles and to appreciate and benefit from diversity.

subject: BIOM
title: PhD Team Building Seminar
description: Seminar focuses on teaching participants to work independently and collaborate in order to accomplish specific results. Students will be exposed to group dynamics, communication, healthy competition, conflict resolution, and innovative means of crossing boundaries between departments, organizations, industries and disciplines.

subject: BIOM
title: Medical Genetics
description: Focus on heritable disorders, genetic mechanisms, patterns of inheritance, phenotype-genotype correlations, genetic/ environmental factors, clinical diagnoses, genomic and precision medicine.

subject: BIOM
title: Mentored Research Practicum
description: Conduct research under the direction of a mentor. Participants will be responsible for submission of a proposal, acquisition of IRB approval, and conduct of the project. BIOM students only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable five times or up to 12 credits

subject: BIOM
title: Advanced Biostatistics for Clinical Research
description: Current methods for analyzing longitudinal and clustered, clinical data through lectures, discussions, and a group analysis. Topic areas include multi-level, multi-state, multi-process, and structural equation models.

subject: BIOM
title: Directed Research
description: Students may register on approval of department.

subject: BIOM
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable seven times or up to 8 credits

subject: BIOM
title: Disasters and Pandemics: Medical and PH Management and Risk Communication
description: Assess impact on health in disasters and diseases. Enhances research skills related to management and communication.
restrictions_raw: BIOM, PH, NURS, and SPA majors only.

subject: BIOM
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. CR/ NC only.

subject: CAAM
title: Mindfulness Meditation and Stress Reduction
description: Practice mindfulness meditation to reduce burnout and live life in the present moment. Learn life skills to handle life better and be more resilient. Respond rather than react to life. No experience necessary.

subject: CAAM
title: Clinical Nutrition
description: Overview of applied clinical nutrition that includes nutrients, dietary recommendations for healthy populations, and medical nutrition therapies for patients with diet related diseases or conditions. Junior standing and higher.
prereq_raw: CHEM 151 (or higher) or PHYL 141 or BIOL 171 or approval from instructor; highly encouraged: FSHN 185 or any other basic nutrition course

children.text: from instructor; highly encouraged: FSHN 185 or any other basic nutrition course

subject: CAAM
title: Introduction to Integrative Medicine
description: Overview of integrative (complementary) medicine covering Traditional Chinese Medicine, Ayurvedic medicine, naturapathy, traditional healing practices, homeopathy, nutrition and diet, herbs and dietary supplements, environmental health, mind-body, energy, spiritual, and positive psychology.

subject: CAAM
title: Nutrition for Clinicians
description: Provides in-depth lectures and case studies reviewing the role of nutritional therapy in health and illness.

subject: QHS
title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results.

subject: QHS
title: Generalized Linear Model
description: Statistical theory of Linear Model and Generalized Linear Model, algorithms use for estimation, inference concepts, and assessment of goodness-of-fit. Covers Proportional Hazard Model and Generalized Estimating Equations.
prereq_raw: 601 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: QHS
title: Bioinformatics I
description: Provides fundamental concepts in bioinformatics with strong emphasis on hands-on training. Topics such as molecular biology, sequence alignment, biological databases, phytogeny, and genomics including microarray and RNA-sequence analysis. Open to nonmajors. (Cross-listed with TRMD 653)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, but credit earned one time only

subject: QHS
title: Bioinformatics II
description: Focus on bioinformatics approaches for functional genomics related to DNA, RNA, and protein. It will provide of virus, bacteria, and human genome and bioinformatics approaches to human disease.
prereq_raw: 610 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

children.text: ( or equivalent) ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: QHS
title: Introduction to Clinical Trials
description: Introduction to clinical trials. Topics include history, definitions/terminology, adverse events, FDA and government regulatory agencies, ethics; monitoring committees, recruitment, introduction to protocol development, basis designs.

subject: QHS
title: Design and Analysis of Clinical Trials
description: Covers basic and advanced statistical methods utilized in clinical trials design, conduct, and data analysis. Topics cover statistician’s role in drug development and DSMB, statistical theory in phases I-IV clinical trial designs and analysis.
prereq_raw: 601 (or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B or consent

children.text: ( or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B or consent

subject: QHS
title: Secondary Data Analysis Practicum
description: Introduces students to issues in working with complex data sets and adds the hands-on experience needed to conduct individual research using secondary databases.
prereq_raw: (601 (or equivalent) and 650) with a minimum grade of B, which can be taken concurrently

children.text: ( or equivalent) and 650 ) with a minimum grade of B , which can be taken concurrently

subject: QHS
title: Special Topics in Quantitative Health Sciences
description: Special topics in quantitative health sciences. Reflects special research interest of QHS faculty or guest lecturers.

subject: QHS
title: Biostatistical Consulting
description: Investigate the roles and responsibilities of the biostatistician as both consultant and collaborator with biomedical researchers, guide students in enhancing problem-solving and communication skills, and provide opportunity to observe real-life biostatistical consultations.
prereq_raw: 601 and 602 (or equivalent) with minimum grades of B, and consent

children.text: ( or equivalent) with minimum grades of B, and consent

subject: QHS
title: Biostatistical Consulting Practicum
description: Under the supervision of biostatistics faculty members, students will have the opportunity to provide statistical consultations to biomedical researchers and gain hands-on experience conducting biostatistical analysis in solving real-life analytic problems.
prereq_raw: 675 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of B
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to six credits

subject: QHS
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through the process of conducting a research study.

subject: CMB
title: Genetics, Evolution and Society
description: The role of genetics in evolution, medicine, behavior, plant and animal breeding and technology; its impact on today’s society.
prereq_raw: one semester of biological science at college level or consent. Not a BIOL major elective

children.text: one semester of biological science at college level

subject: CMB
title: Human Genetics
description: Principles of human genetics. Designed for pre-medical or pre-dental students or others who require a course with emphasis on human genetics.

subject: CMB
title: Genetical Problems
description: Directed reading and research in genetics.

subject: CMB
title: Unit V Topics in Genetics
description: First-year elective course in which medical students may take an in-depth study of genetics.

subject: CMB
title: Bioethics
description: Prepare medical students to identify and resolve ethical dilemmas in medical career and biomedical research, and to maintain integrity and professionalism in accordance with relevant ethical principles, policies, and laws.

subject: CMB
title: Research Topics in Cell Molecular Biology
description: Research elective for medical students.

subject: CMB
title: Evolutionary Genetics
description: Genetic changes involved in the processes of adaptation and in species formation.

children.text: Recommended: population and / or quantitative genetics

subject: CMB
title: Introduction to Neurosciences
description: An interdisciplinary overview of the central nervous system, drawn from current knowledge and research on vertebrate and invertebrate neurobiology.

subject: CMB
title: Public Health Biology
description: Writing intensive asynchronous computer-based course examines biological processes and challenges relevant to the public health professional. Topics include anatomical, pathophysiological, and molecular bases of public health; genetics, immunology, ethics; disease prevention, control, and management. (Once a year)

subject: CMB
title: Seminar in Biomedical Sciences
description: Presentation and discussion of research topics in biomedical science.

subject: CMB
title: Cell Molecular Biology I
description: Molecular approaches to cell structure and function emphasizing cells in multi-cellular plants and animals.
prereq_raw: BIOL 402 or MBBE 402; and BIOC 441, BIOL 408, and graduate standing; or consent. Recommended: CHEM 351

subject: CMB
title: Cell Molecular Biology II
description: Molecular approaches to cell structure and function emphasizing cells in multi-cellular plants and animals.
prereq_raw: 621, BIOC 441, and BIOL 408; and either BIOL 402 or MBBE 402; or consent

subject: CMB
title: Advanced Topics in Genetics
description: Advanced treatment of frontiers in genetics.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in genetics or consent

subject: CMB
title: Ethics in Biomedical Research
description: Topics include responsible data management, recording, reporting, misconduct and scientific fraud, conflicts of interest, critical use of animals and human issues and subjects in research, genetic screening, stem cell and gene therapy and patenting.

subject: CMB
title: Research Rotations
description: Individualized research project in three laboratories of CMB faculty with a written report on each project. Faculty laboratories will be selected by consultation with student’s graduate committee and individual faculty.

subject: CMB
title: Neuropharmacology
description: Physiology and pharmacology of central and peripheral nervous systems, focusing on synaptic chemistry and signaling.
prereq_raw: 606, or consent from the course director

subject: CMB
title: Introductory Biostatistics for the Bench Biologist
description: Lecture and example-based introduction to the critical biostatistics skills commonly required of the bench life scientist. Technical literacy and basic practical application are the goals. Problem sets will be scored.

subject: CMB
title: Introductory Bioinformatics for the Bench Biologist
description: Modern biomolecular and genomic concepts are explored through brief guided hands-on web-based bioinformatic projects using public domain resources. Understanding key concepts and algorithms, technical literacy, and operational confidence are goals. Programming skill development is student-optional.

subject: CMB
title: Population Genetics
description: Mathematical, observational, experimental results on effects of mutation, selection, and systems of mating on distribution of genes. Analysis of non-experimental populations.

subject: CMB
title: Literature Analysis and Scientific Writing
description: Aims to improve the skills of graduate students in Biomedical Sciences in literature search, analysis, and management, as well as in scientific writing and other forms of scientific communication. Graduate students only or consent.

subject: CMB
title: (Alpha) Genetics Seminar
description: Research and topical literature reports in genetics. May be repeated. (B) molecular genetics; (C) molecular biology of cancer; (D) human genetics; (E) cytogenetics; (F) evolutionary genetics; (G) molecular biology of the cell; (H) drosophila genetics; (I) population/statistical genetics; (J) developmental genetics; (K) insect molecular biology; (M) genetics and molecular biology of fungi.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in genetics or consent

subject: CMB
title: Essentials in Grant Writing
description: (1 2-hr Lec) Presentation and discussion of hypothesis-driven research and grant writing. Topics include the process of proposal, submission, and review. Course work includes writing, critiquing, and revising a proposal. Graduate students only. CR/ NC only.

subject: CMB
title: Techniques in Genetics
description: Laboratory training in procedures used in diagnosis of genetic diseases, cytogenetics, immunogenetics, and dermatoglyphics.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in genetics or consent

subject: CMB
title: Techniques in Genetics
description: Continuation of 671.

subject: CMB
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: CMB
title: Special Topics in Neurosciences
description: Advanced topics in neuroscience, from basic neurobiology to clinical neurology and psychiatry. Emphasis on current investigations at the cellular or molecular level.

subject: CSD
title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech and Hearing Mechanism
description: Will overview anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing. Students gain exposure to structures and functions of respiration, phonation, resonance, articulation, deglutition, and hearing systems required for normal communication and swallowing.

subject: CSD
title: Phonetics
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of phonetic and phonological development. International Phonetic Alphabet Transcription of English speech sounds; phonological developments and models; cultural variations; analysis interpretation and other considerations related to speech sound development and production.

subject: CSD
title: Speech and Language Development
description: Will develop an understanding of children’s acquisition of speech, language, and normal communication development from birth through adolescence.

subject: CSD
title: Acoustics and Psychoacoustics of Speech and Hearing
description: Provides an understanding of the fundamental processes underlying the production and perception of speech. Students gain an understanding of the physical and psychological aspects of sound and their measurement.

subject: CSD
title: Introduction to Clinical Methods in Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Provides observation and discussion of the clinical management of individuals with communication disorders, and practical experience related to clinical procedures and requirements.

subject: CSD
title: Introduction to Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Information and theoretical foundations serve as an introduction to the field of communication disorders. Will provide an overview of the normal processes and disorders of speech, language, hearing, and swallowing.

subject: CSD
title: Introduction to Audiometry and Auditory Disorders
description: Covers anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, acoustic, basic knowledge of auditory disorders and testing procedures, and introduction to rehabilitative audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Basic Statistics for Health-Related Professionals
description: Provides students from behavioral sciences and health-related professions with an overview of normal distribution, central tendency, variability, sampling, hypothesis testing, frequency distribution, correlation, regression, and t-test.

subject: CSD
title: Research Methods
description: Research methods applicable to the field of speech-language pathology and audiology; analysis and reporting of data. Required of all CSD graduate students.
prereq_raw: previous coursework in inferential statistics and consent

subject: CSD
title: Neuroscience in Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Explores the neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of the human nervous system as it relates to communication and swallowing and how neurological pathologies lead to behavioral deficits in those areas.

subject: CSD
title: Audiological Foundations for SpeechLanguage Pathology
description: Instrumentation; special tests of hearing.

subject: CSD
title: Seminar in Motor Speech Disorders
description: Provides in-depth examination of various motor speech disorders, including apraxia of speech and dysarthria. Emphasis is on assessment/treatment of these diagnoses. Review of current treatment literature, anatomy/physiology, practical exercises in treatment planning.

subject: CSD
title: Disorders of Phonology and Articulation
description: Study of the etiology, assessment, and remediation of disorders and articulation.

subject: CSD
title: Child Language Disorders
description: Study of the etiology, behavioral characteristics and treatment methods for child language disorders. Examination of methods, test, and instruments employed in diagnosis of child language disorders. Includes identification of language deficits and writing intervention goals.

subject: CSD
title: Language Development for Children with Hearing Deficiencies
description: Language acquisition by hard-of-hearing and deaf children; methods of stimulating growth.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology I
description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, credit earned for six credits only

subject: CSD
title: Audiology Practicum for SpeechLanguage Pathology
description: Clinical practice in administering tests, interpreting results; counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

subject: CSD
title: Voice Disorders
description: Contemporary development and theoretical issues in the diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of vocal system disorders in children and adults; current literature and clinical practice issues are addressed.

subject: CSD
title: Adult Neurogenic Language and Cognitive-Communication Disorders
description: Study of acquired adult language and cognitive communication disorders associated with stroke, traumatic brain injury, and dementia. Application of evidence-based procedures and strategies for assessment and intervention, review of current literature, and discussion of professional issues.

subject: CSD
title: Research–Speech Pathology
description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing speech-language pathology.

subject: CSD
title: Research–Audiology
description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing audiology.

subject: CSD
title: (Alpha) Directed Study
description: To allow student and faculty advisor to design research/study units outside existing academic structure in specialized area. (B) language pathology; (C) audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Amplification: Assessment and Applications
description: Comprehensive study of amplification. Assessment, fitting, evaluation, electroacoustic evaluation, dispensing. Personal instruments and instructional-educational systems.

subject: CSD
title: Disorders of Fluency
description: Contemporary developments and theoretical issues in diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of disorders of fluency such as stuttering in both children and adults.

subject: CSD
title: Electrophysiologic Audiometry
description: Study of early, middle, and late auditory evoked potentials with emphasis on the auditory brainstem response.

subject: CSD
title: Dysphagia: Disorders of Swallowing
description: Explores the dynamics of normal and disordered swallowing across the life span with emphasis on the adult population.

subject: CSD
title: (Alpha) Special Topics in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology
description: (B) study of contemporary developments in speech/language pathology; (C) study of contemporary developments in audiology.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable for credit for different alphas unlimited times

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology II
description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings. Repeatable unlimited times, credit earned for 12 credits only

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology II
description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results; counseling individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

subject: CSD
title: Seminar in Audiology–Diagnostic Procedures
description: Study of diagnostic procedures as reflected in current literature.

subject: CSD
title: Seminar in Audiology–Rehabilitative Procedures
description: Procedures and philosophies presented in recent literature dealing with rehabilitative phases of audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology III
description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedure with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, up to 18 credits

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology III
description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results, counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

subject: FMCH
title: Family Medicine and Community Health Longitudinal Clerkship
description: 5.5-month ambulatory clerkship. Students learn history taking, physical exam skills, and management of family medicine patients. Emphasis on behavioral care, caring for the underserved, sports medicine, preventive care, and common acute/chronic ambulatory problems.
coreq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses

subject: FMCH
title: (Alpha) Electives in Family Medicine and Community Health
description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students may do study of selected topics within the field of family medicine and community health: (B) primary care preceptorship; (C) topics in community health; (D) sub-internship in family medicine; (E) extramural elective in family medicine and community health-miscellaneous; (F) sports medicine preceptorship; (G) longitudinal underserved care preceptorship (6). MED majors only for (G).

subject: GERI
title: Geriatric and Palliative Care
description: Provides an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in the outpatient, inpatient, homecare, and long-term care settings. Various instructional methods are utilized, including clinical experiences, workshops, and case discussions using a range of interdisciplinary teachers.

subject: GERI
title: Geriatric Medicine Research
description: Medical students will have the opportunity to complete a research project in the field of epidemiology of aging, and present an abstract at a local meeting. Basic principles of epidemiology and statistics will be taught.

subject: GERI
title: Geriatric and Palliative Medicine Elective
description: F\Provides an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in the outpatient, inpatient, homecare, and long-term care settings. Various instructional methods are utilized, including clinical experiences, workshops, and case discussions using a range of interdisciplinary teachers.

subject: GERI
title: Medical Student Training in Aging Program
description: Introduces medical students to clinical, research, and academic experiences in geriatrics, under the mentorship of faculty members.

subject: GERI
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: One-on-one independent study for students interested in geriatrics and/or palliative medicine. Students will work with a faculty mentor to define an area of interest and meet regularly for guidance and feedback.

subject: MDED
title: Evidence-Based Medicine
description: Critical appraisal track designed to improve the student’s ability to seek and evaluate new medical knowledge.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 8 Block Selective
description: Through lectures, self-assessments and independent study, second-year medical students will consolidate their knowledge of the application of the biological sciences to patient care.

subject: MDED
title: Clinical Skills Assessment
description: Required comprehensive interdepartment multidisciplinary assessment program for fourth-year medical students.
prereq_raw: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531 or 532

children.text: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531

subject: MDED
title: (Alpha) Senior Interdisciplinary Electives
description: Fourth-year elective in which students study selected interdisciplinary topics. (B) medical education elective; (C) complementary and alternative medicine; (D) leadership in underserved care; (E) Junior PBL course director. MED majors only for (D). CR/NC only for (D) and (E).
prereq_raw: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531 or 532. (Spring only for (D) and (E))

children.text: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531

subject: MDED
title: MD 1 Health and Illness
description: Introduction to concepts of health and disease through lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 1 health care problems in tutorials.

subject: MDED
title: MD 1 Health and Illness Tutorials
description: Introductory series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on concepts of health and disease through MD 1 health care problems.

subject: MDED
title: MD 2 CV/Pulmonary
description: Concepts focusing on cardiovascular and pulmonary systems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 2 health care problems in tutorials.

subject: MDED
title: MD 2 CV/Pulmonary Tutorials
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on cardiovascular and pulmonary health care problems.

subject: MDED
title: MD 3 Renal/Hematology
description: Concepts focusing on renal and hematologic systems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 3 health care problems in tutorials.

subject: MDED
title: MD 3 Renal/Hematology Tutorials
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on renal and hematology health care problems.

subject: MDED
title: MD 4 GI/Endocrine
description: Concepts focusing on gastrointestinal and endocrine systems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 4 health care problems in tutorials.

subject: MDED
title: MD 4 GI/Endocrine Tutorials
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on gastrointestinal and endocrine health care problems.

subject: MDED
title: MD 6 Locomotor System, Nervous System and Behavioral Problems
description: Concepts focusing on the locomotor/neurological systems and behavioral problems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 6 health care problems in tutorials.

subject: MDED
title: MD 6 Locomotor System, Nervous System, and Behavioral Problems
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for second-year medical students focusing on neurological/ locomotor systems and behavioral health care problems.

subject: MDED
title: MD 7 The Life Cycle
description: Concepts focusing on the life cycle through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 7 health care problems in tutorials.

subject: MDED
title: MD 7 The Life Cycle Tutorials
description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for second-year medical students focusing on the life cycle health care problems.

subject: MDED
title: Third Year Colloquia
description: A series of lecture-discussions intended to broaden the perspectives of the Unit VI experiences and healthcare problems.

subject: MDED
title: (Alpha) Senior Seminars
description: Review of topics and issues that will prepare senior students for the end of their undergraduate training and the start of their internship. (B) Week 1; (C) Week 2; (D) Week 3. CR/ NC only. (Fall only for B); (Spring only for C and D)

subject: MDED
title: Introduction to Clinical Skills
description: Introductory lectures and laboratories on history taking and physical exam skills.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 2 Clinical Skills
description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 2.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 3 Clinical Skills
description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 3.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 4 Clinical Skills
description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 4.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 6 Clinical Skills
description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 6.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 7 Clinical Skills
description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 7.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 1 Community Health
description: Field experience placing students in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 2 Community Health
description: Field experience placing students in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 3 Community Health
description: Field experience placing student in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients.

subject: MDED
title: Unit 4 Community Health
description: Field experience placing student in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients.

subject: MDED
title: (Alpha) Preclinical Electives
description: Elective for first and second year medical students. (B) projects in medical education; (C) healer’s art; (D) introduction to student research; (E) health and wellness; (F) quality improvement; (G) introduction to ultrasound. MD majors only for (G).
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to two credits

subject: MDED
title: (Alpha) Topics in Medical Education
description: Summer selectives in medical education for second-year medical students. (B) rural health preceptorship; (C) health issues of the Pacific Basin; (D) projects in medical education; (E) manikin simulations; (F) learning resources; (G) cardiovascular case maps; (H) pulmonary case maps; (I) clinical skills preceptors; (J) global health perspectives.

subject: MDED
title: Research in Medical Education
description: An elective for medical students to work on research projects related to improving medical education, student wellness, and community health under the direction of a faculty member in the Office of Medical Education.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable nine times, up to six credits

subject: MED
title: Internal Medicine Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Six-month long clerkship in ambulatory setting, and four-week hospital-based experience.
prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses

subject: MED
title: Advanced Medicine Clerkship
description: Required 4 weeks duration for fourth-year medical students. Advanced experiences in ambulatory and hospital-based medical care. Proficiency in this course may be established by examination.
prereq_raw: fourth-year standing and completion of 531, or consent

subject: MED
title: (Alpha) Electives in Medicine
description: Fourth-year electives in which students study selected topics within field of medicine. (B) allergy/immunology; (C) cardiology; (D) medicine elective in Asia; (E) dermatology; (F) endocrinology; (G) gastroenterology; (H) general internal medicine: ambulatory care; (I) general internal medicine: inpatient; (K) hematology; (M) nephrology; (N) neurology; (O) nuclear medicine; (P) oncology; (Q) pulmonary diseases; (R) research in medicine; (S) rehabilitation medicine; (T) rheumatology; (U) heart failure/electrophysiology; (W) internal medicine sub-internship. MD students only for (U).

subject: MED
title: (Alpha) Electives in Medicine
description: Fourthyear electives in which students study selected topics within field of medicine. (B) extramural electives in medicine (miscellaneous); (C) internal medicine seminar; (D) infectious disease; (E) internal medicine sub-internship; (F) research in bioethics; (G) neurology critical care; (H) medical informatics; (O) obesity medicine.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for (C)–(E); not repeatable for (F); repeatable two times for (B), (C) and (H); repeatable three times for (G)

subject: MEDT
title: Introduction to Medical Technology
description: Designed to acquaint students to the field of medical technology (clinical laboratory science).

subject: MEDT
title: Introduction to Medical Technology II
description: Basic principles and lab skills in medical technology (medical lab science). Required for second bachelor’s degree students (not MLT credentialed) wishing to major in medical technology. Second bachelor’s degree students only.

subject: MEDT
title: The Clinical Laboratory
description: Theory and clinical application of medical laboratory methods and healthcare professional relationships.

subject: MEDT
title: The Clinical Laboratory II
description: Theory and clinical application of medical technology methods and healthcare professional relationships. Companion course to MEDT 301; and required, for second bachelor’s degree students who were admitted to MEDT major. Second Bachelor’s degree standing or higher.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Lab Management
description: Student will become familiar with fundamental administration of a clinical laboratory to include technical, personnel, and financial management areas.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Parasitology
description: Modern diagnostic practices in parasitology.

subject: MEDT
title: Hematology
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental study of blood in normal and pathological states: formation, development, and classification of blood cells.

subject: MEDT
title: Hematology Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany MEDT 451. Emphasis on writing to study content.

subject: MEDT
title: Immunohematology
description: Antigen-antibody relationships in human blood, study of blood groups, clinical problems in transfusion.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Biochemistry I
description: Biochemical processes in human health and disease states.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Biochemistry II
description: Continuation of 471.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Lab Methods and Analyses I
description: Lab experiments illustrating fundamental principles and methods of clinical laboratory analyses.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Lab Methods and Analyses II
description: Continuation of 477.

subject: MEDT
title: Professional Issues in Medical Lab Science
description: Discussions about various professional issues through oral presentations and critiquing of peer presentations.

subject: MEDT
title: Special Topics in Medical Technology
description: Acquaints student with role of the medical technologist and overlap of major sciences in clinical situations to help student develop qualities unique to med technology.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Microbiology Preceptorship
description: Clinical training for students with bachelor’s degree in microbiology to be able to qualify as clinical microbiologists in a healthcare setting. Includes specimen procurement, processing, detection and identification, susceptibility testing, and other diagnostic technology.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Training in Medical Technology
description: Application of theory and simulated laboratory experiences in immuno-hematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, parasitology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, immunology, to meet stated career entry-level competencies.

subject: MEDT
title: Seminar in Medical Technology
description: Analysis of research and recent literature pertaining to various aspects of medical technology.

subject: NHH
title: Applied Health Disparities Research
description: Instruction on social determinants of health, issues of health equity, and how these issues can be addressed through research. Discussions and activities promote a greater understanding of health disparities research.

subject: NHH
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Junior standing or higher.

subject: NHH
title: Humanities in Medicine I
description: Introduction to medical science stressing key historical figures and significant events to exemplify the development of scientific methods. Special emphasis on writing skills, health team concept, and culture and contributions of the Pacific.
prereq_raw: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

prereq_tree.text: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

subject: NHH
title: Humanities in Medicine II
description: Continuation of 501.

subject: NHH
title: Medical Biology I
description: Foundation in medical sciences, including anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pathology, and pharmacology (focus on respiratory, cardiovascular, and urinary systems); develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Includes lectures, problembased tutorials, and histology and gross anatomy labs.
prereq_raw: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

prereq_tree.text: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

subject: NHH
title: Medical Biology II
description: Continuation of 503.

subject: NHH
title: Medical Biochemistry I
description: Provide background knowledge of chemistry, biochemistry, and molecular biology with emphasis in principles of biochemical processes as well as clinical correlations to medical conditions; develop critical thinking, standardized test taking skills, and problem-solving skills.
prereq_raw: admission to Imi Ho‘ola Post-Baccalaureate Program
