subject: NHH
title: Medical Biochemistry II
description: Continuation of 505.

subject: NHH
title: Native Hawaiian Health and Traditional Healing
description: Introduction to Native Hawaiian health issues and traditional healing practices.

subject: NHH
title: Native Hawaiian Health Care
description: Clinical experience in the Native Hawaiian Health Care System and community health care centers, incorporating both western and traditional Hawaiian medicine. Open to fourth year medical students interested in Native Hawaiian Health Care.

subject: NHH
title: Seminar in Issues of Social Justice in Health
description: Social justice provides an analytical and prescriptive framework to understand health inequities; understand connections between social forces and health outcomes, and the role of the individual student in improving social justice in the health system. Graduate standing only.

subject: NHH
title: Clinical Skills Preceptorship in the Lau Ola Clinic of the Department of Native Hawaiian Health
description: Provides a focused experience in clinical medicine with opportunities to practice the history and physical examination in Lau Ola, the clinical setting of the Department of Native Hawaiian Health.

subject: NHH
title: Directed Reading/Research in Native Hawaiian Health
description: Instruction of medical students in the social determinants of health, issues of health equity, specifically in Native Hawaiians, Pacific Islanders and/or disadvantaged people and teach them how these issues can be addressed through research.

subject: NHH
title: Advanced Applied Health Disparities Research
description: Instruction on social determinants of health, issues of health equity, and how these issues can be addressed through research. Discussions and activities promote a greater understanding of health disparities research.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, or up to 27 credits

subject: NHH
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading and/or research. Graduate standing only.

subject: OBGN
title: Obstetrics and Gynecology Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Year-long clerkship in outpatient setting, covering assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and/or management of common gynecologic problems and normal and complicated pregnancies. Emphasis on prevention and health maintenance.
prereq_raw: third-year standing, and concurrent registration in 532 courses
coreq_raw: FMCH, MED, PED, PSTY, and SURG 632

subject: OBGN
title: (Alpha) Electives in OB/GYN
description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (C) outpatient clinic at Queen’s; (D) Sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives; (J) urogynecology and pelvic reconstructive surgery.

subject: PATH
title: Immunopathology Seminar
description: Autoimmune diseases and transplantation immunity.

subject: PATH
title: Directed Research
description: Pathology of aging, nutrition, alcoholism, and immunology. Open to selected undergraduate students.

subject: PATH
title: Unit II Concurrent Elective
description: Elective course for first-year medical students.

subject: PATH
title: Unit V Concurrent Elective
description: Elective course for second-year medical students.

subject: PATH
title: Unit V Block Elective
description: Required elective for second-year medical students, objectives to be determined by contract. One option is a review of USMLE Part I.

subject: PATH
title: Pathology Practicum
description: Required autopsy experience involving dissection and microscopic examination of tissues and detailed evaluation of disease process.

subject: PATH
title: (Alpha) Unit VII Electives in Pathology
description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology.

subject: PATH
title: Introduction to Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
description: Provides an introduction to the practice of pathology and laboratory medicine and the role pathologists and the laboratory play in the diagnosis and management of disease. MD students only.

subject: PATH
title: Electives in Pathology
description: Individualized instruction in clinical and/or anatomic pathology. Third-year elective.

subject: PED
title: Pediatric Seminars
description: Interactive weekly lecture/seminar designed to teach topics in pediatrics and supplemented by small group 2-hour encounters with faculty clinicians in pediatric emergency medicine, inpatient pediatric, and enonatology to gain exposure in pediatric hospital care. Medical students only.

subject: PED
title: Pediatric Shadowing Encounters
description: Clinical Shadowing – Students are paired with Pediatric Subspecialists in chosen area(s) for 8-10 half days. Required: Log book file describing one concept that the student learned during each of the sessions. CR/ NC only. Field experience.

subject: PED
title: Introduction to Research Methodology, Biostatistics, and Epidemiology
description: Interactive seminar series to cover the following topics: data types, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, selecting a statistical test, data distributions, measures of data spread, statistical test assumptions, standard deviation vs. standard error, etc. Medical students only.

subject: PED
title: Pediatrics Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, covering evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of childhood diseases. Emphasis on primary prevention, normal growth and development of the neonate to adolescent, and arrangement of pediatric care, including outpatient, inpatient, and emergency room experiences.
prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses
coreq_raw: MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, and SURG 532

subject: PED
title: (Alpha) Electives in Pediatrics
description: Fourth-year elective in pediatric sub-specialty areas in which medical students may receive clinical experiences and an in-depth study of selected sub-specialty areas within the field of pediatrics. (B) adolescent medicine; (C) ambulatory pediatric care; (E) clinical genetics; (F) Sub-Internship in neonatology; (G) pediatric cardiology; (H) Sub-Internship in pediatric emergency medicine; (I) Sub-Internship in pediatric hematology/ oncology; (J) Sub-Internship in infectious diseases; (K) Sub-Internship in pediatrics–general ward in pediatrics; (M) extramural electives in pediatrics; (N) pediatric rheumatology; (P) developmental behavioral pediatrics; (Q) pediatric international preceptorship (3 cr.); (R) Sub-Internship in pediatric critical care;. (S) pediatric radiology; (T) pediatric ultrasound; (U) pediatric nephrology; (V) pediatric sports medicine.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times per alpha, up to 36 credits; not repeatable for (Q)

subject: PSTY
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individualized directed readings and/or research in mental health and psychiatry under the supervision of an instructor. Open to non-majors.

subject: PSTY
title: Psychiatry Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, including knowledge, skills, attitudes for assessment, diagnosis, and management of psychiatric problems in medical practice, inpatient, and emergency room settings. Emphasis on development and application of psychosocial cultural formulations in all areas of psychiatric and medical practice.
prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses
coreq_raw: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PEDS, SURG 532 and SURG 535

subject: PSTY
title: (Alpha) Electives in Psychiatry
description: Senior medical student elective providing advanced instruction on the theory and methods of mental health research as well as supervised participation in an assigned research project in the Department of Psychiatry. (B) adult inpatient PSTY; (C) child PSTY; (D) forensic PSTY; (E) journal editing; (F) community mental health; (G) PSTY aspects of OBGN, PED, MED, SURG; (H) sub-internship in adult PSTY; (I) substance abuse; (J) PSTY aspects of rehab medicine; (K) PSTY aspects of SURG; (M) PSTY consult liaison; (N) post-traumatic stress disorder; (O) extramural elective in PSTY; (Q) geriatric PSTY; (R) rural child PSTY; (S) public and rural PSTY; (T) mental health research.

subject: PSTY
title: Philosophy & Human Suffering
description: To see how various philosophies and religions have tackled the question, “why is there suffering in the world?” Read short excerpts from “classic” texts and discuss in a welcoming atmosphere and draw own conclusions. Medical students only.

subject: QHS
title: Mathematic Preparation for Quantitative Health Sciences
description: Mathematics preparation for quantitative health sciences. Includes selective topics in linear algebra, advanced calculus and probability theory.

subject: QHS
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Directed reading/research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through quantitative methodologies and/or the process of conducting a research study.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times or up to 12 credits

subject: QHS
title: Biostatistics Concepts for Clinical Researchers
description: Provide biostatistical concepts to clinical researchers. Students will obtain the ability to demonstrate an understanding of key biostatistical concepts in clinical research; and interpret statistical findings most commonly reported in clinical and healthcare literature. Graduate students only.

subject: QHS
title: Data Management and Visualization for Health Sciences
description: Data management and visualization is essential to all aspects of health sciences. Through hands-on experiences in R, will introduce data processing, manipulation, visualization and reproducibility, with an emphasis on clinical, medical, and health science problems.

subject: QHS
title: Quantitative Health and Clinical Research Seminar
description: Provides overview of research related to health in Hawai‘i and advances in quantitative health and clinical research. Topics include ethnic disparities in health, social and cultural factors, ethics, biostatistics and bioinformatics.

subject: QHS
title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research I
description: Introductory lecture-seminar on the conduct of multidisciplinary research from a culturally competent perspective.

subject: QHS
title: Secondary Data Analysis
description: Will allow students who are new to using secondary data to become comfortable with accessing the data, forming hypotheses, and designing study proposals. Will introduce examples with basic and advanced techniques.
prereq_raw: 601 (or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B-

children.text: ( or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B-

subject: SURG
title: Surgery Longitudinal Clerkship
description: A clinically based, year-long, introductory in general surgery and selected subspecialties. Outpatient-conducted one day per week for six months in a community-based, ambulatory care facility. Inpatient-conducted for four weeks in an acute-care hospital facility.

subject: SURG
title: Emergency Medical Care
description: Clinical experiences in management of medical, surgical, and psychiatric problems requiring urgent care.

subject: SURG
title: (Alpha) Electives in Surgery
description: Advanced clinical experience in: (B) urology; (C) ophthalmology; (D) otolaryngology; (E) plastic surgery; (F) neurosurgery; (G) orthopaedics; (H) anesthesia; (I) surgical intensive care; (J)Sub-I – general surgery; (K) Sub-I – pediatric surgery; (M) diagnostic radiology; (N) radiation oncology; (O) EM Sub-I; (P) extramural elec in surg; (Q) Sub-I – cardiovascular; (R) surgical research; (S) surgical anatomy; (T) preceptorship in Asia; (U) biomedical technology design; (X) transplant surgery; (Y) bedside ultrasounds; (Z) laparoscopic skills. Medical students only for (U), (X), (Y), and (Z).
prereq_raw: 532 for all except (M), (U), and (Y); and consent for (R) and (S); admission into JABSOM for (U) and (Y)

children.text: for all except ( M), ( U), and ( Y); and consent for (R) and ( S); admission into JABSOM for (U) and ( Y)

repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for all except (U), (X), (Y), and (Z); repeatable two times for (U) and (X)

subject: DRB
title: Fertilization and Early Development
description: Lecture on the basics of vertebrate and invertebrate fertilization and early embryonic development. Open to all graduate students.

subject: DRB
title: Seminar in Developmental and Reproductive Biology I
description: Presentations of current research carried out by developmental and reproductive biology graduate program faculty.

subject: DRB
title: Developmental and Reproductive Biology Scientific Investigations
description: Discussion of current research in developmental and reproductive biology.

subject: DRB
title: Stem Cell Biology
description: Seminar designed to teach graduate students and advanced undergraduate students about current topics relating to stem cell biology, as well as the application of stem cells to modern medicine.

subject: DRB
title: Applied Developmental and Reproductive Biology
description: Combined lecture-lab on current technologies and methods for mammalian reproduction and developmental biology.

subject: DRB
title: DRB Research Rotation
description: Introductory laboratory research experience under the supervision of faculty.

subject: DRB
title: Directed Research
description: Research experience in developmental and reproductive biology.

subject: PHRM
title: Introduction to General Pharmacology
description: Drugs discussed with emphasis on sites and mechanism of action, toxicity, fate, and uses of major therapeutic agents.
prereq_raw: mammalian physiology and dental hygiene major

subject: PHRM
title: General Pharmacology
description: Similar to 201 but wider in scope of drugs discussed. Intended for undergraduates in the health sciences and related fields.

subject: PHRM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Directed reading and research in experimental pharmacology.

subject: PHRM
title: Selected Topics in Pharmacology
description: Elective for medical students in Pharmacology.

subject: PHRM
title: Principles of Pharmacology
description: Pharmacology elective course for medical students. MD students only.

subject: PHRM
title: Research in Pharmacology
description: Pharmacology research elective for medical students.

subject: PHRM
title: General Pharmacology
description: Pharmacodynamics, receptor theory, modeling, clinical trials and the FDA will be covered. Concepts in ADME/T and clinical research are also considered.

subject: PHRM
title: Systemic Pharmacology
description: Provides instruction at an organ systems/functional level covering major organ and functional systems of the human body. Concepts in pharmacological research at the animal, organ system and whole human level will also be considered.

subject: PHRM
title: Neuropharmacology
description: Physiology and pharmacology of central and peripheral nervous systems, focusing on synaptic chemistry and signaling.
prereq_raw: CMB 606, or consent from the course director

subject: TRMD
title: One Health: Preparing for the Next Pandemic
description: Focuses on the COVID-19 pandemic as a case study of a global health problem that is optimally approached from a One Health perspective.
prereq_raw: ANSC 200, BIOL 101, MICR 130, PH 201, or consent of instructor

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Journal Club
description: Students gain critical reading skills in the presentation and discussion of published literature on One Health-related topics.

subject: TRMD
title: Principles of Medical Parasitology
description: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections; principles of host-pathogen interactions; public health aspects of parasitic infections.
prereq_raw: MICR 351 with a grade of B or higher or equivalent

subject: TRMD
title: Health Disparities
description: Overview of biosciences research related to health and health disparities in a global setting as well as in Hawai‘i. Workshop topics include health research, Native Hawaiian health, global health, and cultural competency. MHIRT cohort only.

subject: TRMD
title: Medical and Urban Entomology
description: Biology, ecology, health and economic impacts, and control of urban insect pests and medically important arthropods that act as vectors of diseases.
prereq_raw: (PEPS 363 or BIOL 265) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.  DB

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Practicum
description: Provide certificate students with real-world experience and opportunity to integrate and apply classroom learning in a professional environment. Intended for students who prefer to pursue a supervised, practical experience rather than a research-based project.

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Seminar
description: Weekly presentations and discussions on current events and research in the field of One Health. Presentation topics may include research progress, literature reviews, or research proposals.

subject: TRMD
title: Topics in Tropical Medicine
description: Elective for fourth-year medical students for advanced study of selected topics within the field of tropical medicine and medical microbiology.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Topics in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases
description: Elective for medical students in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases. Medical students only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable six times, up to 12 credits

subject: TRMD
title: (Alpha) Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases
description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology.

subject: TRMD
title: (Alpha) Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases
description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology.

subject: TRMD
title: Tropical Medicine Journal Club
description: Students gain experience in the presentation and discussion of topics of current interest in the fields of tropical medicine and infectious diseases. Graduate students only.

subject: TRMD
title: Laboratory Methods in Tropical Medicine
description: Microbiologic methods and techniques for identification of pathogenic viruses, bacterial, and parasitic organisms including specimen handling, culturing, and laboratory safety. Graduate standing only.

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Microbiology I: Medical Parasitology
description: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections; principles of host-pathogen interactions; public health aspects of parasitic infections.

subject: TRMD
title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions.

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Micro II
description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented.

subject: TRMD
title: Tropical Medicine Laboratory Rotations
description: Practical experience in use of equipment and procedures in infectious disease and immunology research; introduction to research in tropical medicine.

subject: TRMD
title: Neurovirology
description: Seminar on neuroinvasive viruses giving basics of viruses causing nervous system diseases and discussing recent advances in the research field of neurovirology.

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Microbiology III
description: Basic structure, physiology, epidemiology, and genetics of pathogenic bacteria as well as the host response to these organisms. Correlation of these characteristics to disease pathogenesis in humans and animal models.

subject: TRMD
title: Advances In Medical Immunology
description: Presentations/discussions of current literature concerning recent advances in immunology relevant to disease and to disease processes.

subject: TRMD
title: Infection and Immunity
description: Combined lecture/discussion of interactions of pathogens with the innate and acquired immune systems. Topics will include the role of novel receptors in pathogen detection, inflammation in disease pathogenesis, pathogen immune evasion, and neuroimmunology.

subject: TRMD
title: Ecological Epidemiology
description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies.

subject: TRMD
title: Vaccinology
description: History/evolution of vaccines, current and next generation vaccines, vaccine immunology, adjuvants, vaccine strategies, vaccines for viral, bacterial, and parasitic diseases, vaccine-proof-of-concept and downstream developmental studies; vaccine safety production processes. Graduate students only.
prereq_raw: (604 and 605) with a minimum grade of B. (Spring only

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Genetics and Evolution of Infectious Diseases
description: An evolutionary perspective to examine the interactive responses between infectious agents and the immune system. Topics will include natural selection, life history evolution, population genetics of pathogens and hosts, and anti-microbial resistance.

subject: TRMD
title: Bioinformatics I
description: Provides fundamental concepts in bioinformatics with strong emphasis on hands-on training. Topics such as molecular biology, sequence alignment, biological databases, phytogeny, and genomics including microarray and RNA-sequence analysis. Open to nonmajors. (Cross-listed with QHS 610)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, but credit earned one time only

subject: TRMD
title: Advances in HIV/AIDS
description: History of HIV, basic biology and virology, epidemiology, HIV pathogenesis and immunology, clinical features, and co-morbidities. Treatment and prevention of HIV/ AIDS, including research methods, statistics, cultural competence, genetics, pathophysiology, drug and vaccine development.

subject: TRMD
title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results.

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Medical Parasitology
description: Consideration of ultrastructure, physiology, biochemistry, in-vitro cultivation and host-parasite relationship of parasites of medical importance.

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Medical Virology
description: In-depth study of the major groups of viruses pathogenic for human; virus replication, host range, pathogenesis, immunology, and epidemiology.

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Medical Bacteriology
description: Role of bacteria in infectious diseases, with emphasis on clinical aspects and identification of etiological agents.

subject: TRMD
title: Epidemiology of Tropical Infectious Diseases
description: Epidemiology of infectious diseases as it relates to tropical medicine. Lecture/seminar format.

subject: TRMD
title: Seminar in Tropical Medicine and Public Health
description: Weekly discussion and reports on current advances in tropical medicine and public health.

subject: TRMD
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.

subject: TRMD
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research in medical microbiology (bacteriology, parasitology, virology).

subject: TRMD
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Approval of department faculty required.

subject: TRMD
title: Special Topics in Tropical Medicine
description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health.

subject: TRMD
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral thesis. Approval of department faculty is required.

subject: ASTR
title: Survey of Astronomy
description: Introduction to the astronomical universe: sky and celestial objects, planetary motion, planets and the Solar System, Sun and stars, the Milky Way and galaxies, cosmology and the universe.

subject: ASTR
title: Survey of Astronomy
description: Introduction to the astronomical universe: sky and celestial objects, planetary motion, planets and the Solar System, Sun and stars, the Milky Way and galaxies, cosmology and the universe.

subject: ASTR
title: Survey of Astronomy Laboratory
description: Observations of constellations and the night sky, the sun and moon, planets, stars, and deep-sky objects; laboratory and observational experiments illustrating basic concepts in astronomy. Offered in the evening.

subject: ASTR
title: Introduction to Archaeoastronomy
description: Astronomy and celestial lore in ancient cultures: Neolithic Europe, Mayan, Mesoamerican, Egyptian, Mesopotamian, American Indian, Chinese, and Polynesian. Concepts of the cosmos, calendars, eclipse predictions, motion of celestial bodies, and navigation. Construction of simple observing tools.

subject: ASTR
title: Voyage through the Solar System
description: An illustrated voyage through the Solar System based on recent scientific results. The class highlights the origin, evolution, and current knowledge of the eight planets, their moons, asteroids, comets, and one star, the Sun. Field trip.

subject: ASTR
title: Introduction to Astronomical Research
description: Introduction to astronomical research, including literature resources, basic computing skills, software tools, data analysis, scientific communication, and research opportunities. Prepares students for effective internships and directed research projects.

subject: ASTR
title: Foundations of Astronomy
description: A rigorous overview of modern astronomy: solar system, stellar, galactic and extragalactic astronomy and cosmology. For science and engineering students.

subject: ASTR
title: Foundations of Astrophysics I: The Solar System
description: Solar system astrophysics. Dynamics of planets, satellite systems, asteroids and comets; planetary atmospheres and internal structure; thermal balance; the Sun as a star. Introduces numerical computing.
prereq_raw: PHYS 170, MATH 242 or 252A, and PHYS 272 (or concurrent)

subject: ASTR
title: Foundations of Astrophysics II: Galaxies and Stars
description: Stellar and galactic astrophysics. Stellar magnitudes, colors, distances, and spectra. Galactic structure and evolution, active nuclei, large-scale structure, Big-Bang cosmology. Stellar interiors, nuclear “burning,” main-sequence and evolved stars. Introduces computer programming.
prereq_raw: 241, PHYS 274 (or concurrent), and MATH 243 (or concurrent) or 253A (or concurrent)

subject: ASTR
title: Evolution of the Universe
description: The Big Bang, origin of the elements, formation and evolution of galaxies and stars.

subject: ASTR
title: Astrobiology
description: Are we alone in the universe? Modern astronomical, biological, and geological perspectives on this fundamental question. Searches for life on Mars, oceans on Europa, planets orbiting other stars. Space exploration and colonies, interstellar spaceflight and communication.

subject: ASTR
title: Observational Astronomy
description: Principles and techniques of optical and near-infrared astronomical observation. Astronomical coordinate systems. Telescopes, cameras, spectrographs, and detectors. Astrometry, photometry, and spectroscopy of astronomical objects.

subject: ASTR
title: Observational Astronomy Laboratory
description: Optical and near-infrared astronomy laboratory. Error analysis, properties of light, data, and image processing. Astrometric, photometric, and spectroscopic measurement.
prereq_raw: 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or 274; PHYS 152L or 274L; MATH 216, 242, or 252A

subject: ASTR
title: Observational Astronomy Projects
description: Astronomical observational research projects. Students use astronomical data and process telescopic observations to produce scientific results, and present these orally and in writing. Students prepare for independent research projects and present research plans orally.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomical Spectroscopy
description: Introduction to astronomical spectroscopy. Stellar atmospheres, line formation, elements of radiative transfer. Phases of interstellar medium. Emission line diagnostics. Doppler shift and kinematics.
prereq_raw: 210 or 242; PHYS 152 or 274; MATH 216 or 242 or 252A

subject: ASTR
title: Modern Extragalactic Astronomy
description: Use of astronomical surveys to map large-scale distribution of galaxies. Internal structure & dynamics of galaxies. Evolution of galaxy populations over cosmic time. Theoretical understanding of galaxy formation in context of modern Big Bang cosmology.
prereq_raw: 210 or 242; and 300 (or concurrent); and PHYS 152 or PHYS 274. Recommended: 280

subject: ASTR
title: History of Cosmology and Scientific Thought
description: History and intellectual context of astronomical discovery; the evolution of ideas of space, time, and motion from the Babylonians to relativistic cosmologies; emphasis on the interaction of astronomy with the history of ideas.

subject: ASTR
title: Directed Study
description: Individual reading, observation, or experimentation in astronomy and astrophysics.

subject: ASTR
title: Stellar Astrophysics
description: Advanced survey of stellar astrophysics, including application of astrometry, photometry, and spectrometry to determine fundamental stellar properties; stellar structure and evolution of single and binary stars; astrophysical distance determination methods; stellar nucleosynthesis.

subject: ASTR
title: Galaxies & Cosmology
description: Survey of extragalactic astronomy and cosmology, including: galaxy morphology and kinematics; luminosity functions; dark matter; properties of galaxy groups/ clusters; gravitational lensing; redshifts; cosmological models; the Big Bang; thermal history of the Universe; structure formation.
prereq_raw: 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or PHYS 274; MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A

subject: ASTR
title: The Solar System
description: Observations and physical nature of planets and moons, asteroids, comets, and other small bodies; formation of the Solar System; discovery of other planetary systems; solar activity.
prereq_raw: 300; and PHYS 152 or 274; and MATH 216, 242, or 252A

subject: ASTR
title: General Relativity & Cosmology
description: Introduction to general relativity & cosmology. Spacetime metrics, geodesics, Einstein field equations, black holes. Geometry of the universe, redshift, cosmological distances. Cosmological models, dark matters, dark energy. Big Bang nucleosynthesis, recombination, cosmic microwave background, inflation.
prereq_raw: PHYS 274; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: 242

subject: ASTR
title: Senior Research Project
description: Seminar focusing on development of professional skills for astronomical research, and on scientific writing as a tool for organizing research. A final paper describing a supervised research project is required.

subject: ASTR
title: Being a Professional Astronomer
description: Seminar for beginning graduate students focusing on professional skills needed for astronomy and discussing possible research opportunities. Graduate students only.

subject: ASTR
title: The Interstellar Medium
description: Astrophysics of diffuse matter, HII regions, molecular clouds, etc.

subject: ASTR
title: Stellar Interiors and Evolution
description: Structure and evolution; energy sources, radiative processes; relations to observables.

subject: ASTR
title: Galaxies
description: Observations and stellar dynamics of elliptical and spiral galaxies including our galaxy, globular clusters, and dark matter. Galaxy formation and evolution.

subject: ASTR
title: Cosmology
description: Geometry and evolution of the universe. Dark matter. Early universe. Formation of large–scale structure, galaxies, and clusters. Cosmological models.

subject: ASTR
title: The Solar System
description: Survey of observational data and physical concepts on planets and smaller bodies; formation of planetary systems; solar activity.

subject: ASTR
title: Radiative Transfer Stellar Atmospheres
description: Excitation, ionization, and radiative transfer in stellar atmospheres; model atmospheres, formation of line and continuum radiation.

subject: ASTR
title: Astrophysical Techniques
description: Telescopes, positional astronomy, photon detection, error analysis, photometry, spectroscopy.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomical Instrumentation
description: Design and operation of astronomical instrumentation. Physics of optical and infrared detectors. Wavefront sensors and adaptive optics. Radio and infrared interferometry. Optical design: methods and software.

subject: ASTR
title: Fundamentals of Astrophysics
description: Applications of fundamental physics to astrophysical situations. Elements of general relativity. Basics of hydrodynamics and shock waves. Radiative processes, high energy astrophysics. Modern dynamics.

subject: ASTR
title: General Relativity
description: Introduction to gravity and general relativity. Tensor basics, classical scalar, vector and tensor field theories. Exact symmetric Einstein equation, gravito-magnetic weak field, and radiation solutions.

subject: ASTR
title: Active Galaxies
description: Phenomenology of active galactic nuclei, black holes, accretion flows and jets, emission mechanisms, host galaxies, and cosmic evolution.

subject: ASTR
title: Astrochemistry-A Molecular Approach
description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomy Seminar I
description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomy Seminar II
description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomy Seminar III
description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

subject: ASTR
title: Astrobiology Seminar: Origin, Evolution and the Role of Water for Life in the Universe
description: Interdisciplinary research topics in astrobiology as they relate to the theme of water: formation in space, role in creating pre-biotic molecules, delivery to earth, and terrestrial planet habitability.
prereq_raw: graduate level sciences and ideas, or consent

subject: ASTR
title: Scientific Grant Writing
description: Principles of scientific grant writing are taught by working on draft proposals through a mix of lectures, discussions, and hands on activities. The final proposal will be reviewed and evaluated via a review panel. Graduate students only.

subject: ASTR
title: Programming and Algorithms for Astronomers
description: Distillation of modern computer science fundamentals and paradigms, with applications to astronomy. Common algorithms and essential programming techniques. Assignments include extensive Python programming practice. Open to graduate students in any physical science. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)

subject: ASTR
title: Modern General Relativity
description: Differential geometry, special relativity, Einstein equations, gravitational phenomena, equivalence principles, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, relativistic stars, experimental tests, computational techniques. Graduate students only in PHYS or ASTR. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: ASTR
title: Star Formation
description: Molecular clouds, collapse processes, physics of circumstellar disks and accretion, properties of young stars, outflows and jets, formation of binaries, extrasolar planets and planet formation, meteorites and the early solar system.

subject: ASTR
title: Astro-ph Seminar
description: Seminar discussions of the most recent research papers covering all areas of astronomy. Student lead discussion sessions and discuss papers of their choice during the semester. Graduate students only.

subject: ASTR
title: Cosmology Seminar
description: Students and researchers will review and discuss the most important and exciting cosmological results in depth. Graduate students only.

subject: ASTR
title: Stars and Planets Lunch and Talks (SPLAT) Seminar
description: Seminar for graduate students and researchers discussing the latest results on solar, stellar, and exoplanet research. Graduate students only.

subject: ASTR
title: Dissertation Research
description: Repeatable unlimited times

subject: BOT
title: Freshman Seminar
description: Discussion of hot topics in botany, including conservation of rare plants, invasive species, marine botany, ethnobotany, poisonous plants, evolution in action, fungal networks, and careers in botany with emphasis on Hawaiian examples. Students should enroll in BOT 100 and 101/101L, or BOT 100 and BIOL 171/171L.

subject: BOT
title: General Botany
description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

subject: BOT
title: General Botany
description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

subject: BOT
title: General Botany Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Lab observations and experiments illustrating basic principles of plant biology.

subject: BOT
title: Plants, People, and Culture
description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

subject: BOT
title: Plants, People, and Culture
description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance
description: Introduction to the native flora of Hawai‘i, its origin, evolution and ecology, and the observation, identification, and systematics of the Hawaiian flora.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance Lab
description: The exploration of concepts and the process of science through hands-on experience in studying Hawaiian and introduced plants, their ecology, and cultural significance.

subject: BOT
title: Magical Mushrooms and Mystical Molds
description: Impact of fungi in nature and on humankind. Selected historical events in which fungi played a significant role, their activities as decomposers and pathogens, and their uses as sources for mind altering drugs in religious ceremonies and in food and beverage production in various societies.

subject: BOT
title: Campus Plants
description: Nontechnical course emphasizing recognition of the many interesting tropical plants seen on campus; origin, status in Hawai‘i, and cultural and economic uses of campus plants.

subject: BOT
title: Sophomore Seminar
description: Presentations by faculty highlighting research in tropical ecosystems. Topics include alien species, biodiversity, ecosystem services, ethnobotany, marine ecology, plant-animal interactions, and systematics of Hawaiian species. Assigned reading and writing exercises from papers in current journals.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity
description: Significance of evolutionary trends in the plant world, including reproductive, morphological, and life history adaptations by algae, fungi, and vascular plants.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Lab exercises in the morphology and systematics of land plants, fungi, and algae.

subject: BOT
title: Biostatistics
description: Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R.
prereq_raw: 101 or BIOL 171 or BIOL 172; MATH 134 or higher, or MATH assessment exam

subject: BOT
title: Conservation Ethics
description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology.
prereq_raw: any DB course or consent. (Once a year)

subject: BOT
title: Plant Conservation Biology
description: Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-inpractice in Hawai‘i and elsewhere.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
description: Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components.

subject: BOT
title: Ecology
description: General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment.

subject: BOT
title: Field Botany
description: Combined lecturelaboratory with intensive field experience for observational and experimental field work in native/impacted Hawaiian ecosystems. Field experience typically held during spring break. Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine habitats considered.

subject: BOT
title: Resource Management and Conservation in Hawai‘i
description: Management of native Hawaiian organisms and terrestrial ecosystems with particular attention to strategies, planning, research, and management actions necessary to control alien influences and promote native species.

subject: BOT
title: Tropical forest Ecology
description: Introduction to the ecological processes and principles of tropical ecosystems, and to conservation issues facing tropical forests, with a particular emphasis on the neotropics.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172, or BOT 101; and BIOL 265

subject: BOT
title: Senior Seminar
description: Current research themes in botany presented in discussion format; reading current research papers. Oral presentations of primary research. Senior standing and consent. (Once a year)

subject: BOT
title: Plant Form and Function
description: Lecture/laboratory to examine the anatomy, physiology, morphology, and functional ecology of plants. Labs will develop skills in microscopy, experimental techniques for studying plant physiology, and basic functional ecology.

subject: BOT
title: The Biology of Fungi
description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts.
prereq_raw: (201, BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: BOT
title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens.
prereq_raw: (430 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C. or consent

subject: BOT
title: Medical Ethnobotany
description: Survey and theory of plants used as medicines, cultural perspectives of herbal medicine, and the botanical/ chemical basis of allopathic and naturopathic medicine. Lecture/discussion, term paper or project.

subject: BOT
title: Ethnoecology and Conservation
description: Ecological implications of cultural uses of plants. Examines the biological basis for, and ecological effects of traditional and local resource management systems.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
description: Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork.

subject: BOT
title: Plant-Animal Interactions
description: Interdependence of plants and animals, emphasizing the influence of animals on plant fitness and evolution. Topics include pollination, fruit/seed dispersal, herbivory, and ant-plant mutualisms.

subject: BOT
title: ‘Āina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawai‘i.

subject: BOT
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
prereq_raw: HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 307/ SUST 317 or HWST/SUST 356

subject: BOT
title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O‘ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.

subject: BOT
title: Systematics of Vascular Plants
description: “Hands-on” experience with Hawai‘i’s unique tropical flora; emphasis on recognition and identification of vascular plant families and the principles and methodologies that define them; evolution of biodiversity.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Ecology
description: Ecological principles and process that determine patterns of plant distribution and abundance. Lectures cover theory and examples from primary literature. Labs cover study design, descriptive and experimental techniques, field skills, and data analysis and interpretation.

subject: BOT
title: Algal Diversity and Evolution
description: Principles of algal diversity, structure, and evolution. Identification of common Hawaiian algae. Develops written communication skills with significant attention paid to developing writing skills and emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: one of 101, BIOL 172, MICR 351, ZOOL 101; or consent

subject: BOT
title: Grant Writing and Your Career in Science
description: Scientific grant writing from inception through management to completion; students will write a DDIG and participate in a panel. Professional skills including “rules,” job applications, interviews, transitioning from graduate student to academic or non-academic job.
prereq_raw: current standing as a graduate student, or consent

children.text: current standing as a graduate student,

subject: BOT
title: Foundations of Current Botany I
description: Discussion of current research and classical papers important to modern concepts in history of science, plant diversity, plant interactions with the environment, and plant integration.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in BOT or consent

subject: BOT
title: Foundations of Current Botany II
description: Discussion of current research and classical papers important to modern concepts in ecology, plant interactions with other plants or animals, and ecosystem functioning.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in BOT or consent

subject: BOT
title: Darwin’s Origin of Species
description: Study and discussion of Charles Darwin’s Origin of Species, 1st edition 1859, and related current literature. Graduate students only.
prereq_raw: BA or BS in BOT, BIOL, GEOL, or related field; or consent

subject: BOT
title: Graduate Research Skills
description: Survey of major research areas in the botanical sciences with emphasis upon research opportunities in Hawai‘i and an overview of 1) skills needed by botanical researchers including writing scientific papers and proposals, practicing ethical research procedures, and collection of specimens; and 2) equipment used by botanical researchers including computers, cameras, measuring and monitoring equipment, and global positioning systems. Lecture/ discussion, laboratory.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in biological science or approval

subject: BOT
title: Botanical Seminar
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in botany.

subject: BOT
title: Advanced Botanical Problems
description: Investigation of any botanical problem; reading and laboratory work.

subject: BOT
title: Perspectives in Modern Botany
description: Lectures by distinguished visiting professor on contemporary botanical topics in the lecturer’s area of expertise. No more than 6 credit hours may be counted toward the MS degree requirements.

subject: BOT
title: Ecohydrology: Theory and Modeling
description: Vegetative response to hydrologic controls and nutrient cycles; quantitative linkages between hydrological dynamics and ecological patterns/ processes. MatLab is used to develop and simulate ecohydrological models.
prereq_raw: college level calculus or consent. (Once a year)

subject: BOT
title: Quantitative Ethnobotany
description: Modern ethnobotanical field research project design, execution, data analysis, and documentation methods. Intended for students preparing to conduct field research studies. Lecture/discussion, term paper.
prereq_raw: 105 and one of 201, 461, ANTH 200, or BIOL 172

subject: BOT
title: Ethnoecological Methods
description: Field techniques for assessing the ecological effects of cultural uses of plants. Emphasis on documenting traditional and local patterns of plant use and measuring the effects on plant individuals, populations, communities, and landscapes.
prereq_raw: previous course work in anthropology or biology

subject: BOT
title: Conservation Ethnobiology
description: Practical field training experience for a scientific career conducting ethnobiological research.

subject: BOT
title: Invasion Biology
description: Theories, models, patterns, and predictive methods relating to the introduction, establishment, and spread of introduced organisms. Application of principles of invasion biology to conservation and natural resource management.
prereq_raw: 456 or MICR 485; and BIOL 375; or consent

subject: BOT
title: Population Biology
description: Theory and applications of population biology; behavior of population models, as revealed by analytical methods and computer simulation; application to population problems such as endangered species; discussion of classical and current literature in population biology.
prereq_raw: one of 456, NREM 680, PEPS 671, ZOOL 620, ZOOL 623; or consent

subject: BOT
title: Population Dynamics Models with R
description: Learn advanced modeling techniques to investigate the dynamics of size-structure populations (using matrix and integral population models in R), and discuss various applications in ecology and conservation biology.

other_notes.Recommended: students have working knowledge of calculus. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: BOT
title: Advances in Plant Ecology
description: A researchoriented course focusing on recent advances in all areas of plant ecology. Involves critical review of recent literature, independent research project, oral and written presentation of project results.

subject: BOT
title: Ecological Statistics with R
description: Learn how to choose appropriate statistical methods to test hypotheses in ecology, evolution, and conservation biology and applications using R as a platform. Lecture/discussion, term paper.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
description: Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips.

subject: BOT
title: High Throughput Sequencing Approaches to Ecology and Evolution
description: Fundamentals of experimental design, lab techniques and data analysis to conduct research using high throughput sequencing. Students will work in groups to conduct an amplicon sequencing study with ten samples.

subject: BOT
title: Nomenclature and Practical Systematics
description: Modern issues of naming and classifying of organisms, with a botanical emphasis. Includes lectures, discussions, class projects, and field trips.

children.text: ( or equivalent) or consent . ( Once a year)

subject: BOT
title: Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution
description: Molecular approaches to evolution, phylogenetics, and systematics. Basic use of chloroplast DNA, mitochondrial DNA, nuclear DNA, and electrophoresis. Phylogenetic analysis using parsimony, distance, and comparative methods.

subject: BOT
title: Scientific Teaching Tools to Promote Active Learning
description: Graduate level course to train students in the pedagogical tools to enhance active learning in STEM classes. Includes discussions of the primary literature, demonstrations and practice using scientific teaching techniques. BOT or ZOOL or MBIO majors only. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: BOT
title: Environmental Physiology Seminar
description: Environmental stress; pollution; salinity, geobotany, and other interactions between the environment and plant processes. Current literature emphasized at multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary levels.
prereq_raw: graduate status in a biological science, geosciences, etc.; consent for well-prepared undergraduates

prereq_tree.text: graduate status in a biological science, geosciences, etc.; consent for well-prepared undergraduates

subject: BOT
title: Marine Macrophytes Seminar
description: Discussion of current literature in physiological ecology, cellular and molecular adaptations to environmental factors by marine plants.

subject: BOT
title: Physiological Ecology of Marine Plants
description: Discussion of current studies in morphological, physiological, cellular, and molecular adaptation to marine environments by macroalgae, phytoplankton, and seagrasses.
prereq_raw: upper division ecology class recommended, 480 (or equivalent), or consent

subject: BOT
title: Physiological Ecology of Marine Plants Lab
description: Field and laboratory research techniques and projects in the physiological ecology of algae and seagrasses.
prereq_raw: upper division ecology class recommended, 470L (or equivalent), 480 (or equivalent), or consent

subject: BOT
title: Conservation Biology
description: Theories and concepts of ecology, evolution, and genetics for conservation of biological diversity. Topics will include restoration ecology, management planning, laws and policies, biological invasions.

subject: BOT
title: Directed Research
description: Research preliminary to thesis or dissertation research.

subject: BOT
title: Thesis Research
prereq_raw: candidacy for MS degree and approval of thesis proposal

subject: BOT
title: Topics in Conservation Biology
description: Advanced topics in conservation and environmental biology.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, up to twelve credits

subject: BOT
title: Dissertation Research
prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD and approval of dissertation proposal

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry and Society
description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of basic chemistry concepts and their application to everyday life. Students who successfully completed 110/SUST 120 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 100 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 110/SUST 120 without instructor override.
restrictions_raw: No credit for science and engineering majors.

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry and Society Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany CHEM 100, 110, or SUST 120. Lab introduces fundamental applications of chemistry, with special emphasis on relevant topics and how chemistry relates to the real world. (For students in non-science fields.)

subject: CHEM
title: Chemistry in a Sustainable World
description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of the role of natural and manmade chemicals in everyday life, with an emphasis on sustainable and environmentally-sensitive use of chemicals to improve our world. Students who successfully completed 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 110/SUST 120 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 110/SUST 120 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 100 without instructor override.

subject: CHEM
title: Preparation for General Chemistry
description: For students lacking preparation in chemistry. Provides background in algebra and elementary concepts of chemistry in preparation for entering the General Chemistry sequence.

subject: CHEM
title: Elementary Survey of Chemistry
description: Nonrigorous but adequate background in fundamentals. Preparation for technical training in life sciences.

subject: CHEM
title: Elementary Survey of Chemistry Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments introducing laboratory techniques and illustrating chemical principles.

subject: CHEM
title: Survey of Organic and Bioorganic Chemistry
description: Structure, nomenclature, properties, reactions of organic compounds emphasizing those of practical importance in related fields.

subject: CHEM
title: Survey of Organic and Bioorganic Chemistry Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Techniques of preparation, purification, identification of organic compounds.

subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry I
description: Basic principles of chemistry, including stoichiometry. Introduction to solution phase chemistry. Gas phase chemistry. Thermodynamics, including enthalpies of formation and reaction. Atomic structure, periodic trends, chemical bonding, molecular structure. Students who successfully completed 171 or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 161 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 or 181A without instructor override.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) in 131 or C (not C-) in 151 or successful completion of placement exam, or consent

subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry Lab I
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments introducing techniques and fundamental principles of chemistry. Students who successfully completed 171 or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 161 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 or 181A without instructor override.

subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry II
description: Continuation of 161. Liquids and solids. Solutions and colligative properties. Continuation of thermodynamics, including entropy and free energy. Principles and applications of chemical equilibrium, including acidbase chemistry (titrations, buffers). Kinetics. Redox reactions and electrochemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: General Chemistry Lab II
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments introducing techniques and fundamental principles of chemistry.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 161L and 162 (or concurrent)

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Chemistry
description: Principles, theories, elementary analytical methods of chemistry. Intended for physical science majors and engineers.
prereq_raw: Satisfactory Placement Exam score, and MATH 241 or MATH 242 or MATH 243 or MATH 251A or MATH 252A or MATH 253A
coreq_raw: 171L. Students who successfully completed 161 or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 171 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161 or 181A without instructor override

children.text: Students who successfully completed 161 or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 171 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161 or 181A without instructor override

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Chemistry Lab
description: (1 3.5- hr Lab) Laboratory experiments illustrating fundamental principles of chemistry. Students who successfully completed 161L or 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 171 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 171L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161L or 181A without instructor override.

subject: CHEM
title: Honors General Chemistry
description: Rigorous, in-depth introduction to chemical principles with emphasis on experimental and applied aspects of modern chemistry. Students who successfully completed 161 or 171 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 181A without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 181A with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161 or 171 without instructor override.

subject: CHEM
title: Honors General Chemistry Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments illustrating chemical principles involving advanced techniques and modern instrumentation. Students who successfully completed 161L or 171L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 181L without instructor override. Students who successfully complete 181L with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 161L or 171L without instructor override.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry I
description: Molecular structure, stereochemistry, spectroscopy, mechanisms, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 162 or 171 or 181A

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry I Lab
description: (1 4-hr Lab) Techniques, synthesis and qualitative analysis, applications of spectroscopy.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 162L, 171L, or 181L; and C (not C-) or better in 272 (or concurrent)

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry II
description: Continuation of 272. Molecular structure, stereochemistry, spectroscopy, mechanisms, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds.

subject: CHEM
title: Organic Chemistry II Lab
description: (1 4-hr Lab) Techniques, synthesis and qualitative analysis, applications of spectroscopy.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 272L and 273 (or concurrent)

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Analytical Chemistry
description: Selected methods and principles, e.g., phase equilibria, ionic equilibria, electrode equilibria, separations, spectroscopy, automation, and process control.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 162 or 171 or 181A, MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A

subject: CHEM
title: Principles of Analytical Chemistry Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Phase separations, chromatography, titrimetry, spectrophotometry, etc.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 162L or 171L or 181L; and 274 (or concurrent)

subject: CHEM
title: Physical Chemistry I
description: Principles and theories; physico-chemical procedures.
prereq_raw: 274, 274L, PHYS 272, PHYS 272L, and MATH 243 or MATH 253A

subject: CHEM
title: Physical Chemistry II
description: Continuation of 351.

subject: CHEM
title: Physico-Chemical Measurements
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory on instrumentation, measurements, and data analysis in thermodynamics, spectroscopy, and other areas of physical chemistry. Emphasis on instruction in scientific reporting writing.

subject: CHEM
title: Bioorganic Chemistry
description: Mechanism of biochemical reactions, biophysical structure, techniques for studying biochemical reactions.
prereq_raw: 273 (with a grade of C or better) or graduate standing with consent, or departmental approval

subject: CHEM
title: Professional Ethics for Chemists
description: Student team-led discussions of contemporary ethical issues and ethical decision making in chemistry using case studies and additional examples from the media. CHEM or BIOC majors only.

subject: CHEM
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading and discussion of scientific journal articles culminating in a written literature review. CHEM or BIOC majors only.

subject: CHEM
title: Directed Research
description: Directed laboratory research culminating in a written research report. CHEM or BIOC majors only.
prereq_raw: minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum in-major GPA of 3.0

subject: CHEM
title: Synthesis and Analysis of Inorganic Compounds
description: Lecture on advanced methods of preparation and characterization of inorganic compounds and materials.

subject: CHEM
title: Preparation and Analysis of Inoraganic Compounds Laboratory
description: Laboratory on preparative methods and analytical techniques and instruments in inorganic chemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
description: Classification, description, fundamental theory.

subject: CHEM
title: Experimental Methods in Materials Research
description: Common experimental techniques in materials testing and research: x-ray diffraction, optical and electron microscopy, thermal and mechanical properties, electrochemical methods—theory and hands-on experience.

subject: CHEM

description: Introduction to multi-step synthesis and instruments/analytical techniques used to characterize organic compounds. Retrosynthesis and diastereoselective reactions; spectroscopy (optical methods, NMR), mass spectrometry. Chromatography (GC, HPLC) and coupled techniques (GCMS, LCMS). CHEM or BIOC majors only.

description: Reactivity and reaction mechanisms of compounds containing metalcarbon bonds.

subject: CHEM

description: Survey of Lewis acids and bases, coordination numbers, geometries, stereochemistry, ligand field theory, formation constants, and bioinorganic chemistry.

subject: CHEM
title: Organometallics II
description: Introduction to the principles of catalysis and the classes of catalytic reactions effected by organometallic compounds.

subject: ICS

description: Overview of the field of data science. Introduction to subjects such as data format, processing, visualization, and storage. Special emphasis on historical and wider context, and simple practical examples.

subject: ICS

description: General course that provides a broad overview of computer science. Will address abstraction, data and information, algorithms, programming, the Internet and the global impact of computers.

subject: ICS

subject: ICS

description: Includes logic, sets, functions, matrices, algorithmic concepts, mathematical reasoning, recursion, counting techniques, and probability theory.

subject: ICS

subject: ICS

subject: ICS

description: What is the subject of computer science? What is a computer? Understand the basic models of computation and the concepts of computability, complexity, and network computation, and learn to use them in practice.

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning Methods
description: Introduction to contemporary mathematical methods for empirical inference, data modeling, and machine learning.

subject: ICS
title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science II
description: Includes program correctness, recurrence relations and their solutions, relations and their properties, divide and conquer relations, graph theory, trees and their applications, Boolean algebra, introduction to formal languages and automata theory.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Science Careers: An Exploration of the Specialties of Computer Science
description: Exploration of the specialties of computer science. Meets every two week for 2.5 hours to explore specific areas in computer science. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Sophomore Project
description: Part of a multi-year project-based courses sequence where students will work in teams on acquiring experience in a beginner-level design of a software project expected to be continued in ICS 396.

subject: ICS

description: (4 1-hr Lec) Design and correctness of algorithms, including divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic programming methods. description: Syntax, semantics, control structures, variable binding and scopes, data and control abstractions. Programming in functional (LISP) and logic (Prolog) programming styles.
prereq_raw: (212 or ECE 205), (311 or ECE 367), and 314; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Software Engineering I
description: Problem analysis and design, team-oriented development, quality assurance, configuration management, project planning. These topics are covered in the sequence 314-414.
prereq_raw: (211 or ECE 205) and [241 or ECE 362 or (MATH 301 and 372)]; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Database Systems I
description: Introduction to relational database systems, data modeling, query processing, transaction processing, storage, and indexing.

subject: ICS
title: Logic Design and Microprocessors
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Basic machine architecture, microprocessors, bus organization, circuit elements, logic circuit analysis and design, microcomputer system design.
prereq_raw: (212 or ECE 205), (311 or ECE 367), and 314; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Operating Systems
description: Operating system concepts and structure, processes and threads, CPU scheduling, memory management, scheduling, file systems, inter-process communication, virtualization, popular operating systems.

subject: ICS
title: Network Design and Management
description: Overview of the internet and its capabilities; introduction to HTTP, TCP/IP, ethernet, and wireless 802.11; routers, switches, and NAT; network and wireless security; practical experience in designing and implementing networks.
prereq_raw: (311 or ECE 367) and 314, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust I: Resource Protections
description: Security and trust in computers, networks, and society. Security models. Access and authorization. Availability and Denial-of-Service. Trust processes and network interactions.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Programming
description: Introduction to the theory of Artificial Intelligence and the practical application of AI techniques in Functional (Common LISP and/or Scheme) and Logic (Prolog) programming languages. Students gain practical experience through programming assignments and projects.
prereq_raw: (215 or 212 or ECE 205) and (311 or ECE 367) and 314; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Computational Media Systems
description: Intermediate object-oriented programming within the context of interactive media systems and video game development. Topics: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, event-driven programming, vectors, geometric primitives, game mechanics, and relevant design patterns.
restrictions_raw: ECE, CENG, ICS, CM, CSCI, THEA, DNCE majors only.

subject: ICS
title: Computing Ethics for Lab Assistants
description: A lecture/discussion/internship on ethical issues and instructional techniques for students assisting a laboratory section of ICS 101. The class uses multiple significant writing and oral presentation activities to help students learn course content.

subject: ICS
title: Junior Project
description: Part of a multi-year project-based courses sequence where students will work in teams on acquiring experience in intermediate-level design, implementation and presentation of a software project that may have been initiated in ICS 296.

subject: ICS
title: Software Engineering II
description: Continuation of 314. Project management, quality, and productivity control, testing and validation, team management. Team-oriented software-implementation project.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Programming for the Web
description: Introduction to emerging technologies for construction of World Wide Web (WWW)-based software. Covers programming and scripting languages used for the creation of WWW sites and client-server programming. Students will complete a medium-sized software project that uses languages and concepts discussed in class.

subject: ICS
title: The Science, Psychology and Philosophy of Systems Design
description: Scientific, psychological and philosophical bases of systems design, including a survey of human-factors and ergonomic standards; the nature of innovation and creativity as it relates to systems design. Web-enhanced course.
prereq_raw: (311 or ECE 367) and 314, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Database Systems II
description: Very large database systems, data integration, data warehousing, designing big data systems, parallel query processing, distributed transactions.

subject: ICS
title: Network Science Methodology
description: Computational and statistical methods for analyzing network models of social, technological, information, and biological networks. Introduction to relevant data analytics and graph analysis software packages.

subject: ICS
title: Data Security and Cryptography I
description: Secret communication and confidentiality data storage. Elements of cryptography and cryptanalysis. Classical ciphers. Symmetric key cryptography. Public key cryptography. Data security in cyber space.

subject: ICS
title: Application Frameworks
description: Experience producing applications with at least two different applications frameworks.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Security and Ethics
description: Theoretical results, security policy, encryption, key management, digital signatures, certificates, passwords. Ethics: privacy, computer crime, professional ethics. Effects of the computer revolution on society.

subject: ICS
title: Computer System Security
description: Information flow, confinement, information assurance, malicious programs, vulnerability analysis, network security, writing secure programs.

subject: ICS
title: Programming Approaches to Software Quality Assurance
description: Examination of best practices associated with developing and supporting software applications with respect to potential security risks. Will augment software engineering practices learned in other courses with the basic principles of cybersecurity.

subject: ICS
title: Digital Forensics
description: Provides students with the knowledge of underlying principles and skills to identify, preserve, and extract electronic evidence for further analysis.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Architecture
description: Memory management, control flow, interrupt mechanisms, multiprocessor systems, special-purpose devices.

subject: ICS
title: Concurrent and High-Performance Programming
description: Principles of concurrent and high performance programming. Multi-threading in C and Java for shared-memory programming. Distributed memory programming with Java. Introduction to cluster computing.
prereq_raw: (212 or ECE 205) and 332 and (311 or ECE 367) and 314; or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Data Science Fundamentals
description: Introduction to critical statistical and probabilistic concepts that underlie data science as well as tools that play a central role in the daily work of a data scientist.

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
description: Introduction to machine learning concepts with a focus on relevant ideas from computational neuroscience. Information processing and learning in the nervous system. Neural networks. Supervised and unsupervised learning. Basics of statistical learning theory.
prereq_raw: 235, or consent. Recommended: MATH 307. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Big Data Analytics
description: Concepts, tools, and techniques for analyzing and mining massive data sets. Data cleaning and pre-processing. Data analysis and mining techniques. Big Data platforms. Big Data visualization.

subject: ICS
title: Theory of Computation
description: Grammars, sequential machines, equivalence, minimalization, analysis and synthesis, regular expressions, computability, unsolvability, Gödel’s theorem, Turing machines.

subject: ICS
title: Analytical Models and Methods
description: Applications of mathematical methods in computer science with emphasis on discrete mathematics, numerical computation, algebraic models, operations research.

subject: ICS
title: Parallel Algorithms
description: Introduction to parallel models of computation and design and analysis of parallel algorithms.

subject: ICS
title: Data Networks
description: Network analysis, architecture, digital signal analysis and design; circuit switching, packet switching, packet broadcasting; protocols and standards; local area networks; satellite networks; ALOHA channels; examples.
prereq_raw: (212 or ECE 205) and (311 or ECE 367) and 314; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Software Design for Robotics
description: Sensors, actuators, signal processing, paradigms of robotic software design, introduction to machine learning, introduction to computer vision, and robot-to-human interaction.
prereq_raw: two ICS 300-level courses or consent. Recommended: 312 and 313. (Once a year: spring)

children.text: Recommended: 312 and 313 . ( Once a year: spring)

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust II: Information Assurance
description: Channel security. Trojan and noninterference. Basic concepts of cryptology. Cryptographic primitives. Protocols for authentication and key establishment.

subject: ICS
title: Artificial Intelligence
description: Survey of artificial intelligence: natural language processing, vision and robotics, expert systems. Emphasis on fundamental concepts: search, planning, and problem solving, logic, knowledge representation.

subject: ICS
title: Artificial Intelligence for Games
description: Techniques to stimulate intelligence in video games: movement, pathfinding with A* search, decision/behavior trees, state machines, machine learning, tactics. Extend games with your own AI implementations; experience “shootout” contests for the best AI algorithm/implementation.
prereq_raw: (212 or ECE 205) and (311 or ECE 367) and 314 and (PHYS 151 or PHYS 170)

subject: ICS
title: Human Computer Interaction I
description: Application of concepts and methodologies of human factors, psychology and software engineering to address ergonomic, cognitive, and social factors in the design and evaluation of human-computer systems.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Hypermedia
description: Basic issues of interactive access to information in various formats on computers. Available hardware and software: editing, integration, programming. Implementation of a sample information system.

subject: ICS
title: Design for Mobile Devices
description: Lecture introducing design issues, programming languages, operating systems and mark-up languages for internet-enabled mobile devices, such as cell phones and PDAs. A-F or Audit.

subject: ICS
title: Cognitive Science
description: Introduces basic concepts, central problems, and methods from cognitive science. Identifies contributions from disciplines such as cognitive psychology, linguistics, artificial intelligence, philosophy, and neuroscience.

subject: ICS
title: Probability, Statistics, and Queuing
description: A hands-on introduction to probability, statistical inference, regression, Markov chains, queuing theory. Use of an interactive statistical graphics environment such as R.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Sequences and Genomes Analysis
