description: Introduction to bioinformatics to computer sciences students by focusing on how computer sciences techniques can be used for the storage, analysis, prediction and simulation of biological sequences (DNA, RNA and proteins).
prereq_raw: (311 or ECE 367) and 314, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Bioinformatics Algorithms and Tool Development
description: Study of commonly used bioinformatic algorithms, with an emphasis on string, tree, and graph algorithms. Presentation of probabilistic and clustering methods. Implementation of the studied algorithms and design of applications.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
description: Fundamentals of computer graphics including graphics hardware, representation, manipulation, and display of two- and three-dimensional objects, use of commercial software.

subject: ICS
title: Topics in Computer Graphics
description: Review of selected graphics literature, with a software development project based on a topic of interest.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Vision
description: Introductory course in computer vision. Topics include image formation, image processing and filtering, edge detection, texture analysis and synthesis, binocular stereo, segmentation, tracking, object recognition and applications.
prereq_raw: (212 or ECE 205) and (311 or ECE 367) and 314; or consent. Once a year

subject: ICS
title: Data Visualization
description: I ntroduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ICS
title: Video Game Design and Development
description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ICS
title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course.

subject: ICS
title: Digital Content Creation I
description: Principles, techniques, and history of 3D computer graphics. Modeling and animation techniques will be covered, as well as basic lighting and rendering.

subject: ICS
title: Digital Content Creation II
description: Software development within a commercial 3D application with a focus on scripting and plugin development for procedural modeling, animation, and shading.

subject: ICS
title: Software Techniques for Computer Visual Effects
description: Principles, techniques, and history of visual effects and underlying software techniques for computer visual effects. Project-based course involving the merging of computer generated imagery with live action footage.

subject: ICS
title: Special Topics
description: Reflects special interests of faculty. Oriented toward juniors and seniors.
prereq_raw: at least two 300-level ICS classes or consent
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for BS/CS students

subject: ICS
title: Special Topics in Security
description: Special topics in security oriented toward juniors and seniors.
prereq_raw: at least two 300-level ICS courses or consent

subject: ICS
title: Capstone Project
description: Project-based course where students work in teams on a software project. Knowledge acquired in the computer science curriculum will be applied to design and implement a software product with potential real-world applicability. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Project
description: Individual or small group projects in system design or application under faculty supervision.

subject: ICS
title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects.
prereq_raw: 313 or ECE 467 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: ( or equivalent), graduate standing ; or consent . ( Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Compiler Theory and Construction
description: Design and implementation of compilers, syntactic and semantic descriptions of programming languages, algorithms for syntactic analysis and object code generation.

subject: ICS
title: Theory of Operating Systems
description: Advanced study in operating systems theory and design with emphasis on case studies and distributed systems.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Software Engineering
description: Fundamental software engineering procedures, including planning, estimation, design, testing, process definition and improvement, and software quality assurance. Measurement techniques are used to support empirically-driven software process improvement throughout the course.

subject: ICS
title: Medical Informatics I
description: Introduction to the field of medical informatics, which is found at the intersection of clinical science, public health, information science, computer technology and communications technology. Concentration on current issues.

subject: ICS
title: Software Quality and Maintenance
description: Introduction to software quality concepts and the major activities involved in software maintenance.

subject: ICS
title: Information Architecture and Web Design
description: User-centered design of websites; survey Information Architecture (IA) systems (organization, navigation, labeling, searching); gain experience in methodologies for creating IA, tools for IA, web standards and usability tests.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in ICS or LIS or related field or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: in ICS or LIS or related field or consent . ( Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Analysis of Algorithms
description: Analysis and design of algorithms: modeling, comparison, measures, applications.

subject: ICS
title: Network Science
description: Modeling human-made and natural systems as networks to understand their structure and dynamics. Computational and statistical methods and research results they enabled. Use of network analysis software. Applications to topics of interest to students.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Cryptography
description: Taxonomy of security properties: methods for defining and proving security. Randomness, pseudorandomness, and indistinguishability. Functional encryption and obfuscation. Zero knowledge.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Data Management
description: Exploration of information retrieval and object-relational tools and methods for the management of distributed multimedia database systems.

subject: ICS
title: Principles of High Performance Computing
description: Principles of high performance computing for single-processor and parallel architectures. Detailed coverage of parallel architectures and exposure to shared-memory, distributed-memory, and hybrid parallelism. Hands-on experience with message-passing and multithreaded programming.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in computer science or closely related field, or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: in computer science or closely related field, or consent . ( Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning
description: Introduction to key theoretical concepts of machine learning. Practical experience with decision free methods, artificial neural networks. Bayesian belief networks and contemporary statistical methods including regression, clustering and classification.

subject: ICS
title: Information Theory in Machine Learning
description: Basics of information processing and learning in the brain; neural networks; learning algorithms based on information maximization; applications in molecular biology and bioinformatics.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in computer science or mathematics background, or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: in computer science or mathematics background, or consent . ( Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Deep Learning with Neural Networks
description: Graduate course on deep learning with artificial neural networks. Provides practical techniques for modeling image, video, text, and graph data with supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning approaches. Includes instruction in the latest software frameworks. Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
description: Covers the latest developments in human-centered artificial intelligence, including ethics, bias, explainability, privacy, fairness, and usability. Involves discussion, writing assignments, and a final project.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Theory of Computation
description: Advanced topics in formal languages, automata, computability, computational complexity.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Parallel Algorithms
description: Design and analysis of parallel algorithms, with emphasis on advanced techniques and latest advances in parallel algorithms.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Networks
description: Elementary principles of modern computer networking. Detailed coverage of overall architecture and the physical, data link, and network layers, with emphasis on the network layer. ICS majos only.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in ICS, or consent

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust III: Cyber Security and Commerce
description: Tools and methods for security managers. Tools and methods to secure and monetize services and applications. Network as a computer and as a market. Problems of cyber war, cyber crime, cyber bullying. Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Architecture I
description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Artificial Intelligence
description: Current issues in artificial intelligence, including expert systems, knowledge representation, logic programming, learning, natural language processing.

subject: ICS
title: Pattern Recognition
description: Nature of the problem in pattern recognition and clustering; explanation of various algorithms.

subject: ICS
title: Human-Computer Interaction II
description: Studies of human performance in designing and using information systems. Emphasizes concepts and methodologies from human factors, psychology, and software engineering relating to human performance.

subject: ICS
title: User Interfaces and Hypermedia
description: Advanced concepts in construction of interfaces between computers and their users. Hypermedia information structures, guidelines, problems, and tradeoffs. Discussion of selected readings, implementation of prototypes.

subject: ICS
title: HCI Design Methods
description: Advanced analytical and empirical methods for the design and evaluation of usable, useful, and robust human computer interfaces. Students will apply selected methodologies to a major system design project.

subject: ICS
title: Social Informatics
description: An advanced introduction to the design of human-computer systems and other technological artifacts for supporting human collaboration in learning, work and social contexts, and to theoretical perspectives and empirical studies of collaboration that inform such design.
prereq_raw: 464 or 465 or 664 or 665 or 667 or LIS 677; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Social Computing
description: Participative analysis of online communities and user-generated content collections. Theoretical and practical aspects of online interaction, identity, trust, and virtual social capital. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Evolutionary Computation I: Survey of Methods
description: Evolutionary computation surveys in the field to prepare students for research. Topics include diverse engineering applications, theory, and concepts including search spaces, representation, objective functions, variation operators, selection, and population based search.
prereq_raw: 211 (B or better) and 241 (C or better) and admitted to a graduate program or capable of graduate-level work in computer sciences, or consent. (Once a year: fall)

children.text: capable of graduate-level work in computer sciences,

subject: ICS
title: Bioinformatics: Sequences Analysis
description: To expose students to bioinformatics at the biological sequences analysis level (DNA, RNA, proteins). Several bioinformatics methods and algorithms are introduced. Students are required to present one paper and to participate in a small group project. .
prereq_raw: graduate standing, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Bioinformatics: Microarrays
description: Introduction to the basic principles of biology relevant for microarray gene expression data and to Bio-conductor. Collaborative open-source project to develop a modular general framework for the analysis of cDNA arrays and gene chips.
prereq_raw: 311 or background in biology, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Computer Graphics
description: Selected advanced topics in computer graphics. Substantial project required.

subject: ICS
title: Numerical Computation
description: Selected topics in numerical analysis, mathematical software, and scientific computation; examples include sparse matrix methods, finite element methods, mathematical programming.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Computer Vision
description: Fundamental problems and core concepts and techniques in computer vision, covering both theoretical and practical issues in the field.
prereq_raw: graduate standing, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Data Visualization
description: Explores advanced techniques in data visualization by surveying visualization techniques from the past 5-10 years, and designing and developing data visualizations leveraging those techniques. Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Virtual and Augmented Reality
description: Students will learn the science, engineering, art, and applications of virtual reality and augmented reality, with an emphasis on the construction of working virtual environments. Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Digital Video Information
description: Principles and techniques of technical and context analysis of digital video information. Video capture and editing tools, compression and analysis algorithms, visual culture, narrative structure, juxtaposition of multimedia elements and their effects on information transmission.

subject: ICS
title: Seminar in ICS
description: Series of talks on advanced research topics.

subject: ICS
title: (Alpha) Topics in Computer Science
description: Reflects special interests of faculty in various areas of computer science. (B) area 1; (C) area 2; (D) area 3; (E) area 4; (G) general.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times in different topics and different areas

subject: ICS
title: Special Topics Seminar
description: Seminar discussing special topics in information and computer science. Topics and number of credits vary.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Special Topics in Security
description: Current topics and upcoming issues relevant to the field of information assurance and cyber security. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ICS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: ICS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.
prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD in computer science

prereq_tree.text: candidacy for PhD in computer science

subject: MATH
title: Survey of Mathematics
description: Selected topics designed to acquaint nonspecialists with examples of mathematical reasoning. May not be taken for credit after 215 or higher.

subject: MATH
title: Math for Elementary Teachers I
description: Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas, problem solving, and reasoning. Number systems, place value, fractions, and properties of operations. Prospective elementary education majors only.

subject: MATH
title: Math for Elementary Teachers II
description: Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas; problem solving; reasoning and proof; and using symbolism. Patterns and algebraic thinking, place value and decimals, geometry, and mathematical modeling.

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus: Elementary Functions
description: Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational exponential and logarithmic functions, composed and inverse functions, techniques of graphing.
prereq_raw: two years of high school algebra, one year of plane geometry

prereq_tree.text: two years of high school algebra, one year of plane geometry

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus
description: Algebra review. Polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, composed and inverse functions, techniques of graphing. Trigonometric functions, analytic geometry, polar coordinates, vectors, and related topics.

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus and Elements of Calculus for Economics and the Social Sciences
description: Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, algebra of functions, techniques of graphing, differentiation and integration of algebraic functions, applications in economics and social sciences.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Programming
description: (3 hr) Introduction to numerical algorithms and structured programming using Fortran, MATLAB, or other appropriate language.
prereq_raw: one semester of calculus (203, 215, 241, 242, 243, 244, 251A, 252A, or 253A) (or concurrent), or consent

subject: MATH
title: Calculus for Business and Social Sciences
description: Basic concepts; differentiation and integration applications to management, finance, economics, and the social sciences.

subject: MATH
title: Applied Calculus I
description: Basic concepts; differentiation, differential equations and integration with applications directed primarily to the life sciences.

subject: MATH
title: Applied Calculus II
description: Differential calculus for functions in several variables and curves, systems of ordinary differential equations, series approximation of functions, continuous probability, exposure to use of calculus in the literature.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus I
description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus II
description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations.
prereq_raw: 241 or 251A or a grade of B or better in 215; or consent

children.text: a grade of B or better in 215

subject: MATH
title: Calculus III
description: Vector algebra, vector-valued functions, differentiation in several variables, and optimization.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus IV
description: Multiple integrals; line integrals and Green’s Theorem; surface integrals, Stokes’s and Gauss’s Theorems.

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus I
description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration. Compared to 241, topics are discussed in greater depth.
prereq_raw: assessment and consent, or a grade of A in 140X and consent

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus II
description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations, introduction to vectors.
prereq_raw: 251A (with a minimum grade of B) or 241 (with a minimum grade of A and consent)

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of A and consent )

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus III
description: Vector calculus; maxima and minima in several variables; multiple integrals; line integrals, surface integrals and their applications.

subject: MATH
title: History of Mathematics
description: The historical development of mathematical thought.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
description: Symbolic logic, sets and relations, algorithms, trees and other graphs. Additional topics chosen from algebraic systems, networks, automata.
prereq_raw: one semester of calculus from mathematics department; or consent. Recommended: one semester programming

children.text: one semester of calculus from mathematics department;

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Differential Equations I
description: First order ordinary differential equations, constant coefficient linear equations, oscillations, Laplace transform, convolution, Green’s function.
prereq_raw: 216 or 243 (or concurrent) or 253A (or concurrent), or consent

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Differential Equations II
description: Constant coefficient linear systems, variable coefficient ordinary differential equations, series solutions and special functions, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Deterministic Models
description: Deterministic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include difference equations, qualitative behavior solutions of ODEs and reaction-diffusion equations. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Deterministic Models Lab
description: Optional laboratory for 304.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Probabilistic Models
description: Probabilistic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include stochastic and Poisson processes, Markov models, estimation, and Monte Carlo simulation. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Probabilistic Models Lab
description: Optional laboratory for 305.

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
description: Introduction to linear algebra, application of eigenvalue techniques to the solution of differential equations. Students may receive credit for only one of 307 or 311.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Linear Algebra
description: Algebra of matrices, linear equations, real vector spaces and transformations. Emphasis on concepts and abstraction and instruction of careful writing. Students may receive credit for only one of 307 or 311.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Advanced Mathematics
description: Formal introduction to the concepts of logic, finite and infinite sets, functions, methods of proof and axiomatic systems. Learning mathematical expressions in writing is an integral part of the course.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Real Analysis
description: A rigorous axiomatic development of one variable calculus. Completeness, topology of the line, limits, continuity, differentiation, integration. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing.

subject: MATH
title: Foundation of Euclidean Geometry
description: Axiomatic Euclidean geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method.

subject: MATH
title: Non-Euclidean Geometries
description: Hyperbolic, other non-Euclidean geometries.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Euclidean and NonEuclidean Geometries
description: Axiomatic geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method; Euclidean geometry; hyperbolic geometry, and other nonEuclidean geometries.

subject: MATH
title: Financial Mathematics
description: Interest rate measurement, valuation of annuities, loan repayment, bond valuation, rate of return. Term structure of interest rates, cashflow duration, and immunization. Financial mathematics actuarial exam topics.

subject: MATH
title: Elementary Probability Theory
description: Sets, discrete sample spaces, problems in combinatorial probability, random variables, mathematical expectations, classical distributions, applications.

subject: MATH
title: Elementary Probability and Statistics
description: Problem-oriented introduction to the basic concepts of probability and statistics, providing a foundation for applications and further study.

subject: MATH
title: Elementary Statistics
description: Estimation, tests of significance, the concept of power.

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations I
description: Integral surfaces and characteristics of first and second order partial differential equations. Applications to the equations of mathematical physics.

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations II
description: Laplace’s equation, Fourier transform methods for PDEs, higher dimensional PDEs, spherical harmonics, Laplace series, special functions and applications.

subject: MATH
title: Ordinary Differential Equations
description: Systems of linear ordinary differential equations, autonomous systems, and stability theory applications. Optional topics include series solutions, Sturm theory, numerical methods.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical solution of equations, interpolation, least-squares approximation, quadrature, eigenvalue problems, numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 407–408.)
prereq_raw: 243 or 253A, and 307 or 311, and one semester programming; or consent

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Continuation of 407. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 407.

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra
description: Vector spaces over arbitrary fields, minimal polynomials, invariant subspaces, canonical forms of matrices; unitary and Hermitian matrices, quadratic forms.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
description: Introduction to basic algebraic structures. Groups, finite groups, abelian groups, rings, integral domains, fields, factorization, polynomial rings, field extensions, quotient fields. Emphasis on writing instruction. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 412–413.)

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
description: Continuation of 412. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 412. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: MATH
title: Optimization: Theory & Methods
description: Introduction to theory and methods for optimization. Topics may include least square analysis, search methods, conjugate direction methods, linear programming, integer programming, and constrained optimization.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to the Theory of Numbers
description: Congruences, quadratic residues, arithmetic functions, distribution of primes. Emphasis is on teaching theory and writing, not on computation.

subject: MATH
title: Topology
description: General topology, including compactness and connectedness; the Jordan Curve Theorem and the classification of surfaces; first homotopy or homology groups.

subject: MATH
title: Principles of Analysis I
description: Topology of Rn , metric spaces, continuous functions, Riemann integration, sequences and series, uniform convergence, implicit function theorems, differentials and Jacobians. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 431–432.)

subject: MATH
title: Principles of Analysis II
description: Continuation of 431. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 431. Emphasis on writing instruction continues.

subject: MATH
title: Vector Analysis
description: Vector operations, wedge product, differential forms, and smooth mappings. Theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss, both classically and in terms of forms. Applications to electromagnetism and mechanics.

subject: MATH
title: Differential Geometry
description: Properties and fundamental geometric invariants of curves and surfaces in space; applications to the physical sciences.

subject: MATH
title: Complex Analysis
description: Analytic functions, complex integration, introduction to conformal mapping.

subject: MATH
title: Topics in Undergraduate Mathematics
description: Advanced topics from various areas: algebra, number theory, analysis, and geometry.

subject: MATH
title: Axiomatic Set Theory
description: Sets, relations, ordinal arithmetic, cardinal arithmetic, axiomatic set theory, axiom of choice and the continuum hypothesis.
prereq_raw: 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent

children.text: in a related field or consent

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Logic
description: A system of first order logic. Formal notions of well-formed formula, proof, and derivability. Semantic notions of model, truth, and validity. Completeness theorem.
prereq_raw: 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent. Recommended: 454

children.text: in a related field or consent . Recommended: 454

subject: MATH
title: Probability
description: Probability spaces, random variables, distributions, expectations, moment-generating and characteristic functions, limit theorems. Continuous probability emphasized.
prereq_raw: 244 (or concurrent) or 253A (or concurrent), or consent. Recommended: 305 or 371 or 372; or consent

subject: MATH
title: Statistical Inference
description: Sampling and parameter estimation, tests of hypotheses, correlation, regression, analysis of variance, sequential analysis, rank order statistics.

subject: MATH
title: Combinatorial Mathematics
description: Finite configurations. Topics may include counting methods, generating functions, graph theory, map coloring, block design, network flows, analysis of discrete algorithms.

subject: MATH
title: Senior Seminar
description: Seminar for senior mathematics majors, including an introduction to methods of research. Significant portion of class time is dedicated to the instruction and critique of oral presentations. All students must give the equivalent of three presentations.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Biology Seminar
description: Reports on research in mathematical biology, reviews of literature, and research presentation. Required for Certificate in Mathematical Biology.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher and consent

subject: MATH
title: Directed Reading
description: Limited to advanced students who must arrange with an instructor before enrolling.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits

subject: MATH
title: Problem Solving for Teachers
description: Practicing teachers develop and improve their problem-solving skills by working on challenging mathematical tasks. Students improve their mathematics content knowledge by working on problems and learning to design challenge problems for their own classes. Practicing teachers in grades K-12 only. All 600-courses prerequisites graduate standing or consent.

subject: MATH
title: (Alpha) Career Skills for Graduate Students in Mathematics
description: Seminar addresses issues important in the career of a mathematician, beginning from their time in graduate school, through navigating the job market and on to their eventual work in industry or academia. (B) teaching. Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, repeatable one time for (B)

subject: MATH
title: Applied Dynamical Systems
description: Continuous and discrete dynamical systems; bifurcation theory; chaotic maps. Additional topics from PDEs and linear algebra. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Methods of Applied Mathematics
description: Linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and partial differential equations. Topics include spectral theory, matrix exponentiation, initial-value problems, dynamical systems, bifurcation theory, first-order PDEs, characteristics, Sturm-Liouville theory, boundary-value problems, Green’s functions.

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations
description: Classical existence and uniqueness theory for PDEs, qualitative properties, classification, boundary value and initial value problems, fundamental solutions, other topics.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical linear algebra including iterative methods, SVD, and other matrix factorizations, locating eigenvalues, discrete approximation to partial differential equations.

subject: MATH
title: Key Elements of Linear Algebra
description: Key concepts of linear algebra for graduate students in mathematics. Specific topics include vector spaces, linear transformations, multilinear forms, and Jordan decomposition. May not receive credit for both MATH 411 and MATH 610. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Modern Algebra
description: Modules, Sylow theorems, Jordan-Holder theorem, unique factorization domains, Galois theory, algebraic closures, transcendence bases. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 611–612.)

subject: MATH
title: Modern Algebra
description: Continuation of 611. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 611.

subject: MATH
title: Group Theory
description: Sylow theorems, solvable groups, nilpotent groups, extension theory, representation theory, additional topics.

subject: MATH
title: Ring Theory
description: Ideal theory in Noetherian rings, localization, Dedekind domains, the Jacobson radical, the Wedderburn-Artin theorem, additional topics.

subject: MATH
title: Lattice Theory
description: Introduction with applications to general algebra. Partially ordered sets, decomposition theory, representations of lattices, varieties and free lattices, coordinatization of modular lattices.

subject: MATH
title: Universal Algebra
description: Introduction to basic techniques, including subalgebras, congruences, automorphisms and endomorphisms, varieties of algebras, Mal’cev conditions.

subject: MATH
title: Key Elements of Topology
description: Key concepts of Topology for graduate students in mathematics; topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; continuity. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Topology
description: Properties of topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; metrizability; convergence and continuity. Additional topics from general and algebraic topology. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 621–622.)

subject: MATH
title: Topology
description: Continuation of 621. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 621.

subject: MATH
title: Geometric Group Theory
description: Geometric, topological, and dynamical methods in the study of finitely generated infinite groups. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Differentiable Manifolds I
description: Differentiable structures on manifolds, tensor fields, Frobenius theorem, exterior algebra, integration of forms, Poincare Lemma, Stoke’s theorem.

subject: MATH
title: Theory of Functions of a Real Variable
description: Lebesgue measure and integral, convergence of integrals, functions of bounded variation, Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral and more general theory of measure and integration. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 631–632.)

subject: MATH
title: Theory of Functions of a Real Variable
description: Continuation of 631. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 631.

subject: MATH
title: Functional Analysis
description: Linear topological spaces, normed spaces, Hilbert spaces, function algebras, operator theory.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus of Variations
description: Simple variational problems, first and second variation formulas. Euler-Lagrange equation, direct methods, optimal control.

subject: MATH
title: Analytic Function Theory
description: Conformal mapping, residue theory, series and product developments, analytic continuation, special functions. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 644–645.)

subject: MATH
title: Analytic Function Theory
description: Continuation of 644. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 644.

subject: MATH
title: (Alpha) Topics in Mathematics
description: (B) logic; (D) analysis; (E) commutative rings; (F) function theory; (G) geometric topology; (H) operator theory; ((I) probability; (J) algebra; (K) special; (M) lattice theory and universal algebra; (N) noncommutative rings; (O) transformation groups; (P) partial differential equations; (Q) potential theory; (R) algebraic topology; (S) functional analysis; (T) number theory and combinatorics; (U) differentiable manifolds II.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable up to nine credits for (U); unlimited times for the other alphas

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Logic
description: Model theory, computability theory, set theory. In particular syntax and semantics of first order logic; incompleteness, completeness, and compactness theorems; Loewenheim-Skolem theorems; computable and computably enumerable sets; axioms of set theory; ordinals and cardinals. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Set Theory
description: Axiomatic development, ordinal and cardinal numbers, recursion theorems, axiom of choice, continuum hypothesis, consistency and independence results.

subject: MATH
title: Recursive Functions and Complexity
description: Recursive, r.e., Ptime, and Logspace classes. Nondeterminism, parallelism, alternation, and Boolean circuits. Reducibility and completeness.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Algebraic Number Theory
description: Number fields and rings of integers; primes, factorization, and ramification theory; finiteness of the class group; Dirichlet’s Unit Theorem; valuations, completions, and local fields. Further topics. Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Advanced Probability
description: Independence and conditioning, martingales, ergodic theory, Markov chains, central limit theorem.
prereq_raw: 631 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: MATH
title: Stochastic Processes
description: Stationary, Gaussian, and Markov processes.
prereq_raw: 671 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: MATH
title: Graph Theory
description: Connected graphs and digraphs. Graph embeddings. Connectivity and networks. Factors and factorizations. Coverings. Coloring. Applications.

subject: MATH
title: Directed Reading and Research for Plan B Masters Students
description: Maximum of 3 credit hours. Graduate standing in MATH.

subject: MATH
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Maximum of 3 credit hours.

subject: MATH
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: MATH
title: Apprenticeship in Teaching
description: An experience-based introduction to college-level teaching; students serve as student teachers to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching and participation in planning and evaluation. Open to graduate students in mathematics only.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in mathematics and consent
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits

subject: MATH
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: MBIO
title: Kūlana Noi‘i: Introduction to Place-Based Methodologies in Hawai‘i
description: Lectures, discussions, and service-learning organized to deepen understanding in: what is a research paradigm; how methods are developed in research designs; and new knowledge for place-based research. Marine Biology Graduate Program students only.

subject: MBIO
title: Career Skills for Marine Biologists
description: Introduction to key professional skills including, but not limited to: grant writing, CV preparation, research logistics, data management, reproducible science, peer review, research ethics, publishing, career options, teaching, and professional presentations.

subject: MBIO
title: Current Research in Marine Biology
description: Discussions with marine biology graduate faculty on current primary literature in marine biology. Graduate students only.

subject: MBIO
title: Mathematical Ecology of Marine Systems
description: Introduction to a broad range of theories and techniques from mathematical ecology with an emphasis on marine systems. Students will learn to assess model assumptions, construct simple models, and apply analytical methods to describe system behavior. Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Introduction to Quantitative Methods in Fisheries Science
description: Fisheries and population models including growth, stock-recruitment, surplus production, age-structured and size-based, parameter estimation, uncertainty characterization, resampling methods, and scientific computing. Graduate students only.
prereq_raw: MATH 215 or 216, or MATH 241 or 242, or consent

subject: MBIO
title: Data Science Fundamentals in R
description: (3 hr Lec/Lab) Introduces project management, data analysis, and mathematical and statistical modeling using R as a platform. Students will learn principles and benefits of programming languages to apply skills to their own research.

subject: MBIO
title: Behavioral Ecology of Coral Reef Fishes
description: Introduction to processes that affect animal behavior and their significance. Exploring a broad range of techniques for studying behaviors of fishes, students will use new techniques in their own research. Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Respiratory Processes in Coral Reef Organisms
description: Multidisciplinary course introduces the respiratory system of fishes and other reef taxa and its significance for ecology and behavior. Students will learn theory, principles, and hot to design/execute experiments for their own research. Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Remote Sensing Applications in Marine Science
description: Introduction to tools for the discover, access, and application of remote sensing for their own research in marine biology, including best practices for data collection, synthesis, and project management. Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Coral Reef Structure and Function
description: Linking organismal traits and habitat features with ecosystem function. Hands-on course with coral reef fieldwork, exposure to new technology, and the potential to develop independent projects in publications. Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Marine Mammal Science and Conservation
description: Will cover the most pressing conservation issues for marine mammals, and include a hands-on field component using traditional and novel techniques to inform their management. Graduate students in MB, ZOOL, BOT, and OCN programs only.

subject: MBIO
title: Place-Based Pedagogy for Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experiences
description: Introduces students to place-based science education with an emphasis on Hawaiʻi marine science classrooms. Includes discussions on inclusive teaching methods, CUREs, and effective instruction in laboratory and field environments. Instructor approval required.

subject: MBIO
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research and reading in various fields of marine biology. Graduate students only.

subject: MBIO
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis; (F) 1 credit. Graduate students only. Satisfactory/ Unsatisfactory only.

subject: MBIO
title: Topics in Marine Fisheries and Natural Resource Management
description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to marine fisheries and natural resource management. Graduate students only.

subject: MBIO
title: Topics in Marine Conservation Biology
description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to marine conservation biology. Graduate students only.

subject: MBIO
title: Topics in Marine Education, Outreach, and Policy
description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to education, outreach, and policy of the marine environment. Graduate students only.

subject: MBIO
title: Topics in Marine Physiology, Behavior, and Organismal Biology
description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to the physiology, behavior, and biology of marine organisms. Graduate students only.

subject: MBIO
title: Advanced Topics in Quantitative Biology
description: Reflects faculty expertise and needs for graduate training in quantitative methods for biology, including statistical, computational, and analytic approaches. Format (lecture/lab/discussion) will vary by topic. Graduate students only.

subject: MBIO
title: Internship in College Teaching (Marine Science)
description: Introduction to college-level science teaching; masters or doctoral students serve as apprentices to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching, planning and evaluation.

subject: MBIO
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Graduate students only. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: NSCI
title: Natural Sciences and Life-Pulling the Puzzles Apart
description: Journey through the Natural Sciences finding fun, excitement, and success in science, mathematics, engineering, medicine, and all that is the natural sciences. Focus upon challenging worldviews of belief, invention, impact, and ethics.

subject: NSCI
title: Seminar for Science Teachers
description: Seminar and discussions of current and significant topics and problems in science where teachers can exchange new and innovative teaching ideas and strategies.

subject: NSCI
title: Computers in Classroom
description: Combined lecture, laboratory and discussion on the use of computers as a teaching tool in the classroom. To be taught in a hands-on manner appropriate for the science teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent.

subject: NSCI
title: Mathematics Workshop for Teachers
description: An in-depth study of topics from intermediate and high school mathematics. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent.

subject: NSCI
title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent.

subject: NSCI
title: Seminar on Science Teaching
description: Effective teaching methods; organization of courses, lectures, laboratory exercises; development and evaluation of examinations; computers and audiovisual aids. Open to graduate students in various science disciplines.

subject: PHYS
title: Survey of Physics
description: Mechanics, electricity and magnetism, waves, optics, atomic and nuclear physics. Only algebra and geometry used. For non-science majors.

subject: PHYS
title: Survey of Physics Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hooke’s law, falling bodies, collisions, Boyle’s law, electric and magnetic fields, induction, waves, optics.

subject: PHYS
title: Physics in the Arts
description: Introduction to physics of sound and light, with applications to music and visual arts: sound perception, harmony, musical scales, instruments; lenses, cameras, color perception and mixing. Uses algebra and geometry. Intended primarily for non-science majors.

subject: PHYS
title: How Things Work: Physics for Everyday Life
description: Introduction to physics and science in everyday life. It considers objects from our daily environment, and focuses on the principles such as motion, forces, heat, electromagnetism, optics, and modern physics.

subject: PHYS
title: College Physics I
description: Non-calculus physics. Mechanics, wave motion, heat.
prereq_raw: MATH 140X, or 215 or higher; or qualifying score on math placement exam

children.text: qualifying score on math placement exam

subject: PHYS
title: College Physics Lab I
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to experimental analysis, physical observation and measurement, experiments on conservation laws, fluid friction, oscillations.

subject: PHYS
title: College Physics II
description: Electricity, magnetism, optics, modern physics.

subject: PHYS
title: College Physics Lab II
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Optics, electric and magnetic fields, DC and AC circuitry.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics I
description: Calculus-based mechanics of particles and rigid bodies: kinematics, force, energy, momentum, rotation, gravitation, fluids, oscillations and waves.
prereq_raw: MATH 242 (or concurrent) or MATH 252A (or concurrent). MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

children.text: MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

restrictions_raw: Intended for physical science and engineering majors.

subject: PHYS
title: Honors General Physics I
description: Special format for topics: mechanics of particles and rigid bodies, wave motion, thermodynamics and kinetic theory.
prereq_raw: MATH 242 (or concurrent) or MATH 252A (or concurrent). MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

children.text: MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics I Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Similar to 151L but at 170 level.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics II
description: Electricity and magnetism and geometric optics.
prereq_raw: 151 or 170 and MATH 242 or MATH 252A, MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

subject: PHYS
title: Honors General Physics II
description: Special format for topics: electricity and magnetism and geometric optics.
prereq_raw: 151 or 170 and MATH 242 or MATH 252A, MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics II Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Similar to 152L but at 272 level.

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics III
description: Relativity, introduction to quantum mechanics, atomic and nuclear physics, and physical optics.
prereq_raw: 152 or 272 and MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent

subject: PHYS
title: General Physics III Lab
description: (1 4-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating selected concepts of 274, including diffraction and interference of light, wave nature of matter, photoelectric effect, atomic spectra, and semiconductors.

subject: PHYS
title: Computational Physics
description: Analysis of physical systems and problem solving using computers and numerical methods. Development of scientific writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.
prereq_raw: 152 or 272 or 272A, and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent

subject: PHYS
title: Theoretical Mechanics I
description: Particle dynamics, rigid-body dynamics, planetary motion.
prereq_raw: 170 or 170A; 272 or 272A; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: MATH 302 (or concurrent)

subject: PHYS
title: Theoretical Mechanics II
description: Rigid-body mechanics continued, fluid dynamics, wave motion, theory of relativity.

subject: PHYS
title: Electricity and Magnetism
description: Electrostatic and magnetostatic fields in vacuum and in matter; induction; Maxwell’s equations; AC circuits.
prereq_raw: 272 or 272A; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

subject: PHYS
title: Individual Work in Advanced Physics
description: Limited to students with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Applications of Mathematics in Physical Sciences
description: Mathematical methods, techniques; applications to problems in physical sciences.
prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A, and MATH 307 or 311; or consent. Recommended: upper division mathematics course

subject: PHYS
title: Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
description: Laws of thermodynamics, heat transfer, kinetic theory, statistical mechanics.

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Physics I
description: Crystal structure: lattice vibrations; phonon effects; electronic processes in solids (metals, semiconductors, and superconductors).

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Physics II
description: Energy-band calculations, optical processes, Josephson effect, theories of dielectrics and magnetism, physics of color centers, order-disorder transformation.

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetic Waves
description: Field equations, plane, spherical and guided waves.

subject: PHYS
title: Physical Optics
description: Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics.
prereq_raw: 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C) or ECE 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-), or consent

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C ) or ECE 372 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C- ) , or consent

subject: PHYS
title: General Relativity & Cosmology
description: Introduction to general relativity & cosmology. Spacetime metrics, geodesics, Einstein field equations, black holes. Geometry of the universe, redshift, cosmological distances. Cosmological models, dark matters, dark energy. Big Bang nucleosynthesis, recombination, cosmic microwave background, inflation.
prereq_raw: 274; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: ASTR 242

subject: PHYS
title: Electronics for Physicists
description: Investigation of Kirchoff’s Laws, electromagnetic circuit theory. Fourier analysis and stability theory with circuits. Applications to physical measurements are stressed.

subject: PHYS
title: Modern Electronics for Physicists
description: Introduction to high performance solid state instrumentation by means of practical research electronics: printed circuit board design/fabrication; complex programmable logic design/verification; integrated circuit SPICE simulation. Detector fabrication and test emphasis during final project.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics I
description: Wave mechanics, Schroedinger equation, angular momenta, potential problems.
prereq_raw: 274, 310, 350, 400 (or concurrent); either MATH 244 or 253A; and either MATH 311 or 307; or consent

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Physics Laboratory I
description: Advanced experiments involving nuclear spectroscopy, angular correlations in positronium annihilation, optical polarization, chaos, measurement of speed of light, numerical simulations. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics II
description: Continuation of 480; atomic physics, scattering, perturbation theory.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Physics Laboratory II
description: Advanced experiments involving measurement of the muon lifetime, crystal x-ray diffraction, nuclear magnetic resonance, the Mössbauer effect, and numerical simulations. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.

subject: PHYS
title: Professional Ethics for Physicists
description: Student seminar on ethical principles and their application to research in physics and astronomy and closely-related fields. Historical examples will be presented and discussed by the participants.
restrictions_raw: PHYS, ASTP, and ASTR majors only.

subject: PHYS
title: Modern Physics
description: Introduction to nuclear and elementary-particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
description: Mathematical tools of theoretical physics. Continuation of 400 but with an independent selection of topics.

subject: PHYS
title: Analytical Mechanics
description: Dynamics of particles, particle systems; rigid bodies; Lagrangian and Hamiltonian equations; special relativity.

subject: PHYS
title: Electrodynamics I
description: Potential theory, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, boundary value problems.

subject: PHYS
title: Electrodynamics II
description: Relativistic electrodynamics, radiation by charged particles.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Optics
description: Contemporary advanced applications in optics including nonlinear optics and optical parametric oscillators, atomic lasers and laser systems, and free-electron lasers.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Seminar
description: Discussions and reports on physical theory and recent developments.

subject: PHYS
title: Condensed Matter Seminar
description: Results and discussions of current topics in condensed matter physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Seminar on Atomic and Solid-State Physics
description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in atomic, surface, and solid-state physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Seminar on Elementary Particle Physics
description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in elementary particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: PHYS
title: Topics in Particles and Fields
description: Topics in current theoretical research; e.g., unified field theories, general relativity, gravitation, and cosmology.

subject: PHYS
title: Special Topics: Experimental Physics
description: Topics in current experimental research in low-energy physics, high-energy physics, cross-disciplinary physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Topics in Condensed Matter Theory
description: Topics in condensed matter theory, e.g., group theory, many-body techniques, renormalization group, density functional theory, other topics of current interest.

subject: PHYS
title: Statistical Physics I
description: Equilibrium thermodynamics; Gibbs ensembles; quantum statistics; ideal and non-ideal Fermi; Bose and Boltzmann gases; phase transitions; and critical phenomena.

subject: PHYS
title: Statistical Physics II
description: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics, transport theory, fluctuation dissipation theorem, many-body Green’s function methods, normal Fermi and Bose liquids, superfluidity, superconductivity.

subject: PHYS
title: Modern General Relativity
description: Differential geometry, special relativity, Einstein equations, gravitational phenomena, equivalence principles, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, relativistic stars, experimental tests, computational techniques. Graduate students only in PHYS or ASTR. (Alt. years: fall)

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Field Theory I
description: Relativistic wave equations and their solutions. Dirac’s theory of the electron, propagator techniques. Applications to quantum electrodynamics.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Field Theory II
description: Local gauge invariance, Yang-Mills theory: quantum chromodynamics, spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone bosons; the standard electroweak theory; grand unified theories.

subject: PHYS
title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
description: Nuclear physics; electrodynamics; hadron structure and partons. Techniques of particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Nuclear and Particle Physics II
description: Quantum chromodynamics; electroweak interactions; the standard model. Techniques of particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Theory
description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, electron-electron interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Theory
description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

subject: PHYS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: DH
title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology
description: The study of the structure and functions of the head and neck with emphasis on structures in or related to the oral cavity; of tooth morphology.
prereq_raw: PHYL 141, PHYL 141L, PHYL 142, PHYL 142L, and either BIOC 141 or CHEM 161

subject: DH
title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Application of DH 231 didactic concepts to laboratory activities and practices.
prereq_raw: PHYL 141, PHYL 141L, PHYL 142, PHYL 142L, and either BIOC 141 or CHEM 161

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene I
description: Relationship to dentistry, problems, trends, issues; role and functions of dental hygienists to prevent and control chronic oral diseases; preliminary dental hygiene clinical, includes team concepts in dentistry. Emphasis on teaching writing for the profession.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene I Lab
description: Application of preliminary dental hygiene clinical and support procedures including instrumentation, vital signs, and team concepts in dentistry.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene II
description: Basic dental hygiene theory and skills including competencies in health history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, plaque control and support procedures.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene II Lab/Clinic
description: Laboratory and clinical experiences in basic dental hygiene skills and competencies including history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, and clinic procedures.

subject: DH
title: General Histology
description: Cells, tissues, the organs they make up, and their embryologic origin.

subject: DH
title: Oral Histology and Embryology
description: Cells and tissues as they relate to the oral cavity and the embryological development of the head, neck, and related oral structures.

subject: DH
title: Dental Radiography
description: Basic principles of radiation and fundamental information to understand and safely use radiation in dental radiography.

subject: DH
title: Dental Radiography Lab/Clinic
description: (1 3-hr Lab/Clinic) Preparation and evaluation of radiographic survey of patients with varying dentition; methods, and indications of safety considerations in clinical application of roentgen rays.

subject: DH
title: Health Education and Promotion
description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups and the larger public.
prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

subject: DH
title: General Pathology
description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases an tissue alterations associated with the human body organ systems.

subject: DH
title: Oral Pathology
description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases affecting the teeth and the structures of the oral cavity.

subject: DH
title: Dental Materials
description: Science of dental materials and its application to dentistry and dental hygiene.

subject: DH
title: Dental Materials Lab/Clinic
description: Laboratory and clinical application of concepts in the science of dental materials.

subject: DH
title: Expanded Functions in Dental Hygiene
description: Basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene.

subject: DH
title: Expanded Functions in Dental Hygiene Lab/Clinic
description: (2 1.5-hr Lab/Clinic) Application of basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene.

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I
description: Development of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research.

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I Clinic
description: Clinical instruction and application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing, and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research.

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II
description: Continued development of dental hygiene concepts, skills, emergency procedures, team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating oral hygiene care of patients. Review and analyze dental periodicals and conduct a case study. Emphasis on writing.

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
description: Continuation of 375. Clinical application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care to patients.

subject: DH
title: Pain Control and Local Anesthesia in Dentistry
description: Basic concepts of pain control and local anesthesia in dentistry with appropriate emphasis on psychological preparation, pharmacological preparation, and safe and effective administration of anesthesia in the practice of dental hygiene.

subject: DH
title: Periodontology I
description: Normal periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy. Emphasis on writing.

subject: DH
title: Periodontology II
description: Continuation of DH 390. Normal periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy. Emphasis on writing.

subject: DH
title: Community Health
description: Introduction and application of the principles of health education and dental public health into practice in schools, community agencies, and private dental offices (inclusive of problem assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation processes); epidemiology and biostatistics.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene I
description: An in-depth knowledge and clinical application of expanded function in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Dental Hygiene I Clinic
description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II
description: In-depth knowledge, communicated via oral delivery, on development of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modifications in behavior.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

subject: DH
title: Pediatric Growth and Development
description: Focus on the normal growth and development of children based on current clinical practice guidelines and evidence in pediatric research.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Health and Diagnostic Assessment for Pediatric Patients
description: Focus on advanced health and diagnostic assessment for pediatric patients. Includes behavior management techniques as well as oral habits and subsequent malocclusions and speech difficulties.

subject: DH
title: Pharmacological Principles and Clinical Therapeutics in Pediatric Dental Care
description: Focus on pharmacological principles and clinical therapeutics in pediatric dental care.

subject: DH
title: Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Simulation Lab
description: Focus on interprofessional practice principles and competencies while providing students an opportunity to participate in interprofessional team simulations to address health care issues of children.

subject: DH
title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical I
description: Field experience. Clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age.

subject: DH
title: Management of Pediatric Dental Emergencies
description: Focus on the management of dental emergencies in children.

subject: DH
title: Community-Based Dental Hygiene Care of Vulnerable and Special Needs Children
description: Emphasizes community-based oral health promotion, dental disease risk reduction and management in children 0-5 years of age with a focus on vulnerable and special needs populations.

subject: DH
title: Community-Based Practice Capstone
description: Provides an opportunity to synthesize, analyze, and develop solutions to an oral health care problem affecting children ages 0-5 years. Requires one credit to be spent in fieldwork to meet course requirements.

subject: DH
title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical II
description: Advanced clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age.

subject: DH
title: Directed Reading, Field Work, or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading, field work, or research for major under supervision in related areas of dentistry and dental hygiene.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Professional Nursing I
description: This first level course focuses on nursing practice and education. Professional responsibilities in the practice of nursing are emphasized.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Professional Nursing II
description: This second level course builds on the knowledge and skills gained in the first level and focuses on professional responsibilities in nursing practice and education.

subject: NURS
title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan
description: Focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. It introduces the nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice.
prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

subject: NURS
title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. Introduces nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice.

subject: NURS
title: Professionalism in Nursing
description: Professional responsibilities of nursing practice are examined through the history of nursing, practice and education, legal and ethical issues, contemporary issues, and nursing roles.
prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

subject: NURS
title: Pathophysiology
description: Focus on pathophysiological concepts that are basic to understanding illness and injury and the corresponding spectrum of human responses, which serve as a foundation for the formulation of clinical decisions and care planning.
prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

subject: NURS
title: Pharmacology for Nursing
description: This course will help students to gain knowledge of the mechanism of action, toxicity, adverse reactions, side effects, therapeutic uses, and nursing implications of the major categories of drugs.

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness I
description: Focuses on nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness.

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness I Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on using nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness. Nursing skills are integrated into clinical experiences.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Evidence Based Practice and Health Promotion
description: Provides an introduction to the HSNC Competencies and spiraling of concepts and is based on the assumption of student responsibility for learning. Emphasis on writing instruction, and research evidence to support nursing care.

subject: NURS
title: Statistics in Nursing Research
description: Focuses on the basic concepts and applications of statistics as applied to nursing research.

subject: NURS
title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health
description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute care and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools for providing culturally sensitive, client-centered care. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health Lab
description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools when providing culturally sensitive, family-centered care. Emphasis on teaching writing for the profession. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Child and Family Health
description: Nursing care and health promotion for children and families. Emphasis on concepts related to the delivery of familycentered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Child and Family Health Lab
description: Nursing care and health promotion lab for children and families. Application of concepts related to the delivery of family-centered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Contemporary Ethical Issues in Health Care
description: Explore contemporary ethical issues and their legal implications in health care. Focus on decision-making in professional practice and social policy formation.
prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

subject: NURS
title: Gerontology: Its Nursing Implications
description: Explores attitudes toward the aged, biological and psychological aspects, ethnicity, sexuality, nutritional problems, community resources, other related topics.
prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

subject: NURS
title: Nursing in the Multicultural Milieu
description: Relates values, beliefs, attitudes, family organization, lifestyles, and health practices in different ethnic groups to health-care and nursing practice.
prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness III
description: Focuses on complex situations requiring strong recognition skills, and rapid decision making. The evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored.

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness III Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on complex situations requiring application of strong recognition skills and rapid decision making. Evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored.

subject: NURS
title: Health Education and Promotion
description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups, and the larger public.
prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

subject: NURS
title: Professionalism in Nursing II
description: Continuation of 211. Focus is on current issues in nursing and health care and nursing roles. Principles of organizational structure, leadership, decision-making, priority setting, and change will be discussed.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Nursing Research
description: Introduction to the research process and an understanding of the applicability of the scientific approach to nursing. Analysis and resolution of contemporary medical ethics issues in research and general nursing practice are primary focuses.

subject: NURS
title: Principles of Nursing Research and Evidence-Based Practice
description: (Lec) Introduces the process for research application and evidence-based practice. Includes: EBP questions, evidence sources, literature search and synthesis, levels and quality of evidence, and determination of clinical significance. Focus on contemporary medical ethics issues. .

subject: NURS
title: Directed Reading/Research I, II
description: Limited to juniors and seniors in nursing.

subject: NURS
title: Student Ambassador Program
description: Focuses on professional leadership development, mentorship, and professional skills for nurses. Students learn to be representatives between the Department of Nursing and alumni, prospective students, and the general public.
prereq_raw: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador

prereq_tree.text: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador

subject: NURS
title: NCLEX Review
description: Overview of the NCLEX-RN licensure examination and regular, systematic practice in taking multiple choice examinations.
prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

subject: NURS
title: Cooperative Education in Nursing
description: A two-semester course with seminar in professional role development in addition to paid work experience in nursing at a local agency. Upper division NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Summer Internship
description: Summer practicum experience for students to learn the role of the professional nurse by building on previously learned knowledge and skills in the nursing program.

subject: NURS
title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies
description: Survey of complementary and alternative therapies used for health promotion of individuals and groups.
prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

subject: NURS
title: Veteran Healthcare, Education, and Cultural Needs
description: Provides a broad overview of the Veteran-Military population and their unique culture, educational, and health care needs. Open to non-nursing majors.

subject: NURS
title: Gerontology, Health Care, and the Law (Elder Law)
description: Provides a basic foundation for studies at the intersection of gerontology, health care, and the law and places an emphasis on proactive and preventive law for older adults in society.

subject: NURS
title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing
description: Theory course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing with an emphasis on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.

subject: NURS
title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing emphasizing application of strategies to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local, national, and international levels. Emphasis on oral and writing instruction.

subject: NURS
