description: Laboratory instruction will include leadership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed for students pursuing Navy and Marine Corps commissions. CR/NC only

subject: NAVL
title: Introduction to Naval Science
description: Overview of the Navy’s mission, customs, traditions, and the duties required of Junior Officers. Provides students with a basic knowledge of damage control, shipboard organization, and safety procedures prior to their first summer training cruise.

subject: NAVL
title: Seapower and Maritime Affairs
description: Study of the Navy and the influence of seapower upon history that incorporates both an historical and political perspective to explore major events and circumstances that have shaped a bold and proud history.

subject: NAVL
title: Navigation
description: Designed to provide midshipmen with an in-depth study of the theory, principles, procedures, and application of plotting, piloting, and electronic navigation, as well as an introduction to maneuvering boards.

subject: NAVL
title: Navigation
description: Designed to provide midshipmen with an in-depth study of the theory, principles, procedures, and application of plotting, piloting, and electronic navigation, as well as an introduction to maneuvering boards.

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Ships System I: Engineering
description: Will learn ship design and control, hydrodynamic forces, stability, electrical theory, and damage control coupled with design of steam, gas turbine and nuclear propulsion. Case studies merging both ethical and technical challenges.

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Ship Systems II: Weapons
description: Outlines the theory and employment of naval warship weapons systems. Supplemented with review/ analysis of case studies involving the moral and ethical responsibilities of leaders in the employment of weapons.

subject: NAVL
title: Evolution of Warfare
description: Will imbue students with an understanding of the origins of modern warfighting theory through an analysis of historical philosophies, domains, tactics, and technology.

subject: NAVL
title: Fund of Maneuver Warfare
description: Introduction to the foundational concepts and history of the USMC as the premiere Maneuver Warfighting Organization. Theoretical course that utilizes historical examples.

subject: NAVL
title: United States Pacific Fleet Internship
description: Leadership development, teamwork, and activities designed for NROTC students. Learn how to write a federal resume, be a Federal Employee, and learn the skills needed to complete and present their U.S. Pacific Fleet capstone project.

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Operations and Seamanship
description: Study of U.S. Navy ships professional and efficient operations. Lecture series on Fleet communications, tactical employment, relative motion plotting, seamanship, Joint Warfare, and employment of naval forces as an element of National Security.

subject: NAVL
title: Leadership and Ethics
description: Introduces ethical theories in discussion-oriented formats to provide a solid foundation of various moral, ethical, and leadership philosophies. Serves to guide, refine, and strengthen moral character and increase awareness of different ethical decision-making tools.

subject: ANTH
title: Emerging Humanity
description: Introduction to human biological evolution and the archaeology of culture in the world prior to AD 1500. Open to nonmajors, recommended for majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Culture and Humanity
description: Introduction to cultural anthropology. How humans create, understand, order and modify their natural, social, supernatural and physical environments, and make meaning and order. Open to non-majors, required for ANTH majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Polynesian Surf Culture
description: Examines environmental and cultural factors in the development of Polynesian surf culture, surfing’s decline due to Western influence, and its revitalization as a modern recreational activity. Business practices of the surfing industry are critically analyzed.

subject: ANTH
title: Polynesian Surf Culture Field Lab
description: 175 co-requisite lab. Surfing sites are visited, ancient and modern Polynesian surfing practices and surfboard design and technology are discussed. Shoreline assessments emphasize ocean safety. Social issues surrounding surfing sites in Hawai‘i are analyzed.

subject: ANTH
title: Historical Ecology of Hawai‘i
description: The Hawaiian socio-ecosystem is the product of centuries of human land use and resource exploitation. Explores the events and processes that have shaped the islands’ ecology and future sustainability.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology
description: Introduction to prehistoric archaeology; methods and techniques of excavation and laboratory analysis; brief survey of theory in relation to change and diversity in prehistoric human groups.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
description: Human evolution, primatology, human genetics, biological variation, human adaptability, growth and development.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany 215.

subject: ANTH
title: Quantitative Reasoning for Anthropologists
description: Achieve basic quantitative literacy and to familiarize them with statistical reasoning so that they are prepared to carry out anthropological (and other social science) research.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Sports
description: Explores sports from anthropological viewpoint: biological, cultural, linguistic, and archaeological. Open to nonmajors. Sophomore standing only.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Love
description: Explores love from multiple anthropological viewpoints: biological, cultural, archaeological.

subject: ANTH
title: Contemporary Social Issues
description: Contemporary issues in the field of anthropology and in society, including race, ethnicity, gender, inequality, colonialism and decolonization, health disparities and environmental change, from the perspective of cultural anthropology, biological anthropology and archaeology.

subject: ANTH
title: Culture and Health
description: Social and cultural aspects of medicine; the relationship of medicine to the beliefs, social systems, ecological adaptations, and cultural changes of human groups.

subject: ANTH
title: Human Origins
description: Theory of evolution, evolutionary systematics, and taxonomy; evolutionary biology of primates; fossil records for primate and human evolution. Laboratory included.

subject: ANTH
title: Visual Anthropology
description: Historical development of documentary films of non-Western peoples; critical examination of ways in which ethnographic films represent different cultures.

subject: ANTH
title: Sex and Gender
description: Cross-cultural theories and perceptions of sexual differences; linkage between biology and cultural constructions of gender; relationship of gender ideology to women’s status.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Tourism
description: Anthropological perspectives on the subject of the global phenomenon of tourism. Includes issues of cultural performance, identity, and commoditization. Open to nonmajors.

subject: ANTH
title: Pacific Islands Archaeology
description: Origins of Pacific peoples; chronology of settlement; sequences of culture in Australia, Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia.

subject: ANTH
title: Origins of Cities
description: Combined lecture/ discussion on the emergence and development of ancient cities in comparative perspective and the dynamics of (pre)modern urban life. Examples are drawn from the Near East, Mediterranean, Africa, India, China, and the Americas.

subject: ANTH
title: American Folklore and Folklife
description: Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnohistory
description: Review of ethnohistory, i.e., the interdisciplinary, holistic and inclusive investigation of the histories of native peoples drawing not only on documented sources, but also on ethnography, linguistics, archaeology, ecology and other disciplines as an alternative to conventional Eurocolonial history.

subject: ANTH
title: Food Origins, Food Culture
description: Lectures and discussion offer an anthropological introduction to how humans created and transformed food through time.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Peoples and Cultures of North America
description: Survey of Indigenous peoples of North America. Integrates documentary records, ethnography, and archaeology to explore variability among native communities. Contemporary topics include political recognition and self-determination, health and education, and natural resources and economic development.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Surfing
description: Applies cultural anthropology to assess surfing as an indigenous Hawaiian and modern globalized activity. Discusses the history of surfing, surfing culture, and the impacts of surfing tourism on coastal development, reef ecology, and ocean safety.

subject: ANTH
title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
description: Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ANTH
title: Society and Environment
description: Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems.

subject: ANTH
title: Historical Ecology
description: Examines the recursive relationship between humans and the environment across deep time.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Virtual Worlds
description: Anthropological study of computer mediated interaction. Focus on the ethnography of massively multiplayer online games, text-based chat rooms, and blogs.

subject: ANTH
title: Aggression, War, and Peace
description: Biocultural, evolutionary, and cross-cultural perspectives on the conditions, patterns, and processes of violence, war, nonviolence, and peace.

subject: ANTH
title: Pacific Island Cultures
description: Introduction to cultures of Polynesia, Micronesia, and Melanesia from time of first settlement to emergence of modern nation states.

subject: ANTH
title: Primate Behavioral Ecology
description: As primates are our closest living relatives, studying the range of variation in areas like life history, diet, communication, and social systems within the order primates can inform on how we ourselves evolved.

subject: ANTH
title: Households in Cross-Cultural Perspectives: Home, Hale, Casa
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in household and community level organizations in Latin America and elsewhere. Topics may include gender relations, kinship structures, political economy, impacts of colonialism, modernization, and globalization on households.

subject: ANTH
title: Household Archaeology
description: Focuses on the differences in the composition, activities, roles, and relationships to be observed archaeologically between households that comprised ancient communities and how these differences inform us about the dynamics of social change. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnographic Field Techniques
description: Problems and techniques of social-cultural anthropological fieldwork; ethnographic literature; work with informants.

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Indigenous Peoples of Latin America
description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different alphas

subject: ANTH
title: Race and Human Variation
description: Human genetic and physical variation; latitudinal, longitudinal, and altitudinal variation across human populations; history of racism; contemporary issues in race and racism.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing, recommend 152 and 215; or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology Practicum
description: Students will gain practical archaeological experience (e.g., materials processing, analysis, documentation, conservation) under the direction of practicing archaeological professionals in the local community and in collaboration with supervising archaeological faculty. ANTH majors or minors only. Sophomore standing or higher.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to 6 credits

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Lab Techniques
description: Laboratory analysis and evaluation of field data; preservation and restoration of artifacts. Preparation for publication.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Field Techniques
description: Archaeological survey and excavations; field trips, mapping, photography. May focus on terrestrial or underwater. May be taught entirely in the field at a national or international archaeological site.

subject: ANTH
title: How Archaeology Works
description: Uses archaeological examples to illustrate social science research techniques. Students learn how to create, analyze, and evaluate data through lab-based exercises, and examine ethical issues inherent in anthropological practice. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Skeletal Biology
description: Introduction to the human skeleton and methods for analyzing archaeological human remains including age, sex, ethnicity, paleodemography, skeletal and dental variation, paleopathology, population studies.

subject: ANTH
title: Skeletal Biology Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany 384.

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Undergraduate Seminar
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethics in Anthropology
description: Seminar surveying ethical cases, problems, issues and questions from the inception of anthropology to the present. Junior standing or higher or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Museum Anthropology
description: Anthropological study of museums and related sites of cultural production (historic sites, memorials, theme parks). (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Evolutionary Anthropology
description: Lecture discussion providing an overview of evolutionary theory in anthropology: focus on the evolution of culture, behavioral ecology, and cultural diversity; emphasis on archaeological and ethnographic research and explanatory models.

subject: ANTH
title: Language and Gender
description: The role of language in the construction of gender and in the maintenance of the gender order. Field projects explore hypotheses about the interaction of language and gender. No previous knowledge of linguistics required.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language.

subject: ANTH
title: Wealth, Culture, and Economic Anthropology
description: Analysis of economic activities in non-Western, non-industrial societies; production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services in a variety of cultures.

subject: ANTH
title: Political Anthropology
description: Character of political institutions and their development in nonWestern and non industrial societies.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Anthropology
description: Exploration of how anthropology studies indigenous groups throughout the world. An examination of the changing contexts of anthropological practice as calls for reflexivity lead anthropology of all backgrounds to bring insights from their “homes.” Issues include the question of objectivity, the emicetic distinction, and the ethics of different kinds of anthropological research and the role of anthropologists in indigenous self-determination.

subject: ANTH
title: Communication and Culture
description: Anthropological introduction to communication; intercultural and interspecies comparisons; verbal and nonverbal. Ethnography of communication, discourse and structural analyses, ethnomethodology.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Magic, Witchcraft, and Religion
description: Cults, legends, millennial movements, myths, possession, rituals, sacred healing, shamanism, sorcery, spirits, symbolism, witchcraft, and other forms of religious and symbolic expression and experience, from small scale to highly urban societies.

subject: ANTH
title: Social and Cultural Change
description: Various approaches to examples of social and cultural change in non-literate societies; evolution, diffusion, acculturation, revolution, etc. Historical features and social processes of colonialism.

subject: ANTH
title: Islands as Model Systems: Human Biogeography of the Pacific
description: Applying the concept of islands as “model systems;” explores the impacts of human populations on the natural ecosystems of oceanic islands, and the reciprocal effects of anthropogenic change on human cultures.

subject: ANTH
title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
description: Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization.

subject: ANTH
title: Food, Health, and Society
description: How human groups identify, collect, create, and transform foods; how they shape those into dietary behaviors, and the influence of those behaviors on health.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of the Body
description: Exploration of the history and development of theories of the body via topics such as phenomenology, perception, bodily rituals, gender, sex, race, colonialism, power, pain, medicalization, immunology, reproductive health and cyborgs.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Consumer Cultures
description: Examines the practices and meanings of consumption in the contemporary world. Topics include social class, branding, fandom, global-local nexus.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Crops/Food Systems
description: Schemes for managing sequences and combinations of crops and crop production activities. Ecosystem and social determinants. Multiple cropping. Analysis of alternative cropping systems.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only

subject: ANTH
title: The Agriculture of Identity: Food and Farming in Anthropological Perspective
description: Exploration of agriculture from the perspective of anthropology, with a focus on alternatives to industrial agriculture, especially in the context of Hawai‘i. Readings include academic writing and also literary non-fiction and journalism.

subject: ANTH
title: Globalization and Identity in the Himalayas
description: Examines the influence of local culture and global flows on identity formation in the Himalayan region. Topics include: Hindu caste and gender, constructions of ethnicity, Tibetans and tourists, Sherpas and mountaineers, development ideologies, and consumerism.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Buddhism
description: Selected aspects of national, regional and local manifestations of Buddhism are explored through the perspective of anthropology with an emphasis on the daily lives of monks, nuns and lay persons in their socio-cultural contexts.

subject: ANTH
title: Spiritual Ecology
description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of the relationships between religions, environment and environmentalism. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Sacred Places
description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of sites which societies recognize as sacred and their cultural, ecological and conservation aspects.

subject: ANTH
title: Southeast Asian Cultures
description: Cultures of Southeast Asia from hunting and gathering groups to high civilizations; kinship, economic, political, and religious systems; recent developments.

subject: ANTH
title: Polynesian Cultures
description: Analysis of Polynesian cultures from their origins to contemporary states.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Melanesia
description: Close study of cultures of Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, and Fiji through anthropological ethnography.

subject: ANTH
title: Decolonizing Anthropology Through South Africa
description: Decolonizing approaches to anthropology explored through the archaeology and ethnography of South Africa. Topics include race, inequality, nationalism, migration, heritage, and violence. (Alt years)

subject: ANTH
title: Forensic Anthropology
description: Application of physical anthropology to problems in human identification. Determination of age, sex, ancestry, etc., of the skeleton and preparation of reports for legal medicine.

subject: ANTH
title: Extinctions
description: An extraordinary number of plants and animals have gone extinct. Delves deeply into the primary literature that focuses on extinction and conservation from the beginning of the earth to the present day.

subject: ANTH
title: Asian Paleoanthropology
description: Neogene-Quaternary paleoenvironmental reconstructions; human evolution in East Asia during the Pleistocene; Out of Africa I; modern human origins.

subject: ANTH
title: Southeast Asian Archaeology
description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania.

subject: ANTH
title: East Asian Archaeology
description: Prehistory and protohistory of China, Japan, and Korea from earliest human occupation to historic times. Geographical emphasis may vary between China and Japan/Korea.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Global Health and Development
description: Seminar explores the definitions and histories of development and global health initiatives in developing countries from an anthropological perspective. Reading materials include scholarly and popular texts that propose and critique solutions to global poverty. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Hawaiian Archaeology
description: Archaeological perspective in Hawai‘i’s past; origins of Hawaiians; early settlement and culture change; settlement patterns and material culture; historic sites preservation.

subject: ANTH
title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
description: Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Quantitative Archaeology
description: Combined lecture/lab. Introduction to the basic principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data. Exploratory data analysis approach. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Biomedicine and Culture
description: Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies and practices of modern medicine.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, 152, or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Field Mapping
description: Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Ceramic Analysis in Archaeology
description: Concepts, methods, and approaches used in the analysis of ancient pottery. Emphasis placed on ceramic technology, stylistic analysis.

subject: ANTH
title: Lithic Artifact Assemblage Analysis
description: Combined lecture/lab on the manufacture and analysis of stone tools. Students work with experimental collections and engage in stone tool production. The ways in which lithics enlighten us about past human behavior are discussed.

subject: ANTH
title: Faunal Analysis in Archaeology
description: Analysis of archaeologically recovered faunal collections with emphasis on identification and interpretation of nonhuman vertebrate remains.

subject: ANTH
title: Spatial Analysis in Archaeology
description: Lecture/lab. Introduction to the use of Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and spatial statistics in archaeological research. Topics include: map creation; spatial database management; spatial analysis; image processing, data reporting; and data display. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Anthropology
description: The application of anthropological methods and concepts to solving practical human problems such as homelessness, domestic violence, maternal morbidity, conflict over resources, and the loss of indigenous languages. Includes a significant service-learning component.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
description: Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature.

subject: ANTH
title: Japanese Culture and Behavior
description: Sociocultural factors in Japanese behavior. Social structure; traditional institutions

subject: ANTH
title: Japanese Popular Culture
description: Explores contemporary Japanese popular culture through themes such as gender, consumerism, globalization and nostalgia. Rather than a survey of popular culture genres, the course is organized thematically around issues and problematics.

subject: ANTH
title: Pre-European Hawai‘i
description: Pre-European society and culture from an anthropological viewpoint.

subject: ANTH
title: Peoples of Hawai‘i
description: Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawai‘i using anthropological and ethnic studies approaches. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values of peoples indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia.
prereq_raw: junior standing or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Okinawa and Its Diaspora
description: Explores the ties of identity that exist within and between Okinawa and its diasporic populations.

subject: ANTH
title: Chinese Culture: Ethnography
description: Critical interpretations of ethnographic and biographic texts depicting individual and family lives in different socioeconomic circumstances, geographical regions, and historical periods of modern China.

subject: ANTH
title: History of Anthropology
description: Development of anthropological ideas, focusing on theoretical issues concerning culture, society, and human nature. Required of majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Special Topics in Southeast Asian Art History: Monuments and Nationalism in Southeast Asia
description: Focused study of particular periods, regions and critical themes in Southeast Asian art and architectural history. Monuments and nationalism in Southeast Asia.

subject: ANTH
title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
description: Literature, methodology, ethics and project design of oral history research. Students develop and execute an oral history project.

subject: ANTH
title: Senior Thesis I
description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. First semester of a two-semester sequence with 496. May be taken concurrently with 496. Optional for majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Senior Thesis II
description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. Second semester of a two-semester sequence with 495. May be taken concurrently with 495. Optional for majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnology
description: Survey, in historical perspective, of theory in social and cultural anthropology, from the origin of anthropology to 1976. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Linguistic Anthropology
description: Investigation of mutual influences of linguistic theory and methodology and anthropological theory and methodology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology
description: Development of critical and analytical skills in assessment of archaeological literature; emphasis on the science, theory, explanation, and paradigms that comprise archaeology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Biological Anthropology Core
description: Human evolution and human variability in extant and previously existing populations; emphasis on history of physical anthropology, evolutionary systematics, primate biology and behavior, paleontology, anthropological genetics, climatic adaptation, growth, and nutrition. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Discursive Practices
description: Emphasizes linguistic, semantic, and interactional aspects of culture, exploring ways that discourse constructs social action and social realities, examining processes by which culture is produced as meaningful behavior in actual situations.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Infectious Disease
description: The role of human behavior, including its social and cultural determinants, in understanding the distribution of infectious diseases and in shaping preventive and therapeutic strategies.

subject: ANTH
title: History and Memory
description: History and collective memory as culturally formed and politically contested realities. The role of narrative, ritual, and media technologies in shaping representations of the past.

subject: ANTH
title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawai‘i, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation.

subject: ANTH
title: Contemporary Anthropological Theory
description: Graduate seminar that examines the history of theory in sociocultural anthropology from 1960 to present. Designed to be taken in sequence after 601.

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology
description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.

subject: ANTH
title: Advanced Pacific Islands Archaeology
description: Advanced theoretical and methodological examination of archaeological research in Oceania, a region including the islands of Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Methods and Theory in Archaeology
description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

subject: ANTH
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawai‘i and the region. (Alt. years: spring only) .

subject: ANTH
title: Decolonizing Anthropology
description: Decolonizing approaches to anthropology with a focus on South Africa and its relevance for the Pacific and U.S. Topics include race, inequality, nationalism, migration, heritage, and violence.

subject: ANTH
title: Advances in Extinctions
description: To delve deeply into the primary literature that focuses on the subjects of extinction and conservation broadly speaking, with particular emphasis on the 6 mass extinction events, including the Anthropocene. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Paleoanthropology of Asia
description: Survey of the Asian paleoanthropological record, particularly in its paleoenvironmental setting; Out of Africa I; modern human origins.
prereq_raw: graduate standing and relevant background in anthropology or related field

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Perspectives on Southeast Asia
description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia, and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, india, Australia, and Oceania.
prereq_raw: background in archaeology or Southeast Asian history or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Global Aid
description: Examines ideologies of development, humanitarian, and global health interventions from an anthropological perspective. Explores the disjuncture between discourses that portrays global aid as easing suffering and those that accuse it of maintaining relationships of domination. (Alt. years: spring)

subject: ANTH
title: Advanced Hawaiian Archaeology
description: An advanced theoretical and methodological examination of past and current archaeological research in the Hawaiian Islands.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Data Analysis
description: Advanced introduction to the fundamental principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data. (Alt. years)

subject: ANTH
title: Biomedicine and Culture
description: Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies, and practices of modern medicine.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology Field Methods
description: (5 7-hr Lab) Laboratory and field training in the principles and practice of methods of archaeology—survey, mapping, excavation, conservation.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to 12 credits

subject: ANTH
title: Advanced Household Archaeology
description: Focus on the differences in the composition, activities, roles, and relationships to be observed archaeologically between the households that comprised ancient communities, and how these differences inform us about the dynamics of social change. Graduate students only.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Archaeology Practicum
description: Applies course work in archaeology to handson activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. MA track in Applied Archaeology students only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to 12 credits

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Method and Theory in Hawaiian Archaeology
description: Graduate seminar focused on method and theory in the practice of applied archaeology in Hawai‘i.

subject: ANTH
title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures. Graduate students only or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Cultural Anthropology
description: Theory, methods, and results of application of cultural anthropological concepts to practical problems. Graduate students only.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Cultural Anthropology Practicum
description: Applies course work in cultural anthropology to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Graduate students only.

subject: ANTH
title: Professional Skills Develop in Anthropology
description: Seminar prepares graduate students for entry into profession, including employment opportunities, research, presentations, ethics and outreach. Required of all Plan B students.

subject: ANTH
title: Directed Reading or Research
repeatable_raw: Repeatable nine times, up to 12 credits

subject: ANTH
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable nine times, up to 12 credits

subject: ANTH
title: Seminar in Research Methods in Cultural Anthropology
description: Ethnographic research methods. Introduction to the approaches and techniques of participatory research, including the collection, analysis, and interpretation of social and cultural data. Politics and ethics of research practice.
prereq_raw: graduate standing in anthropology or consent

subject: ANTH
title: Seminar in Research Design and Proposal Writing
description: Research design and proposal writing. For students preparing for advanced research.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Japan
description: Japan examined through three dimensions of cultural anthropology: cultural/symbolic, social/organizational, and individual/psychological. Selected topics analyzed and interpreted in terms of conjunctions of these dimensions.

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Research Seminar
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.

subject: ANTH
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: COM
title: Introduction to Communication
description: An overview of communication emphasizing intercultural, organizational and international communication and media arts with introduction to multimedia, ICTs, and public relations perspectives.

subject: COM
title: Media Arts
description: Combined lecture-discussion on theories and criticism of visual media, covering aesthetic development and delivery through multimedia and cinematic principles.

subject: COM
title: Communication and Communities
description: Combined lecture-discussion on communication within organizational communities and between organizations and their communities with attention to intercultural issues in local, global, and online interactions.

subject: COM
title: Communicating Sustainability
description: Application of scientific communication theory, strategic communication, and multimedia techniques to select issues of environmental sustainability.

subject: COM
title: Information and Communication Technology Concepts
description: Combined lecture discussion on basic technical concepts related to ICTs embedded in sociocultural context.

subject: COM
title: Techniques of Video and Digital Cinema
description: Orientation to techniques of production. Emphasis on history, language, and theory of the creative process and application to media productions.

subject: COM
title: Media Arts Techniques
description: Combined lecture-lab providing an orientation to, and examination of, procedures and techniques of media arts production. Emphasis on new media literacy, human-computer interaction, and basic electronic media tools for communication design.

subject: COM
title: Public Relations Writing
description: Enhance students’ professional writing skills in the contemporary public relations field and equip students with the foundations of essential techniques for persuasive communication. COM majors or consent.

subject: COM
title: Intercultural Communication
description: Problems and opportunities of communication in a variety of intercultural contexts. Focus on theory, research, and managing intercultural effectiveness.

subject: COM
title: Information Technology and Health Communication
description: Combined lecture-discussion on the application of ICTs for health communication from the aspect of technologies, systems, services, and policies.

subject: COM
title: Computer-Mediated Communication
description: Combine lecture-discussion on the evolution of computer-mediated communication from the 1970s to current day. Examines the development of online communities, technologies, and their networked online and offline social practices. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Digital Cultures
description: Introduction to the social, cultural, and ethical implications of information and communication technologies by studying new and emerging media including games, interactive media, and virtual worlds. COM majors or consent.

subject: COM
title: Esports and Society
description: Introduction to professional and collegiate esports (electronic sports) in global context, including theories related to leisure and gaming, and current academic and industry developments. No previous technical or gaming experience is required.

subject: COM
title: Media Communications and Conflict
description: Mass communication and conflict; deals with understanding the role of news media in influencing conflict, and introduces students to conflict-sensitive communications working to assist in resolving conflicts. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: COM
title: Emerging Topics in Communication
description: Emerging communication topics of interest to faculty and students.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time on different topics, up to six credits

subject: COM
title: Survey of Inquiry Methods in Communication
description: Exploration of quantitative and qualitative research methods commonly used in communication studies and related professional work.

subject: COM
title: Communication in Multicultural Organizations
description: Cultural diversity in multicultural and multinational organizations is examined regarding communication-related aspects of working life. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Public Relations Strategies
description: Exploring the practice and effects of public relations. Strategic management functions, including use of communication technologies, communication with diverse publics, ethics and social responsibility will be emphasized. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Public Relations Campaigns
description: Synthesizing and applying the principles and techniques of public relations to create comprehensive campaigns.

subject: COM
title: Filming Social Change
description: Introduction to visual documentary theory and methods. Basic instruction in using digital video technology and hands-on production to tell visual stories and examine social issues related to diverse peoples, cultures, and communities through video projects.
prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent

subject: COM
title: Environmental Storytelling Through an Indigenous Lens
description: Through media arts storytelling techniques, will focus on reframing perspectives and creativity from an Indigenous lens to communicate environmental-centric stories geared toward improving our communities’ quality of life. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Studio Production
description: Studio production ranging from three-camera studio production to broadcast and magazine show formats to on-line web production. Fundamental knowledge of lighting, sound, blocking, and equipment competency.

subject: COM
title: Social Media
description: Combined lecture-discussion on the sociocultural, political, psychological, historical and policy dimensions of social media for societies past, contemporary, and future. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Video Scriptwriting
description: Application of communication theory to creating and revising commercial and dramatic script material for video production.

subject: COM
title: Media Effects
description: Social, political, economic, and cultural effects of mediated communication are examined to understand their impact on human behavior. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Telecommunication in the Pacific Hemisphere
description: Development of international telecommunication, with special emphasis on the wireless communication, the internet, and emerging technologies. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Communication and Gender
description: Theories and issues related to gender and communication applied to organizational, intercultural, and technology mediated communication. COM majors only or consent.

subject: COM
title: Building Communication Theory
description: Major theories of communication in terms of requirements for a theory, theory development, associated research, and application.
prereq_raw: COM major and junior standing, or consent

subject: COM
title: Special Topics in Communication
description: Topics of relevance to the focus areas of Communication in Communities, Media Arts, and ICTs & Policy; taught by regular and visiting faculty. COM majors only or consent.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable on different topics to six credit hours

subject: COM
title: Political Communication in the Digital Era
description: An examination of how various aspects of digital media platforms, such as affordances and communication processes impact political outcomes. COM majors or consent.

subject: COM
title: Capstone in Media Arts Design and Development
description: Design, development, and evaluation of computer-based media arts communication. Emphasizes authoring and production of such media elements as video, audio, and graphics.

subject: COM
title: Capstone in Communication in Communities
description: Synthesize knowledge, apply research findings in service to community, and develop proposal for intervention or campaign through assignments that emphasize the development of writing skills.
prereq_raw: 310 and 320 and 330; and 340 or 421; or consent

subject: COM
title: Capstone Project in ICTs and Policy
description: Written research or media project focused on specific ICT and policy problems, including social media, digital games, and the internet.
prereq_raw: 310 and 320 and 330; and 432 or 438; or consent

subject: COM
title: Communication Seminar
description: Application of theoretic and methodological criteria to researchable questions. Topics will vary.

subject: COM
title: Communicating Creativity
description: The role of communication in fostering or inhibiting creativity. Exploration of theoretical bases for shared scientific or artistic creativity in communication research. COM major or consent.
prereq_raw: 201 and senior standing, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: COM
title: Senior Thesis Project
description: Completion of the thesis project appropriate to the selected focus area within the context of a seminar. Emphasis on ongoing process of writing, editing, review, and revision.
prereq_raw: COM major and senior standing, or consent

subject: COM
title: (Alpha) Communication Internship
description: Application of communication skills and knowledge. Under faculty supervision, interns participate in operations of an organization and analyze communication processes and effects; (B) community setting; (C) Communication program activity. Maximum of three credits per semester; six credits total toward major; each alpha

subject: COM
title: Special Problems
description: Independent study of selected topics under faculty supervision.
prereq_raw: COM major and junior standing, or consent

subject: COM
title: Communication Theories
description: Systematic study of major theories of communication and current status of communication research.

subject: COM
title: Communication Inquiry
description: Introduction to inquiry and the array of quantitative and qualitative research methods commonly used in communication.

subject: COM
title: Strategic Organizational Communication
description: Theories, concepts, and applications of strategic communication and public relations to achieve organizational goals.

subject: COM
title: Information and Communication Technologies
description: Information and communication technologies, structures, processes, and networks as an area of research and study in the social sciences.

subject: COM
title: Social Media
description: Systematic study from a social science perspective of current and emerging social media. Attention to user needs and impact.

subject: COM
title: Intercultural Communication
description: Problems and opportunities of intercultural communication from theory and research, consulting and training, and policy and program perspectives.

subject: COM
title: Global Communication and Journalism
description: Analysis of the emerging global media landscape as digital technologies enable the sharing of news, information, and commentary across geographical and cultural borders. Focuses on causes, characteristics, and consequences.

subject: COM
title: Digital Storytelling
description: Focus on development of narrative-based creative activities in all mediums (text, audio, video, etc.) within communication contexts, i.e., journalism, film, public relations, etc.

subject: COM
title: Intervention in Multicultural Organizations
description: Describes the array of communication-related intervention programs designed to enhance effectiveness in multicultural organizations at home and abroad.

subject: COM
title: Media Effects
description: Critical examination of major media effects theories and topic areas. Must be enrolled in one of the following majors: COM, CIS majors only.

subject: COM
title: Public Diplomacy and Communication
description: Analysis of the emerging trends in international relations from communication and public relations perspectives. Focuses on factors, characteristics, and processes.

subject: COM
title: ICT Policy and Planning
description: Processes and methods of planning appropriate to the information and communication sectors, including future economic, social, political, technical, and environmental perspectives.

subject: COM
title: Communication Topics
description: Coverage in depth of some area of theory and research.

subject: COM
title: Communication Research Seminar
description: General research seminar in communication. In-depth coverage of specific research methods to develop, refine, or interpret graduate students’ thesis or dissertation projects. Graduate students only.
prereq_raw: 611 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: COM
title: Communication Practicum
description: Supervised work experience, study of an organization, and career planning. Required of Plan B students in the main communication program.

subject: COM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Individual reading and/or research.

subject: COMG
title: Everyday Communication with Numbers: A Survival Guide
description: Understanding, communicating, and evaluating quantitative information in everyday contexts. Topics include describing and interpreting data, basic statistics, and evaluating the validity of results.

subject: COMG
title: Personal and Public Speech
description: Develops communication skills necessary to function effectively in today’s society. Students will enhance their communication skills in one-on-one situations, public speaking, and small group situations. Ideal for new majors and non-majors.

subject: COMG
title: Introduction to Nonverbal Communication
description: Beginning course on the fundamental components of nonverbal communication. Aspects of body movements, facial expressions, eye behavior, physical appearance, voice, touch, space, smell, time, and environmental features will be examined in a lecture/discussion format. Extensive practice in skills.

subject: COMG
title: Introduction to Interpersonal Communication
description: Introduction to basic principles of interaction between two people. Emphasis is on enhancement of skills in a variety of interpersonal contexts.

subject: COMG
title: Multicultural Communication Skills
description: Expose students to practical skills needed for effective intercultural communication. Offer guidelines for improvement in diverse cultural settings such as business, education, counseling, and healthcare.

subject: COMG
title: Principles of Effective Public Speaking
description: Combined lecture/laboratory providing extensive practice in preparing and presenting effective public speeches with special emphasis on organization, outlining, audience analysis, analytical reasoning, and delivery skills.

subject: COMG
title: Interviewing
description: Principles and practice; training in informational, persuasive, employment, appraisal, and research interviewing.

subject: COMG
title: Introduction to Communicological Theories
description: Introduction to the theoretical perspectives that are the foundations of the communication discipline. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Research Methods
description: Introduction to methods of inquiry in the field of communication. Topics include research design and problem formulation, sampling, analytic and observational techniques, and data interpretation. Ethical issues in communication research will be discussed. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Instructional Communication
description: Analysis of and practice in using models of communication in the classroom. Extends application of oral communication skills to various instructional and teaching contexts. Emphasis on organization, preparation, and delivery.

subject: COMG
title: Professional Presentations
description: Extends application of public speaking skills to professional contexts: group sales, press conferences, and corporate annual reports. Emphasis on organization, preparation, and delivery.

subject: COMG
title: Group Decision-Making and Leadership
description: Study of decision-making within the small group. Effects of organization, leadership, membership, and goals on achieving group purposes. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Argumentation and Debate
description: Adapting communication theory to forensic strategies for social action. Practice in formal argument. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits

subject: COMG
title: Leadership and Organizational Communication
description: Principles and practices of organizational communication and its relationship to networks, leadership, power, conflict, cultures, and other contemporary views of organizational work, change, and development. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Persuasion
description: Theories, concepts, strategies, and processes of persuasion and social influence in contemporary society. Focus on analyzing, developing, and resisting persuasive messages. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Creating Understanding
description: Introduction to theory and research on human communication, comprehension, and creation of understanding. Discussion of information and message processing theories. Topics include prediction, inference-making, communication systems, and deception. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Family Communication
description: Focuses on the role of interaction patterns (both constructive and destructive) in the evolution of family communications. The impact of family dynamics upon these interaction patterns is given equal attention. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Interpersonal Relations
description: Theory and research on the development, maintenance, and termination of interpersonal relationships. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Culture and Communication
description: Survey of major factors affecting interpersonal communication between members of different cultures. Emphasis upon interaction between U.S. and Asian-Pacific peoples. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Special Topics in Culture and Communication
description: Contemporary research and theory on intercultural communication. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Interrogation and Interviewing
description: Survey of theory and research on the communicative demands of obtaining reliable information from others. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Evolution and Human Communication
description: Analysis of the role of human communication in mate attraction, intrasexual competition, cooperation, family dynamics, and coalition formation; discussion on the biological function of language, laughter, yawning, and emotion expressions. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Research on Communication Behavior
description: Survey of research on communication behavior. Verbal and nonverbal data collection; analysis of research data. Students design and implement a research project.

subject: COMG
title: Internship
description: Analysis and application of communication knowledge and behaviors in organizational settings.

subject: COMG
title: Social Identity and Intergroup Communication
description: Surveys theory and research on communication between members of different social groups, highlighting how communication influences and is influenced by social identity. Applies concepts to intergenerational, health, family, educational, multilingual, and computer-mediated contexts. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Political Communication
description: Survey of interpersonal and mass communication theories in the political context. Topics may include communication in public opinion processes, elections, debates, political campaigning and advertising. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Conflict Management
description: Examination of the theories, assumptions, practices, models, and techniques of managing interpersonal conflicts. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Science Communication
description: Introduction to principles for communicating science information effectively to a variety of audiences including the general public, policy makers, and profession peers. Application of these principles to create written and oral science communication products. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Human Communication and Technology
description: Analysis of evolving communicative exchanges in the Internet age including how people communicate with computer technology: focus on personal, interpersonal, and cultural effects associated with technology use.

subject: COMG
title: Theories and Research in Strategic Communication
description: An in-depth overview of theories related to strategic communication and scientific approaches to attitude formation and changes. Junior standing or higher.

subject: COMG
title: Nonverbal Communication
description: Understanding communication beyond the words themselves. Review of theory and research on gestures, facial expressions, touch, personal space, and physical appearance. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Verbal Communication
description: Roles of language in human communication and social relationships; language variation, change, and social consequences. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Deceptive Communication
description: Survey of major social scientific theories, concepts, and research findings on deceptive communication, in a lecture/discussion format. Emphasis is on how people create deceptive messages, induce deception, and strategies used to detect deception. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Relational Management
description: Survey and critical discussion of current theory and research in relational management. Focus on written analysis of the role of communication in the initiation, maintenance, decline, and dissolution of different types of relationships.

subject: COMG
title: Communicating Social Support
description: Survey of major theories, concepts, research, and application regarding communication and social support in interpersonal relationships.

subject: COMG
title: Teaching Speech
description: For communicology majors who lead, under supervision, a freshman seminar section of communicology.

subject: COMG
title: Health Communication
description: Develop understanding of the process through which communication influences health outcomes, and learn how to design effective health communication programs using theory and research. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

subject: COMG
title: Directed Reading
prereq_raw: consent of department chair and instructor

subject: COMG
title: Master’s Plan B/C Studies
description: Enrollment for degree completion.
prereq_raw: master’s Plan B candidate and consent
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits

subject: COMG
title: Theories in Communicology
description: Major theoretical foundations; humanistic and social scientific perspectives. Examination of the research and the development of different models of human communication.

subject: COMG
title: Research Methods in Communicology
description: Design and analysis of quantitative research in communicology. Focus on measurement issues, research design, descriptive and inferential statistics.

subject: COMG
title: Advanced Research Methods in Communicology
description: Advanced focus on survey, laboratory, and field study design, data collection, and data analysis. Emphasis on control of variance through design and statistical analysis. Appropriate preparation for graduate theses and dissertations.

subject: COMG
title: Practicum for Instructional Communication
description: Combined seminar and lecture/ discussion format on techniques and procedures for teaching communication skills and their related components in a laboratory setting.

subject: COMG
title: Business Communication
description: Analysis of communication issues in business through discussion of verbal/nonverbal messages, interpersonal relationships, conflict, and persuasion. Focus on interviewing, group communication, and public speaking skills.

subject: COMG
title: Persuasion and Social Influence
description: Theories of persuasion and resistance to persuasion; assessment of attitudes and measurement of change.

subject: COMG
title: Creating Understanding
description: Theory and research on human communication, social cognition, comprehension, and creation of understanding. Discussion of information and message processing theories, metacognition, prediction, inference-making, and communication systems.

subject: COMG
title: Relational Communication
description: Major models and theories of interpersonal communication; research on interpersonal relationships; interaction and functions of human communication.

subject: COMG
title: Foundations of Intercultural Communication
description: Major models, theories, and concepts of intercultural communication; basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to intercultural communication; research on intercultural communication. Graduate standing only.

subject: COMG
title: Directed Research
description: Only three credits can count toward degree.

subject: COMG
title: Thesis Research
description: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

subject: COMG
title: Approaches to Instructional Communication
description: Seminar on communication theories and models in instructional environment; emphasis on message processing, classroom dynamics, cognitive and metacognitive processes associated with learning, and learning assessment.

subject: COMG
title: Research in Intergroup Communication
description: Theory, concepts, research, and application of communication processes between members of different social groups.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Special Topics in Communicology
description: Substantive areas in communication that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addresed in other COMG courses. Topics vary each semester. Content to be announced.
prereq_raw: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B), or consent

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Persuasion and Influence
description: Contemporary research in persuasion and influence.
prereq_raw: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent

subject: COMG
title: Issues in Message Processing
description: Contemporary research in verbal and nonverbal message processing.
prereq_raw: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Relational Communication
description: Contemporary research in interpersonal relations.
prereq_raw: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent

subject: COMG
title: Research on Intercultural Communication
description: Functional approach to the study of communication in intercultural settings. Examination of culture-based variables and their impact on social influence, relational management, and message processing.
prereq_raw: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent

subject: COMG
title: Artificial Intelligence and Communication
description: Comprehensive understanding of the role and function of computer technology (including. A.I.) within the field of communication. Basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to semi-intelligent artifacts as information source or receiver. COMG majors or consent. Graduate students only.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Health Communication Research
description: Contemporary interpersonal and/ or public communication issues in health communication research. Topics include communication functions such as information management, interpersonal influence, relational management, emotional management, social influence.

subject: CUL
title: Faculty Seminar Series
description: Seminar consists of a series of presentations by certificate faculty on topics of ongoing research. Presentations will open current debates about theory and method in cultural studies.

subject: CUL
title: International Cultural Studies: History and Theory
description: Seminar on the history and theory of interdisciplinary cultural studies. The politics of culture are examined in comparative perspective, focusing on their significance for identity formation, intercultural relations, and global flows of images, people and capital. Approaches to the study of media and popular culture are taken up in terms of their relevance for contemporary issues, especially in Hawai‘i and the Asia/Pacific/U.S. region.

subject: CUL
title: International Cultural Studies: Research Project
description: Directed reading and research culminating in a project that engages issues in international cultural studies. Types of projects include scholarly essays, community-based projects, performances or exhibitions. Written statement of purpose and selfevaluation required.

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Economics
description: One semester survey of the principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics to enable students in all disciplines to understand current economic events.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Microeconomics
description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: An introduction to macroeconomics–the study of the overall economy. Topics include the determination of national income, causes and effects of inflation, unemployment, and income inequality; causes and consequences of international differences in economic growth; sources of business cycle expansions and contractions; role of government policy in stabilizing the economy and promoting long-term growth; financial markets and monetary policy; taxes, spending, consequences of budget deficits, determination of trade imbalances, exchange rate fluctuations, and balance of payment crises.

subject: ECON
title: Data Analysis and Visualization
description: Develops basic techniques of data analysis and visualization. Introduces sources of economic data; methods of preparing data from various file/data formats for analysis; methods of visualization: bubble plots, scatterplot matrices, heatmaps, hexbins, rug plots, etc.

subject: ECON
title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts used to study the overall macroeconomy and policies that affect it. Study the determinants of national income and long-run growth; causes and consequences of unemployment, inflation, and business cycle fluctuations; determination of foreign exchange rates and current account imbalances, and the role of government policy in various settings.

subject: ECON
title: Intermediate Microeconomics
description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts of microeconomic theory. Learn to use economic reasoning to understand the social consequences of decisions made by individual consumers, producers, and governments. Analyze the nature of market outcomes under alternative market structures, and further discuss possible welfare-improving government policies when markets fail to be efficient. Special attention is paid to the analysis of strategic behavior and markets with public goods and externalities.

subject: ECON
title: The Economy of Hawai‘i
description: Descriptive understanding of the history of development of Hawai‘i’s economy; current economic problems; future prospects. Emphasizes the written communication of the intuition behind economic concepts in practice in Hawai‘i.

subject: ECON
title: The Japanese Economy
description: Analysis of Japan’s growth past and present. Does Japan’s economy look different in terms of its international trade structure, industrial structure, labor market, savings patterns, government policies, etc.? Does it matter?

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Tourism Economics
description: Examines tourism from an economic perspective. Topics include: the determinants of consumer demand for leisure travel, structure of competition among suppliers of tourism services, benefits and costs of tourism development to the host community, government’s role in the taxation, subsidy, regulation and protection of the tourism industry, tourism’s impact on the environment, and sustainable tourism development.

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Statistics
description: Basic elements; descriptive statistics, probability, inference, distributions, hypothesis testing, regression, and correlation analysis.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Global Climate Change
description: Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation.
prereq_raw: 120 or 130 or 131, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ECON
title: Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources.

subject: ECON
title: Financial Markets and Institutions
description: The determination of asset prices; the risk and term structure of interest rates; efficient markets hypothesis; risk management and financial derivatives, asymmetric information models of financial market structure, innovation, regulation and deregulation; and financial crises.

subject: ECON
title: Comparative Economic History
description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions.

subject: ECON
title: The History of Economic Thought
description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy. (Alt. years)

subject: ECON
title: Sustainable Development
description: Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawai‘i. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls.
prereq_raw: 120 or 130 or 131, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ECON
title: Network Economics
description: Fundamental questions about the connections in the social, economic, and technological worlds. Topics include: matching markets, traffic, financial and social networks; and the political and economic consequences of the internet and other large networks.

subject: ECON
title: Games and Economic Behavior
description: Introduces students to the study of strategic behavior with applications to economics, business, and public policy. Simple economic models of strategic decision making are used to analyze provision of public goods; competition, cooperation, and coordination among firms; bargaining between employers and labor unions; international trade negotiations; reputation as a competitive advantage, and others.

subject: ECON
title: Environmental Economics
description: Nature and causes of environmental degradation/economic solutions, with emphasis on relevant ethical issues and decision-making. Topics include air and water pollution, toxic waste, deforestation, soil erosion, biodiversity, global warming, and sustainable development.

subject: ECON
title: Seminar: Women and International Development
description: Women’s role, status, work and treatment in the Third World; economic development, changing work/family roles, and improvement/ deterioration in gender equity across the Third World; global feminization of poverty; efforts to promote gender equity. Open to non-majors.
prereq_raw: a 100 level economics course or any women’s studies course; or consent

subject: ECON
title: Trade Policy and Globalization
description: Political economy of the world trading system. Case studies of trade cooperation and conflict under the World Trade Organization and other institutions. Future challenges, including investment policies, environmental and labor standards.

subject: ECON
title: Internship for Economics
description: Economics majors and minors work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations. Students combine academic work with practical experience.

subject: ECON
title: Cooperative Education
description: Economics majors and minors, under the supervision of faculty members, work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations. The Econ Co-op integrates academics with practical work experience.

subject: ECON
title: Contemporary Topics in Economics
description: Economic analysis of current events. Topics announced each semester.

subject: ECON
title: Directed Reading
description: Economics majors and minors participate in faculty supervised reading of economic literature. Enables students to self-study topics not covered in the department’s scheduled course offerings.

subject: ECON
title: The Ocean Economy
description: Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection.

subject: ECON
title: Economic History of the United States
description: U.S. economy from colonial times: government policies, institutions, industries, financial markets, economic growth, economic crises.

subject: ECON
title: Global Economic Crisis and Recovery
description: Causes and consequences of financial and economic crises: crisis origins and global transmission; macroeconomic and regulatory policy responses; recovery challenges.

subject: ECON
title: Asian Economic Development
description: History and economic development. Resources, population, and income, saving, investment, and consumption patterns. Role of government and private enterprise.

subject: ECON
title: The Chinese Economy
description: The Chinese economy during the imperial and republican periods, under Mao, and into the present reform era, with a brief comparison to Taiwan and Hong Kong.

subject: ECON
title: Pacific Island Economies
description: Historical and current economic development of the Pacific islands (excluding Hawai‘i). Analysis of selected economic issues such as tourism, population growth, etc.

subject: ECON
title: Mathematical Economics
description: Mathematical techniques applied to theories of the consumer, the firm, markets. Linear programming, input-output analysis.

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Econometrics I: Data Exploration and Regression Analysis
description: Types of data, exploratory data analysis, generalizing from random samples, simple and multivariate regression, non-linear relationships, measurement error, extreme values, weights, correlated and heteroskedastic errors, instrumental variables, models for binary or discrete dependent variables.
prereq_raw: 321 or MATH 241 or BUS 310 or NREM 310 or (MATH 251A and NREM 203) or (MATH 371 and MATH 373) or (MATH 471 and MATH 472); or consent

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Econometrics II: Prediction and Causal Inference
description: Prediction types, error measures, training and test data, cross validation, machine learning, regression trees, random forests, boosting, classification, forecasting time series, modelbased versus design-based causality, potential outcomes framework, matching, difference-in-differences, panel data, synthetic controls.
prereq_raw: 425 (with a minimum grade of B- or better)

subject: ECON
title: Spreadsheet Modeling for Business and Economic Analysis
description: Introduction to quantitative decision-making methods for effective agribusiness management in resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, risk analysis, inventory, and forecasting. Emphasis on problem identification, model formulation and solution, and interpretation and presentation of results.
prereq_raw: 130 or NREM/SUST 220, and 321 or NREM 310; or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ECON
title: Labor Economics
description: Economic analysis of labor market. Investment in human capital, education, health, migration, etc.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Population
description: Determinants and consequences of growth and structure of human populations. Relationships between economic factors and fertility, population growth and economic growth.

subject: ECON
title: Health Economics
description: Private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; efficient production and utilization of services; models of hospital and physician behavior; optimal public policy.

subject: ECON
title: Monetary Theory and Policy
description: Micro-foundations and critical analysis of monetary and macroeconomic theory and policy. Topics include the causes and consequences of inflation, optimal monetary policy and international monetary systems, bank risk and insurance, and national debt and taxation.

subject: ECON
title: Development Economics
description: Theoretical foundation and empirical evidence for analyzing key issues facing today’s developing world. Topics include characteristics of underdeveloped economies, economic growth, structural change, poverty, inequality, education, population growth, foreign aid and financial sector.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Happiness
description: Topics covered include: measuring happiness, what individual and country characteristics contribute to individual well-being, what are the consequences of happiness on behavior, and whether happiness is a cause or an effect.

subject: ECON
title: Public Economics
description: Welfare economics, public expenditure and policy evaluation, public finance by debt and taxes.
