subject: ECON
title: State and Local Finance
description: Fiscal institutions, operations, and policy questions within state and local governments in U.S. grant programs and other links with central government.

subject: ECON
title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
description: Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources.

subject: ECON
title: International Trade and Welfare
description: Theory of international specialization and exchange; general equilibrium, tariffs, quotas, common markets.

subject: ECON
title: International Macroeconomics
description: The determination of output, price levels, exchange rates and the balance of payments for economies that are integrated with the global economy; theory and application to historical and/or contemporary policy issues.

subject: ECON
title: Industrial Organization
description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of contemporary topics in industrial organization. Uses economic theory to analyze important issues facing firms, and examines the practical challenges of empirical applications of theory.

subject: ECON
title: Law and Economics
description: Legal issues of property rights, contracts, torts, and crime. Efficiency of U.S. legal process. Economics of law enforcement, juries, prosecutors; evolution of legal rules.

subject: ECON
title: Land and Housing Economics
description: Microeconomics explains urban land and housing phenomena, and analyzes selected land and housing issues relevant to Honolulu.

subject: ECON
title: Contemporary Economic Issues
description: Economic analysis of current events. Topics announced each semester, e.g., environmental pollution, crime control, racial discrimination, traffic congestion.

subject: ECON
title: Advanced Directed Research
description: Economics majors and minors conduct research, under faculty supervision, on a topic of their choice.
prereq_raw: minimum GPA of 3.0 in economics and consent

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomics for Business and Policy Analysis
description: Theory of the consumer, firm, and market. Perfect competition and efficiency. Market power and firm strategy. Market efficiencies. Role of the government.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomics for Business and Policy Analysis
description: Topics on production, consumption, labor market, asset market, economic growth, and business cycles are discussed with emphasis on real-economy applications and policy analysis. Implications of monetary, fiscal, and international finance and economic policies are explored.

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomic Theory I
description: Theory of the firm: production, costs, duality; theory of the market: competition, monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition; theory of the consumer: preferences, expenditures, duality; expected utility theory.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomic Theory I
description: Neoclassical theory of real and monetary equilibrium, economics of J. M. Keynes, standard IS/LM models and aggregate demand/supply analysis in the closed and open economy, theory of rational expectations.

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomic Theory II
description: General equilibrium analysis: production, consumption and Walrasian equilibria; Pareto efficiency, fundamental theorems of welfare economics; externalities; public goods; game theory; information theory.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomic Theory II
description: Models of economic growth and fluctuations; stochastic and dynamic macroeconomic models; econometric testing of rational expectations models; theory of public debt; current topics in macroeconomic theory.

subject: ECON
title: Economic Development
description: Nature and causes of economic growth and structural change. Roles of macroeconomic policy and foreign trade.

subject: ECON
title: Economic Development Policy
description: Analysis of policies for the promotion of industrial and agricultural development. Project evaluation, industrial regulation, public administration, investment and capital market policies, land-use policies, trade policies, pricing, and stabilization.

subject: ECON
title: Economic Development of Japan
description: Analysis of growth from Meiji period to present. Problems of population change, capital formation, income distribution, industrial structure.

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomic Theory III
description: Game theory and strategic behavior. Economics of information and incentives principal-agent theory. Economic design. Applications include: theory of contracts; incentive compatible mechanism for provision of public goods; auction theory.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomic Theory III
description: Will equip students with the ability to understand, undertake, and critically evaluate theoretical and quantitative research in modern macroeconomics with a focus on the application of the search and matching methodology.

subject: ECON
title: Mathematics for Economics
description: Sets, functions, limits, convexity, continuity; constrained and unconstrained optimization; difference and differential equations; matrix algebra; simultaneous equations; comparative statics; Kuhn-Tucker theory; game theory; mathematical programming.

subject: ECON
title: Econometrics I
description: Review of probability, estimation, small sample and asymptotic properties. Bivariate and multiple regression and matrix algebra formulation. Regression diagnostics. Introduction to heteroskedastidity, autocorrelation, simultaneity, dichotomous variables, advanced topics.

subject: ECON
title: Econometrics II
description: Specification, statistical estimation, inference and forecasting of econometric models. Includes advanced topics for single-equation models, pooled models, qualitative dependent variables, simultaneous systems, distributed lags, and time series.

subject: ECON
title: Econometrics III
description: Will equip students with the ability to undertake, understand, and critically assess empirical research using state-of-the-at econometric methods.

subject: ECON
title: Disasters and Economic Policy
description: Economic analysis of disasters. The economics of prevention and mitigation, as well as post-disaster economic consequences and policy, will be examined. Graduate students only.

subject: ECON
title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options.
prereq_raw: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent

subject: ECON
title: Resource Economics
description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

subject: ECON
title: Environmental Resource Economics
description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development.

subject: ECON
title: Marine Resource Economics
description: Seminar on the economics of the marine environment. Topics include fisheries management, ocean recreation, shipping, and coral reef protection.

subject: ECON
title: Foundations of Public Policy
description: Microeconomic principles for expenditure and tax policies. Externalities, public goods, non-convexities, regulation; cost-benefit analysis, general equilibrium, shadow-pricing; rent-seeking, corruption; optimal taxation, incidence, excess burden; dynamic public finance, national debt, social security.

subject: ECON
title: Public Economics
description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of public-sector allocation. Adverse selection, moral hazard, networks, auctions, public choice and political mechanisms; tax and mandate incidence; economics of education and local public goods; social insurance programs.

subject: ECON
title: International Trade and Welfare
description: Classical and new theories of international trade: why nations trade, gains from trade, patterns of trade, and trade policy effects under perfect and imperfect competition. Empirical trade and other special topics.

subject: ECON
title: Advanced International Trade and Investment
description: Surveys theoretical and empirical research on topics such as regionalism and multilateralism, trade and wages, foreign direct investment and multinational firms, trade and the environment, and trade and economic growth.

subject: ECON
title: International Macroeconomics
description: Advanced international monetary and macroeconomic theory: balance of payments, output, price and exchange rate determination, international aspects of growth and economic fluctuations, alternative exchange rate regimes, international capital flows.

subject: ECON
title: Applied International Finance
description: Surveys empirical research in international macroeconomics, finance and econometric methods: including balance of payments adjustment, international equilibrium, international prices, interest rates and exchange rates, models of exchange rate determination, capital flows, balance of payments crises.

subject: ECON
title: Labor Economics and Policy
description: Supply of and demand for labor; implications for labor markets and unemployment level.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Population
description: Economic determinants and consequences of population change.

subject: ECON
title: Health Economics and Policy
description: Economic analysis of health-care policy; efficient design of health-care financing schemes; private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; provider behavior.

subject: ECON
title: Strategic Behavior and Experimental Economics
description: Experimental economics: methodology. Experimental game theory. Market experiments. Applications include: topics in industrial organization, provision of public goods, asset markets, auctions.

subject: ECON
title: Advanced Topics in Economics
description: Reflects interests of visiting and permanent faculty, focusing on specialized methods or topics in economics.

subject: ECON
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: ECON
title: Research Seminar
description: Selected issues emphasizing research techniques. Required for students who have passed the two theory qualifying exams and have not passed the comprehensive exam.

subject: ECON
title: MA Capstone Research
description: Student applies theoretical and quantitative techniques, critical thinking, and communicative skills to prepare a written and oral presentation of original research on a topic of his or her choice.

subject: ECON
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
description: Concepts and theories analyzing ethnic group experiences in relation to colonization, immigration, racism, and social class. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values rooted in the experiences of peoples indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia.

subject: ES
title: Race, Class, Gender in Popular Culture
description: Contemporary issues of race, class, and gender in popular culture (film, television, music, social media, sports, etc.). Introduction to critical media analysis and social science theories and methods.

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Relations
description: Race and ethnic relations in world perspective; social, economic, and political problems associated with perception, existence, and accommodation of these groups within the wider society.

subject: ES
title: Hawaiians
description: The sustainable social system, culture, spirituality, language, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians. Transformation of the sustainable Hawaiian social system by a capitalist economy. Resiliency, land issues, and Native Hawaiian quest for sovereign governance.

subject: ES
title: Filipinos in Diaspora
description: Introduction to Filipinos in diaspora. Topics include: race, empire, migration, representation, cultural production, identity formation, and decolonization.

subject: ES
title: Ethnic Identity
description: Individual and group problems of identity, identity conflict, culture conflict, inter-ethnic relations. Critical review of available material on Hawai‘i.

subject: ES
title: African American Experience I
description: Afrocentric perspective. Analysis of the black political/cultural diaspora, including ancient African kingdoms, the slavery experience, organized resistance, emancipation struggles, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

subject: ES
title: African American Experience II
description: Black sociopolitical perspectives of the Reconstruction period, Jim Crow, intellectual and cultural awakenings, civil rights movements, and contemporary issues as examined through students’ written analysis and creative projects.

subject: ES
title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
description: Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent

subject: ES
title: Ethnicity and Community: Hawai‘i
description: Site visits to museums, social welfare units, etc., as well as guest lecturers from the community including police, health, education.

subject: ES
title: Asian America
description: History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation.

subject: ES
title: Hawai‘i and the Pacific
description: Hawai‘i as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples.

subject: ES
title: Japanese in Hawai‘i
description: Issei roots in Japan; the role of Japanese in labor, politics, and business; sansei and perspectives on local identity and culture. The Japanese in light of changing economic, social, and political conditions in Hawai‘i today.

subject: ES
title: Power and Place: Chinatowns
description: Historical and contemporary experiences of Chinese in Hawai‘i and the U.S. continent with a focus on Chinatowns; urbanization; economic development, community organizing; comparative racialization.

subject: ES
title: Filipinos in Hawai‘i
description: Historical and contemporary experiences; immigration; traditional culture and values; plantation experience; labor organizing; development of Filipino community; racism; discrimination; and ethnic identity.

subject: ES
title: American Indian Experience
description: Provides a comprehensive look at the indigenous foundation of life and society in the Americas and elaborates on historical and contemporary importance of American Indian rights issues.

subject: ES
title: South Asian Migrants: Culture and Politics
description: Historical and contemporary experiences of South Asian migrants in North America, Pacific, Caribbean, and/or African diasporas; causes and patterns of migration, inter-ethnic relations policies; role of race, gender, culture in community, identity formation. Pre one ES or WGSS course in the 100, 200 or 300 level; or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ES
title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawai‘i
description: Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities.

subject: ES
title: The Sounds of Race and Inequality
description: Explore inequality as manifested and contested in silence, music, dialect, nature, voice, and acoustic space by listening through a matrix of race, ethnicity, gender, class, and sexualities. Combination of hands-on work and current scholarship.

subject: ES
title: Economic Change and Hawai‘i’s People
description: Hawai‘i’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy.

subject: ES
title: Immigration to Hawai‘i and U.S.
description: Historical overview: “push and pull factors”; effect of changing economy; experiences of various ethnic groups; problems of recent immigrants; immigration policies in the U.S. and Hawai‘i.

subject: ES
title: Pacific/Asian Women in Hawai‘i
description: Adaptive strategies of Hawaiian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Samoan, and Southeast Asian women in Hawai‘i; feminist anthropological and historical analysis.
prereq_raw: one ANTH, SOC, or WGSS course

subject: ES
title: Literatures of Hawai‘i
description: Writings of various ethnic groups in Hawai‘i, ancient to contemporary. Songs, stories, poetry, fiction, essays that illustrate the social history of Hawai‘i.
prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ES
title: Asian American Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of Asian American literature by writers from a variety of backgrounds.
prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: ES
title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics.

subject: ES
title: Issues of Diversity in Higher Education
description: Examines issues of diversity within higher education. Examines different dimensions of diversity including ethnicity, gender, national origin, age, and sexual orientation. Will utilize national and local case studies. Junior class standing or higher.

subject: ES
title: Fieldwork in Ethnic Studies
description: Supervision of individual student research projects pertinent to ethnic studies, including service learning, civic engagement, internship, oral history, or supervised practicum experience in teaching select ethnic studies courses.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable to total of 6 credit hours

subject: ES
title: Social Movements in Hawai‘i
description: Examines, through writing and collaboration, interethnic movement building among Native Hawaiian, other Pacific Islander, and Asian peoples of Hawai‘i through intersectional theories of social change to evaluate strategies to create just and sustainable futures.

subject: ES
title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
description: Historical and sociological studies of race and gender in U.S. society; grassroots feminist and racial/justice activism on the continent and in Hawai‘i.

subject: ES
title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
description: Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent

subject: ES
title: Change in the Pacific—Polynesia
description: Impact of cultural and physical change and their interrelationship.

subject: ES
title: Multiethnic Popular Culture: Hip Hop
description: Historical, social, cultural, and political aspects of the formation and development of Hip Hop culture in Hawai‘i and other Pacific islands. Special attention to the significance of Hip Hop in facilitating cultural interactions. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

subject: ES
title: Ethnic Studies in the Digital World
description: The digitally networked world mediates race and ethnicity–and vice-versa. We will challenge racism and discrimination manifested in social media, changing notions of identity and group belonging, ewaste, gaming, big data, and more.

subject: ES
title: Race, Class, and the Law
description: Historical context and implications of landmark court decisions and legal issues affecting social change in ethnic communities in Hawai‘i and the continental U.S.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

subject: ES
title: Women and Work
description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global.
prereq_raw: one 300-level ES or WGSS course, or SOC 300; or consent

subject: ES
title: American Ethnic and Race Relations
description: Surveys ethnic and race relations in the U.S. Focus on historical conflicts and critical issues such as racism, immigration, affirmative action, changing economic structures, and the role of government.

subject: ES
title: Mixed Race Identities, Multiracial Experiences
description: Critically examines historical and contemporary issues surrounding mixed race identities and experiences through themes that resonate in localized contexts within the continental U.S. and Oceania.
prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent

subject: ES
title: Filming Social Change
description: Introduction to visual documentary theory and methods. Basic instruction in using digital video technology and hands-on production to tell visual stories and examine social issues related to diverse peoples, cultures, and communities through video projects.
prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent

subject: ES
title: Contemporary Diasporas in Comparative Perspective
description: Compares the circumstances under which contemporary Asian, Pacific Islander, or African migrants form diasporas across the globe; focus on a particular ethnic group to examine its site-specific experiences.

subject: ES
title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered.

subject: ES
title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawai‘i
description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor

children.text: at least one course in WGSS

subject: ES
title: Raciolinguistics
description: Theory and applications of critical race studies, ethnic studies, and linguistic anthropology as they pertain to the science of language, language behavior, language attitudes, and language in the public sphere.

subject: ES
title: (Alpha) Topics in Comparative Ethnic Conflict
description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C). ((C) Cross-listed as SUST 455)

subject: ES
title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawai‘i
description: The historical and contemporary social processes involved in inter-ethnic relations in Hawai‘i.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent

subject: ES
title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151, WGSS 175, WGSS 176, or WGSS 202; or consent

subject: ES
title: Global Ethnic Conflict
description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

subject: ES
title: Latinx Experience in Hawai‘i
description: Examines historical, socio-cultural, and contemporary Latinx presence; relations among Latinx, other immigrant, and Indigenous communities; causes and patterns of immigration; racism and discrimination; ethnicity and identity issues; struggles for justice.
prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent

subject: ES
title: Practices and Methods in Oceanic Ethnic Studies
description: Engagement with theoretical elements and qualitative and quantitative research methods of Oceanic Ethnic Studies: theories of class, race, indignity, migrancy, diaspora and political economy; community-based and participatory research methods.
prereq_raw: one upper division ES or SOCS course or consent

subject: ES
title: Peoples of Hawai‘i
description: Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawai‘i using anthropological and ethnic studies approaches. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values of peoples indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia.
prereq_raw: junior standing or consent. (Once a year)

subject: ES
title: Politics of Multiculturalism
description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent

subject: ES
title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
description: Literature, methodology, ethics and project design of oral history research. Students develop and execute an oral history project.

subject: ES
title: Hawai‘i’s Labor History
description: Conditions of work under varying political, social, and economic transformations in Hawai‘i; anthropological, sociological, and historic data.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

subject: ES
title: Special Topics in Ethnic Studies
description: Selected themes in ethnic studies exploring current issues and new topics; taught by regular and visiting faculty.

subject: GEO
title: The Natural Environment
description: Introduction to physical geography including weather, climate, vegetation, soils, geology, and landforms. Environmental issues and natural hazards. DP

subject: GEO
title: The Natural Environment Lab
description: A survey of field and laboratory methods commonly used by physical geographers.

subject: GEO
title: World Regional Geography
description: World’s major cultural regions; geographic aspects of contemporary economic, social, political conditions.

subject: GEO
title: Digital Earth
description: Cartographic representation and meaning in a digital age. Earth models, map projections, coordinate systems, scale, distance, and direction. Data types and transformations in graphic and digital representation. Manual, automated, and web-based map making and analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Geography and Contemporary Society
description: Elements of economic geography and resource management, population and urban geography; application to current problems of developed and underdeveloped worlds.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Climatology
description: Elements and controls of climate. World patterns of insolation, temperature, evaporation, precipitation, atmospheric circulation. Climatic classifications.
prereq_raw: 101 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Global Environmental Issues
description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment. (Once a year)

subject: GEO
title: General Geomorphology
description: Introduction to geomorphological concepts, process mechanics, and relationships between forms and processes. Emphasis on various subdisciplines of geomorphology: coastal hillslopes, fluvial, aeolean, and glacial.

subject: GEO
title: Water and Society
description: Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Biogeography
description: Introduction to ecosystem concept; environmental adaptations for energy and nutrient transfer; characteristics, dynamics, productivity, and distribution of principal vegetation communities. Human dominance.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Planning
description: Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawai‘i planning–research problems from a multidisciplinary approach.

subject: GEO
title: Tropical Agrarian Systems
description: Analysis of environmental potential and constraints and of spatial organization of economy and society of tropical agrarian systems. Emphasis on change through colonial and post-colonial periods.

subject: GEO
title: Economic Geography
description: Examines how factors of production like land, labor and capital; economic activities like consumption, trade, production, and investments; and institutions like state, markets, and corporations alter economic space.

subject: GEO
title: Globalization and Environment
description: Debates on globalization and development, population and resources; root causes of environmental degradation; impacts of globalization on environmentalism and environmental change; social approaches to managing environmental change.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Global Tourism
description: Tourist landscape in relation to resources, spatial patterns of supply and demand, impacts of tourism development, and models of tourist space. Flows between major world regions. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Geography, Environment, and Society
description: Examines the geography of resources and environmental change with a holistic and multi-scale perspective. Social approaches to resolving environmental problems.

subject: GEO
title: Culture and Environment
description: Critically examines changing views of nature, nature-culture relationships, and perceptions of the environment across different cultures.

subject: GEO
title: Islands and Archipelagos
description: Applies an island studies perspective to critically evaluate the commonalities and differences across islands and archipelagos in several world regions. Examines how island geographies influence social identities and movements and are impacted by environmental conditions.

subject: GEO
title: Politics, Nations, and States
description: Examines the political organization of space in the sovereign state system. Contemporary and historical analyses of boundaries, geopolitics, homelands, nations, nationalism, and territory.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Geography of North America
description: Overview of the physical and cultural geography. Regions and characters. Patterns of population, natural resources, industry, agriculture, and transportation/ communication networks.

subject: GEO
title: Intersectional Feminist Geographies
description: Explores space and place from intersectional feminist perspectives including Indigenous, Black, island, post-colonial and queer geographies. Focuses on contemporary case studies in gender and sexuality.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Japan
description: Regional synthesis of physical and cultural features; economic, social, political geography; origins and development of cities.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of China
description: Topics: environmental parameters and resource base, ecological control and resource management, institutional and technological transformation of agriculture, industrial potential and industrial location, settlement patterns and rural urban symbiosis.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of South Asia
description: Introduction to physical and human geography of India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Himalayan kingdoms. Environmental, economic, social, cultural, and political factors in development.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Southeast Asia
description: An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of the Pacific
description: Physical character of the Pacific; cultural, political, economic geography of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia (except Hawai‘i).

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Honolulu
description: Development of Honolulu and O‘ahu from 1778. Evolution of function, land use, and social patterns. Contemporary planning and environmental issues arising from urban growth.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Hawai‘i
description: Regional, physical, cultural geography. Detailed study of people and resources.

subject: GEO
title: UAV and Aerial Photography
description: Introduction to UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle systems) and the measurement, interpretation, analysis, and use of photography acquired by UAV and other aerial systems.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Cartography and Air Photo
description: Principles of cartography: compilation and measurement from aerial photographs, alternate forms of data presentation, symbolism, design, and map projection.

subject: GEO
title: Map Design and Production
description: (3 2-hr Lab) Compilation, design and production of maps for presentations, research, and illustration using artists and mapping software.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Statistical Methods in Geography
description: Quantitative statistical methods will be explored for describing and interpreting geographic/environmental phenomena. Topics will include data display, measurement, sampling, spatial statistics, dimensional analysis, nonparametric and parametric models.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to GIS
description: Design, implementation, and use. Database construction and documentation. Techniques for spatial data manipulation and display. Evaluation of existing systems. Student research projects.

subject: GEO
title: Directed Reading
description: Limited to senior majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in geography.

subject: GEO
title: Vegetation and the Climate System
description: Role of vegetation in the climate system; links to hydrology and biogeochemical cycling; vegetation and climate history; evolution of terrestrial ecosystems; effects of global warming.
prereq_raw: 101 or 300 or 401 or 402 or 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Climate Change
description: Approaches to the study of past and future climate change.
prereq_raw: 101 or 300 or 401 or 402 or 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Agricultural Climatology
description: Analyzing climatic data; relation to photosynthesis, phenological development, and crop yields. Crop-weather models as guides to improved land-use planning and agronomic practices.
prereq_raw: 101 or 300 or 400 or 401 or 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Fluvial Geomorphology
description: Introduction to the single most important geomorphic agent shaping the terrestrial environment. Focus on fluvial process, fluvial dynamics, fluvial landforms, and sediment transport.

subject: GEO
title: Climate, Air Quality, & Policy
description: Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legal aspects of pollution control.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Water in the Environment
description: Water fluxes in the environment. Occurrence and movement of water; methods of quantification. Water balance of soil-plant system: precipitation, interception, infiltration, runoff, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and groundwater recharge.
prereq_raw: 101 or 300 or 400 or 401 or 402 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Conservation and Evolutionary Biogeography
description: Theories and techniques for the analysis of spatial microevolutionary patterns, taught from an interdisciplinary perspective. Examples and readings emphasize Hawai‘i and the Pacific region.
prereq_raw: either 309, BIOL 265 or BIOL 487, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Cultural Biogeography
description: Coevolution of human societies and plants over the last 10,000 years. Foraging, farming and urban societies economies; spread and modification of selected plants; issues of preservation of genetic resources and traditional plant knowledge. The form and function of gardens.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Human Role in Environmental Change
description: Human impacts through time on vegetation, animals, landforms, soils, climate, and atmosphere. Special reference to Asian/Pacific region. Implications of long-term environmental change for human habitability.
prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B, one of 101, BIOL 101, BIOL 123 and either 322 or BIOL 310; or consent

subject: GEO
title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
description: Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Introduction to analytical methods for identifying, measuring, and quantifying the impacts of changes or interventions in resource, human-environment, and other geographic systems.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Resource Management in Southeast Asia
description: Challenges associated with the management of land, water resources, fisheries, forests and agriculture in modern Southeast Asia. Case studies are used to illustrate current problems and evaluate potential management solutions.

subject: GEO
title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
description: Investigation of the forces behind natural and technological hazards, and human actions that reduce or increase vulnerability to natural disasters.

subject: GEO
title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Urban Geography
description: Origins, functions, and internal structure of cities. Problems of urban settlement, growth, decay, adaptation, and planning in different cultural and historical settings. Dynamics of urban land use and role of policies and perceptions in shaping towns and cities.

subject: GEO
title: Agriculture, Food and Society
description: Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to non-majors.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Marine Policy
description: Introduction to the law and policies concerning the marine environment, commerce and security. Role of science, law and politics in historical and current policies for maritime trades, navigation safety, marine resources, and marine exploration.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Regional Analysis
description: Spatial dynamics and environmental implications of urban and rural development. Concepts of regions, process of regional development, patterns of spatial interaction, and theoretical bases for development strategies; emphasis on Hawai‘i.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Geographies of Popular Culture
description: Examines contemporary geographical debates related to concepts of discourse, identity, space/place, power, representation, and popular culture. Considers various landscapes of popular culture and how popular culture mediate a sense of place, geopolitics, and identity formation.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Environment, Resources and Society
description: Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues.

subject: GEO
title: Tea and Culture
description: Examines cultural practices of tea in different parts of the world, focusing on history and culture of tea in China, Japan, and England. Also includes changing technologies and economies of tea worldwide.

subject: GEO
title: Gender, Fashion, & Globalization
description: Explores ethics of the present and historic expansions of the fashion industry and its environmental impact globally. Examines how gender/race/class shape garment production and consumption and fashion activism in world regions. Emphasis on oral/written communication.

subject: GEO
title: Political Geography of Oceans
description: The geopolitics of the oceans and the law of the sea as applied to regions of conflict and cooperation in marine resource development and preservation. Focus on Indo-West Pacific, South China Sea, Arctic Ocean.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Peace and War
description: Geographical factors underlying conflict in the world.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Environment and Society in China
description: Explores the relationship between environment and society in the Chinese society, including both traditional nature-culture connections and modern human-environmental issues. Examines China’s long-range cultural change, environmental transformations, and modern development challenges.

subject: GEO
title: Topics in Geography
description: Selected topics in geography not offered in the regular geography curriculum.

subject: GEO
title: Remote Sensing
description: Introduction to the principles of remote sensing and image processing skills. Topics include electromagnetic spectrum, sensors, aerial photo and satellite imagery interpretation, geometric and radiometric correction, digital image processing. Research project, lab.

subject: GEO
title: 3D Mapping and Analysis
description: Environmental mapping and analysis using 3-dimensional geographical data acquired from high resolution remote sensing systems.

subject: GEO
title: Field Mapping
description: Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

subject: GEO
title: Web Mapping
description: (3 2-hr Lab) Introduction to interactive web mapping techniques for sharing and visualizing various forms of geospatial data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

subject: GEO
title: GIS and Spatial Analysis for Social Sciences
description: Introduction to spacial analysis and GIS for social science studies, using open-source GIS tools to collect, visualize, and analyze social data; public health, socio-economic and social media data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

subject: GEO
title: GIS for Environmental Sciences
description: Applications of GIS technologies to solve real-world problems in natural and environmental sciences. Research project, lab.

subject: GEO
title: Senior Thesis
description: Preparation of research paper under individual faculty supervision. Recommended for admission to graduate program.

subject: GEO
title: Practicum in Geography
description: Internship in applied geography under professional and faculty supervision. Field placement integrated with academic study.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable up to six credit hours maximum

subject: GEO
title: Capstone Undergraduate Seminar
description: Current and historical geographic literature provides a background for local and global issues. Through discussion, written reviews, and research reports, the geographic perspective in modern life will be explored.

subject: GEO
title: Directed Research
description: Geography majors conduct research under faculty supervision on a topic of their choice. Minimum GPA of 3.0 and consent. Senior standing only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to six credits

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Climatology
description: Methods of determining energy budget and water balance; applications in agriculture, hydrology, climatic classifications. Theory of climatic change. Bibliography.
prereq_raw: 300 or 400 or 401 or 402 or 405 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 or ATMO 320; or consent

subject: GEO
title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawai‘i, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation.

subject: GEO
title: Human Environment Systems
description: Role and potential of systems science in analysis of human environment interaction, especially resource management. Framework and methodology for problem structuring; overview of techniques.
prereq_raw: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing with consent

subject: GEO
title: Theories and Policies of Development
description: Will critically examine what constitutes progress, advancement, or betterment in this highly uneven world, where inter-regional, inter-class, inter-group, and inter-gender differences in development are expanding. Graduate standing only.

subject: GEO
title: Coastal Planning and Management
description: Theory and practice of coastal planning and management in the U.S. and abroad. Case studies investigate topics such as coastal land conservation, marine protected areas, coastal hazards, fisheries, and aquaculture.

subject: GEO
title: Advanced Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Theory and practice of environmental impact assessment. Policy and planning frameworks supporting environmental assessment in the U.S. and abroad. Cumulative environmental effects and strategic environmental assessment.

subject: GEO
title: Seafood in Southeast Asia
description: Seafood production in Southeast Asia, including both regional fisheries and aquaculture. Case studies used to illustrate challenges to the implementation of sustainable seafood production and emerging approaches, such as community supported seafood.

subject: GEO
title: Environment and Development
description: Theories and practice of development; how changing development paradigms shape different ideas concerning the environment and the management of natural resources; emerging debates in development and environment in post-modern era.

subject: GEO
title: Community-based Natural Resource Management
description: Concepts and theories of community, resource access, and governance. Practical challenges to CBNRM in contemporary political economy. Graduate students only.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Geography of Southeast Asia

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Geography of the Pacific
description: Investigation of geographic problems of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia.

subject: GEO
title: Geospatial Analysis of Natural Resource Data
description: The application of geostatistics to estimate spatial dependence to improve soil and regional sampling; provide insight into underlying soil, geographic, and geologic process, and to provide quantitative scaling up of point measurements to fields, regions, and watersheds. State-space modeling also will be included.

subject: GEO
title: Human Geography Research Methods
description: Introduction to research methods in human geography. Explores and provides guided practical experience with research methods and analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Faculty Seminar Series
description: Graduate seminar required of all department MA students and PhD students. Single credit course in which faculty present ongoing research in their fields.

subject: GEO
title: Technology and Natural Risks Methods of Analysis
description: Survey of tools for evaluating risks to human health from technological and natural hazards. Historical and international context of methods.

subject: GEO
title: Concepts and Theories in Geography
description: Concepts, theory, models. Geographic approaches to spatial and environmental problems. Required of entering graduate students unless waived by department.

subject: GEO
title: Research Design/Methods in Geography
description: Elements of research design, practical field experience, exposure to research and ideologies, broad exposure to heritage and ethos of the discipline.

subject: GEO
title: Geomorphology
description: Current understanding of geomorphological concepts, processes, and the dynamic relationship between human landscape modification and system response.

subject: GEO
title: (Alpha) Special Topics
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. (B) regional and locational analysis; (C) geography, environment, and culture; (H) Multi-objective decision analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Political Ecology
description: Introduction to political ecology. Content will examine the historical development of and contemporary scholarship in political ecology from a human and environmental geography perspective.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar: Resource Management in Asia-Pacific
description: Examination of resource management problems in Asia and the Pacific. Problems of resource use—agriculture, forestry, energy, minerals, ocean, air quality.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar: Political Geography
description: Topics vary; may include borders, boundaries, geopolitics, homelands, identity politics, nations and nationalism, social categorization, the sovereign state system, territoriality.
prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent. (Once a year)

subject: GEO
title: Seminar: Geographies of Migration
description: Topics vary; may include immigration, borders, refugees, asylum, climate change, and displacement.

subject: GEO
title: Society and Space
description: Advanced seminar on social production of space. Topics include spatial metaphor in social theory; western spatiality from the renaissance through the enlightenment, modernity and post modernity; and geography of the body, home, landscape, and nation.

subject: JOUR
title: Journalism and Society
description: News literacy, and the role of journalism in society–its influence, rights and responsibilities; issues and trends.

subject: JOUR
title: Introduction to Multimedia Journalism
description: Fundamentals of multimedia reporting: finding and developing story ideas, photojournalism, audio storytelling, design, infographics, and cross-platform digital convergence.

subject: JOUR
title: Media Writing
description: Fundamentals of writing for various news media and public relations; ethics.

subject: JOUR
title: Reporting
description: Theory and practice of information gathering using a variety of primary and secondary sources, finding information online, use of databases and interviews for news stories, with emphasis on writing. JOUR majors only, or consent.

subject: JOUR
title: Governing, Policy, and Political Journalism
description: Survey of the institutions of democratic governance and the role of journalism in covering and analyzing public policy.

subject: JOUR
title: Photojournalism
description: Production, selection, and use of digital photographs for publications. Storytelling action and feature photography with digital cameras, worked up through Adobe Photoshop and InDesign programs. Students must have a digital camera.

subject: JOUR
title: Advanced Editing
description: Intensive training in editing, planning, and organizing stories and visual elements for publication; news judgment; managing projects. JOUR majors only, or consent.

subject: JOUR
title: Visual Journalism: Multimedia
description: Fundamentals of visual journalism; visual theory, principles, and tools to create multimedia journalism projects for online, emerging media, and print platforms. JOUR majors only, or consent.

subject: JOUR
title: Sports Media
description: A practice-based writing approach to the production of sports media in contemporary mediums of all types (written, audio, video, etc.) for various communication contexts (e.g., journalistic, public relations, etc.

subject: JOUR
title: Magazine Writing
description: Writing nonfiction articles for magazines, newspapers, and newsletters; preparing material for specific audience; marketing articles.

subject: JOUR
title: Interpretive Journalism
description: Writing articles of news analysis, editorials, and critical reviews.

subject: JOUR
title: Video Journalism
description: Fundamentals of video journalism using digital video cameras for writing, reporting, editing, and producing news stories, with significant attention to oral communication skills.

subject: JOUR
title: Journalism History and Trends
description: Development of the news media and trends that may affect the future of journalism.

subject: JOUR
title: Communication and Law
description: An exploration of key legal issues related to the practice of journalism in Hawaiʻi, including comparisons with other jurisdictions in the United States and elsewhere. JOUR majors only, or consent.

subject: JOUR
title: Practicum
description: Working on campus student or quasi-professional publications under professional and faculty supervision.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to six credits

subject: JOUR
title: (Alpha) Journalism Workshops
description: Intensive workshops in practice-based journalism, focused on building skills and making public projects in: (B) emerging media; (C) reporting; (D) editing; (E) multimedia journalism; (F) public relations. JOUR majors only, or consent.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable in different alphas up to 6 credits

subject: JOUR
title: Advanced Photojournalism
description: Computer experience in the creation, manipulation, and editing of color news, feature, sports, and documentary images. Study of the ethical and legal dimensions of electronic imaging.

subject: JOUR
title: Publication Layout and Design
description: Visual display concepts and procedures for newsletters, brochures, newspapers, magazines.

subject: JOUR
title: Special Topics
description: Topics of interest to faculty and students; taught by regular and visiting faculty.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time for different topics

subject: JOUR
title: Media Ethics
description: Ethics and social responsibility for media professionals. Application of ethical theories and principles to case studies and research projects through writing assignments.

subject: JOUR
title: Broadcast Projects/Production
description: Applied, problem-based application of skills and knowledge of visual story telling to the production of broadcast newscasts. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: 250, 300, 330; and ICS 101 or ICS 110 or ICS 111 or LTEC 112

subject: JOUR
title: Advanced Multimedia Journalism
description: Advanced fundamentals of multimedia writing and reporting, including finding and developing journalistic story ideas, photojournalism, audio storytelling, design, infographics, and cross-platform digital convergence. Junior standing or higher.

subject: JOUR
title: Global Communication
description: Problems and opportunities of communication in a variety of international contexts, focused on journalistic issues. JOUR majors only, or consent.

subject: JOUR
title: Advanced Video Journalism
description: Advanced experience in field and studio production of short and long form video journalism; with emphasis on social media fundamentals and content distribution across multiple digital platforms.

subject: JOUR
title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Journalism
description: Exploration of the leading edge of the journalistic ideology today as well as a projection of future forms, styles, and strategies, with writing skills as the foundation of such exploratory activities. Junior standing or higher.

subject: JOUR
title: Internship
description: Internship in media or PR operations under professional and faculty supervision.

subject: JOUR
title: Directed Research
description: Individual research projects.
prereq_raw: senior standing and consent of department chair

subject: LIS
title: Library and Information Studies Workshop
description: Designed for in-service librarians and other information specialists needing to update their professional skills, focus on a particular topic, or learn new approaches and concepts. Credits earned in these courses cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

subject: LIS
title: Introduction to Reference and Information Services
description: Philosophy, principles, and practice of reference services in libraries, information centers and information literacy. Bibliographic control, reference research, reference interview, online searching, evaluation of bibliographic and Webliographic material. Field component. MLISc degree required course.

subject: LIS
title: Resource Discovery
description: Techniques and strategies for discovery of information resources from professional online databases and the Web. Query formulation and use of advanced functions to match retrieved resources with user needs for research and reference work. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Metadata Creation for Information Organization
description: Theory and practice of metadata creation for organization of information resources, cataloging code for resource description and access, Library of Congress and Dewey Decimal Classification schemes, use of OCLC.

subject: LIS
title: Foundations of the Information Professions
description: Lecture/discussion/survey of the information professions, development of professional identity, professional values and ethics, historical development, current issues in the information professions.

subject: LIS
title: Intellectual Freedom
description: Seminar surveying the core philosophical principles and practices of intellectual freedom with special application to librarianship and information sciences.

subject: LIS
title: History of Information
description: History of the recording, preservation, and transmission of knowledge. Development of libraries and other information organizations as instruments of cultural transmission.

subject: LIS
title: Navigating Information Organizations
description: Principles of effective management of information organizations, with emphasis on organizational information flows, team skills, communication, planning, resource allocation, assessment, outreach, and advocacy. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Collection Management
description: Principles and issues of collection management and care. Criteria and tools for selecting and deselecting materials. Relationships with publishers/producers.

subject: LIS
title: Preservation Management
description: Introduction to preservation management. Focus on management strategies for preservation of materials in libraries and archives. Covers preservation planning, condition surveys, disaster planning, grantsmanship, and basic issues relating to deterioration.

subject: LIS
title: Community Engagement
description: Explores how information professionals in libraries and other settings collaborate with community members and organizations. Provides an overview of theory and practice emphasizing critical analysis of policies, services, and trends. Required course for CALIS. (Alt. years)

subject: LIS
title: Introduction to Hawai‘i and Pacific Librarianship
description: Overview of resources and issues concerning librarianship in Hawai‘i and the Pacific Islands. Reference strategies and materials to answer common research questions, collection development, and management issues. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Indigenous Librarianship
description: Development and delivery of information services with and for indigenous communities. Issues include cultural protocols, traditional knowledge organization and ethics of access. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Multicultural Resources for Diverse User Groups
description: Examines resources and materials targeted for diverse user populations in libraries and community organizations, locally and globally. Surveys issues and trends related to diversity initiatives affecting the publishing industry, libraries, and cultural institutions worldwide. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Traditional Literature and Oral Narration
description: Analysis of traditional literature including Asian and Pacific Island resources. Selection and evaluation of traditional literature emphasizing cultural values. Introduction to oral tradition, history and techniques of storytelling.

subject: LIS
title: Responding to Reading in Libraries
description: Research-intensive seminar that explores the reading process in library contexts and similar settings. Critical examination of ways in which library and literacy services impact reading engagement and interests of library users. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Digital Librarianship
description: Lecture with demonstrations to introduce the essential types of digital resources and the software tools for finding high quality and relevant information efficiently from digital journal archives and reference databases.

subject: LIS
title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
description: Literature of Asia in Western and Asian languages; bibliography, reference tools, research methods, sources, published and archival repositories.

subject: LIS
title: Government Documents
description: Survey of government documents at the federal, state/local and international levels in all formats. Covers methods of acquisition and organization, including depository arrangements. Current issues of government information dissemination policies and practices discussed.

subject: LIS
title: Management of Libraries and Information Centers
description: Theories and principles of administration for effective management of libraries and information centers, with emphasis on planning, resource allocation, team skills, project management, assessment, leadership, outreach, and advocacy.

subject: LIS
title: Archival Arrangement and Description
description: Principles and techniques for arrangement and description of archival materials. Topics include basic metadata standards, authority sources, record context, series identification, scope and content.

subject: LIS
title: Records, Archives and Memory
description: Introduction to records, archives, and memory including the global history and nature of records, archives, and the archival profession. Topics include cultural memory, ethics and values, tribal and indigenous records, archival theory, practice and perspectives.

subject: LIS
title: Digital Archives
description: The role of technology in archival theory and practice. Topics include digital preservation, authenticity assessment, arrangement and description, content management, and access systems. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Moving Image Archives
description: Principles and technologies of processing, preservation, and accessibility of archival audiovisual materials in moving image archives. Topics include moving image repositories, critical analysis of archival footage, format identification, digitization strategies, equipment, and vendor considerations. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Records Management
description: Management of records in all media formats. Selection of media format based on government and internal records requirements. Problems associated with electronic media such as legality and shelf life.

subject: LIS
title: Archival and Special Collections Management
description: Management of archives, manuscript collections, and special collections using approaches and best practices from archival studies. Topics include management theory, appraisal theory, facilities issues, privacy, intellectual property, records management, advocacy, fundraising, reference, and educational outreach. Graduate standing only.

subject: LIS
title: Archival Access, Representation and Use
description: Principles and techniques for arrangement and description of archival materials. Topics include basic metadata standards, authority sources, record context, series identification, scope, and content. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Informatics
description: Sociotechnical concepts and processes underlying information systems, services, and use. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Asian Informatics
description: Lecture/discussion on the transformative effects of information and communication technologies in East Asia. Topics include media, mobile devices, social media, publishing, e-government, and e-commerce. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Digital Instruction
description: Study and application of principles and practices that influence digital instruction related to information literacy in libraries and other information environments. Focus on application of instructional design and standards-based outcome assessment. Field research component.

subject: LIS
title: Technology for Libraries and Information Centers
description: Survey of theories, concepts, methods and practices relating to the application of information technology to support the administration and use of information resources. Includes digital, printed and audiovisual materials.

subject: LIS
title: Media Technology and Resources
description: Overview of the use of media technology and the development of media collections and services in libraries. Use and integration of new emerging technologies, including problems and issues.

subject: LIS
title: Database Design and Creation
description: Designing and creating textual and/or directory databases from the viewpoint of information specialists and content providers. Needs analysis, file design, record content and structuring, software choice. Students implement prototype database.

subject: LIS
title: Creating Digital Libraries
description: Principles, techniques, and technologies supporting the creation of user-centered digital libraries. Selection, organization, maintenance, access, and retrieval of digital collections. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Human Dimension in Information Systems
description: Lecture/discussion on human element in information systems, including physical, cognitive and affective behavior in interaction with information systems. Information retrieval, human-computer interaction and cognitive science research, quantitative and qualitative research methods. Research component.

subject: LIS
title: Books and Media for Children
description: History and criticism of children’s literature. Contemporary books and media. Trends in book publishing and media production. Developmental needs and interests of children. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

subject: LIS
title: Books and Media for Young Adults
description: History and criticism of literature for young adults. Contemporary books and media. Trends in media for young adults. Developmental needs and interests of adolescents. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

subject: LIS
title: Services in Public Libraries
description: Planning and implementing services and programming in public and school libraries. Trends, issues, networking, public relations, outreach, competencies, services for the disabled and other special groups.

subject: LIS
title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure.

subject: LIS
title: Internship
description: Field experience in library or information agency settings with supervision of professional librarians or information specialists. Available to classified students only. Selection based on academic advisor approval, application form, interview and possession of required competencies. Students must apply and be accepted before registration. Selection is by agency.

subject: LIS
title: Masters Seminar
description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio and preparation for professional practice. Peer mentoring and student presentations. MLISc degree Plan B required course.

subject: LIS
title: Masters Seminar II
description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio or thesis. Peer mentoring, faculty, and student presentations. MLISc degree required course. Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Special Topics in Information Studies
description: Includes issues of topical interest in the information professions. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as services for specific groups and special collections. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times if course content is different

subject: LIS
title: Special Topics in Information Technology
description: Includes issues of topical interest in information technology. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as digital archives, content management systems and informatics. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times if course content is different

subject: LIS
title: Practicum School Librarianship
description: Skill development and application of academic study through observation and practice in a fieldwork program with accompanying seminar. Required for school library certification in Hawai‘i.
prereq_raw: 12 credits in LIS degree program and consent of practicum coordinator required
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits

subject: LIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading and/ or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses. Enrollment requires approval before end of previous semester, with specification of goals, work requirements, number of credits, rationale.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, credit earned up to six credits

subject: LIS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: LIS
title: Seminar in International Librarianship
description: International and comparative librarianship; professional organizations; comparative methodology; research; periodicals; international agencies; influence of literacy and social, cultural, political factors.

subject: PACE
title: Survey of Conflict Management
description: Survey of contemporary conflict management and resolution: negotiation, mediation, conciliation, ombuds, fact-finding, facilitation techniques, arbitration, and litigation.
prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent

subject: PACE
title: Governing, Policy, and Political Journalism
description: Survey of the institutions of democratic governance and the role of journalism in covering and analyzing public policy.

subject: PACE
title: Survey Peace and Conflict Studies
description: Survey of basic concepts, ethical relationships, methods, and debates in modern peace research and the oral skills needed for conflict resolution studies.
prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent

subject: PACE
title: Personal Peace: Stories of Hope
description: Interviewing, writing, and publishing stories of those who have overcome great difficulties to find personal peace.
prereq_raw: grade of B or better in ENG 100 or consent

children.text: grade of B or better in ENG 100

subject: PACE
title: Greek and Roman War Literature
description: Survey of war-related literature from Greece and Rome, its major themes, and how it reflects the wide range of social, political, intellectual, and literary perspectives on war found in the ancient world.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

subject: PACE
title: Aggression, War, and Peace
description: Biocultural, evolutionary, and cross-cultural perspectives on the conditions, patterns, and processes of violence, war, nonviolence, and peace.

subject: PACE
title: Nonviolent Political Alternatives
description: Exploration of scientific and cultural resources for nonviolent alternatives in politics.
prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course; or consent

subject: PACE
title: Media Communications and Conflict
description: Mass communication and conflict; deals with understanding the role of news media in influencing conflict, and introduces students to conflict-sensitive communications working to assist in resolving conflicts. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: The Meaning of War
description: Exploration of ethical questions related to the many facets of war–e.g., patriotism, tribalism, holy war, self-sacrifice, cowardice, media coverage, propaganda, torture, genocide, pillage, suicide tactics, battlefield immunity.

subject: PACE
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in peace and conflict resolution.

subject: PACE
title: Media Ethics
description: Ethics and social responsibility for media professionals. Application of ethical theories and principles to case studies and research projects through writing assignments.

subject: PACE
title: Peace Processes in Philippines and Hawai‘i
description: History of Philippine Islam and the Moro struggle, the peace process in Mindanao and sovereignty movement for Hawaiian nation. 75 min. Lec, 75-min. joint online discussion with Philippine students. Junior standing only.

subject: PACE
title: History of Peace Movements
description: Examination of two centuries of U.S., European, Australian, and Hawaiian peace, thought, and action. Also surveys early Christian and secular attitudes to war. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PACE
title: Gandhi, King, and Nonviolence
description: Life and thought of Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King, Jr.
prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent

subject: PACE
title: Terrorism
description: Multidisciplinary approach to the origins, dynamics, and consequences of international terrorism, including the psychological, legal, ethical and operational concerns of counterterrorism.

subject: PACE
title: Introduction to Human Rights: International and Comparative Perspectives
description: Introduction to international, regional, and domestic human rights law; comparative perspectives on the theoretical origins of human rights and policy debates on the protection of human rights, dispute resolution, and enforcement mechanisms.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level social sciences course, or consent

children.text: level social sciences course, or consent

subject: PACE
title: Negotiation
description: Negotiation theory, negotiation skills and application of negotiation in conflict prevention, conflict management and conflict resolution with an emphasis on oral communication and contemporary ethical issues.
prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent

subject: PACE
title: Leadership for Social Change
description: In-depth study of current models and emerging theories of ethical leadership in community service; development of tangible leadership skills, including communication, conflict resolution, team-building, and management skills. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Geography of Peace and War
description: Geographical factors underlying conflict in the world.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

subject: PACE
title: Peacebuilding in Performance
description: Provides an exploration of peacebuilding, its contributions to community and its intersectionality with the arts to influence non-violent conflict resulting in cultural performance for all to engage and enjoy. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Introduction to Mediation
description: Learn the core components of the mediation process and the tools for empowering mediation participants to reach customized resolutions. Emphasis on learning and applying the skills through exercises and mock mediation sessions.

subject: PACE
title: Protest Under Occupation
description: Explore nonviolent protests when one Independent State controls the territory of another Independent State (or international organization, such as the United Nations), without the transfer of sovereign title. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Indigenous Nonviolent Action in the Asia-Pacific
description: Study of nonviolent methods (i.e., United Nations structures, international law, boycotts, and peaceful protest) used to gain political goals and examines their successes, failures, and the prospects for those that remain ongoing. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Introduction to Facilitating Organizational Change
description: Explores the characteristics of organizations from different perspectives including structural, political, ethical, and cultural frames from organizational theory and practice. Focuses on how to design organizational change strategies and facilitate their implementation. Sophomore standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any 200-level DS course (with a minimum grade of C+)

children.text: any 200 -level DS course ( with a minimum grade of C+

subject: PACE
title: Advocating for Children: Rights and Welfare
description: Multi-disciplinary advocacy for children’s rights and welfare in various social and political systems; the role of families, justice, economics, media, race, culture, environment on policy-making for children. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Culture and Conflict Resolution
description: Conflict resolution techniques for major world culture. Emphasis on cultures of the Pacific Basin, Pacific Islands, and Asia.

subject: PACE
title: International Law and Disputes
description: Management, prevention, resolution of international disputes and the role of international law.
prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent

subject: PACE
title: ‘Ike Kūpuna: Introduction to Indigenous Frameworks for Peace Building
description: Survey of the concepts and major theories of indigenous epistemology that can create social change.

subject: PACE
title: Managing Human Conflict
description: Introduction into the field of conflict analysis and resolution through the examination of theory and role-play. Major theories of conflict studies are considered and the forms of conflict resolution, such as negotiation, mediation, and arbitration. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Research and Peace
description: Introduction to and survey of the interdisciplinary field of peace research, combining theory, methodology, and empirical aspects. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Topics in Peace and Conflict Resolution
description: Recent issues, practices in peace and conflict resolution.

subject: PACE
title: Hiroshima & Peace
description: 10-day intensive course at Hiroshima City University, Japan, in the 2-weeks before the annual August 6 commemoration of the atomic bombing. Home-stay with Japanese family. Sophomore standing.
prereq_raw: any 200 level social science course, or consent

subject: PACE
title: Practicum and Internship
description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses.
