title: Seminar: Research Methods
description: Conceptual strategies, data collection approaches, and data analysis techniques appropriate to political inquiries.

subject: POLS
title: Writing Politics
description: Seminar on the politics of writing, grammar, translation, argument, genre, and style with significant content on indigenous issues of oral traditions, alternative modes of writing and argument, and language continuance.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Political Thought
description: Pre-announced topics. At least one section a year.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Indigenous Theory
description: Pre-announced topics may include gender and sexuality studies, postcolonial theory, colonial discourse analysis, globalization, historiography; emphasis on indigenous epistemologies and the work of native scholars.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: International Relations
description: Pre-announced problems of both international organization and politics. At least one section a semester.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Comparative Government and Politics
description: Pre-announced topics. At least one section a semester.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Public Administration
description: Pre-announced administrative theory, comparative and development administration, and functional aspects.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Public Policy
description: Pre-announced topics.
prereq_raw: consent of instructor. At least one section a year

children.text: At least one section a year

subject: POLS
title: Indigenous Nations and the Problems of Sovereignty
description: Examines intersections of sovereignty and indigenity from comparative and critical perspectives. Engages indigenous studies of sovereignty and of alternative political frameworks. (Alt. years)

subject: POLS
title: Decolonial Futures
description: Topic engages probable and preferable futures of indigenous struggles and resistances. Emphasis placed on the ethics and responsibilities used to move towards those futures.

subject: POLS
title: Seminar: Politics of Regions
description: Analysis of political development, international relations, decision-making processes, and systems of political thought in regions and subregions of the world.

subject: PPC
title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent

subject: PSY
title: Survey of Psychology
description: An overview of the field: psychophysiology, perception, learning, cognition, stress, personality, social psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Personal Development
description: The application of psychology to the understanding, management, and enhancement of one’s life.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Gender
description: Survey of topics in psychology relevant to gender and its impact on the lives of women and men: socialization of gender, mental health, racial identity, majority-minority status, sexual orientation, life-span issues and violence.

subject: PSY
title: Survey of Research Methods
description: Survey of standard methods and related conceptual issues employed in psychological research. Both experimental and non-experimental methods will be reviewed.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Behavioral Psychology
description: Outline of basic learning principles. A general, unified approach to study of human personality and behavior. Based upon a learning conception; various areas of psychology and the other social sciences are treated.

subject: PSY
title: Statistical Techniques
description: Frequency distributions; graphic methods; central tendency; variability; correlation; reliability; tests of significance.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Psychobiology
description: Survey of study of behavior from a natural sciences viewpoint. Evolution, ethological analysis of behavior genetics, neural mechanisms, drugs and behavior, biological development.

subject: PSY
title: Developmental Psychology
description: Emotional, mental, physical, social development from infancy to adulthood; interests and abilities at different age levels.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology
description: Cognitive, behavioral, and emotional effects of people: interpersonal relations, attribution, attitudes, group behavior, stereotypes, social roles, aggression, helping, self-concept; applications.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Personality
description: Scientific study of personality, its meaning, assessment, development, relation to cultural-social determinants.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
description: History, theories, nature of psychological problems, methods of assessment, forms of intervention, current developments.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Community Psychology
description: Examination of human functioning in social and ecological context. Topics include stress, health, intergroup relations, culture, ethnicity, social competence, and community empowerment.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
description: Psychology applied to education, including cognitive, sociocultural, and multicultural approaches to teaching, learning, development, and research. Develops knowledge and written communication skills through and introduction to classroom, assessment, instruction, motivation, classroom management, and standardized testing.

subject: PSY
title: Learning and Motivation
description: Theoretical interpretations; survey of major theorists and contemporary controversial issues; major influences in classical and instrumental conditioning.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Emotion
description: Survey of traditional views and leading theories, and research in related topics.

subject: PSY
title: Cognitive Psychology
description: Survey of cognitive processes involved in perception, attention, memory, language, problem-solving, reasoning, judgment, intelligence and consciousness, among others.

subject: PSY
title: Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Coverage of the relationship between the brain and body on learning and memory, stress, motivated and regulatory behavioral functions, and mental disorders.

subject: PSY
title: Psychopharmacology
description: Coverage of the principles of pharmacology in relation to the effects of drug actions on the brain and behavior.

subject: PSY
title: Sensation and Perception
description: In-depth coverage of the basic principles involved in sensing and perceiving our environment.

subject: PSY
title: Social Development of Children
description: Survey of the social and emotional development of children and adolescents.

subject: PSY
title: Adult Development and Aging
description: Overview from a multidisciplinary, life-span perspective. Includes research techniques, personality development, family relationships, occupational attainment, death.

subject: PSY
title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
description: Psychological theories and cultural systems; understanding of own and other cultures; psychological and cultural perception of social motivation; cultural similarities and differences in interpersonal relations.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
description: Psychosocial aspects of human sexual relationships. Social psychology of emotional and physiological arousal, interpersonal attraction, and societal regulation of intimate relationships.

subject: PSY
title: Abnormal Psychology
description: Nature and causes of psychological disorders.

subject: PSY
title: Consumer Behavior
description: Analysis of consumer behavior and motivation; principles of learning, personality, perception, and group influence, with emphasis upon mass communication effects.

subject: PSY
title: History of Psychology
description: Origin and development of contemporary points of view.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar on the Psychology of Knowledge
description: Selected topics in the psychology of knowledge and mind from Western and/or non-Western perspectives.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable in different topics up to 9 credit hours

subject: PSY
title: Practicum in Psychology
description: Supervised psychological experience in school, clinic, hospital, industry, social welfare, government, etc.

subject: PSY
title: Teaching General Psychology
description: Supervised experience.
prereq_raw: 100, at least 12 additional credit hours in psychology, and written consent. Repeatable one time. A-F only

children.text: at least 12 additional credit hours in psychology,
written consent . Repeatable one time. A-F only

subject: PSY
title: General Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research.

subject: PSY
title: Psychometrics: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory, research, or methodology relevant to individual differences, measurement, or aspects of psychometrics.

subject: PSY
title: Experimental Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research, in cognitive psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Psychobiology: Advanced Topics
description: Indepth coverage of some area of theory and research in psychobiology, physiological psychology, or sensory processes.

subject: PSY
title: Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology
description: Social and emotional maladjustment in children and adolescents, developmental disabilities, pediatric psychology, psychological interventions with children and adolescents.

subject: PSY
title: Development Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in developmental psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in social psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Health Psychology
description: Psychological principles for understanding and dealing with wellness and illness. Theories and research on stress-related disorders; prevention of stress through lifestyle and healthy behaviors.

subject: PSY
title: Communicating Social Support
description: Survey of major theories, concepts, research, and application regarding communication and social support in interpersonal relationships.

subject: PSY
title: Teaching Personal Development
description: Supervised experience in leading a seminar in personal development.
prereq_raw: 170 and 12 additional credits in PSY and written consent

children.text: additional credits in PSY and written consent

subject: PSY
title: Advanced Topics in Adjustment/ Treatment/Prevention
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in clinical psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Applied Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: Coverage in-depth of some areas of theory and research.

subject: PSY
title: Special Topics in Psychology
description: Covers topics of current or special interest not covered in regular course offerings or advanced topics seminars.

subject: PSY
title: Directed Reading or Research
repeatable_raw: Repeatable eight times, up to nine credits

subject: PSY
title: Methodologic Foundations of Psychology
description: Methods used in psychological research; observational, correlational, and experimental types of design.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Regression
description: Introduction to quantitative methods in behavioral sciences and the general linear model with a focus on regression. Topics include correlation, bivariate and multiple regression, mediation, and moderation. Requires basic statistics. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

subject: PSY
title: Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and Related Methods
description: Introduction to ANOVA and its extensions from both traditional and general linear model approaches. Topics include single and multi-factor ANOVA, multiple comparisons, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), and repeated-measures ANOVA.

subject: PSY
title: Factor Analysis and Structural Equation Models (SEM)
description: Theories and applications to latent variables models. Topics include path analysis, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation models (SEM), multi-sample SEM, mean structure, latent growth curve models, and multilevel SEM. Requires basic knowledge of regression.

subject: PSY
title: Multivariate Analysis
description: Analysis of multiple dependent variables. Topics include multivariate normal distribution, Hotelling’s 72, multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA), discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, canonical correlation, and principal components analysis (PCA).

subject: PSY
title: Measurement in Education and Social Sciences
description: Test theories and applications in education and social sciences. Topics include the true score model; reliability; generalizability theory; validity; item response theory; and applications in research. Class requires knowledge in ANOVA and regression.

subject: PSY
title: Advanced Psychometrics
description: Theories and applications of modern psychometrics. Topics include unidimensional and multidimensional models of item response theory, detecting biased items, measurement invariance, scaling methods, and current issues in psychometrics.

subject: PSY
title: Categorical Data Analysis
description: Theories and methods for data analysis with categorical and discrete variables. Topics include contingency tables; logistic regression; log-linear models; and introduction to generalized linear models.

subject: PSY
title: Analysis of Multilevel Models and Longitudinal Data
description: Theories and applications of analysis of nested (clustered) data. Topics include fixed and random effects, intra-class correlation, cross-sectional multilevel models, and multilevel models, and multilevel models with repeated measures and longitudinal data. Requires basic knowledge of regression.

subject: PSY
title: Principles of Learning
description: Survey of the principles of learning, including important discoveries in the development of the study of learning, major theories, and both basic and applied research in contemporary literature.

subject: PSY
title: Cognitive Psychology
description: In-depth survey of the computational and representational structures and processes of cognition. Special attention devoted to consideration of the relationship between brain, mind, and computation.

subject: PSY
title: Thinking
description: Provides an introduction to higher cognition (thinking and reasoning) and its foundations, particularly as they relate to the larger field of cognitive science. (Alt. years)

subject: PSY
title: Comparative Cognition
description: Survey of the historical and contemporary study of cognition across species, including learning, memory, attention, navigation, reasoning, social interaction, and communication.

subject: PSY
title: Selected Topics in Comparative Psychology
description: Intensive review of comparative, communicative, sensory, or learning mechanisms in animals.

subject: PSY
title: Psychopharmacology
description: Basic principles of pharmacology as they apply to the brain and specific psychological disorders such as anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress disorders, schizophrenia, psychosis, memory, and drug use.

subject: PSY
title: Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Relation of central and peripheral nervous systems to behavior.

subject: PSY
title: Developmental Foundations
description: Historical, theoretical, and methodological foundations of developmental psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Cognitive Development
description: Familiarizes students with current research and theory in cognitive development through readings of original journal articles and monographs.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology
description: Theories and research in social cognition and behavior.

subject: PSY
title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
description: Application of psychological theories to cross-cultural phenomena; assessment of cross-cultural processes and social motivations; culture and personality; research evaluation and design.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology and Social Issues
description: Conflict, dissent, community issues, problems; social change and its relation to mental disorder.

subject: PSY
title: Applied Social Psychology
description: Problems in use of social psychology principles in human affairs; multidisciplinary considerations.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology of Love and Sex
description: Seminar in psychosocial aspects of human sexual relationships. Social psychology of cognitive, emotional and physiological arousal, interpersonal attraction, mate selection, and antecedents and consequences of intimate relationships.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
description: Preparation for becoming a clinical psychologist with emphasis on scientist-practitioner model, professional ethics, diversity and professional development.
prereq_raw: graduate student in psychology or consent of instructor

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Assessment I
description: Psychometric theory; ethics; diversity issues; principles and methods of cognitive-intellectual, neuropsychological, and personality assessment.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Assessment II
description: Administration and interpretation of cognitive-intellectual and personality assessment devices.
prereq_raw: 670 and 671 or consent and enrollment in Clinical Studies Program

subject: PSY
title: Advanced Assessment
description: Conceptual and methodological foundations of clinical applications of assessment.
prereq_raw: 671 and 672 and enrollment in Clinical Studies Program, or consent. (Once a year)

subject: PSY
title: Treatment Research
description: Idiographic and nomothetic approaches to clinical treatment research methods and findings.

subject: PSY
title: Psychopathology
description: Comprehensive study of the mental disorders across the lifespan. (Once a year)

subject: PSY
title: Child Practicum
description: Supervised clinical assessment and treatment of children and adolescents.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable ten times, up to 33 credits

subject: PSY
title: Adult Practicum
description: Supervised clinical assessment and treatment of adults.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable ten times, up to 33 credits

subject: PSY
title: External Practicum
description: This supervision-style class will cover cases and issues related to student’s clinic work, supervision, or educational goals while training in external practicum sites.

subject: PSY
title: Cultural Community Psychology
description: Graduate seminar on cultural considerations and issues in the history, methods, theories, interventions, and professional roles in community psychology. Small class size (up to 10). Open to graduate students.

subject: PSY
title: Practicum: Behavioral Change and Community
description: Supervised experience in educational, mental health, correctional, consulting, or community action agencies.

subject: PSY
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Minimum of six credit hours is required.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable six times up to seven credits

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in History and Theory of Psychology

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Quantitative Psychology
description: Specific and newly emerging topics in statistics, including casual inference, analysis of missing data, and statistical machine learning. Content varies and focuses on advanced topics not covered in other PSY methods and statistics courses.
prereq_raw: 610 (with a minimum grade of B) or instructor consent

subject: PSY
title: Research in Psychometrics
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Experimental Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Developmental Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Social Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Child Treatment
description: Psychological interventions for youth, as well as parent training.

subject: PSY
title: Adult Treatment: Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy
description: Training in cognitive-behavioral strategies for treating adults. Enrolled in Clinical Studies Program only.

subject: PSY
title: Health Psychology: Behavioral and Biological Bases
description: Psychological and biological bases of health psychology and behavioral medicine. Overview of cognitive, behavioral, and psychophysiological mechanisms; theories and methods of prevention in physical disease.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Clinical Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Community Psychology Research
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: PUBA
title: Survey of Public Policy and Analysis
description: Students will learn about the policy making process, the results of policy decisions and how public policy is assessed, analyzed, and responded to. Also discusses important policy issues that currently fill the political landscape.

subject: PUBA
title: Research Methods for Policy Evaluation
description: Explores methodological approaches to the evaluation of public policies and strengths and weaknesses of various social science research methods. Students will learn how to employ them to determine the effectiveness of various public policies. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PUBA
title: Foundations of Nonprofit Management
description: Broad overview of nonprofit organizations, including what it means to be a nonprofit, strategies of nonprofit organizations, and the management of nonprofits. Topics include advocacy, leadership, and evaluating success.

subject: PUBA
title: Multicultural Leadership in Public Service
description: Develop students’ culturally agile leadership to allow them effectively lead in work on international, regional, and local projects and problems of compelling public interest that cross cultures.

subject: PUBA
title: Practicum and Internship
description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses.
prereq_raw: any two other PACE courses or consent

subject: PUBA
title: Directed Reading and Research in Public Administration
description: Independent research and reading on topics in public administration, public service, and community development.

subject: PUBA
title: Program Evaluation for Public and Nonprofit Organizations
description: Methods for evaluating the effectiveness of programs in the public and nonprofit sectors; performance measurement to inform managerial decision making.

subject: PUBA
title: Introduction to Public Administration
description: Develop a comprehension of the history and foundation of public administration. Topics include economic, political, and social dynamics; decision-making and leadership theories, management challenges, human resources, budgeting, program evaluation, policy, and technology. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Organizations: Theory and Change
description: Explores characteristics and structural, human resources, political, and cultural frames of organizational theory. Focus on organizational change strategies and theories. Discusses how to use these frames and theories in everyday management of public service organizations. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Leadership and Ethics
description: Applies leadership and ethical theories to public and non-profit sectors, focusing on ethical leadership; emphasizes critical thinking to address value conflicts; and teaches moral reasoning as a practical professional skill. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Effective Communication in Public Administration
description: Knowledge and skills to effectively communicate in the public sector. Focus on communication foundations and skills, levels and contexts of public sector communication, and handling challenges such as diverse and multi-cultural settings. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Public Administration Personnel Management
description: Understand the pivotal role that effective human resource management (also known as personnel management) plays in improving organizational effectiveness. Topics include managing diversity, employment law and discrimination, performance appraisal, and labor-management relations. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Public Administration Research Methods
description: Introduction to research methods for public administrators to understand the principles and methods used to conduct and analyze valid research. Examples are oriented to the field; theory and hands-on practice utilized. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Public Budgeting
description: Institutions and issues related to public-sector budgeting at federal, state, and local levels. Process of developing public budgets and constraints on public policy reflected in budgets.

subject: PUBA
title: Policy Analysis and Implementation
description: Explore contemporary policy issues relating to public administration practice. Develop analytic techniques and models of public policy-making processes, administrative rules, and policy implementation strategies. Learn how social forces, political, and economic pressures influence policy orientation.

subject: PUBA
title: Reforming Public Organizations
description: Looks at the challenges and opportunities for changing public organizations so that they may be more successful in meeting their public responsibilities and better places for people to work. Focus is on the creation of positive images of organization and effective change strategies.

subject: PUBA
title: The Political Environment of Public Organizations
description: Seminar on the role of public managers in shaping public opinion and public policy. Using evidence from theory and practice presents students with tools for understanding management roles within a political context.

subject: PUBA
title: Strategies of Change: Leaders and Leadership
description: Explores the key elements of leadership in public settings by examining what leaders actually do, looking at popular media portrayals of leadership, and talking together with guests about the challenges of leadership, effective followership, and positive change.

subject: PUBA
title: Law, Economics, and Public Administration
description: Explore U.S. law as applied to public institutions using economic lens. Rationale of property, contract, and tort law; evolution of administrative law, economic efficiency of common law system, effects of legal rules on economic behavior.

subject: PUBA
title: Collaboration for Public and Nonprofit Leaders
description: Theories, skills, and tools needed to effectively manage networks in government and nonprofit organizations; explores how to administer, assess performance, and evaluate success in these dynamic new partnerships. Graduate students only or consent.

subject: PUBA
title: Managing Workplace Diversity and Inclusion
description: Examines rationales, impacts, and various dimensions of diversity and inclusion beyond race and gender. Students learn and apply public management tools used to foster workplace diversity and inclusion.
prereq_raw: 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

subject: PUBA
title: ICT Policy and Planning
description: Processes and methods of planning appropriate to the information and communication sectors, including future economic, social, political, technical, and environmental perspectives.

subject: PUBA
title: Public Policy and Advocacy
description: Designed to deepen students’ ability to understand and influence the policy process in Hawai‘i and the U.S. Topics include theories of the policy process, and advocacy strategies, legal constraints, and coalition building. PUBA majors only or approval of instructor.

subject: PUBA
title: Nonprofit Management
description: Fundamental aspects of managing a nonprofit organization: overview of the nonprofit sector; mission and scope of nonprofit organizations; organizational structures and functions; resource and volunteer development; major management issues. A-F only

subject: PUBA
title: Nonprofit Management Practices and Tools
description: Skills and tools needed by nonprofit managers. Topics include but are not limited to grantwriting, strategic planning, business practices, program evaluation, and advocacy.

subject: PUBA
title: International Perspectives on Public Administration
description: Key dimensions of public administration systems on a global scale; historic and contemporary forces shaping national systems; the dimensions that distinguish them, the opportunities and constraints for comparison and the transfer of knowledge and experience.

subject: PUBA
title: Indigenous Governance
description: Overview of indigenous governing systems, particularly in the Americas and the Pacific. Students will learn the legal frameworks and principles of these systems, and how services are provided to citizens.

subject: PUBA
title: Special Topics
description: Topics of current interest in the field of public service and public administration, taught by regular and visiting faculty.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable for different topics up to six credit hours

subject: PUBA
title: MPA Practicum
description: Placement in public, private, and nonprofit organizations to observe and analyze organizational functions and processes while undertaking projects of use to the host agency.
prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B: 602, 603, and 604

subject: PUBA
title: Certificate Practicum
description: Students in the nonprofit management track of the certificate will learn by doing and observing in a nonprofit organization selected in consultation with the student’s advisor. PUBA graduate certificate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Capstone Seminar
description: Culminates public administration core courses by incorporating theoretical, analytical, and practicum observations into examination of public issues of importance to Hawai‘i and the region.
prereq_raw: (601, 602, 607) with a minimum grade of B

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Sociology
description: Basic social relationships, social structures, and processes.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Data Analysis
description: Basic analytic skills widely used in quantitative analysis of social science data, including descriptive statistics, rates and probability, comparison of groups, introduction to causal relationships, and application of these techniques to real life examples.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to International and Global Studies
description: Introduces undergraduate students to the major political, social, economic, cultural, technological, and historical dimensions of globalization. Special attention will be paid to globalization process that have impacted Hawai‘i and the Asia-Pacific region. FGB

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Relations
description: Race and ethnic relations in world perspective; social, economic, and political problems associated with perception, existence, and accommodation of these groups within the wider society.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Social Problems
description: Theoretical and substantive survey of the nature and causes of social problems; selected types: poverty, inequality, deviance, etc

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Juvenile Delinquency
description: Forms of juvenile deviance; conditions and processes that result in alienation and deviance of youth. Juvenile corrections as institutionalized societal responses.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to the Sociology of Punishment
description: Multiple social theories about different forms of formal and informal punishments and social control across different societies and times.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Sociology of the Family
description: Family patterns, mate selection, parent-child interaction, socialization of roles, legal sanctions, trends in organization, functions.

subject: SOC
title: East Asian Popular Cultures
description: East Asian popular culture, with a focus on Korea and Japan, as well as the Chinese language sphere. Analyzes social forces shaping pop culture industries, artists, and productions in the region from a global perspective.

subject: SOC
title: Principles of Sociological Inquiry
description: Basic methods of sociology for production and analysis of data. Foundations for understanding research and for advanced courses in methods and statistics.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Urban Sociology
description: Urban processes and social problems, such as poverty, crime, racial segregation, homelessness, housing policy, urbanization, and neighborhood ethnic diversity. How places shape identity and opportunity. Research methods applied to communities, places, and neighborhoods of Hawai‘i.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Health
description: Explores current issues in the conceptualization and delivery of health care for women.
prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or WGSS 202, or POLS 110; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Inequality and Stratification
description: Introduction to social stratification theory and research; definition and measurement of socioeconomic status; racial, ethnic and gender inequality; differences in lifestyles and life chances; social mobility.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Work
description: Work from viewpoint of individuals; meaningfulness versus productivity; how work, economics, and the industrial system affect individual goals.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Change
description: Causes, processes, and effects of social change, using single and multi-cause models in simple and complex industrialized societies.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Social Policy
description: Social and economic policies affecting women in families, education, social services, government, health care, the economy; public policy implementation and development; policy impact on women.
prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociological Theory
description: Major theorists and their influences, from Comte to today.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Law
description: Law as a political enforcement of the social order; how it is organized and operates; determinants of effectiveness; ways it adapts to and facilitates changing social conditions.

subject: SOC
title: Criminology
description: Concepts used in crime, law enforcement, criminal justice, and corrections. Types of criminal behavior; costs and effects of control.

subject: SOC
title: Drugs and Society
description: Use of mood- and mind-altering drugs in America among adults, youth, and cross-culturally. Illicit drug culture, psychedelics, and perception; social norms and deviant behavior.

subject: SOC
title: Deviance and Social Control
description: Interrelations of deviance, criminology, juvenile delinquency, corrections, social control, sociology of law. Key concepts, theories. DS

subject: SOC
title: Criminal Justice Organizations
description: Examines major criminal justice organizations–police, courts, and prisons. Using organizational theory, identifies the role of organizational goals, structure, resources, legitimacy, culture, and front-line workers in shaping criminal justice policy and practice.
prereq_raw: 100 or a 200-level SOC course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Psychology
description: Major principles; social attitudes, theories of conformity and change, person perception and attribution theory, social role, role conflict and role behavior, group structure, and behavior.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Happiness in Unsettled Times
description: Combines theoretical, scientific and ‘hands-on’ learning to explore how happiness and well-being can be cultivated, even in this challenging era of extreme global climate events.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Education
description: Formal education as one aspect of socialization. Emphasis on American system; business, military, and religious institutions.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Aging
description: Aging as a social phenomenon, including social impacts of growing elderly population and emerging social patterns among the elderly. Important theoretical perspectives and cross-national research.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Medical Sociology
description: Social factors in disease and treatment; illness behavior, roles of patients and healers; nature of healing professions; use of medical services; alternative systems of medical organization.

subject: SOC
title: Chinese Society and Culture
description: Social institutions, family, community, education, stratification, government, economy; impact of modernization and revolution on their contemporary transformation.

subject: SOC
title: Japanese Society and Culture
description: Persistence and change in economy, policy, religion, education, family, and other institutions of modern Japan.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Korea
description: Social institutions, family, education, religion, cultural values, social classes, economic development, social movements, gender relations, North-South relations, and unification issues.
prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Gender
description: Effect of sex and gender roles (both traditional and nontraditional) on attitudes and behavior within the family and educational, economic, and governmental systems.
prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Law, Politics and Society
description: Relationships between law, politics, and society will be explored. Emphasis is placed on several dimensions of legality: legal “indeterminacy” and some of the many things that law does for us and to us; law’s response to violence; the connections between law and social change; access to the law and its sociological dimensions; how/why law fails and what happens when it does.
prereq_raw: 100 or any 200 level SOC course, or a 100 level or 200 level POLS course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Internship for Sustainability and Social Justice
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience in addressing sustainability issues. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent. Consent of instructor.

subject: SOC
title: Food, Body, and Women: Analysis of Biopolitics
description: Explores how food, body, and other “matter of life” are imbedded in biopolitics from the feminist perspectives.
prereq_raw: WGSS 300, or one 300-level WGSS or ES course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Urban Sociology
description: Urbanization in developed and developing countries, the rural-urban continuum, structure and process of metropolitan regions, theories of urban location and growth, housing and urban renewal.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Social Stratification
description: Approaches to research in social inequality: community studies; historical and cross-cultural analyses of poverty, working class, middle class, power structure, social mobility, etc.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Population and Society
description: Global and U.S. patterns of population growth; composition and distribution, elementary demographic techniques; development issues and population policy.

subject: SOC
title: Economy and Society
description: Study of the dominant trend of economic change and its impact on society; globalization of economic activities and transformation of industrial society to postindustrial one; corporate restructuring and downsizing and their impact on employment and income distribution; gender relations in workplaces; the impact of globalization on the newly industrializing countries.

subject: SOC
title: Technology and Society
description: Nature of technology, social forces that affect its adoption; impact on society; innovation.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Work
description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global.
prereq_raw: 300, or one 300-level WGSS or ES course; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Organizations and Society
description: Schools, hospitals, industries, prisons, and government agencies analyzed in terms of self-actualization, alienation, human relations, communication, leadership, organizational conflicts.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Criminology & Juvenile Delinquency
description: Research in systematic social deviation. Scaling and measurement of delinquents/ criminals, official data, gangs, identification and measurement of delinquent/criminal value orientations, etc. DS

subject: SOC
title: Punishment & Society
description: Institutions, organizations, and individuals charged with carrying out punishment in the criminal justice system and beyond. DS

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Law and Social Change
description: Interrelationships between legal orders and other social institutions; use of “law” to change major status relationships, e.g., boss-worker, woman-man, child-adult.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Crime
description: Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system.
prereq_raw: 300, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Prisons
description: Prisons, jails, and other detention facilities across historical, social, and/or international contexts.

subject: SOC
title: Social Structure and the Individual
description: Effects of social institutions on individuals. Role of socioeconomic status, cultural background, family structure, peer group, schools, and occupational roles in socialization.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Gender Violence
description: Historical and structural theories of gender-based violence, including domestic and sexual abuse, prostitution, trafficking, cross-cultural perspectives, social policy and practices. Junior standing or graduate standing only.

subject: SOC
title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
description: Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives.
prereq_raw: 300, WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Marriage and the Family
description: Theory and methods of studying social interaction in marriage and the family; examination of marriage, mating, love, and choice. Empirical research emphasizing Hawai‘i.

subject: SOC
title: Marriage and Family: A Feminist Perspective
description: Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries.
prereq_raw: 300, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Sociology of Aging
description: Social and research issues significant to delivery of long-term care services to the elderly; cost, quality, availability of services, evaluation of programs, role of family, formal and informal care services.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Medical Sociology
description: Application of sociological theories and concepts to medical social situations and behavior; problems of obtaining data for research.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Religion
description: Seminar in research on sociological aspects of religious sectarianism; attention to Hawai‘i.

subject: SOC
title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawai‘i
description: The historical and contemporary social processes involved in inter-ethnic relations in Hawai‘i.
prereq_raw: 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of the Arts
description: Relation of art to society; role of artist, audience, critic, patron, museum; Western and other societies; attitudes toward new styles.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Sports and Society
description: Critical perspectives on sports and society. Topics include power and inequality; mobility, status, and economics; youth development; globalization; gender; and violence in sports and the wider society.

subject: SOC
title: Popular Culture
description: Popular culture as manifested in film, sports, TV, comics, magazines, etc.; relation to sociological theories and studies.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Survey Research
description: Survey research design and analysis, including theory selection instrument construction, sampling techniques, data collection, computerized data analysis, and writing up research reports of the findings.

subject: SOC
title: Social Statistics
description: Common statistical procedures emphasizing univariate and bivariate description; some attention to multivariate techniques and statistical inference, within context of research procedures.

subject: SOC
title: Social Statistics Laboratory
description: Required lab for computer applications for analysis of sociological data.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Field Research Methods
description: Techniques for collecting and analyzing qualitative data. Participant observation; small groups in natural settings; community studies. Grounded theory; theories of everyday life; reality construction.

subject: SOC
title: Discussion Group Leader–Freshman Seminar
description: A unique opportunity for students to gain leadership, teaching, and public speaking skills as a SOC 100 leader for a section of 10 freshmen students while being mentored weekly by a faculty course coordinator.

subject: SOC
title: Politics of Multiculturalism
description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S.
prereq_raw: 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Social Sciences Internship
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester; Consent of instructor.
repeatable_raw: repeatable two times, up to 12 credits

subject: SOC
title: Topics in Sociology
description: Topics course that explore current issues and try new ideas.

subject: SOC
title: Topics in Sociology: Student Projects
description: Students create their own study group and solicit an advisor from faculty. Consult department for assistance.

subject: SOC
title: Statistics for Regression Analysis
description: Dealing with the multiple linear regression and logistic regression models, focusing on modeling, i.e., specification of the explanatory variables to answer different research questions. Emphasis on applications using statistical package programs. SOC 605L is required.

subject: SOC
title: Regression Analysis Laboratory
description: Lab for computer analysis skills is required for students taking 605.

subject: SOC
title: Research Methods and Design
description: Emphasis on theory selection, theory construction, and choice of research strategies.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Methods of Content Analysis
description: Content analysis combines quantitative and qualitative methods to analyze text systematically. Covers sampling and case selection; manual and computer-assisted methods of coding and analyzing textual data; writing reports using content analysis data. (Once a year)

subject: SOC
title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar Qualitative Research
description: Advanced seminar on conducting fieldwork in natural social settings with emphasis on qualitative techniques, political and ethical considerations, data management and assessment, interpretation and reflexive writing.

subject: SOC
title: Classical Sociological Theory
description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociological theory from 19th-century to the 1960s, including intellectual contexts and historical development. Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Contemporary Sociological Theory
description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociology theory from the 1960s to the present, including intellectual contexts and historical development. Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Organizational Analysis
description: Theoretical approaches to organizations; organizational structure and process; organizational pathologies and effectiveness; the organization and its environment.

subject: SOC
title: Medical Sociology
description: Covers the major paradigms in medical sociology for analyzing social epidemiology, the political economy of health systems, health service organizations, health and wellness behaviors illness perception and help-seeking, doctor-patient interaction, and adaptations to illness. Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Stress and Health
description: Analysis of current theory and empirical research on relationship of stress and health; sociological, psychological, and community psychiatry models and current issues.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Mental Health and Illness
description: Examines sociological research and theories about mental health and illness. A key question in medical sociology will be addressed: What is the relationship between society and mental health?

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Social Stratification
description: Classical theories of social class, contemporary developments; crucial research issues, appropriate methodologies. Classified graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Feminist Criminology
description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Criminology
description: Major current theories, history of their development, elaborations of typologies, implications for treatment modalities.

subject: SOC
title: Criminal Justice System
description: Examination of the criminal justice system; the exercise of discretion and limits placed upon it.

subject: SOC
title: American Punishment
description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prison-industrial complex. Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Human Population
description: Comparative analysis of quantitative and qualitative aspects of population; factors affecting size, distribution, and composition; impact of population size and composition on society.

subject: SOC
title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, urbanization; projections and stable population theory.

subject: SOC
title: Teaching Seminar
description: Examines research on teaching, learning, and ethics, as well as practical skills for teaching at the university level. Syllabi and teaching philosophies are developed, which are useful for the academic job market. Graduate standing only.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Sustainability
description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives. Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Evaluation Research
description: Research design, data collection, field problems and analysis in the evaluation of social programs. Examples from criminal justice, corrections, drug treatment, mental health, and public health.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Statistics
description: Dealing with advanced statistical methods beyond multiple linear regression, such as logit, event history analysis, and multi-level analysis. Emphasis is on applications of the techniques to social science research.

subject: SOC
title: Cultural Analysis
description: Contemporary issues in cultural sociology, covering key theoretical perspectives, analytic methods and substantive areas for empirical research.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Sociology of Knowledge
description: Sociological theory applied to bases of knowledge in everyday life, professional communities, and the sciences. Research and theory-building activities of sociologists; ethnomethodology; construction of social structure, culture, and consciousness.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Current Issues in Sociology
description: Substantive areas that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addressed in other courses.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Medical Sociology
description: Application of theoretical paradigms and methodologies to the examination of selected research topics in the field of medical sociology.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Aging, Culture, and Health
description: Overview of the major theories, perspectives, and empirical findings relating to aging in various cultural contexts.
prereq_raw: 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent
restrictions_raw: SOC, PSY, NURS, SW, PH majors only.

subject: SOC
title: Comparative Family and Gender
description: Discusses the major perspectives on family and gender relations and examines related empirical research. Emphasis is on the cross-cultural comparisons across the U.S. and Asia in the context of globalizing economies and cultures. (Alt. years)

subject: SOC
title: Comparative Study of East Asia
description: Comparative analysis of social organization, social processes, and change of both capitalist and communist countries of East Asia, with each other and other areas of the world.

subject: SOC
title: Social Change–Pacific Islands
description: Analysis of social change; transformation from subsistence societies to commodified, wage-labor societies with participation in world economy.

subject: SOC
title: Modern Japanese Society
description: Social and behavioral studies of Japanese values, social organization, and personality development. Problems of value conflict, political protest, world role, tradition, and social change.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Modern Chinese Society
description: Developmental policies, social change, and impact on modern Chinese social institutions. Includes China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. May include social and demographic change, population, social stratification, gender, and family problems.

subject: SOC
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Race and Ethnicity
description: An examination of how ideas of “race” and “ethnicity” are constructed, and how this reflects and shapes social structures and relationships: (B) antiracism studies; (C) ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict; (D) race, place, and inequality. Graduate students only. (Alt. years)
repeatable_raw: Repeatable up to two times in different alphas

subject: SOC
title: Conflict Analysis/Resolution
description: Seminar on the analysis of conflict resolution. Faculty from law, planning, political science and guest practitioners will present multidisciplinary analysis and intervention strategies on contemporary conflicts. Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Social Structure and the Individual
description: Intensive study and individual research projects in a selected topic. Theoretical and methodological issues in relating social and individual levels of analysis.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Social Movements
description: Study of sociology of social movements, plus independent student research.

subject: SOC
title: Development in Asia
description: Theories and available research methods examined for applicability to developing areas; specific examples from Asia. Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Urban Sociology
description: Demographic trends in urban growth: nature and dimensions of urbanization and urbanism; ancient, American, and Third World cities; ecological theories of urban growth; lifestyles.

subject: SOC
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: SOCS
title: Leadership and Social Issues
description: Fosters understanding of key societal and community issues, social science perspectives on them, the qualities of effective leadership, and invites examination of personal responsibilities, intentions, and abilities to make a difference on those issues.

subject: SOCS
title: Street Science: Evaluating and Applying Evidence in Daily Life
description: Develops necessary tools for effective reasoning and problem-solving through use and application of analytic techniques, including question formation, understanding/interpreting data presented in the public sphere, and evaluating the validity of sources.

subject: SOCS
title: Statistical Analysis for Social Sciences
description: Statistical reasoning in the analysis of social science data, including descriptive statistics, exploratory data analysis, inference measures of association, decomposition of variance, and regression analysis. Lab required.
prereq_raw: any 100 level social science course or consent

subject: SOCS
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: SOCS
title: Introduction to Digital Media for the Social Sciences
description: Incorporates hands on instruction for creating informational media content, to include learning how to use camera and sound equipment, learning how to edit and create graphics, and learning presentation techniques.

subject: SOCS
title: Intermediate Digital Media Design and Production for the Social Sciences
description: Focus on theoretical and practical methods for media design and production of high-quality creative digital content. Emphasis on social media strategies and oral communication skills to attract mass online audiences. Junior standing or higher.

subject: SOCS
title: Social Sciences Service Learning and Micro Internship
description: For students undertaking service-learning or micro-internship options separately or for another class. Discussions and research related to learning experiences and issues encountered while in the field.

subject: SOCS
title: Pilina: Topics in Indigenous Social Sciences
description: Explores pilina (relationship, connection) of selected topics and issues of interest in the social sciences through Indigenous voices, perspectives, and scholarship.

subject: SOCS
title: Advanced Digital Media for Social, Cultural, and Community Engagement
description: Advanced digital media techniques for creating high-quality video content that promotes social, cultural, and community engagement. Focus on writing and oral skills with emphasis on visual storytelling and distribution on broadcast and social media platforms. Junior standing or higher.

subject: SOCS
title: Social Sciences Internship
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester; Consent of instructor.
repeatable_raw: repeatable two times, up to 12 credits

subject: SOCS
title: Topics in Teaching Innovations
description: Examination and critical analysis of contemporary curriculum and instruction issues in social sciences. Concepts, theories, principles underlying active learning, critical thinking, values inquiry, assessment, and multidisciplinary approaches to integration of knowledge.

subject: SOCS
title: Ocean Policy and Management
description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing the world’s oceans and coasts at all scales and on the role of scientific knowledge in managing marine and coastal resources.

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to LGBTQ+ Studies
description: Introduction to a survey of the key terms, texts, and histories of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender communities with special attention to Hawai‘i and Oceania. A-F only

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to the World’s Goddesses
description: Cross-cultural analysis of the religious narratives, beliefs, practices, iconography, and sacred sites related to female deities in the Americas, Polynesia, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and Europe from prehistory to 1500 C.E.

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to Women’s Studies
description: Introduction to feminist interdisciplinary analysis from global and critical perspectives; relationships between women and men from Asia-Pacific, Hawaiian, and other cultures, with a focus on gender, race, class, and sexual dynamics; exploration of women’s negotiations with institutional dynamics.

subject: WGSS
title: History of Gender, Sex, and Sexuality in Global Perspectives to 1500 CE
description: Explores how gender, sex, and sexuality become key elements in human society from prehistory to 1500 CE. Examines ancient world civilizations from multiple perspectives stressing issues and forces still influential today.

subject: WGSS
title: History of Gender, Sex and Sexuality in Global Perspective, 1500 CE to the Present
description: Explores how gender, sex, and sexuality become key elements in human society from 1500 CE to present. Examines world cultures from multiple perspectives, stressing issues and forces of continuing influence.

subject: WGSS
title: Culture, Gender, and Appearance
description: Social construction of gender within culture and its visual expression through appearance. Analysis of role, identity, conformity, and deviance in human appearance. Open to nonmajors.

subject: WGSS
title: Psychology of Gender
description: Survey of topics in psychology relevant to women’s lives: socialization of gender, mental health, violence against women, achievement motivation, lifespan issues, domestic violence.

subject: WGSS
title: Women Philosophers
description: Introduces students to the ideas of women philosophers.
prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL or WS, or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Women Writers of World Literature
description: Major women writers of world literature examined in context of female literary tradition.

subject: WGSS
title: Sexual Identity in Literature
description: Selected themes in major works of various types, cultures, periods. Requires a minimum of 3,000 words of writing.

subject: WGSS
title: Women, War, and the Military
description: The military as it includes and excludes women as soldiers, nurses, wives, prostitutes, and victims. Women and war economics; feminism, war, and peace.
prereq_raw: one of 151, 362, 375 or SOC 362; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Health
description: Explores current issues in the conceptualization and delivery of health care for women.
prereq_raw: 151 or 202, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or POLS 110; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Indigenous Women’s Health
description: Examines issues of indigenous women’s health pre and post colonial in Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific regions.
prereq_raw: one of 151, 202, 305; or HWST 107, HWST 270 or HWST 285; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: U.S. Women’s History
description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work in and outside the household, women’s involvement in social movements, changing norms about gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences among women.

subject: WGSS
title: Sex and Gender
description: Cross-cultural theories and perceptions of sexual difference; linkage between biology and cultural constructions of gender; relationship of gender ideology to women’s status.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Social Policy
description: Social and economic policies affecting women in families, education, social services, government, health care, the economy; public policy implementation and development; policy impact on women.
prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Sport
description: Explores the influence of gender in sport from cultural, psychosocial, and political perspectives. Through extensive writing, students examine gendered experiences of participants, spectators, and employees in sports organizations.

subject: WGSS
title: South Asian Migrants: Culture and Politics
description: Historical and contemporary experiences of South Asian migrants in North America, Pacific, Caribbean, and/or African diasporas; causes and patterns of migration, inter-ethnic relations policies; role of race, gender, culture in community, identity formation. subject: WGSS
title: Intersectional Feminist Geographies
description: Explores space and place from intersectional feminist perspectives including Indigenous, Black, island, post-colonial and queer geographies. Focuses on contemporary case studies in gender and sexuality.

subject: WGSS
title: 20th-Century Literature by Women
description: Twentieth-century women writers and their works; novels, short stories, poems, autobiographies. Interrelations of gender and literature.

subject: WGSS
title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Sex Differences in the Life Cycle
description: Human sex differences, their biological basis and significance, ethical considerations of genetic, hormonal, and behavioral determinants of sexual differentiation; biology of gender, sexuality, parenting, menopause, and aging.

subject: WGSS
title: Women, Ideas, and Society
description: Status of women in American society today in light of the cultural, historical, and philosophical forces that have produced it.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Religion
description: Examining roles of, and attitudes toward, women in major religious traditions through autobiographies, films, and primary texts.
prereq_raw: 149 or REL 149 or REL 150 or HIST 151 or WGSS 151

subject: WGSS
title: Queer Dance Exploratory
description: Queer dance exploration in movement practices and performance. Open to all majors.

subject: WGSS
title: Pacific/Asian Women in Hawai‘i
description: Adaptive strategies of Hawaiian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Samoan, and Southeast Asian women in Hawai‘i; feminist anthropological and historical analysis.
prereq_raw: any ANTH, SOC, or WS course

subject: WGSS
title: Seminar: Women and International Development
description: Topics: Women’s role, status, work and treatment in the Third World; economic development, changing work/family roles, agriculture and business, improvement/deterioration in gender equity across the Third World global feminization of poverty. Open to nonmajors.
prereq_raw: a 100 level economics course or any women’s studies course; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
description: Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Women and the Media
description: Media portrayal of women and men; role of the media in reproducing gender inequality. Women as producers and consumers of media. Feminist alternatives to mainstream media.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality and Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of literary constructions of gender and sexuality; emphasis on teaching gender and sexuality through writing and oral communication.
prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Island Feminisms: Art, Literature, and Culture
description: Examines island feminisms and explores ways women have engaged in various forms of cultural production (art, literature, film). Interdisciplinary, intersectional, and transnational. Key themes discussed: settler-colonialism, race, gender, and sexuality.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Politics
description: Women’s role in political institutions and processes in the U.S. and other countries; female and male approaches to power; feminist political goals and actions.
prereq_raw: 151 (or concurrent) or 362 (or concurrent) or any 100 level POLS course (or concurrent); or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
description: Historical and sociological studies of race and gender in U.S. society; grassroots feminist and racial/justice activism on the continent and in Hawai‘i.

subject: WGSS
title: Sexualities
description: Multi-disciplinary course draws from psychology, sociology, biology, history, cultural anthropology, law, Hawaiian, ethnic, feminist, gender, and queer studies to explore human sexualities with emphasis on the U.S., Hawai‘i and the AsiaPacific regions.

subject: WGSS
title: Co-ops, Communes, Collectives
description: Theory and practice of democratic organizations: women’s and feminist organizations; co-ops, communes, and collectives; indigenous people’s organizations; workplace democracy and social change.
prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course or POLS 390 (or concurrent) or WS 151, or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
description: Examines gender in Okinawa in relation to historical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region with attention to issues such as militarism and violence, colonialism and memory, and tourism and commodification of indigenous culture.

subject: WGSS
title: Women, Gender, & Sexuality in Performance
description: Feminist and performance studies approaches to performances by women and other genders; focus on the representation and status of women

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Work
description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Issues in Philosophy
description: Examination of basic feminist issues in philosophy, and of responses to them.
prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WS, or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality and Digital Media
description: Students learn how gender and sexuality are constructed online and produce a website to post their analysis and contribute to knowledge production about gender and sexuality in cyberspace.

subject: WGSS
title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
description: Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization.

subject: WGSS
title: Seminar in the Biology of Women
description: Embryological, anatomical, and physiological development of human female; hormonal, neural, and behavioral determinants of female sexual behavior; psychobiology of pregnancy, ovariectomy, and menopause.
prereq_raw: 350 or BIOL 172 or BIOL 350, or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Fashion, & Globalization
description: Explores ethics of the present and historic expansions of the fashion industry and its environmental impact globally. Examines how gender/race/class shape garment production and consumption and fashion activism in world regions. Emphasis on oral/written communication.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Madness
description: Interdisciplinary critical examination of the relationship between gender and mental health. Psychological research, feminist theory, autobiography, literature, and cinema.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Crime
description: Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system.
prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 300; or consent

children.text: -level WS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Justice and Law
description: Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Violence
description: Interdisciplinary course will examine western constructs of gender violence on its correlates with ethnicity, class, sexuality, nation, and empire.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Environmental Philosophy
description: Interdisciplinary approach to feminist perspectives on environmental issues; critical analysis of eco-feminism as political movement with reference to race and coloniality; cross-cultural comparison of differently-imagined relationships to non-human others, with emphasis on ethics and writing.
prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WGSS or any course 200 or above with a DB or DP designation, or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Theory
description: Contemporary debates in feminist theory concerning gender, race, and class; subjectivity and representation; gender and colonialism; bodies, sexualities and “nature.”
prereq_raw: any 300 level WS or POLS course, or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Methods and Research
description: Overview of feminist issues with dominant theories of knowledge and major methodologies employed in the social sciences; and exploration of role of gender theory and feminist politics in feminist research.

subject: WGSS
title: Queer Theory
description: Intensive survey of the key theories, texts, and questions of the interdisciplinary fields that make up queer theory.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Consumption in a Global World
description: Students learn theories of the global economy, histories of consumerism, constructions of gendered public spaces, and how the cultural production of consumers and consumer culture functions in the process of globalization.

subject: WGSS
title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
description: Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
description: Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives.
prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, SOC 300; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawai‘i
description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor

children.text: at least one course in WGSS

subject: WGSS
title: Marriage and Family: Feminist Perspective
description: Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries.
prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 300; or consent

children.text: -level WS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender Issues in Education
description: Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close attention to the writing process and the skills needed to compose a well-written research paper.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality, and Global Popular Culture
description: A study of gender, race, and sexuality as constructed in contemporary global popular culture, including music, films, novels, television shows, and internet culture.

subject: WGSS
title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminism, Nation and Empire
description: Examines U.S. feminist movements in the 19th and 20th century by exploring how U.S. racism, nationalism and imperialism have provided the context from which feminism emerged.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Globalization in Asia
description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory.
prereq_raw: one of 360, 361, 439, AMST 310, AMST 316, AMST 318, AMST 373, AMST 455, POLS 339; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
description: Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g. with class, religion, ethnicity).

subject: WGSS
title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
description: Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. Junior standing or higher.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender in Action Cinema
