description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. Junior standing or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Film
description: Exploration of film as a philosophical and artistic form in the context of gender, race, and sexuality.
prereq_raw: one of 151, 175, 176, or THEA 201; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Indigenous Feminisms
description: Examines the origins and futures of Indigenous feminist theory and praxis. Topics explored include cultural revitalization, colonialism, and sexual violence in Indigenous communities, citizenship and sovereignty, and contemporary Native gender roles and identity.

subject: WGSS
title: Studies in Literature and Sexuality and Gender
description: Intensive study of selected problems and issues in the construction and representation of sexuality and gender in specific genres, social and cultural contexts, thematic or figurative clusters.
prereq_raw: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Disasters
description: Explores disasters and their consequences for women, with attention to gender, race, sexuality, and class. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: at least one course in WS, or consent of instructor

children.text: at least one course in WS,

subject: WGSS
title: Social Sciences Internship
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester; Consent of instructor.
repeatable_raw: repeatable two times, up to 12 credits

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Revolution
description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons.

subject: WGSS
title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/masculine/ gender nonconforming/sexual)
description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration.

subject: WGSS
title: Selected Topics
description: Problems and issues for reading and research: feminist theory, criticism, affirmative action, etc.
prereq_raw: any WS course in appropriate area

prereq_tree.text: any WS course in appropriate area

subject: WGSS
title: Teaching Women’s Studies
description: Strategies for teaching women’s studies; addressing complex issues of gender, race, nation, class, sexuality and culture in a contemporary multiethnic campus environment. Emphasis on classroom techniques, teaching pedagogies, and hands-on experience.
prereq_raw: 151 and one or more WS course with a grade of B or better in all relevant courses, instructor recommendation; or consent

children.text: more WS course with a grade of B or better in all relevant courses, instructor recommendation;

subject: WGSS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: WS students only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits

subject: WGSS
title: Transnational Feminist Teaching and Research
description: Introductory graduate seminar designed to develop common vocabulary and explore the core debates in transnational feminist teaching and research to encourage critical reflection about teaching assumptions, approaches, and techniques in the contemporary college or university environment. Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Faculty Seminar Series
description: Seminar/discussion to introduce students pursuing the Graduate Certificate to the Woman’s Studies faculty and their areas of research, and to initiate student’s graduate studies in a woman’s studies field. Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Women in American Culture
description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Research and Methods of Inquiry
description: Examination of an emergent body of literature about how to shape questions concerning gender, sex, race, class, colonialism, and other vectors of power. Includes methods from social sciences and humanities and debates in the philosophy of science. Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Performance, Culture, and Theory
description: Survey of major critical works in fields of performing arts and public culture (e.g., dance, theater, music, commemoration). Topics include: theoretical application for the discipline of American studies, and the impact of social movements and labor migration on the performing arts.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Theory
description: Selected ideas from contemporary feminist theory concerning power, knowledge, and self; articulating women’s voice; deconstructing gender.

subject: WGSS
title: Writing and Publishing in an Interdisciplinary Field
description: Writing-intensive and publishing-focused class, students learn how to publish in an interdisciplinary field. Readings and assignments are designed to help students succeed in academic publishing. Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminism and Its “Others”
description: Relationship between feminist and other sites of critical insight and scholarship that have contributed to creating anticolonial, antiracist, antihomophobic theory, method and action. Questions the legacy of feminist coalition practices and engages the ongoing transformations that have begun to produce new alliances and coalitions that disrupt traditional boundaries of identity and power. Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Topics in Feminist Social Policy Research
description: Feminist social scientists from a variety of fields have explored issues of gender, social change and social justice. Draws from their work to critically examine strategies for conducting social policy research that is feminist in values and impact. Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Criminology
description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls.

subject: WGSS
title: Advanced Queer Theory
description: Advanced graduate seminar on the key ideas within queer theory. Students will become familiar with theories of queer relationality, queer of color critique, globalization of sexuality, disability and transgender studies, and queer indigeneities.
prereq_raw: undergraduate or graduate course work in women’s, gender, sexuality, or LGBTQ studies

children.text: graduate course work in women’s, gender, sexuality,

subject: WGSS
title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region.

subject: WGSS
title: Research in Feminist Studies: Capstone Experience
description: Provide women’s studies graduate certificate students with an opportunity to design, develop and complete a research project culminating in a publishable quality work and a professional quality seminar presentation. Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: (Alpha) Research Seminar in Chinese Literature
description: Study of authors, a genre, a period, or a problem. (M) modern; (T) traditional. A-F only for (M).
prereq_raw: 613, 615, 650, or EALL 611; or consent for (M); CHN 612 or consent for (T). )

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Weather and Climate
description: Introductory physical science course for all undergraduates in any major. A non-mathematical introduction to basic atmospheric variables, Earth’s past climates, global warming, air pollution, El Nino, hurricanes, tornadoes, and forecasting weather in Hawai‘i.

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Weather and Climate Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Exercises with meteorological data and measurement systems. Characteristics of Hawaiian winds, temperatures, and rainfall

subject: ATMO
title: Pacific Climates and Cultures
description: Highlights the interface between the observed weather and climate of the Pacific and the past and future culture of the people of the Hawaiian and Pacific islands. (Alt. years)

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
description: Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real-world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics.
prereq_raw: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140X)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score required for MATH 140X

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to MET Undergraduate Directed Research
description: Students gain familiarity with ATMO research. Students can select 1-3 credits per semester for maximum 6 credits over 4 semesters. Students must pre-arrange research and reading content with instructor. Freshman and sophomore standing only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, up to six credits

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Processes and Phenomena
description: Atmospheric variables, gas laws, radiation processes, thermodynamics, conservation laws, dynamic approximations, clouds and precipitation, convection, atmospheric circulations, mid-latitude and tropical weather systems, forecasting, climate.

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Physics
description: Energy and thermodynamics, statics and stability, physical processes of cloud formation, radiation and Earthatmosphere heat balance, kinetic theory, optical effects.

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Atmospheric Dynamics
description: Scalar and vector development of basic laws of hydrodynamics, equations of motion, kinematics, divergence and vorticity, viscosity and turbulence, introduction to numerical weather prediction, general circulation.

subject: ATMO
title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawai‘i. ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only. (Alt years: Spring) DP

subject: ATMO
title: Meteorological Instruments and Observations
description: Each week targets a different meteorological instrument and culminates in a lab exercise and report. The focus is on accurate measurement and scientific-style writing.

subject: ATMO
title: Global Environmental Change
description: Global environmental change problems such as carbon dioxide and the greenhouse effect, acid rain, chlorofluorocarbons and the ozone layer, global deforestation and the effect on climate, etc.
prereq_raw: 200, OCN 201, ERTH 101, ERTH 103, or ERTH 170; or consent

subject: ATMO
title: Programming for Meteorologists
description: Scientific programming in Fortran 77, graphics software and meteorological applications. A-F or Audit.

subject: ATMO
title: Undergraduate Internship
description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors.

subject: ATMO
title: Undergraduate Directed Reading
description: Individual reading in Atmospheric Sciences. ATMO students only. Junior and senior standing only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to three credits

subject: ATMO
title: Applied Atmospheric Dynamics
description: Advanced concepts in dynamics: vorticity, cyclogenesis, jet streams, fronts, mesoscale circulations.

subject: ATMO
title: Synoptic Satellite Meteorology
description: Satellite applications to synoptic meteorology and forecasting, including orbital elements, ephemerides, viewing geometry, radiation, satellite sensors, and interpreting satellite data.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Meteorology
description: History; tropical clouds and hydrometeors; typhoons; monsoons; local and diurnal effects.

subject: ATMO
title: Meteorological Analysis Lab
description: (2 4-hr Lab) Techniques and methods of forecasting extratropical systems with analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems. Students will be instructed on how to communicate and discuss a weather forecast and how to present a research paper.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Analysis Lab
description: Techniques of portraying and analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems in tropical and equatorial regions; forecasting tropical systems.

subject: ATMO
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis, and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. Senior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: ATMO
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Capstone for senior Meteorology majors. Undergraduate thesis project includes literature review, experiment or research design, data collection and analysis, technical writing of a final thesis paper and oral presentation of the paper. Junior and senior standing only.

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Dynamics I
description: Governing equations for moist atmospheric motions, approximations, basic theoretical models, boundary layer dynamics, atmospheric waves, quasi-geostrophic theory for mid-latitudes.
prereq_raw: 402, and either MATH 402 or MATH 405; or consent

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Dynamics II
description: Overview of dynamic meteorology, numerical weather prediction, geophysical fluid instabilities, approximate dynamical systems, atmospheric general circulation, stratospheric dynamics.

subject: ATMO
title: Cumulus Dynamics
description: Dynamics of convective systems: tornadoes, waterspouts, squall lines. Interactions with synoptic scale.

subject: ATMO
title: Mesoscale Meteorology
description: Scale analysis. Observational and theoretical aspects of mesoscale circulation systems.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Climate and Weather
description: Climate and general circulation of the tropics; El Niño and Southern Oscillation; intraseasonal oscillation; trade winds; tropical weather systems; energy balance; typhoons.

subject: ATMO
title: Satellite Data Applications
description: Principles and practices of satellite remote sensing as used in the atmospheric sciences, specifically clouds, aerosols, precipitation, ocean and land cover datasets from various satellites. Develop skills including data manipulation, analysis, and visualization using Matlab.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Cyclones
description: Lecture covering fundamentals of tropical cyclone structure, motion, and impacts on society. Observations from satellites, aircraft, ships and buoys, and numerical simulations focusing on storm structure and track. Some forecasting exercises.

subject: ATMO
title: Monsoon Meteorology
description: Synoptic components of monsoons, regional and temporal variability, numerical models, research exercises.

subject: ATMO
title: Physical Meteorology
description: Molecular kinetics, atmospheric thermodynamics, cloud physics, precipitation processes, atmospheric electricity, scattering and absorption of solar radiation, absorption and emission of infrared radiation, radiative transfer.

subject: ATMO
title: Radar Meteorology
description: Radar hardware, electromagnetic propagation and scattering, radar equation, signal processing, precipitation estimation and polarimetric applications, Multi-Doppler wind synthesis, mobile and spaceborne radars, forecasting, and data assimilation applications.
prereq_raw: 620 (with a minimum grade of B- or higher) or consent

subject: ATMO
title: Statistical Meteorology
description: Probability; frequency distributions of atmospheric variables; linear models; time series analysis (frequency and time domain); principal component analysis; statistical weather forecasting and verification.

subject: ATMO
title: Advanced Statistical Methods in the Geosciences
description: Methods for numerous multivariate analyses will include singular spectrum, extended empirical orthogonal function, singular-value decomposition, canonical correlation, discriminant and cluster analysis. Other advanced topics include wavelet analysis, statistical downscaling and Bayesian analysis. A-F only and audit.

subject: ATMO
title: Paleoclimate Model-Proxy Synthesis
description: Basics of Earth System Model development, parameterizations, intermodel variability and design of paleoclimate simulations. Types of proxies, tools and techniques for paleoclimate record development and reconstructions. Hypothesis testing and methods for proxy-model comparison studies. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring)
restrictions_raw: ATMO, GEO, EPET, NREM, OCN, and ORE majors only.

subject: ATMO
title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes.
prereq_raw: MATH 402 and 403 (or their equivalents) and either 600 or OCN 620; or consent

children.text: ( or their equivalents) and either 600 or OCN 620 ; or consent

subject: ATMO
title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the stateof-the-art theories and observations of large-scale ocean-atmosphere interaction, as well as conveying the fundamental understanding that has been developed during the past 30 years. Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Niño/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change.

subject: ATMO
title: Numerical Weather Prediction
description: Fundamental methods and techniques in numerical weather prediction: time differencing, spatial finite differencing, spectral methods, numerical stability, explicit and implicit methods. Modern operational and research forecast models. Hands-on laboratory includes simple to complex dynamic models, with a term project.
prereq_raw: 600 or OCN 620; MATH 407 or 408; or consent

subject: ATMO
title: Climate and Climate Variability
description: Physical basis of climate, numerical climate models, paleoclimatic indicators, modern instrumental climate records, assessment of human impact on climate, predictions of future climate.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Climate Dynamics and Modeling
description: Overview of current progress in tropical climate dynamics with a particular focus on large-scale atmosphere-ocean interactions; introduction of basic numerical techniques for students to construct and run immediate tropical atmosphere and ocean models.

subject: ATMO
title: General Circulation of the Atmosphere
description: Theory, observations, large-scale analyses, and global model simulations that describe characteristic large-scale circulation of the Earth’s atmosphere. Includes zonally averaged climatology, asymmetric features of the general circulation, and El NinoSouthern Oscillation phenomenon.

subject: ATMO
title: Special Topics in Meteorology
description: Concentrated studies on selected atmospheric problems.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to nine credits

subject: ATMO
title: Seminar in Meteorology
description: Participation in departmental seminars and presentation of a seminar on research results. Includes written critiques of departmental seminars.

subject: EPET
title: Space Exploration
description: Introduction to science and engineering of Solar System exploration with laboratory exercises. Covers planetary science, model-based systems engineering, mission planning, constraints on payload and spacecraft design, human spaceflight technology. Research projects emphasize written communication.

subject: EPET
title: Space Science and Instrumentation
description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces and their measurement. Design of space flight instrumentation.
prereq_raw: 201, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272

subject: EPET
title: Introduction to Human Spaceflight
description: Effects of spaceflight conditions on human physiology and psychology. Astronaut selection, training, crew composition. Ethics of space exploration. Politics & sociology of public and private human space flight. Selection of capstone project. Significant written communication.

subject: EPET
title: Space Mission Design
description: Covers all aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, budgets, and ethical issues that are important to consider in producing a fully successful mission.

subject: EPET
title: Capstone Project: Producing a Science Satellite
description: Develops a space mission with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists. Will build a small spacecraft and payload and seeks to answer important science questions. Emphasizes review report and proposal writing.

subject: EPET
title: Human Spaceflight Mission Elements
description: Engineering aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, and budgets for human spaceflight missions. Design of environmental control and life support systems. Capstone project design. Significant oral and written communication.

subject: ERTH
title: Dynamic Earth
description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip. DP

subject: ERTH
title: Dynamic Earth Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on study of minerals, rocks, and topographic maps. Examine volcanism, hydrology, coastal processes and hazards, geologic time and earthquakes. Field trips to investigate landslides, beaches and O‘ahu geology.

subject: ERTH
title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change.

subject: ERTH
title: Geology of the Hawaiian Islands
description: Hawaiian geology and geologic processes: origin of Hawaiian islands, volcanism, rocks and minerals, landforms, stream and coastal processes, landslides, earthquakes and tsunamis, groundwater, geologic and environmental hazards. Field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Volcanoes in the Sea
description: Lecture with field trips covering the manner in which geological conditions, resources, and events have affected past and present circum-Pacific societies.

subject: ERTH
title: Voyage through the Solar System
description: An illustrated voyage through the Solar System based on recent scientific results. The class highlights the origin, evolution, and current knowledge of the eight planets, their moons, asteroids, comets, and one star, the Sun. Field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Humans and the Environment
description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale.

subject: ERTH
title: Solar System Studio
description: Explore the wonders of the Solar System through hands-on experience of science. Will study satellite images, evaluate planetary surface observations, analyze data of objects in our Solar System, conduct experiments, and communicate their findings.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Volcanoes
description: Examines the origin and classification of volcanoes, volcanic eruptions, and volcanic deposits. Includes the history of volcanic studies, myths, and legends. Emphasis on volcanic eruptions, eruptive products, volcanic hazards, and risk management.

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Hazards
description: Introductory course covering the causes of, and effects from, earthquakes, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, landslides, rockfalls, and other natural geologic phenomena. Open to non-majors. Field trips. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Disasters and Human History
description: Examines how natural hazards have affected the course of human culture and societies from pre-history to the present in Hawai‘i/Oceania, Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
description: Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real-world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics.
prereq_raw: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140X)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score required for MATH 140X

subject: ERTH
title: Physical Geology
description: Structure, composition and evolution of Earth; processes responsible for formation, deformation and transformation of rocks; plate tectonics. Emphasis on quantitative methods, problem solving and critical thinking to geology. Laboratory and field trips required.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Directed Research
description: Lower division reading and research in any area of ERTH under the direction of a faculty member.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable four times or up to six credits

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Inquiry
description: Origin and age of the solar system and earth: interior of the earth; plate tectonics and records of biological evolution and past environments. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.
prereq_raw: 101L and one of 101, 103, 104, 106, or 130; or consent. 101L may be taken concurrently. ERTH and GEOL majors only. Consent required for all non-majors

children.text: 101L may be taken concurrently. ERTH and GEOL majors only. Consent required for all non-majors

subject: ERTH
title: Climate Change
description: Introduction to the science of climate change focusing on Earth’s past, present and future, specifically, the causes, consequences, and record of past changes; future projections, mitigation, and adaptation. Appropriate for both science and non-science majors.
prereq_raw: 101 or 103 or 104 or 106 or 111 or 130 or ATMO 101 or GES 102, or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Scientific Programming
description: Introduction to solving scientific problems by computer programming. Overview of the MatLab programming language and environment. Emphasis placed on good style, logical reasoning, and applied mathematics.

subject: ERTH
title: Physical Volcanology
description: Volcanic eruptions and their consequences. Includes models for volcanic eruptions including explosive eruptions and lava flows, monitoring of active volcanoes, evaluation and impacts of volcanic hazards, and mitigation of volcanic risk. Field trips. Normally fall. ERTH and GEOL majors or consent.
prereq_raw: (200 or 201) with a minimum grade of B+ or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Mineralogy
description: Introduction to the chemistry, crystalline structure, geologic occurrence, and physical properties of minerals. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.
prereq_raw: 200 or 201 and (CHEM 162/162L or CHEM 171/171L). or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Igneous Petrology
description: Survey of composition, classification, and occurrence of igneous rocks. Hand-specimen identification and optical petrography of igneous rocks. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Hazards & Geomechanics
description: Dynamic behavior of Earth’s surface, physical processes driving geohazards, and the risks posed to society. Theory, practical techniques, and data visualization to measure, analyze, and interpret hazards and implications.
prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or 103 or 104 or 106 or 130, MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A, and PHYS 151 or PHYS 170; or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Field Methods
description: Methods used in geological investigations in the field. Eight hours on Saturday in the field.

subject: ERTH
title: Work of Water
description: Physical properties of water, geological aspects of surface water and ground water occurrence, surface water and groundwater resources, use, and problems.

subject: ERTH
title: Sedimentary Processes and Environments
description: Modern and past terrestrial and oceanic processes and environments that form sediments and sedimentary rocks, and their interpretation in Earth history. Incorporates properties, principles and applications of sedimentology, sedimentary petrology, geochemistry and stratigraphy.
prereq_raw: 200 or 201 or consent, and 333 or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods.

subject: ERTH
title: Plate Tectonics and Geodynamics
description: Mechanics of lithosphere deformation related to plate convergence, rifting and strike-slip faulting, and the evolution of mountain belts. Use of theory and skillbuilding techniques to measure, describe, analyze, and interpret structures on Earth.
prereq_raw: 200 or 201; and 250; and MATH 241 or MATH 251A; and PHYS 170

subject: ERTH
title: Physics of Earth and Planets
description: Essentials of geophysics: application of physics understanding Earth, planetary, and solar dynamics. Topics include heat flow, gravity, geodesy, electromagnetism, seismology. Applications to core and mantle dynamics, plate tectonics, volcanoes, hydrology, environmental concerns, and archaeology.
prereq_raw: 250, 303, 313, MATH 242, and PHYS 272, PHYS 272L; or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Geochemistry
description: Theory and applications of chemical principles and chemical analysis to Earth, ocean and environmental sciences; chemistry of hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere system, origin/ differentiation of Earth/Solar system, volcanic processes, natural radioactivity, organic/inorganic chemistry.
prereq_raw: 200 or 201, and MATH 241 or MATH 251A, and CHEM 162 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Earth Materials and Structures
description: Lecture and lab that covers formation, occurrence, and identification of common minerals, rocks, and geologic structures. Lab work will include study of hand-samples, thin-sections, and field experiences.

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Internship
description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors.

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Research in Earth Sciences
description: Research experience for Earth Science undergraduates. Under the guidance of a mentor, the student will conduct research and write a report on the background, methods, data, interpretations, and conclusions of the work. Earth Sciences majors only.

subject: ERTH
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in earth sciences. Junior/ Senior standing only.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to mineral Physics
description: Scientific study of the materials that make up the Earth. Properties of minerals on micro- and macro-scales; their properties and behavior.

subject: ERTH
title: Hawaiian Geology
description: Consists of lectures, discussions, and field trips on the geologic processes and geologic history of the Hawaiian islands, with emphasis on writing communication.

subject: ERTH
title: Remote Compositional Analysis: Spectroscopy, Mineralogy, and Geochemistry of Planetary Surfaces
description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces. Comparative studies of fundamental planetary science phenomena. Planetary surface science discoveries. Sustainability of planetary environments.
prereq_raw: (101 or 105 or 107 or ASTR 150; and CHEM 161; and MATH 241 and 242 and PHYS 272) with a minimum grade of C+; or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Disasters: Geoethics and the Layman
description: Evaluates ethical practice of geoscience as it relates to studies of natural disasters that result from geological and meteorological phenomena and the means that earth scientists interact with the laymen.

subject: ERTH
title: Energy and Mineral Resources
description: Lecture and discussion on the origin, distribution and exploitation of fossil fuels, renewable energy resources and ore deposits. Coverage and detail will depend partly on student interest and background.

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Seminar
description: Gain professional training and practical experience giving scientific presentations emphasizing Earth and planetary sciences, including analysis of associated ethical issues. Grading is distributed 60/40 between three oral communication assignments and related ethics content.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data.

subject: ERTH
title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
description: Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites. Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Marine Geology
description: Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins.

subject: ERTH
title: Environmental Geochemistry
description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants.

subject: ERTH
title: Coastal Geochemistry
description: Covers aqueous geochemistry at the land-ocean interface, including the distribution of major and minor ions, trace metals, organic chemicals, and nutrients.
prereq_raw: 200 or 201, CHEM 162, and MATH 241 or MATH 251A; or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Plate Tectonics
description: Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses.

subject: ERTH
title: Earthquakes and Crustal Deformation
description: Earthquakes and crustal deformation through modern seismological and geodetic observations; elastic properties of rocks, seismic waves, causes, detection, and location of earthquakes; crustal motions of the earthquake cycle; tsunami generation, liquefaction, and planetary observations.

subject: ERTH
title: Engineering Geology
description: Solutions of geotechnical problems by geologists and engineers through recognition, characterization, evaluation, and assessment of geologic processes that impact people, engineering structures, and engineering operations. Group format. Junior standing and higher.
restrictions_raw: ERTH, GEOL, and CEE majors only.

subject: ERTH
title: Hydrogeology
description: Occurrence, characteristics, movement, quality, development, and contamination of water in the Earth’s crust.

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Remote Sensing
description: Combined lecture-lab on the concepts behind, geologic uses for, and techniques of satellite and airborne remote sensing. Lab work will consist of computer image processing. Field trips. Open to non-majors.

subject: ERTH
title: Geospatial Information
description: Combined lecture/lab covering the collection, analysis and use of geospatially registered field data.

subject: ERTH
title: Planetary Geology
description: Comparative geology of the terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, tectonism, geomorphology, weathering; manned and unmanned space exploration.

subject: ERTH
title: Lunar Geology
description: Introduction to the basics of the geology and spectroscopy of our Moon. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ERTH
title: Origin of the Solar System
description: Exploration of the origin and evolution of our solar system. Understanding the composition of the universe and its constituents (planets, asteroids, stars, comets, and meteorites).
prereq_raw: 101 or 103 or 104 or 106 or 130 and CHEM 161 and PHYS 170

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

subject: ERTH
title: Earth and Planetary Sciences Workshops
description: Designed for in-service school professionals to learn new approaches and concepts in the fields of earth and planetary sciences. Credits earned in these courses cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

subject: ERTH
title: Equations of Geophysics
description: Least-square approximation of functions by orthogonal series; potential, wave heat flow equations; boundary value problems; Bessel Hankel functions, spherical harmonics, potential theory, plane waves, spherical waves; emphasis on geophysics application.
prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A, PHYS 400, or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Explosive Volcanism
description: Explosive volcanic eruptions: from causes to consequences. Review of current physical volcanology including ascent and fragmentation of magma, transport and deposition processes in pyroclastic eruptions, volcanic crisis management and volcanic eruption scenarios. Seven-day field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Theoretical Petrology
description: Derivation of phase diagrams from basic thermodynamics principles. Equilibria of natural silicate systems. Crystal chemistry, kinetics, diffusion, etc., Applied to igneous and metamorphic petrology.

subject: ERTH
title: Petrology of Ocean Lithosphere
description: Petrogenesis of the oceanic lithosphere, including mantle processes and rocks from mid-ocean ridges, seamounts, oceanic hotspots, back-arc basins, and intra-oceanic arcs.

subject: ERTH
title: Disaster Science: Understanding Hazards and Disasters
description: Combined lecture/ discussion focusing on the scientific understanding of the forces and processes underlying natural hazards; and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and planning.

subject: ERTH
title: Lava Flow Rheology and Morphology
description: Effusion eruptions: from eruption to final flow form. Includes: rheology, effusion rate, heat loss, and field measurements, followed by inflation, flow forms, lava lakes, domes, flow hazard and modeling. Field trips to Kilauea and Makapuu.

subject: ERTH
title: Current Events in Volcanology
description: Discussion of active areas of volcanism and new publications on volcanology.

subject: ERTH
title: Submarine Volcanoes
description: Seminar exploring different aspects of submarine effusive and explosive volcanism, hydrothermal activity, and volcano-hosted ecosystems.

subject: ERTH
title: Isotopes and Trace Elements
description: Principles of radiogenic and stable isotope, and trace element geochemistry as applied to igneous petrology, mantle dynamics, plate tectonics, and terrestrial evolution.

subject: ERTH
title: Graduate Teaching Geology
description: For ERTH graduate students who lead, under faculty supervision, a scheduled class in Geology and Geophysics. The instructor will define the student’s responsibilities when offering ERTH 609, and these responsibilities must be met for a passing grade. As the consent to take the class must also be granted by the department chair, the chair will also review the responsibilities required by the instructor. ERTH graduate students only.
prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair

subject: ERTH
title: Graduate Seminar
description: Seminar in which students present a 15- to 20-minute talk on their research or a related topic. Meets once a week with two to three talks per meeting. Graduate students are required to register for this course once per year.

subject: ERTH
title: Accelerated Introduction to Earth Sciences I
description: Lecture presenting a rapid-paced survey of earth sciences for graduate students. Includes origin of the Solar System, tectonics, volcanology, whole-earth composition, phase transformations, petrology (igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary), historical geology, and hydrology. Saturday field trips.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data. Credit earned only one time for either 413 or 613.

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Field Study
description: Shipboard and land-based projects.

subject: ERTH
title: Literate Programming With R and RStudio
description: Literate programming with R, RStudio, and R Markdown for data analysis and research. Introduction to Matlab for rapid modeling. Emphasis on the preparation of research papers for scholarly publication in the Earth and environmental sciences.
prereq_raw: competence in basic differential and integral calculus

subject: ERTH
title: How to Write a Scientific Paper
description: Designed for students who have collected data and want to know how to publish their work in a scientific journal. Covers the essential parts of paper preparation and submission. ERTH students only.

subject: ERTH
title: Summer Fieldschool Program: Hydrogeophysics in Volcanic Environments
description: Will cover the full hydrogeophysical workflow including theory, acquisition design, field data acquisition, data processing, data inversion, and hydrogeological interpretation. Methods include ambient seismic, 3D electrical resistivity tomography and induced polarization, and self-potential.

subject: ERTH
title: Coastal Geology
description: Geological history and geologic framework of the Hawaiian shoreline. Modern climate change, paleoclimate, focus on sea level change. Modern coastal management and problems in the coastal environment. Coastal planning.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, credit earned one time

subject: ERTH
title: Electron Microprobe Analysis
description: Combined lecture-lab on the principles of geochemical analysis by electron microprobe and X-ray fluorescence. Hands-on experience with the electron microprobe. Required to operate the UH electron microprobe.

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Environmental Geochemistry
description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system and remediation methods. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase and isotope chemistry of environmental contaminants.

subject: ERTH
title: Numerical Modeling of Physical Systems
description: Finite difference, finite element, and other modeling techniques applied to geological and geophysical problems. Physical modeling of heat flow, molecular diffusion, solidification and melting, deformation, fluid flow, wave propagation, and other phenomena. (Once a year)

subject: ERTH
title: Geophysics–Solid, Fluid, and Wave Mechanics
description: Continuum mechanics in geophysics, as applied to the deformation of Earth materials (elastic, viscous, viscoelastic, and plastic deformations) and seismic wave propagation (body waves, surface waves, anisotropy, and attenuation).
prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170, PHYS 272, and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent)

children.text: for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 ( or equivalent)

subject: ERTH
title: Geophysics–Gravity, Magnetics, and Heat Transfer
description: Fundamental theory and practical applications of the use of gravity, magnetics, and heat conduction to probing the structure of the Earth; heat transfer via mantle convection is a major control on Earth’s internal structure.
prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170, PHYS 272, and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent)

children.text: for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 ( or equivalent)

subject: ERTH
title: Seismology
description: Elasticity, wave equations, body waves, surface waves, free oscillations, seismometry, seismogram interpretation, tectonics, inversion, source theory, and waveform modeling.

subject: ERTH
title: Earth System Science and Global Change
description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmospheric-sediment system and co-evolution of the biota.
prereq_raw: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus; or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Stable Isotope Biogeochemistry
description: Stable isotope geochemistry applied to questions of biogeochemical cycling in the oceans, sediment diagenesis, paleoceanography, environmental geochemistry and ecology.

subject: ERTH
title: Coastal Geochemistry
description: Geochemistry at the land-ocean interface: coastal hydrology, subterranean estuaries and coastal mixing and their importance in governing the distribution of selected radiotracers, trace metals and nutrients. Combined lecture-lab with field trips and group projects.
prereq_raw: CHEM 162, and MATH 241 or MATH 251A; or consent

subject: ERTH
title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
description: Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry.

subject: ERTH
title: Elemental Composition Changes
description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles.

subject: ERTH
title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions.
prereq_raw: CHEM 171, or CHEM 161 and CHEM 162; PHYS 152; and MATH 242 or MATH 252A; and consent

subject: ERTH
title: Geomagnetism and Cosmic Magnetism
description: Magnetic fields of Earth, planets, stars, and galaxies; dynamo theories; paleomagnetism; terrestrial and lunar rock magnetism; planetary, regional, and local geomagnetic sounding.

subject: ERTH
title: Groundwater Contamination
description: Principles of groundwater chemistry; chemical evolution in natural groundwater flow systems; sources of contamination; mass transport processes; hydrochemical behavior of contaminants.

subject: ERTH
title: Groundwater Modeling
description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation.

subject: ERTH
title: Astrochemistry–A Molecular Approach
description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

subject: ERTH
title: Planetary Surfaces
description: Comparative geology of terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, geomorphology; remote sensing; manned and unmanned space exploration.

subject: ERTH
title: Cosmochemistry
description: Formation and evolution of planets as astrophysical objects, geologic bodies, and abodes of life; current understanding from studies of the Solar System, star formation, meteorites, exoplanets; theory of formation and dynamics; atmospheres, oceans, habitability, biosignatures.

subject: ERTH
title: (Alpha) Remote Sensing
description: Spectroscopic, radar, thermal, and other methods for remote sensing applied to geologic problems; instrumental design and data analysis. (B) planets; (C) volcanoes.

subject: ERTH
title: Seminar in Tectonics
description: Evolution of ocean basins, margins, foldbelts, and platforms, from plate tectonics and regional syntheses of structure, petrology, geophysics, and stratigraphy. (Alt. years)

subject: ERTH
title: (Alpha) Extraterrestrial Material
description: Mineralogical and compositional characteristics of extraterrestrial matter and the implications for the origin and history of the solar system. The subject is treated in two full-semester courses: (B) meteorites; (C) petrology of the Moon and Mars.

subject: ERTH
title: Paleoceanography
description: Study of the paleoceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere and biosphere.

subject: ERTH
title: The Generic Mapping Tools
description: Introduction to the Generic Mapping Tools (GMT). Processing of scientific data and the automated preparation of maps and illustrations using GMT on UNIX workstations, with introduction to UNIX and the C shell environment.

subject: ERTH
title: Data Exploration and Processing
description: Time- and frequency analysis, filtering, factor and cluster analysis, interpolation, quantitative map analysis, and introduction to wavelets and fractals.

subject: ERTH
title: Bayesian Data Analysis
description: Linear and nonlinear techniques for model selection, parameter estimation, simulation and forecasting, from Bayesian principles with particular attention to large data sets and sparse noisy data.

subject: ERTH
title: Physics of the Earth’s Interior
description: Interpretation of geophysical and laboratory data to understand elastic and anelastic properties, composition, phase relationships, temperature distribution in the Earth.

subject: ERTH
title: Fractures and Faults
description: Lecture on elasticity theory, fracture mechanics and boundary element modeling, with application to faults and fractures in the Earth.

subject: ERTH
title: Selected Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
description: Content to be announced.

subject: ERTH
title: Special Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
description: Content to be announced.

subject: ERTH
title: MGeo Seminar
description: Seminar to improve student awareness of trends and practices in geoscience professions, and develop ability to prepare, deliver, and evaluate a professional scientific presentation. Targets abstract writing, oral presentation, and technical criticism.

subject: ERTH
title: MGeo Professional Project
description: Practical hands-on professional experience, typically with a local company or agency, and involving a final written report and an oral presentation. A grade of credit is assigned when the internship presentations are satisfactorily completed.

subject: GES
title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST. Restricted to GES majors.

subject: GES
title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability. (

subject: GES
title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
prereq_raw: 102 (or concurrent) or OCN 102 (or concurrent) or SUST 112 (or concurrent)

subject: GES
title: GES Thesis Proposal
description: Supports GES majors in producing a thesis proposal that outlines and describes the timeline, required resources, etc. of the degree-required project.

subject: GES
title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawai‘i. ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only. (Alt years: Spring) DP

subject: GES
title: The Changing Earth and Climate System
description: Covers the Earth system, including mass and energy transfers, biogeochemical cycles, natural and anthropogenic changes on regional and global scale.
prereq_raw: MATH 241, and GES 302 (or concurrent) and OCN 201 (or concurrent)

subject: GES
title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
description: (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement GES 311. Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling.
prereq_raw: 311, MATH 242, PHYS 170/170L, and CHEM 161/161L; or consent

subject: GES
title: Aquatic Pollution
description: Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives.

subject: GES
title: Environmental Data Science
description: Provides an introduction to environmental data science by applying python-based programming techniques to Earth science datasets.
prereq_raw: MATH 242, and ICS 110P or ICS 110C or ERTH 250

subject: GES
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science.

subject: GES
title: Biogeochemical Systems
description: Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course with an emphasis on improving student writing skills. Senior standing only.
prereq_raw: OCN 201, GES 311, BIOL 172/172L, CHEM 162/162L, ERTH 101/101L, GES 319L (or concurrent), ATMO 200 (or concurrent), and GES/OCN 499 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: GES
title: Earth’s Microbiome
description: Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
prereq_raw: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172

subject: GES
title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
prereq_raw: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172

subject: GES
title: Data Analysis in Earth Science
description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory.

subject: GES
title: Advanced Environmental Data Science
description: Advanced applications of environmental data science: combine data with Bayesian inference, make predictions using artificial neural networks, and analyze data in space and time using the Python language with biological and geophysical datasets.

subject: GES
title: Communication of Research Results
description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material. GES majors only in their final semester.

subject: GES
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST. Restricted to GES majors.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
prereq_raw: 102 (or concurrent) or GES 102 or (or concurrent) SUST 112 (or concurrent)

subject: OCN
title: Sustainability in a Changing World
description: Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawai‘i/Oceania. Active learning environment.

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Challenges
description: Scientific approach to evaluating human-caused environmental challenges and their potential solutions. Open to non-majors.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
description: Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real-world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics.
prereq_raw: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140X)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score required for MATH 140X

subject: OCN
title: Research Experiences in Marine Science
description: Inquiry-driven and experimental marine biology summer program based on the expertise of HIMB researchers whose specialties demonstrate how human impacts and global change affect coral reef ecosystems. Emphases on student team research projects. High school or UG freshman only.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Directed Research
description: Reading and research in any area of Oceanography under the direction of a faculty member.

subject: OCN
title: Science of the Sea
description: Origin and features of ocean basins and seawater; global cycles of carbon and nutrients; currents; waves; tides; characteristics of marine organisms; marine ecological principles; marine pollution; climate change causes and consequences. Online asynchronous; synchronous format.

subject: OCN
title: Science of the Sea Laboratory
description: Experiments, computer exercises, and field trips demonstrating the geological, physical, chemical, and biological principles of earth and ocean sciences.

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Change
description: Global environmental change problems such as carbon dioxide and the greenhouse effect, acid rain, chlorofluorocarbons and the ozone layer, global deforestation and the effect on climate, etc.
prereq_raw: 200, OCN 201, ERTH 101, ERTH 103, or ERTH 170; or consent

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods.

subject: OCN
title: The Role of Models in Global Environmental Science
description: Introduction to philosophy of science for those with some background in the natural sciences. Special emphasis on issues arising from the construction and use of models.
prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or any course 200 or above with either DB or DP designation, or consent

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
description: Introduction to environmental monitoring systems for earth science students. Students will learn how to construct, program, and deploy simple environmental monitoring systems to collect in-situ environmental data.
prereq_raw: 201/201L or ERTH 101/101L, CHEM 161/161L, and MATH 241; or consent

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
description: (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement GES 311. Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling.
prereq_raw: GES 311, MATH 242, PHYS 170/170L, and CHEM 161/161L; or consent

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Pollution
description: Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives.

subject: OCN
title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent

subject: OCN
title: Mineral and Energy Resources of the Sea
description: Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration, and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints.

subject: OCN
title: Living Resources of the Sea-Mai ke Kai Mai ke Ola
description: Marine fisheries, aquaculture, and law of the sea. Principles of management of renewable resources. Political and scientific constraints and limitations.

subject: OCN
title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawai‘i.
prereq_raw: (BIOL 171 and BIOL 172) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

subject: OCN
title: Undergraduate Internship
description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Undergraduate SOEST majors only. Open to GES majors. CR/ NC only.

subject: OCN
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science.

subject: OCN
title: Biogeochemical Systems
description: Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course with an emphasis on improving student writing skills. Senior standing only.
prereq_raw: 201, GES 311, BIOL 172/172L, CHEM 162/162L, ERTH 101/101L, GES 319L (or concurrent), ATMO 200 (or concurrent), and GES/OCN 499 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: OCN
title: Marine Functional Ecology and Biotechnology
description: Marine functional genomics, biodiversity of marine natural habitats, marine microbial communities and their ecological functions, interactions of marine microbes and their host, climate change and marine biodiversity, marine biotechnology.

subject: OCN
title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
description: Builds upon 318 using more advanced microprocessors and environmental sensors, 3D printing, programming, etc. to construct, program, and deploy environmental monitoring systems to collect and stream in-situ time-series environmental measurements.
prereq_raw: 318, MATH 242, PHYS 272/272L, and CHEM 162/162L; or consent

subject: OCN
title: Marine Geology
description: Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Deep-Sea Biology
description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deepsea organisms and communities. Topics including bentho-pelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction and global climate change.

subject: OCN
title: Climate Change and Urbanization
description: The following topics will be addressed: How are cities impacted by, and impacting climate change? How do urbanization, alteration of atmospheric processes, and extreme weather events affect urban systems and populations?

subject: OCN
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro.

subject: OCN
title: Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.

subject: OCN
title: Plate Tectonics
description: Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses.

subject: OCN
title: Aquaculture Production
description: Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics, and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery.
prereq_raw: ANSC 321 and ANSC 445: or BIOL 172/172L and CHEM 162/162L or higher

children.text: : or BIOL 172 / 172L and CHEM 162 / 162L or higher

subject: OCN
title: Earth’s Microbiome
description: Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
prereq_raw: 102 or 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172

subject: OCN
title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
prereq_raw: 102 or 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172

subject: OCN
title: Ridge to Reef: Coastal Ecosystem Ecology and Connectivity
description: Watershed and coastal biogeochemistry/ecosystem science. Emphasis on field surveying and sampling of stream and reef habitats; laboratory chemical/biological analyses. Analysis of land use impacts on ecosystem health and ahupua‘a resource management.
prereq_raw: 201/201L; and either OCN/ATMO 310, or GES 311; or consent

subject: OCN
title: Data Analysis in Earth Science
description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory.

subject: OCN
title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
description: Combined lecture and discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems.
prereq_raw: 201/201L, GES 311, GES 319L, and PHYS 272/272L; and consent

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
description: Introduction to modeling biogeochemical and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on plankton blooms. Students learn ecosystem dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming.
prereq_raw: (OCN/ATMO 310 or GES 311 or PHYS 272, and OCN/ERTH 312) with a minimum grade of B-

subject: OCN
title: Communication of Research Results
description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material. GES majors only in their final semester.

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Global Environmental Science
description: Lecture and discussion or seminar. Current topics in environmental science explored in detail. Typically offered by faculty in their specialties, or developed in response to student interest.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, credits earned up to six credits

subject: OCN
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

subject: OCN
title: Physical Oceanography
description: Introduction to properties of seawater, oceanographic instruments and methods, heat budget, general ocean circulation, regional oceanography, waves, tides, sea level. Formation of water masses, dynamics of circulation.

subject: OCN
title: Biological Oceanography
description: Factors governing productivity, population dynamics, distribution of organisms in major ecosystems of the ocean, emphasis on ecology of pelagic zone.

subject: OCN
title: Geological Oceanography
description: Marine geological processes, ocean basin structure and tectonics, sedimentation.

subject: OCN
title: Chemical Oceanography
description: Chemical processes occurring in marine waters; why they occur and how they affect oceanic environment.

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Photosynthesis
description: Biochemical and biophysical concepts of photosynthesis. Application and interpretation of ecological processes of photosynthesis in aquatic systems. Open to nonmajors.

subject: OCN
title: Marine Microplankton Ecology
description: Distribution, abundance, and ecology of marine microplankton, including bacteria, algae, and protozoans, with an emphasis on metabolic rates and processes.

subject: OCN
title: Ecology of Pelagic Marine Animals
description: Ecology of pelagic animals including feeding, energetics, predation, and anti-predation tactics. Life-history strategies, vertical flux of materials, population dynamics, fisheries.

subject: OCN
title: Benthic Biological Oceanography
description: Processes controlling the structure and function of benthic communities, including organism-sediment-flow interactions, sediment geochemistry, feeding strategies, recruitment, succession, and population interactions.

subject: OCN
title: Molecular Methods in Marine Ecology
description: Molecular methods for studying marine functional ecology; emphasis on hand-on tools for ecological and biogeochemical processes of microbes; developing practical skills for research project in marine microbial ecology and biological oceanography.

subject: OCN
title: Deep-Sea Biology
description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deep-sea organisms and communities. Topics including bentho-pelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction, and global climate change.

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Minerals
description: Distribution, origin, processes of formation. Sulfides, oxides, and placer minerals. Comparative studies of continental ore bodies. Submarine rift, subduction, and abduction.

subject: OCN
title: Biogeochemical Methods in Oceanography
description: Current methods of analysis used in the ocean sciences, both in the field and in the laboratory. An ocean-going field trip provides students with hands-on training in sample collection and processing. The latter is followed by laboratory analyses of the collected samples throughout the remainder of the semester.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and CHEM 161 and ERTH 101; or consent

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Chemistry
description: Chemical reactions support lie and stabilize Earth’s climate. We explore marine and fresh waters through chemical dquilibrium and reaction kinetics. Topics include mineral stability, ocean acidification, complexation/bioavailability, pollution, and quantitative approximation of natural systems.

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Microbial Geochemistry
description: The synergy between the biogeochemistry of element cycling and the microbial organisms involved, interfacing across disciplines from the perspective of a practical blend of aquatic chemistry, microbiology, biogeochemistry, and molecular biology.

subject: OCN
title: Earth System Science and Global Change
description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmosphere-sediment system and co-evolution of the biota.
prereq_raw: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus

subject: OCN
title: Observational Physical Oceanography
description: Application of the scientific method; physical regimes in the ocean; ocean processes and observational strategies; resolution, sampling, array design and observing systems; models and data assimilation; major field programs; operational oceanography and climate prediction.

subject: OCN
title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
description: Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry.

subject: OCN
title: Elemental Composition Changes
description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles.

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Marine Geochemistry
description: Seminar on a broad topic; discussion and critique of research papers.

subject: OCN
title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions.

subject: OCN
title: Math Techniques for Oceanographers
description: Introduction to numerical methods, data analysis, error propagation, box models, linear and nonlinear least squares, perturbation theory, numerical integration.

subject: OCN
title: Methods in Microbiology Oceanography
description: (1 8-hr Lab) Modern methods for sampling microbial populations from the sea and for quantifying biomass and in siturates of metabolism. Integrated field projects, theme varies.

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Waves I
description: Survey of wave types-acoustic, capillary, gravity, inertial, vorticity. Basic wave concepts emphasized: phase and group velocities, standing waves, energy conservation, dispersion, refraction, diffraction. Rotation and boundary effects are covered: reflection, basin modes, trapping, tides.

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Waves II
description: Baroclinic gravity waves, inertial waves, mid-latitude Rossby waves, topographic waves, equatorial waves.

subject: OCN
title: Marine Hydrodynamics
description: Introduction to classical hydrodynamics and continuum mechanics. Techniques for solution of Navier Stokes equations on various scales of oceanic motion; potential theory, dynamic modeling, and viscous and rotational processes.

subject: OCN
title: Satellite Oceanography
description: Techniques of satellite observations of the ocean, including temperature, pigment concentration, currents, and winds; analysis of a satellite data set as term project.

subject: OCN
title: Oceanographic Instrumentation and Technology
description: Measurement techniques in physical oceanography, including pressure, temperature, salinity, oxygen, optical sensors, current meters, navigation systems, ocean acoustics, and mooring structures. Includes a laboratory research project.

subject: OCN
title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes.
prereq_raw: MATH 402 and MATH 403 (or their equivalents) and either 620 or ATMO 600, or consent

children.text: ( or their equivalents) and either 620 or ATMO 600 , or consent

subject: OCN
title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the state-of-the-art theories and observations of large-scale ocean-atmosphere interaction, as well as conveying the fundamental understanding that has been developed during the past 30 years. Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Nino/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics I
description: Basic concepts and equations to describe large-scale ocean circulation; numerical models; boundary layers; models of wind-driven circulation of a homogeneous ocean.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics II
description: Thermodynamics of stratified fluids; convection; mixing; models of the thermohaline circulation; the role of eddies in the large-scale ocean circulation.

subject: OCN
title: Paleoceanography
description: Study of the paloeceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere, and biosphere.

subject: OCN
title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
description: Combined lecture/discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems.
prereq_raw: previous course in marine science, or consent

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
description: Introduction to modeling biological and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on biological production. Students will learn biological-physical dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming.

subject: OCN
title: Data Science Fundamentals in R
description: (3 hr Lec/Lab) Introduces project management, data analysis, and mathematical and statistical modeling using R as a platform. Students will learn principles and benefits of programming languages to apply skills to their own research.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Statistics in R
description: (2 hr Lec, 1 hr Lab) In-depth introduction to the modern statistical methods necessary for analyzing biological/ecological data, including GLMs, GAMs, mixed models, ordination, etc. Students will learn how to perform these methods in R.

subject: OCN
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Biological Oceanography
description: Seminar. Literature and concepts in one of several active fields considered in detail.
