repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, credits earned up to 12 credits

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Physical Oceanography
description: Near-shore processes, advanced mathematical techniques, recent developments, etc. Typically given by visiting professors in their specialties, or in response to student interest.

subject: OCN
title: Seminar
description: Oceanographic topics of current interest.

subject: OCN
title: Proposal Development
description: Introduction to the organization and functioning of oceanography funding agencies, the peer-review process, and the design and development of a research proposal.
prereq_raw: two of the following: 621, 626, 627 (or concurrent), or 628 (or concurrent); or consent

subject: OCN
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: OEST
title: International Exchange Study/Research
description: Study overseas in an approved international exchange or similar program.
restrictions_raw: GES, ERTH, and MET majors only.

subject: OEST
title: The College Experience
description: Required for entering SOEST majors to develop skills and applications for a successful college experience. Students will examine academic goals and implement strategies to achieve goals including time management and career exploration.

subject: OEST
title: Natural Hazards
description: Science of natural hazards: impact on human civilization of events in the lithosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere (e.g., earthquakes, hurricanes, red tides, and floods), and impact of humans on their exposure to and mitigation of the hazards.

subject: OEST
title: An Introduction to Integrative Systems Biology: Hawaiian Biomes as a Framework
description: Lecture/discussion introduces students to the field of biology through the integration of microbiology and macrobiology into a single, comprehensive systems biology with a focus on Hawaiian biomes and ecosystem sustainability.

subject: OEST
title: Contemporary Issues in Energy Systems
description: Introductory experience in energy systems including current status of fossil fuel, renewable energy technologies, energy utilization and conservation; environmental and policy aspects.

subject: OEST
title: Ethics in Scientific Research
description: Introduction to issues of ethics in scientific research and scientific misconduct. ERTH, GES, or ATMO majors only.

subject: OEST
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Introduction to the principles of sustainability analysis through execution of Life Cycle Analysis applied to products, processes, or systems. LCA and the evaluation of environmental impact will be presented. Personal computer or laptop (Word 97 or higher) OS, and minimum of 4GB RAM. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: (CHEM 161 and PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent

subject: OEST
title: Earth Sciences Professional Development Education
description: Specialized Earth Science topics workshops designed for in-service teachers who wish to learn new approaches and content areas in geology and geophysics, meteorology and oceanography. Credits earned cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

subject: OEST
title: Communicating Ocean Sciences
description: Application of current learning theory and pedagogical practices in formal and informal learning environments to improve communication and instructional skills. Graduate students from multiple science disciplines welcome. Requires knowledge of biology, earth sciences, and/or chemistry.
prereq_raw: at least one course in introductory biology, geology, earth science, chemistry or marine science, an interest in ocean science, and enthusiasm for teaching science; or consent

children.text: at least one course in introductory biology, geology, earth science, chemistry
marine science, an interest in ocean science,

repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to 3 credits

subject: OEST
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Selected interdisciplinary ocean/earth-related topics involving science, technology, engineering, and/or policy.

subject: OEST
title: Ocean Policy and Management
description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing the world’s oceans and coasts at all scales and on the role of scientific knowledge in managing marine and coastal resources.

subject: ORE
title: Ocean Technology—Man in the Sea
description: Survey of human activities in the ocean, from the most traditional to the most innovative technical and engineering accomplishments.

subject: ORE
title: Surf Science and Culture
description: Introduction to wave science covering generation, propagation, transformation, and coastal processes related to surfing and the human interaction with the ocean using Western science and cultural perspectives.

subject: ORE
title: Surf Science and Culture Lab
description: Practical laboratory dedicated to wave science covering generation, propagation, transformation, and coastal processes related to surfing and the ocean environment through technology.

subject: ORE
title: Mineral and Energy Resources
description: Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints.

subject: ORE
title: Buoyancy and Stability
description: Ship nomenclature and geometry, hydrostatic principles of surface ships and underwater vehicles in free-floating, partially waterborne, and damaged conditions. Subdivision of ships. Launching.

subject: ORE
title: Ocean and Resources Engineering Laboratory
description: Design, construction, and evaluation of an engineering system. Laboratory and field experience and data analysis supplemented with appropriate theory.

subject: ORE
title: Oceanography for Ocean Engineers
description: Physical, chemical, biological, and geological ocean environments for ocean engineers. Introduction to ocean dynamical processes and general circulation. Ocean measurement techniques, theory of underwater acoustics. Sonar, swath bathymetry, and tomography applications.

subject: ORE
title: Water Wave Mechanics
description: Governing equations in free surface flow, deterministic and probabilistic wave theories, wave transformation, wave-induced coastal currents, tides, ocean engineering operational sea state, and design wave criteria.

subject: ORE
title: Probability and Statistics for Ocean Engineers
description: Probability and statistical analysis including distributions, multiple regression and correlation, autocovariance, cross-spectra, and practical applications in ocean engineering.

subject: ORE
title: Hydrodynamics of Fluid-Body Interaction
description: Hydrodynamics of ships, coastal and offshore structures. Wave forces by potential theory and by Morison’s equation. Method of source distribution for potential flow problems. Flows with prescribed body motion, fixed and freely floating bodies.

subject: ORE
title: Dynamics of Ocean Structures
description: Response of floating platforms and vessels to wave action, spectral analysis in sea keeping. Frequency and time domain analyses of rigid body motions in six degrees of freedom.

subject: ORE
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk.
prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable

subject: ORE
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change.

subject: ORE
title: Structural Analysis in Ocean Engineering
description: Structural and finite element analyses and design of ocean structures to withstand hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loading of the sea. Considerations include material type, safety factor, stress concentration, and fatigue.

subject: ORE
title: Environmental Fluid Dynamics
description: Fluid dynamics for coastal and estuarine environments. Turbulent mixing processes in homogeneous and stratified fluids. Buoyancy driven flows, internal hydraulics, topographic effects and estuarine circulation. Spill and pollutant dispersal.

subject: ORE
title: Applications in Ocean Acoustics
description: Using sound to observe the ocean. Fundamentals of propagation. Topics include marine mammals, navigation and communication, seismics, ships, wind and rain, ocean dynamics, flow and biological imaging and measurement, seafloor mapping, and the forward/ inverse problem.

subject: ORE
title: Autonomous Marine Systems
description: Identifies the unique challenges faced by autonomous underwater and surface vehicles, and analyzes approaches to address those challenges. Topics include hydrodynamic vehicle modeling, propeller theory, subsystem integration, and motion control strategies. Graduate students only.
prereq_raw: MATH 307 or MATH 311 (or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 (or equivalent), or instructor consent

children.text: ( or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 ( or equivalent), or instructor consent

subject: ORE
title: Coastal and Harbor Engineering
description: Planning and design of seawalls, groins, jetties, breakwaters, and layout of ports. Design requirements for harbor entrances and channels. Littoral drift and sedimentation problems. Navigation and mooring requirements.

subject: ORE
title: Nearshore Processes and Sediment Transport
description: coastal areas and its effect on morphological processes. Effect of man-made structures on littoral drift and shoreline.

subject: ORE
title: Marine Renewable Energy
description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power.

subject: ORE
title: Marine Mineral Resources Engineering
description: Activities in marine minerals development are examined in a multidisciplinary systems approach involving engineering, Earth and environmental sciences and economics.

subject: ORE
title: Ocean Engineering and Resilience in a Changing Climate
description: Focus on understanding the changing ocean conditions (e.g. waves and sea levels) relevant to the resilience of practical ocean engineering applications. Graduate students only.

subject: ORE
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.

subject: ORE
title: Thesis Research
prereq_raw: candidacy for MS in ocean and resources engineering

subject: ORE
title: Nonlinear Water Wave Theories
description: Higher-order theories. Forced oscillations. Stoke’s theory. Nonlinear shallow-water wave equations and hydraulic jumps; effects of rotation. Internal waves. Analytical techniques necessary will be developed as course progresses.

subject: ORE
title: Numerical Methods in Ocean Engineering
description: Formulation and application of numerical methods for simulating and solving ocean engineering problems. Mathematical and computational fundamentals; accuracy and stability; numerical interpolation, differentiation, and integration; boundary element, finite difference, and finite element methods.

subject: ORE
title: (Alpha) Capstone Design Project
description: Major design experience based on knowledge and skills acquired in earlier course work and incorporating realistic constraints that include economic, environmental, ethical, social, and liability considerations. Emphasis is placed on teamwork and consultant-client relationship. (B) coastal engineering; (C) offshore engineering; (D) ocean resources engineering; (E) oceanic engineering.
prereq_raw: (411, 603, and 607) with a minimum grade of B-; or consent. (Fall only for (E))

subject: ORE
title: Special Topics in Ocean and Resources Engineering
description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting and permanent faculty.

subject: ORE
title: Seminar in Ocean and Resources Engineering
description: Attendance at 15 approved seminars is required along with submission of notes.

subject: ORE
title: Dissertation Research
prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD in ocean and resources engineering

subject: BIOL
title: Biology and Society
description: Characteristics of science, historical development of scientific concepts, and interaction of society with science illustrated by topics from biological science. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology & Society Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawai‘i. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Option Program Seminar
description: Overview of ocean issues and organizations involved with marine activities, management, education, research, and business. Exploration of internships, research, and career opportunities. Preparation of resumes, proposals, and professional presentations. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Current Topics in Biomedical Research Seminar
description: Overview of contemporary laboratory- and population-based studies of disease. Discussion of career pathways in human health sciences. Public health and epidemiology of cancer.

subject: BIOL
title: Hawaiian Environment Science
description: Characteristics of science and interaction with society illustrated by topics in geology, astronomy, oceanography, and biology of Hawaiian Islands. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology I
description: Introductory biology for all life science majors. Cell structure and chemistry; growth, reproduction, genetics, evolution, viruses, bacteria, and simple eukaryotes.
prereq_raw: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 171L (or concurrent), or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology I Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 171. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
prereq_raw: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 171 (or concurrent) or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology II
description: Anatomy, physiology, and systematics of plants and animals; behavior; ecosystems, populations, and communities.
prereq_raw: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 172L (or concurrent), or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology II Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 172.
prereq_raw: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 172 (or concurrent) or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Biostatistics
description: Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R.
prereq_raw: 171 or 172 or BOT 101; MATH 134 or higher, or MATH assessment exam

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
description: Principles of ecology and evolution for life science majors stressing integrated approach and recent advance.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 171/171L, 172, 172L (or concurrent)

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 265. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 265 (or concurrent)

subject: BIOL
title: Cell and Molecular Biology
description: Integrated cell and molecular biology for life science majors. Modern advances in recombinant DNA technology.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 171/171L and CHEM 272

subject: BIOL
title: Cell and Molecular Biology Lab
description: (1 4-hr Lab) Laboratory for Cell and Molecular Biology.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 275 (or concurrent) and CHEM 272

subject: BIOL
title: Service Learning for Biology Majors
description: Directed participation on tutorials and related activities in public schools and approved community and UH Mānoa organizations.

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Ecology and Evolution
description: Ecological and evolutionary factors creating and maintaining patterns of biological diversity in major marine ecosystems. Emphasis on the biphasic life histories of many marine organisms. The development of quantitative skills and critical thinking.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 265, 301L (or concurrent), and OCN 201; or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Ecology and Evolution Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 301.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 301 (or concurrent)

subject: BIOL
title: Biotechnology: Science and Ethical Issues
description: Introduction to the concepts, goals, ethical issues and consequences of biotechnology using real-life case studies of GMOs, cloning, DNA fingerprinting, gene therapy and genetical engineering.
prereq_raw: 171 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology
description: General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment.

subject: BIOL
title: Ethology
description: Introduction to animal and human ethology and sociobiology; emphasis on social and interspecific behavior, its causes and adaptive significance. Lab optional.
prereq_raw: 171 and 171L and 172 and 172L or ANSC 201; or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Ethology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Application of methods in the study of animal behavior by demonstrations, labs and projects.

subject: BIOL
title: Environmental Issues
description: Global environmental problems in historical perspective; physical, biological, sociocultural views.
prereq_raw: one of 101, 123, or GEO 101; or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Vertebrates
description: Introduction to the evolution and systematics of vertebrates, with emphasis on comparative morphology, physiology, and ecology.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Vertebrates Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 325.

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Mammal Biology
description: Overview of marine mammal science, significance and roles of marine mammals in their ecosystems, and marine conservation issues. Current research topics in marine mammal science will also be covered.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 171/171L, 172/172L, and 265, 265L; or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics, Evolution and Society
description: The role of genetics in evolution, medicine, behavior, plant and animal breeding and technology; its impact on today’s society. Not a BIOL major elective.
prereq_raw: one semester of biological science at college level or consent

children.text: one semester of biological science at college level

subject: BIOL
title: Parasitology
description: Animal parasites of man, and domestic and wild animals; systematics, comparative morphology, life history, pathology, treatment, control.

subject: BIOL
title: Sex Differences in the Life Cycle
description: Human sex differences, their biological basis and significance, ethical considerations of genetic, hormonal, and behavioral determinants of sexual differentiation; biology of gender, sexuality, parenting, menopause, and aging.

subject: BIOL
title: Island Ecosystems
description: Characteristics of island biota; examples from Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Impact of island and continental cultures; policy and ecosystem endangerment; contemporary legislation, policy, and management practices.
prereq_raw: one semester of biological science or consent. Not a BIOL major elective

subject: BIOL
title: Biological Field Studies
description: Biological survey, collection, and analysis techniques will be reviewed and applied through field studies. Students will be introduced to the uniqueness of the Hawaiian environment and its diversity of life. Emphasis on diversity, evolution and ecology.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 265/265L (or equivalent), or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics
description: Genetic concepts at advanced undergraduate level; genetic transmission, recombination, gene action, mutation, population and evolutionary genetics.

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics Laboratory
description: (1 4-hr Lab) Experiments with a variety of organisms to illustrate principles discussed in BIOL 375.

subject: BIOL
title: Communicating in Biological Sciences
description: Combined lecture/lab impart essential knowledge and skills in technical writing, poster design, and oral presentations for effective communication for life science majors. Research papers, lab reports, project proposals, conference presentations are covered.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 171/171L, 172/172L, and ENG 100

subject: BIOL
title: (Alpha) Teaching Internship
description: Teaching internship in the Life Sciences that includes the preparation and demonstration of laboratory experiments or classroom activities. (B) general; (C) oral emphasis, includes emphasis on instruction in oral communication.

subject: BIOL
title: Ocean Internships and Research
description: Students carry out marine-related internships, practica, research projects or field experience on-or off-campus with faculty guidance.
prereq_raw: minimum cum GPA of 2.5, junior or senior standing in any field of study and IS 100/BIOL 104 or consent, project proposal

children.text: in any field of study and IS 100 / BIOL 104 or consent , project proposal

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Biotechnology
description: General principles, applications, and recent advances of the rapidly growing science of biotechnology. Topics include impact of biotechnology on medicine, animal sciences, environment, agriculture, forensics, and economic and socio-ethical issues.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 275 or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Biotechnology Lab-Gene Editing by CRISPR/Cas9
description: (1-hr Lec, 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 401. Students learn advanced gene editing techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9 to engineer prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

subject: COA
title: Directed Reading and Research forJuniors and Seniors
description: Individual reading or research under supervision of COA-affiliated faculty. Juniors and seniors only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to nine credits

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Public Health
description: Introduces public health concepts with an emphasis on principles and tools for population health, disease prevention, health professions and healthcare systems, and public health professions and systems.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Issues in Hawai‘i
description: Application of general public health concepts and tools with broader public health issues as they relate to the State of Hawai‘i.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Global Health
description: Introduction to the basic principles of global PH. Topics include the application of these principles to global PH issues, exploration of links between health, economic, and social status, health disparities and global interventions.

subject: PH
title: Quantitative Reasoning for Public Health
description: Inductive and deductive reasoning; tabular, symbolic, verbal, and graphical forms of functions and relations; graphs and pictorial representations of data; interpretations of probabilistic data; surveys and statistical studies as related to public health.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Student Success in the College Experience
description: Required for entering PH majors to gain strategies for a successful college experience while studying public health. Students will examine academic and career goals and implement strategies to achieve them.

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Public Health Issues
description: Seminar will explore current issues and case studies in epidemiology, issues and causes of chronic and infectious diseases, how the environment interacts with health, and how social and behavioral factors affect personal health.

subject: PH
title: Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
description: Seminar to work with faculty in applying evidence-based knowledge on social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Epidemiology
description: Lecture/discussion on the fundamental principles of epidemiology, exploring patterns of disease, threats to health and EPI methods for prevention, control, and treatment.
prereq_raw: 201, and 210 or MATH 140X or MATH 161 or higher; or instructor approval

subject: PH
title: Youth Risk and Protection–Public Health Research, Practice, and Policy
description: Application of public health, related to youth health risks and protective factors using an eco-developmental framework.

subject: PH
title: The United States Health Care System
description: Overview of the U.S. health care system. Topics will include health economics, health service expenditures, comparative health systems, health policy, and issues of cost containment, access, and quality of care.

subject: PH
title: Public Health and the Environment
description: Examines a variety of issues associated with environmental effects on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. Sophomore standing and above.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Biology and Pathophysiology
description: Explores the biological basis of human disease and the role public health measures play in reducing both the extent and impact of chronic and acute diseases on individuals and society.
prereq_raw: 201, and one of the following: BIOL 101 or BIOL 171 or BIOL 172 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 141 or FSHN 185

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Biostatistics
description: Basic biostatistics methods in public health and biomedical research. Topics covered include data collection, data analyses, and interpretation of statistical results.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Epidemiology
description: Students will gain a deeper understanding of the core concepts used in epidemiologic research and practice. Upon completion, students will have the knowledge and skills necessary to conduct an epidemiologic study. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Nutrition and Disease Prevention
description: Lecture/discussion. Examines a variety of issues associated with the effects of diet on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Social Behavioral Health I: Health Promotion for Individuals and Groups
description: Focus on the application of social and behavioral theory in health education, and how health promotion programs are constructed for various populations with an emphasis on cultural diversity and social determinants of health. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Social Behavioral Health II: Health Promotion in Communities
description: Introduction to health education and health promotion programming in public health, and to social/behavioral theories used to develop health interventions that affect communities, institutions, and policies. Introduction to common program planning models.

subject: PH
title: Tobacco & Community Disparities
description: Assessing the facilitators and barriers of smoking initiation, cessation, and exposure to second-hand smoke within communities. Use of photovoice and its application to policy and addressing disparities.

subject: PH
title: Health Policy and Management
description: Examines the role that health policy and management plays in population-based public health practice, including the delivery, quality, and costs of health care and the structure, process, and outcomes of health services delivery. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.
prereq_raw: 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200; or consent

subject: PH
title: Introduction to One Health
description: Familiarizes students with the fundamentals of One Health–an interdisciplinary field of study linking ecosystems to human and animal health. It uses contemporary examples and emphasizes oceans and human health connections. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: (201, or ANSC 200, or BIOC 141, or BIOL 101, or BIOL 171, or BOT 101, or ERTH 101, or GES 102, or OEST 101, or OCN 102, or ATMO 150, or SOC 180) with a minimum grade of C or better; or consent

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Environmental Microbiology
description: Lecture/discussion. Will define the nature and biological activities of microorganisms in different environments and evaluate the effects of these microbes on human activities and health. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Social Determinants of Indigenous Peoples’ Health
description: Examines indigenous peoples’ health inequities using social determinants of health framework: considers this approach within the historical, political, cultural, and social context of Indigenous population’s health status to generate solutions.

subject: PH
title: Application of Public Health Principles in Research and Practice
description: Introduction to a diverse range of public health projects and associated methods while working to develop a written applied learning project literature review. Students will present their findings at a public forum. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Applied Learning Experience
description: Allows students to execute an independent, mentor-supervised, applied learning project as implementation of skills learned in previous public health coursework. Applied project is a required component of the public health undergraduate degree program.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Undergraduate Capstone Seminar
description: Synthesis of public health knowledge, skills, and practice acquired during the public health undergraduate degree. Students also reflect on, finalize, and present written applied learning experience projects at a public form. Senior standing and higher.
prereq_raw: completed public health applied learning experience and consent

children.text: completed public health applied learning experience

subject: PH
title: (Alpha) Current Issues and Topics in Public Health
description: Current and emerging issues and varying topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (T) public health. Each alpha Open to nonmajors. Sophomore standing and above.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Foundations
description: Focus will provide a broad introduction to the field of public health and orientation to overarching issues in the field.

subject: PH
title: U.S. Health Care Services and Policy
description: Overview of the historical, conceptual, ethical and political context for health care delivery in the U.S. Explores current trends, practices and issues in the delivery of health care services in both private and public sector.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Biology
description: Writing-intensive asynchronous computer-based course examines biological processes and challenges relevant to the public health professional. Topics include anatomical, pathophysiological, and molecular bases of public health; genetics, immunology, ethics; disease prevention, control, and management. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Fundamentals to One Health
description: Familiarizes students with the fundamentals of One Health–an interdisciplinary field of study linking ecosystems to human and animal health. It uses contemporary examples and emphasizes oceans and human health connections. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Health Promotion Theory and Methods
description: Individual and community health; implications for public health practice, individual and social change processes.

subject: PH
title: Health Economics
description: Integrated concepts in health economics and its application towards health policy issues; market failures in health care; factors affecting U.S. health care spending potential impact on equity/efficiency stemming from changes in health care delivery. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Cultural Competency in Health Care
description: Presents both analytical and practical approaches to cultural competency domains, concepts, models, frameworks, patterns and communication that occur in cross-cultural healthcare situations.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Health Activism
description: Examines how Indigenous Peoples and their allies (individually and collectively) accomplish social change in society. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Health Seminar
description: Examines public health through an Indigenous lens, integrates competencies across all public health disciplines, and will apply them in context of working for and with Indigenous communities to improve health and wellness. PH majors or consent. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Topics in Health Policy
description: Examines major federal and local policies that impact health and health care delivery in the U.S. and other nations; considers effectiveness of these policy-making institutions for improving population health; covers methods in policy analysis.

subject: PH
title: Grant Writing in Public Health
description: Lecture/discussion on grant writing with public health focus. Includes basic components of grant proposals, assessing appropriate funding opportunities, data sources/resources for justifying grants, and the funder’s perspective. Student will prepare a brief foundation grant proposal. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Program Planning, Management, Evaluation, and Leadership
description: Foundation to inform, educate, and improve health for individuals, communities, and populations. Knowledge/acquisition of skills through program planning, management, evaluation and leadership that span the social-ecological range from individual-level to population-level programs.

subject: PH
title: Needs Assessment
description: Knowledge and skills acquisition in conducting needs assessment in public health practice.

subject: PH
title: Ecological Epidemiology
description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies.

subject: PH
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar
description: Topics such as contemporary issues in global health and population studies, international health programs, demographic methods, global economy and health, human right and humanitarian assistance, social justice, global environmental changes and health.

subject: PH
title: Global Health and Human Security
description: Provides the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to successfully manage health security crises and protect human vulnerability in the global context with a special focus on problems with high likelihood and risk in the Pacific.

subject: PH
title: Biostatistics I
description: Introduction to statistical methods for public health sciences. Probability, experimental design, t tests and analysis of variance, 2X2 contingency tables, linear regression, introduction to life tables.

subject: PH
title: Biostatistics II
description: Poisson distribution, Fisher’s exact test, contrasts in ANOVA, two way ANOVA, multiple linear regression and analysis of covariance, path analysis, logistic regression, method of maximum likelihood, likelihood ratio tests.
prereq_raw: 655, completion of one semester of calculus; or consent

children.text: completion of one semester of calculus;

subject: PH
title: Computer Applications in Public Health
description: Applications of computers to problems common to public health. Emphasis on data analysis and processing using existing computer programs.

subject: PH
title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, and urbanization; projections and stable population theory.

subject: PH
title: Principles of Epidemiology I
description: Introduction to epidemiologic principles and methods. Topics covered include: outbreak investigation, measures of morbidity and mortality, measurements of risk, biological variability, screening, measurements of error, sampling, statistical significance, study design, and association and causation.

subject: PH
title: Principles of Epidemiology II
description: Lecture/discussion on: design and interpretation of experimental and observational studies; causation and casual inference; biases in study design; random error and statistics role in epidemiology; and epidemiological data analysis.

subject: PH
title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions.

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Infectious Disease Control
description: Strategies for controlling important infectious diseases in the Pacific area. Emphasis on epidemiology, ecology, and public health principles.
prereq_raw: 663 (or concurrent) and one semester in microbiology, or consent

subject: PH
title: Infectious Disease Micro II
description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented.

subject: PH
title: Epidemiological Study Design Critique
description: Critique of study design using published public health literature. Emphasis on exchange of ideas, alternative approaches; stresses epidemiology as science of public health.

subject: PH
title: Community and Public Health Practice
description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery.

subject: PH
title: Leading and Managing Health Programs
description: Assess how to organize community partnerships to create and communicate a shared vision for a changing future; discuss solutions to organizational and community challenges; maximize motivation to reach public health goals.

subject: PH
title: Native Health Ethics, Law, and Policy
description: Review theories and laws concerning health care ethics, policy, and practice using Indigenous case studies. Topics include Indigenous health systems, advocacy, and the intersecting issues of self-determination, ethics, agenda setting, and the policy cycle. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Advanced Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
description: Applications of evidence-based knowledge about the social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians.

subject: PH
title: Community Engaged Research and Practice
description: Explores collaborative and engaged approaches with communities in public health research and practice. With a focus on Indigenous Peoples’ health, we delve into Indigenous knowledge and empowerment in evaluation, needs assessment, intervention, and health promotion. PH majors or consent. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Hawai‘i Public Health Policies on Infectious Diseases
description: Examines quarantine/ isolation of patients infected with Hanson’s disease. Focus on PH policies before 1823 and after; analysis of other infections in Hawai‘i and the world to examine differences in policies and their effect on the public. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Managing Global Health Service Delivery
description: Provides knowledge, skills, attitudes and resources that health managers require to manage and maintain the quality of partnerships, facilities, programs, community services, people, drugs, and information in limited resources settings.

subject: PH
title: Health Emergencies in Large Populations
description: Health Emergencies in Large Populations is run by the Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance and the Red Cross. It provides knowledge, practical skills, and networking for global health practitioners.

subject: PH
title: Environmental Determinants of Health
description: Environmental factors in personal and community health; implications for public health practice. Consideration of major issues from local, U.S., and international perspectives.

subject: PH
title: Global Nutrition
description: Examination of global food and nutrition problems, programs, issues, policies, and strategies for improvement.

subject: PH
title: Supplemental and Nutritional Approaches in Disease Prevention and Treatment
description: Examines a variety of issues associated with nutritional and supplemental approaches to reduce disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Child and Adolescent Nutrition
description: Addresses nutrition, growth, and development in children and adolescents and nutrition-related issues, such as childhood obesity and chronic disease risk factors, with a focus on current research in the Pacific region.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Peoples’ Food Systems, Environment and Health
description: Explores Indigenous Peoples’ food systems as local food resources Indigenous People acquire through specific cultural knowledge of traditional territories. Global forces transforming these food systems and their impact on population health and nutrition are explored. PH majors or consent. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Nutritional Epidemiology
description: Dietary, biochemical, anthropometric and clinical methods used for evaluating nutrition and diet in the etiology and epidemiology of disease.

subject: PH
title: Global Health Challenges
description: Addresses critical, contemporary, and transnational issues best addressed by cooperative international action. Health issues are examined in the context of intersecting effects of limited resources, socioeconomics, politics, and environmental change. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Fundamentals of Environmental Epidemiology
description: Examines the complex relationship between environmental contaminants and human health. Emphasis on environmental epidemiology study design, environmental exposure monitoring and risk assessment, disease and environmental exposure mapping, and spatial data analysis and modeling with GIS. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Promoting Physical Activity
description: Overview of the theoretical and applied study of physical activity epidemiology. Physical activity content includes benefits, factors that influence, levels, valid instruments to assess, and programs to promote physical activity.

subject: PH
title: Health Communication
description: Skills-oriented course introduces the basic structure of health communication strategies in different settings, selected elements of communication theory, the development of health communication material, and a practical training in motivational counseling skills.

subject: PH
title: Health Promotion Research
description: Focus on research methods commonly used in health promotion. Topics will include randomized trials, quasi-experimental design, sampling, measurement, and correlational studies. Labwork will focus on the use of SPSS to analyze data for applied research problems.

subject: PH
title: Community-Based Participatory Research
description: Explores ways academic and lay communities collaborate on research, key theoretical perspectives in the development of CBPR, and the challenges in implementing CBPR approaches. Format includes lectures, discussions, readings, writing assignments, and a fieldwork project.

subject: PH
title: Systematic Literature Review in Public Health
description: Imparts skills in conducting a systematic review of the literature. Students provided critiques by instructor and classmates on their written and presented work. Intended for doctoral students to complete their qualifying paper. PH majors only; doctoral students only.
prereq_raw: consent or PhD in PH or EPID only

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Applied Research Methods
description: Qualitative research methods design, implementation, and analysis with special focus on methodological, ontological, and ethical issues unique to conducting research with Indigenous communities.

subject: PH
title: Survey Methods for Indigenous People
description: Advanced application of health disparities research methodologies to address health and social injustices faced by Indigenous people. Grounded in survey design, implementation, and analyses through a public health and Indigenous lens. PH majors only or consent. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Qualitative Research for Public Health Sciences
description: Provides a basic understanding of qualitative research approaches, methodologies, and techniques and for public health research and practice (needs assessment, program development, and evaluation strategies). Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Statistical Methods in Epidemiological Research
description: Multiple variable statistical methods currently used in chronic disease epidemiology. Logistic regression, conditional logistic regression, proportional hazards regression modelling, generalized estimating equation-based methods, delta method approximations, exact tests.

subject: PH
title: Chronic Disease Epidemiology
description: Will cover selected topics in chronic diseases with critical analysis of the current epidemiologic literature. Methodologic issues, contemporary findings and recommendations for future research will be discussed.

subject: PH
title: Epidemiology of Diabetes and Obesity
description: Provides an overview of the epidemiology and prevention of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and associated complications. Discusses methodological issues associated with evaluating these in epidemiologic studies.

subject: PH
title: Health Behavior Change
description: Provide an understanding of the relationship between health behaviors and outcomes including psychological, physiological, and quality of life aspects. It will also focus on the major theories of behavior and behavior change. Emphasis will be placed on understanding concepts, principles, explanations, and how these are translated into practical interventions for adoption and maintaining behavior change.

subject: PH
title: Social Epidemiology
description: Examine the epidemiologic study of the social distribution and social determinants of states of health, including the identification of social-environmental exposures and their relation to physical and mental health outcomes.

subject: PH
title: Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis
description: Covers modern methods for longitudinal data analysis. Topics include random effects and growth curve models, generalized linear models for longitudinal data including generalized estimating equations, and generalized linear mixed models.

subject: PH
title: Survival Analysis
description: Construction and interpretation of various types of life tables, treatment of censored data, proportional hazards, relative risk regression models, and parametric survival analysis.

subject: PH
title: Neuroepidemiology
description: Lecture/discussion providing an overview of the epidemiology of neurological and neurodegenerative diseases and their risk factors, and methodological considerations for the study of these diseases.

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Tropical Medicine and Public Health
description: Weekly discussion and reports on current advances in tropical medicine and public health.

subject: PH
title: Special Topics in Tropical Medicine
description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health. Repeatable unlimited times.

subject: PH
title: Evolution, Epidemiology, and Public Health
description: Will explore several aspects of human health through the perspective of how natural selection and evolution influence disease risk, with the aim of improving treatment and prevention. Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Health Program Evaluation
description: Examines advanced principles of and frameworks for evaluation. Students integrate utilization-focused evaluation methods to improve service delivery and quality, outcomes and impact to improve community and population health.

subject: PH
title: (Alpha) Doctoral Seminar in Translational Research
description: Required for students in the PhD PH program. (D) evidence-based public health; (E) health policy and leadership.

subject: PH
title: Teaching Practicum
description: Provide doctoral students with theoretical and practical teaching and course development experiences under the guidance of a faculty mentor. Students will have a portfolio documenting their accomplishments. Graduate standing in PH only.
prereq_raw: 602 and 623 and 655 and 663 and 681 and 770(Alpha), or departmental approval

subject: PH
title: Research Practicum
description: Hands-on research experience with a faculty mentor. Meet in small groups to discuss issues related to research in public health. Final project will be submission of a publishable quality paper. Graduate standing in PH only.
prereq_raw: 602 and 623 and 655 and 663 and 681 and 770(Alpha), or departmental approval

subject: PH
title: Public Health Proposal and Dissertation Writing
description: Intended for doctoral students to complete and defend their proposals and dissertations. Research and presentation methods will be reviewed, and students will be provided critiques by instructor and classmates on their written and presented work.
prereq_raw: consent or PhD in PH or EPID only

subject: PH
title: Environmental Health Lab Methods
description: Hands-on training for laboratory methods used in monitoring and detecting environmental health risk factors; learning and application of immunological-, animal cell culture- and molecular biology-based techniques for studying environmental pathogens and toxic pollutants. (Once a year)

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Public Health Sciences
description: Topics related to recent developments in major areas; student and faculty research activities. Sections: (1) biostatistics; (2) environmental health; (3) epidemiology; (4) public health nutrition.

subject: PH
title: Integrative Seminar
description: Integrative seminar in public health required as part of the student capstone experience to bring together key aspects of their courses, competencies, and practicum.
prereq_raw: completed PH field practicum and consent

subject: PH
title: Advanced Public Health Practice
description: Observation, study, and supervised practical work in student’s area of specialization.
prereq_raw: public health degree candidate and completion of 15 PH credit hours and consent

subject: PH
title: (Alpha) Current Issues and Topics in Public Health
description: Current and emerging issues and topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Indigenous Health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health. PH majors only for (D) and (I).

subject: PH
title: Special Practicum/Project
description: Supervised practical training beyond the required practicum in an area of particular interest. Provides additional opportunity to synthesize, integrate, and apply practical skills and knowledge in a public health work environment.

subject: PH
title: (Alpha) Exploration in Public Health
description: Investigation of emergent fields of inquiry in public health. (B) biostatistics; (D) environmental health; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (I) Native Hawaiian and Inigenous health; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (U) public health.

subject: SW
title: The Field of Social Work
description: Orientation to the profession of social work; historical development, values and philosophy, scope and aims.

subject: SW
title: General Social Work Practice I
description: Orientation to practice principles, concepts, values, knowledge base, and their application.
prereq_raw: 200 (complete with C or better) and majors only

children.text: ( complete with C or better ) and majors only

subject: SW
title: General Social Work Practice II
description: Introduction to practice skills with individuals, families, groups, and communities. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction congruent with professional expectations.
prereq_raw: 302 (complete with C or better) and majors only

children.text: ( complete with C or better ) and majors only

subject: SW
title: History of Social Welfare
description: Historical developments and implications of social welfare activities, institutions, and policies and European backgrounds; introduce social welfare developments in selected non-European countries.

subject: SW
title: Social Welfare as a Social Institution
description: Study of U.S. social welfare institutional structures, programs, and policies addressing human need; focus on Hawai‘i’s legislative processes and social service programs; emphasis on oral communication inherent to advocacy, legislative, and policymaking processes.

subject: SW
title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment
description: Examination of complex sociocultural factors that privilege some and oppress/marginalize others. Challenges commonly held tropes and complicates the discourse regarding individual, family, group, organizational and community development within the social environment.

subject: SW
title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment II
description: Focus on human development across the lifespan with attention given to unique challenges and opportunities faced in each phase. Emphasis on “populations at risk” and the strengths and assets unique to diverse populations.
prereq_raw: 360 with a grade of C or better. Recommended: 200. DS

subject: SW
title: Topics in Social Welfare
description: An examination of current trends in the field of social welfare.

subject: SW
title: Undergraduate Field Education I
description: Introduction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
prereq_raw: 302, 325, 326 (or concurrent), 360, and 361 (or concurrent) complete with C or better; and majors only

children.text: complete with C or better ; and majors only

subject: SW
title: General Social Work Practice III
description: Use of problem-solving processes and ethical models of decision-making in practice with individuals, families, groups, and communities.
prereq_raw: 303, 326, and 361 complete with C or better; and majors only

children.text: complete with C or better ; and majors only

subject: SW
title: General Social Work Practice IV
description: Examination of practice methods and intervention models; identification and analysis of issues related to practice. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction congruent with professional expectations.

subject: SW
title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.
prereq_raw: 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200; or consent

subject: SW
title: Research Development in Social Welfare
description: Introduction to and application of language of research, theoretical concepts underlying advancement of knowledge, practical steps in research.
prereq_raw: completion of required junior-level SW courses (i.e., 302, 303, 325, 326, 360, 361, and 391) with C or better

children.text: completion of required junior-level SW courses ( i.e., 302

subject: SW
title: Native Hawaiian Perspectives: A Cultural Context for Well-Being
description: To preserve the cultural knowledge of kupuna as it relates to health and wellbeing. Disseminate cultural knowledge of health and well-being to social work students and students in allied health professions. SW or Social Welfare students only.

subject: SW
title: Ke A‘o Mau: Learning Preserved
description: To provide a holistic examination of issues and to explore culturally-anchored resolutions and practices to achieve social justice and health and well-being. SW, Social Welfare, or PH students only.

subject: SW
title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
description: Provides students with a body of knowledge, skills, and values that facilitate social work with Native Hawaiians. SW or Social Welfare students.

subject: SW
title: Social Services with Children
description: Study of current social services for children in the U.S. with focus on familiarization of child welfare programs and services in Hawai‘i.

subject: SW
title: Social Welfare Concepts and Issues in Gerontology
description: Aging and its effect on the individual, family groups, associations, and communities. Impact of aging on social service delivery systems, public policy and role of social work.

subject: SW
title: Topics in Social Welfare
description: An examination of current trends and issues in social work.

subject: SW
title: Undergraduate Field Education II
description: Intermediate instruction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
prereq_raw: 391 complete with C or better, and majors only

children.text: complete with C or better , and majors only

subject: SW
title: Undergraduate Field Education III
description: Advanced instruction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
prereq_raw: 490 complete with C or better, and majors only

children.text: complete with C or better , and majors only

subject: SW
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Planned individualized study or research in special area related to social work practice interest. Up to 3 credit hours.
prereq_raw: majors only, senior standing, and consent of program chair and faculty advisor

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Individuals
description: Beginning practice course introduces students to the basic processes of social work and the roles and skills needed for generalist practice. Relevant theories of social work practice with individuals are explored for the efficacy with various problems and for their applicability to practice with various ethnocultures, social classes, and oppressed populations. Interviewing and interpersonal skill development are incorporated.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Families and Groups
description: Practice course builds upon the generalist framework and foundation content presented in 606. Special emphasis is given on models for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of practice with families and groups. Relevant theories of groups and the principles of group dynamics and group work methods are examined in regard to task, therapeutic, psychoeducational, and social development groups. Family content includes structural, behavioral, communication/experiential, and culturally-specific theories of intervention.

subject: SW
title: Social Welfare Policy and Services
description: Examines in a historical and comparative framework the economic, social, political, organizational, and administrative factors influencing the development, formulation, and implementation of social welfare policies in the U.S. Provides opportunity for the application of various models of social policy analysis in major areas of social welfare programming and service delivery.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice in Communities and Organizations
description: Community conceptualization; organized roles of developer, enabler, broker, mediator, and advocate; diagnostic and problem-solving technology; the special characteristics of the social worker as community organizer; matrix of structural objectives; sources and use of power; how to build an organization; and interorganizational negotiation.

subject: SW
title: Organization and Administration in Social Work
description: Introduction to formal organization theory. Social service administration examined and implications for service delivery systems developed.

subject: SW
title: Policies, Programs and Services on Aging
description: Explores policies, programs, and services for older adults. Students learn about the aging network, assess older adults’ needs, link older adults to appropriate services in the community, and track legislative bills that address older adults’ quality of life.

subject: SW
title: Death and Dying
description: Physical, social, cultural, psychological, and spiritual dimensions of dying, death, and bereavement.

subject: SW
title: Social and Cultural Aspects of Aging
description: Overview of aging from the biopsycho, socioeconomic and cultural perspectives. Explores common theories of aging. Emphasis on bridging the gap between the realm of concepts and theories, and the world of practice in gerontology.

subject: SW
title: Introduction to Scientific Methods and Principles in Social Work
description: Understanding and interpreting results of nomothetic and idiographic research; design principles and statistical analyses and their relationship to practices; use of published research.

subject: SW
title: Research Designs and Data Analyses for the Evaluation of Practice Effectiveness
description: Extending the study of scientific methods introduced in 640. Covers the range of empirical research methods and data analytic procedures suitable for knowledge building and practice evaluation at all levels of intervention from case to program.

subject: SW
title: Quantitative Methods I
description: Introduction to quantitative methods in behavioral sciences. Introduction to general linear model as principle of data analysis. Course requires basic statistics. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

subject: SW
title: Applied Regression and Analysis of Variance
description: Introduction to linear statistical models as principle of data analysis. Topics include multiple regression models with continuous and categorical predictors. ANOVA with multiple factors, ANOVA with repeated measures, and ANCOVA.

subject: SW
title: Multivariate Methods
description: Multivariate forms of multiple linear regression, analysis of variance, and analysis of co-variance. Multiple discriminant analysis, canonical correlation, and principal components analysis are discussed.

subject: SW
title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment I
description: Examination of complex factors that privilege some and oppress/marginalize others; challenges commonly held tropes and complicates the discourse regarding individual, family, group, organizational and community development within the social environment.

subject: SW
title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment II
description: Focus on human development across the lifespan with attention given to unique challenges and opportunities faced in each phase. Emphasis is placed on “populations at risk” and the strengths and assets unique to diverse populations.

subject: SW
title: Treatment of Chemical Dependency
description: Introduction to treatment of alcoholism and other chemical dependencies. Application of social work strategies in work with individuals and families in the disease and recovery process.

subject: SW
title: Child Welfare as a Field of Social Work
description: Emphasis on the developments in child welfare; issues, concerns with regard to needs and rights, and the application of social work services to problems associated with needs for protection. Review of historical, theoretical, empirical, and legal findings for skill development in intervening in dysfunctional parent/child interaction.

subject: SW
title: Community and Public Health Practice
description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery.

subject: SW
title: Topics in Social Welfare
description: Current trends in field of social welfare. Recent courses have focused on forensic social work, immigrants and refugees, and leadership in human services. Meets seminar requirement.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time in different topics

subject: SW
title: Marriage and Family Therapy
description: Introduction to couple and family therapy offers an overview of family systems perspective, theory and technique relevant to informing effective social work case planning, case management, advocacy, and interaction with clients. Graduate students only.

subject: SW
title: Generalist Field Education I
description: Field education is the signature pedagogy of social work education. Students will engage in supervised social work practice and have the opportunity to apply generalist knowledge, skills, values, and ethics to practice.
prereq_raw: 606 (or concurrent)(with a minimum grade of C)

subject: SW
title: Generalist Field Education II
description: Field education is the signature pedagogy of social work education. Students will engage in supervised social work practice and have the opportunity to apply generalist knowledge, skills, values, and ethics to practice.
prereq_raw: 690 and 607 (or concurrent) and 631 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of C)

children.text: ( all with a minimum grade of C )

subject: SW
title: Health and Aging
description: Biological and physiological changes associated with aging. Social and psychological factors associated with health maintenance. Major threats to health, changing patterns of morbidity and mortality of the aged.

subject: SW
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Students, on the basis of special interest, select a faculty member to work with on a problem for which planned individualized study or research is deemed advisable.

subject: SW
title: Thesis Research
description: Independent research under supervision of a thesis committee. Includes formal proposal and defense of finished research.

subject: SW
title: Methods of Group Psychotherapy
description: Designed specifically to train students in the theory and practice of leading psychotherapy groups; it includes historical developments, research, theories, and application of group psychotherapy, group techniques and exercises.

subject: SW
title: Therapeutic Strategies with the Older Adult
description: Focuses on interdisciplinary strategies with older adults: individual, family, and group therapy; eclectic mental health approaches; case management; and environmental intervention. Emphasis placed on the use of these strategies as preventive, as well as supportive, measures for the well, transition, and frail elderly. Meets seminar requirement.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Children and Families
description: Advanced practice course for students specializing in social work with children and families. Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of both theoretical formulations and therapeutic techniques for practice in the field of family and child welfare. Emphasis placed on the development of specialized knowledge and skills for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of a variety of common child and family practice situations.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work Practice with Children and Families
description: Designed for students in the child and family concentration and builds upon past knowledge and skill development in practice classes and in the practicum. Students integrate, demonstrate, and extend earlier learning, acquire new knowledge, and learn and practice new skills. Organized around student case presentations in a consultation format. Meets seminar requirement.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice in Health Care
description: Didactic and experiential learning activity focuses on the major role functions of the social worker in the health field including assessment, contracting, counseling, advocacy, case management, discharge planning, family group work, community and team building. Covers health care policy, research directions in practice and social work management issues.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Health Care
description: Through the use of case studies developed by the students, social work practice is examined in three areas of health care: primary care provided in health departments and medical groups, hospital-based services, and long-term care. Meets seminar requirement.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Mental Health
description: Prepares students for social work practice in mental health settings. Focused on engagement and assessment while emphasizing cultural, person in environment, and strengths-based approaches.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice in Mental Health
description: Prepares students for social work practice in mental health settings, with a focus on history and policy in the U.S. and Hawai‘i, as well as culturally-grounded and evidence-based practice.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Older Adults
description: Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of theoretical formulations and intervention strategies for working with older adults and their families. Emphasis on diversity/justice.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work with Older Adults
description: Designed for gerontology specialization students to gain advanced knowledge for working with diverse older adults and their families. Emphasis on strength perspectives on aging.

subject: SW
title: Social Policy Analysis
description: Students pursue in-depth a specific topic in the areas of social planning, social policy analysis, evaluation of social programs, administration, supervision, and consultation. Selectively a comparative perspective is introduced and case studies used to illustrate concepts, principles, and techniques, with implications for practice. Meets seminar requirement.

subject: SW
title: Social Work and the Law
description: Knowledge of judicial systems and law relevant to social work practice in corrections, child-family welfare, health, and mental health. Skills for effective participation in the legal process are acquired in moot court and in practice for testifying.

subject: SW
title: Review of Research in Social Work
description: In-depth study of research in a substantive area. Each seminar will be devoted to a particular topic: e.g., foster care of children, effectiveness of social work intervention, etc.

subject: SW
title: Individual or Group Research Project— Plan B
description: Independent research (group of two to seven students or by an individual student) undertaken under the sponsorship of a faculty advisor. Elements are selection of a topic related to the practice of social work or knowledge relevant to that practice, utilization of empirical research methodology in collecting and analyzing original data, and preparation of a scholarly paper.

subject: SW
title: Individual or Group Research Project– Plan B
description: Same as 743.

subject: SW
title: Individual or Group Research Project– Plan B
description: Same as 743. A-F only

subject: SW
title: Analysis and Development of Knowledge for Social Work
description: Focuses on developing an understanding of philosophy of science, theory development, social work epistemology, and the analysis and development of knowledge for social work practice.
prereq_raw: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent

subject: SW
title: Quantitative Methods II
description: Empirical research methodology with emphasis on design principles and measurement theory; design and measurement issues and problems in cross-cultural research.
prereq_raw: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent

subject: SW
title: Qualitative Research: Philosophical, Methodological and Analytic Approaches
description: Theories and methods of qualitative research; problem formulation, informant selection, study design, data collection and analysis utilizing qualitative approaches.

subject: SW
title: Dissertation Seminar
description: Culminating experience in social welfare doctoral specialization; integration of PhD core and specialization course work.
prereq_raw: classified student in PhD in social welfare program or consent

children.text: classified student in PhD in social welfare program

subject: SW
title: Seminar in International Social Work
description: Approaches to social problems and trends in the profession in international, cross-cultural perspectives. Emphasis on developmental aspects of social work. Political, economic, social, and cultural forces shaping social welfare in national development. Meets seminar requirement.

subject: SW
title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
description: Hawaiian culture, past and present. Explores and examines possible approaches to working with Hawaiians and part-Hawaiians. Special emphasis on supports in the Hawaiian system that may promote maximal functioning for those Hawaiians experiencing problems in today’s society. Meets seminar requirement.

subject: SW
title: Seminar on Women and Health
description: Women’s health and the role of women health professionals. Current literature and research regarding attitudes, roles, rights, and health care.

subject: SW
title: Specialist Field Education I
description: Instruction in the field is continued. The field experience in the second year provides an opportunity for the student to test out concepts, principles, theories, and alternate approaches in actual practice settings.
prereq_raw: 717 (or concurrent) or 722 (or concurrent) or 724 (or concurrent) or 726 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of B -)

children.text: ( all with a minimum grade of B -)

subject: SW
title: Specialist Field Education II
description: Continuation of 790.
prereq_raw: 790 and; 718 (or concurrent); or 723 (or concurrent); or 725 (or concurrent); or 727 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of B-)

children.text: ( all with a minimum grade of B- )

subject: SW
title: Advanced Social Welfare Policy Analysis and Change
description: Builds on 630 and emphasizes a more thorough and comprehensive examination of major policies, programs, and populations central to a concentration (Health, Mental Health, Gerontology, Child and Family). Students learn a more focused and applied analysis of the relationship between social policy, research, and social work practice.

subject: TIM
title: International Exchange Programs
description: UH Mānoa School of Travel Industry Management majors participating in approved international exchange programs.

subject: TIM
title: Internship I
description: Introduction to travel industry. Discussion of job search strategies, TIM internship requirements, career and academic planning.

subject: TIM
title: Introduction to Travel Industry Management
description: Overview of travel industry and related major business components. Analysis of links between hotel, food, transportation, recreation, and other industries comprising tourism.

subject: TIM
title: Food and World Cultures
description: An integrated cross-cultural approach to the study of foods and cultures. Examine history, concepts, principles of cultures and cuisines, the background of food tradition including habitat, social status, religious beliefs, gender, and other environmental considerations.

subject: TIM
title: Internship II
description: A minimum of four hundred hours of travel industry experience. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required.

subject: TIM
title: Internship III
description: A minimum of four hundred hours of travel industry experience. Position must be different from TIM 200 position and of a more responsible nature or in a different organization. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required.

subject: TIM
title: Legal Environment of the Travel Industry
description: Origin, development, and principles of common, statutory, constitutional, international, and maritime law relating to hospitality industry.

subject: TIM
title: Information Systems Technology
description: Computer applications in the travel industry; operation and evaluation of specific travel industry systems and applied business systems.
prereq_raw: 101; and either ICS 101, or both LTEC 112 and LTEC 113

subject: TIM
title: Management of Service Enterprises
description: Principles and philosophies of management with special emphasis on those principles and theories that are most relevant to management in service-based industries. Students may not earn credit for 303 and BUS 315.

subject: TIM
title: Principles of Travel Industry Marketing
description: Concepts, problems, processes of marketing within the travel industry; development of marketing strategies including product, place, promotion, and price for travel institutions. Students may not earn credit for 304 and BUS 312.

subject: TIM
title: Financial Management for the Travel Industry
description: Cash flow determination and management strategies for financing hospitality ventures and expansion. Determining the financial viability of proposed and existing operations through traditional and state-of-the-art techniques.
prereq_raw: 101, ACC 200 and ACC 210; and NREM 203, MATH 203, MATH 215, MATH 241, or BUS 250

subject: TIM
title: Human Resource Management: Travel Industry
description: Comprehensive overview of human resources management (HRM) with emphasis on the supervision in the travel industry, including HRM as a firm’s strategic asset, contemporary theories, issues and developments, to improve employee recruitment productivity and retention.

subject: TIM
title: Institutional Purchasing
description: Procurement responsibilities in hospitality management. Emphasis on institutions supplying hospitality operations and legislation which controls standards of industrial supplies and goods.

subject: TIM
title: Club Management
description: Introduction to club and institutional management, including operations, services, and facilities.

subject: TIM
title: Foodservice Management
description: Critical and essential aspects of managing foodservice operations including principles of food safety and sanitation, procedural knowledge in front and back of the house and guest relations.

subject: TIM
title: Hotel Management
